Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. Slater-Condon parameters are typically overestimated by 20-50 percent (with some 3d outliers underestimated by 1-20 percent) because of the missing dynamic correlation, so the authors explicitly do not recommend minimal active space CASSCF-SO where accurate term excitation energies are needed, and recommend CASPT2 or NEVPT2 instead for quantitative work. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z; SOC detail: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization

compound_name: QUESTDB benchmark database - 542 vertical excitation energies with automated APC active-space selection
point_group: reduced to the highest available symmetry implementable for each molecule
geometry_source: QUESTDB benchmark geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF with MC-PDFT (tPBE) and NEVPT2, using automated entropy-ranked active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: Automated 'max(n,m)' spaces capped by a maximum CSF count: max(4,4) (N_max_CSF = 20), max(5,5), max(12,12) and others. Orbitals are ranked by occupancy and entropy pairs (n_j, S_j) and pruned until the CSF count falls under the cap.
active_space_protocol: Approximate pair-coefficient (APC) automated selection with a 'max(n,m)' cap set by a maximum CSF count: orbitals carry an occupancy and an approximated entropy (n_j, S_j) and are admitted in entropy order until the CSF count would exceed N_max_CSF. A worked example takes a max(4,4) target (cap 20 CSFs) and returns a (5,4) space with exactly 20 CSFs. Critically, the authors then FILTER: 20-30% of the automatically generated active spaces were poor and were eliminated by applying a threshold to the SA-CASSCF absolute error, leaving 373 of the 542 excitations for the method comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Largest benchmarking of MC-PDFT and HMC-PDFT to date, over the QUESTDB set of 542 vertical excitations. After discarding the 20-30% of automatically chosen active spaces that were poor, HMC-PDFT performs about as well as NEVPT2 and CC2 on the remaining 373 excitations. The optimal fraction of SA-CASSCF energy to mix into HMC-PDFT with the tPBE on-top functional was found to be 25%, i.e. the value already used in tPBE0. NEVPT2 performance is significantly affected by active-space quality, and at normal grid size tPBE is on average about 114x cheaper than NEVPT2 for large max(12,12) spaces.

formula: 14 TM ions in 2+ and 3+ charge states
method: renormalized internally contracted multireference coupled cluster with singles and doubles (RIC-MRCCSD) in a spin-free formulation, needing no reduced density matrices or cumulants beyond three-body; compared against NEVPT2, approximate fourth-order NEVPT4(SD), multireference CEPA(0) and Koehn's IC-MRCCSD

electronic_structure_description: Errors in excitation energies relative to experiment, shown as violin plots against other multireference methods. Increasing the flow parameter s consistently reduces both the MAD and the spread, as expected since larger s recovers more dynamic correlation - at the cost of numerical robustness, with s = 0.5 Eh^-2 failing to converge. At the largest convergent value, s = 0.4 Eh^-2, RIC-MRCCSD accuracy with the 3d-only space lies between NEVPT2 and NEVPT4. Adding the 4d orbitals reduces the error further, with RIC-MRCCSD then even beating IC-MRCC on MAD - but the authors qualify this: the double-shell effect is traditionally invoked to compensate for missing dynamic correlation and should ideally not be needed by a high-accuracy multireference method, and indeed most standard MR methods barely change when the space is expanded.

geometry_source: not stated in the main text read
method: restricted active space configuration interaction in the hole and particle approximation, RAS(h,p) - the full CI within RAS2 plus all configurations with one hole in RAS1 and one electron in RAS3 - corrected at second order by Epstein-Nesbet (EN) and Davidson-Kapuy (DK) partitionings, with and without an energy level shift; benchmarked against NEVPT2 and literature reference data
basis_set: several basis sets compared; the DK correction is shown to depend weakly on basis set
active_space_orbital_description: RAS1, RAS2 and RAS3 subspaces in the hole-and-particle truncation; per-molecule spaces are not given in the main text
electronic_structure_description: RAS(h,p) lacks effective dynamic correlation and systematically overestimates singlet excitation energies by about 0.8 eV, with much smaller errors for triplets. Epstein-Nesbet perturbation gives only marginal improvement and increases the statistical scatter; Davidson-Kapuy gives a more consistent correction but tends to overcompensate, and adding an energy level shift to the DK partition removes that bias. Decomposing the correction shows that the dominant contribution comes from terms resembling a state-specific orbital relaxation through singles, while the more expensive 1h2p and 2h2p terms matter little - which the authors read as a route to cheaper targeted perturbative schemes. Because the DK-based corrections depend only weakly on the basis set, a composite strategy works: large-basis RAS(h,p) energies combined with small-basis DK-plus-shift corrections give significant savings at minimal accuracy cost.
reference_short: Perumal Marisami & Casanova, Assessing Second-Order Perturbative Corrections to Restricted Active Space CI for Valence Excitations in Organic Molecules, J. Phys. Chem. A 2025, 129, 11736-11748

formula: the organic molecules of Thiel's benchmark set, minus ethene and cyclopropene
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of Thiel's benchmark set
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2), a new zeroth-order Hamiltonian partitioning that interpolates between state-specific and state-averaged Fock operators through a dynamical weighting parameter zeta; compared throughout against SA-CASSCF, single-state CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2
software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of Thiel's benchmark set, which differ from molecule to molecule and are not restated here

The paper stresses that careful selection is what makes doubly excited states reachable at manageable cost, and that 0.1-0.2 eV accuracy is achievable with appropriate spaces. Whether the 3s Rydberg orbital is included in the space materially changes the answer: leave it out and a single genuine double excitation appears, put it in and the doubly excited configuration mixes with the Rydberg one.
electronic_structure_description: For one of the difficult cases the two computed states at 7.979(40) and 8.170(41) eV from CIPSI agree well with the reference 7.979 and 8.185 eV. Both states carry important singly and doubly excited configurations, combined in phase for the lower state and out of phase for the upper one; the mixing is weak at CASSCF and becomes pronounced only after the perturbative correction. Enlarging the basis from 6-31+G* to aug-cc-pVDZ or aug-cc-pVTZ stabilizes the (n -> 3s) Rydberg configuration relative to the (n,n -> pi*,pi*) one and suppresses the strong mixing - 6-31+G* is simply too compact to model it. Downgrading to CC4 or CCSDT also unmixes the two configurations, giving one genuine double and one Rydberg single; oddly the mixing returns at CC3, but for the wrong reason.

geometry_source: Experimental geometry from the cited structural references was used, so all reported excitations are vertical. The molecule was placed in the xy plane; no numerical geometry or Cartesian block is printed.
method: state-averaged extended-active-space CASSCF(6,12) followed by state-specific multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP) for each individual state; oscillator strengths use CASSCF transition moments and MRMP transition energies
software: MOLPRO for CASSCF reference wave functions; MR2D Version 2 for MRMP perturbation calculations; IBM RS6000-590 workstations at IMS
basis_set: Dunning cc-pVTZ on carbon and cc-pVDZ on hydrogen, with H polarization omitted in the production calculations; the explicit test compared [4s3p2d/2s] with [4s3p2d/2s1p] and changed valence excitation energies by <0.03 eV. No Rydberg functions were included.
active_space_orbital_description: Six pi electrons distributed among twelve pi orbitals. Starting from the six-valence-pi-orbital CAS (three bonding pi plus three antibonding pi* orbitals), the authors doubled the active orbital count in every symmetry. The paper does not print a complete symmetry-by-symmetry list of the six added pi orbitals. Sigma electrons remain outside the CAS and their dynamic sigma-pi polarization is introduced by MRMP.
active_space_protocol: (6,6): six pi electrons in the six valence pi/pi* orbitals; (6,12): active orbital count doubled in every symmetry and the same state calculations repeated. This row records the converged extended (6,12) results.
nroots_per_mult: five D6h singlet components and five D6h triplet components are tabulated (with D2h component labels); the exact root groups and weights used in each state average are not stated
electronic_structure_description: The enlarged pi space primarily improves the ionic plus states by moving part of the important sigma-pi polarization/nondynamical response into the reference. Covalent-state CASSCF energies change little, while ionic-state CASSCF excitations decrease by about 0.3-0.5 eV. The resulting MRMP spectrum reaches <=0.23 eV error for the tabulated singlets and <=0.29 eV for triplets. Detailed CASSCF configuration coefficients are printed only for the smaller CAS(6,6), not for this extended reference.
Other: TOTAL ENERGY: ground-state MRMP energy with twelve active pi orbitals = -231.62903 Eh; the authors note that the smaller-space MRMP energy is paradoxically 0.00170 Eh lower because second-order perturbation theory can overestimate correlation when its zeroth-order Hamiltonian is incomplete. VERTICAL SINGLET RESULTS (Table VII; D6h state [D2h component], CASSCF/MRMP eV, oscillator strength): 1^1B2u- [1^1B3u-] 4.89/4.67, f=0; 1^1B1u+ [1^1B2u+] 7.57/6.14, f=0; 1^1E1u+ components [1^1B3u+ and 2^1B2u+] both 8.78/6.84, f=0.8599 for each printed component; 1^1E2g- components [2^1Ag-,1^1B1g-] both 8.04/7.71, f=0. VERTICAL TRIPLETS: 1^3B1u- [1^3B2u-] 3.85/3.83; 1^3E1u- [1^3B3u-] 4.83/4.47, with the degenerate 2^3B2u- component printed at CASSCF 4.83 but no separate MRMP number in Table VII; 1^3B2u+ [1^3B3u+] 6.78/5.45; 1^3E2g- components [1^3Ag-,1^3B1g-] both 7.15/6.92 eV. EXPERIMENTAL COMPARISONS printed in Table VII are 4.90 (1B2u), 6.20 (1B1u), 6.94 (1E1u), 7.80 (1E2g), 3.95 (3B1u), 4.76 (3E1u), 5.60 (3B2u), and 6.83 eV (3E2g). The extended MRMP deviations are therefore -0.23, -0.06, -0.10, -0.09, -0.12, -0.29, -0.15, and +0.09 eV, respectively. ACTIVE-SPACE EFFECT: relative to CAS(6,6), CASSCF ionic-state excitations fall by 0.34 eV (1B1u), 0.51 eV (1E1u), and 0.46 eV (3B2u), while corresponding MRMP predictions rise toward experiment by 0.31, 0.51, and 0.38 eV. The dipole-allowed 1E1u oscillator strength improves from 0.7558 to 0.8599, versus 1.25 experiment. H polarization changes valence excitation energies by <0.03 eV and oscillator strengths negligibly. No Rydberg functions/states are included.

software: PySCF (AVAS active-space generation and CASSCF convergence) with cross-checks in ORCA 6.0.1; Gaussian 16 also used

method: CASSCF with systematic enlargement of the active space, used to obtain reference spin densities against which density functional results are assessed

active_space_orbital_description: The same minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces as the quartet, enlarged along a different sequence: eleven orbitals adding virtuals with iron dxz and dxy character, twelve adding one with dyz character, and finally fourteen including the fourth iron dz2 double-shell orbital together with an additional empty ligand orbital.
active_space_protocol: The same construction and enlargement strategy as for the quartet but with a different order of orbital admission, reflecting which double-shell orbitals could be stabilised in this state. The largest space contains the four iron dxz, dxy, dyz and dz2 double-shell orbitals. The contributions of the iron double-shell orbitals to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for this state than for the quartet.
electronic_structure_description: For the doublet state the spin density shows larger deviations with respect to the size of the active space than the quartet does, converging gradually toward the largest reference as the space is enlarged. The minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces, without double-shell orbitals, are qualitatively similar to the reference and suffice for a qualitative estimate, but quantitatively correct spin densities require the iron double-shell orbitals to be included. Spaces containing thirteen active electrons give very similar spin densities. The same bonding picture applies as for the quartet, with one iron d orbital non-interacting and three interacting covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals.
Other: The space is built up from a qualitative molecular orbital picture: four metal 3d orbitals plus both nitrosyl pi-star orbitals, extended by a fifth metal d orbital, giving a minimal seven electrons in seven orbitals; adding both nitrosyl pi orbitals gives eleven electrons in nine orbitals. It is then systematically enlarged toward a double shell, one metal d orbital at a time, through eleven, twelve, thirteen and fifteen orbitals for the quartet and eleven, twelve and fourteen for the doublet. The obstacles encountered are reported rather than glossed: identifying the double-shell orbitals is described as not trivial because they mix considerably with antibonding ligand orbitals, so additional ligand orbitals had to be admitted to keep the space stable; in one case a double-shell orbital rotated into an empty ligand orbital and a further virtual had to be added to recover it; the fifth metal double-shell orbital could not be included at all because its destabilization by the point-charge environment would require many more ligand orbitals; and an alternative route adding a ligand sigma and sigma-star pair proved incompatible with including the remaining double-shell orbitals. The result is that convergence depends on which state is asked about. For the quartet the spin density depends only weakly on the space, and the minimal seven-orbital and nine-orbital calculations without any double-shell effect already agree qualitatively with the largest reference. For the doublet the deviations are larger, the spin density converging gradually toward the reference as the space grows, and the authors state the distinction precisely: the minimal spaces suffice for a qualitative estimate while quantitatively correct spin densities require the metal double-shell orbitals. Consistently, the double-shell contributions to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for the doublet than for the quartet. So the same molecule, same property, different spin state, and the answer to whether a double shell is needed flips. The bonding picture the space reveals is stable across all of them: one metal d orbital does not interact with the ligand at all, while three others interact strongly and covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals to give two bonding, two antibonding and one nonbonding combination. One structural caveat: the ligand field is modelled by point charges rather than real ligands, and the authors note that the modelled field is not strong enough, so the environment that destabilises the fifth double-shell orbital is itself an approximation.

ligand_set: unsubstituted porphyrin dianion and a carbonyl
point_group: C2v used for the CASSCF calculations
geometry_source: Optimized with the B3PW91 functional in the BS-I basis, with vibrational frequencies confirming minima and transition states; the CASSCF calculations were single points in BS-II on those geometries
method: CASSCF used as a diagnostic of multireference character on species from a reaction path otherwise computed by density functional theory; geometries and frequencies from the hybrid functional, energies re-evaluated in the larger basis
software: MOLCAS 6.0 for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 03 for the density functional work and NBO 3.1 for population analysis
basis_set: BS-II: cc-pVDZ on carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and hydrogen with a Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn effective core potential and a (311111/22111/411) valence basis on ruthenium
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen orbitals itemized by symmetry block as five a1, three b1, three a2 and three b2, chosen by three stated rules: all ruthenium 4d orbitals, the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them for the double-shell effect, and the four Gouterman porphyrin pi orbitals (two occupied in a1 and b2, two unoccupied in a2 and b1).
active_space_protocol: The same fourteen orbitals are used for every species in the series, with only the electron count changed to follow the charge, so that comparisons between oxidation states cannot be an artifact of a different orbital choice.
electronic_structure_description: Much less stable than the singlet, by 48.4 kcal/mol. Its geometry was optimized separately with the unrestricted functional. The leading configuration carries 89.40% of the weight, the largest of the five species, and assigns ruthenium +II.
Other: The active space here is specified by three stated rules rather than by a number, and the rules are what make the five species comparable. All ruthenium 4d orbitals and their electrons must be in the space; the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them must also be in, to capture the double-shell effect; and the four porphyrin pi orbitals of the classic Gouterman set -- two occupied, in the totally symmetric and one of the antisymmetric blocks, and two unoccupied -- must be in. That gives fourteen orbitals, itemized by symmetry block as five, three, three and three, and the SAME fourteen orbitals are used for the neutral singlet, the neutral triplet, the cation and the anion, with only the electron count changing to follow the charge: fourteen, fourteen, thirteen and fifteen. Holding the orbital set fixed while the electron count tracks the charge is exactly the design needed to compare oxidation states, since any difference between species then cannot be blamed on a different choice of orbitals. Only for the oxo anion is the set enlarged, by one further orbital added specifically to represent the ruthenium-oxygen antibonding interaction -- an enlargement made because a specific bond is being broken, not to recover more correlation. The space is used as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than as a source of energetics. The reported result is that the leading configuration carries more than 85% of the weight in every one of the five species (85.66, 89.40, 88.80, 88.02 and 85.65 percent), from which the authors conclude static correlation is small and a single-determinant method is adequate; they further check that the natural orbitals from the unrestricted density functional calculation are essentially the same as the multiconfigurational ones. Two independent checks pointing the same way is a stronger licence for the cheaper method than either alone. The second finding is chemical and cuts against the experimental proposal that motivated the calculation: the leading configuration assigns ruthenium the +II oxidation state in ALL five species, including the cation and both anions, so the experimentally proposed +I-to-+III change is not what the wave function shows -- the added or removed electron sits on the porphyrin ring, not on the metal. The scope limit is that these are CASSCF wave functions with no perturbative correction, so the weights speak to static correlation only, and a fourteen-orbital space concentrated on the metal d shell and the Gouterman four cannot report multireference character arising anywhere outside it. The calculations were run in the smaller correlation-consistent basis under C2v symmetry even for the species whose optimized geometry is C4v.

correlation_correction: None; the CASSCF wave function is used to measure the weight of the leading configuration, not to produce correlated energies

method: CASSCF(8,8) single points and geometry comparison; (U)B3LYP for geometries, frequencies and thermochemistry

active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight active orbitals: the six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair (pN), and the sigma orbital located at the divalent carbon atom C1.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF was run for an explicitly diagnostic purpose — "to check the viability of such a single-determinant approach and to describe the nature of the singlet and triplet H2NC6H4+" — after the bulk of the study had been done at B3LYP. The test is the weight of the ground-state reference determinant in the CASSCF wave function, read from the coefficient of the lowest eigenvector and from the fractional populations of the eight active orbitals. The same test had been applied to the parent phenyl cation, where the reference determinant contributes more than 90% (eigenvector coefficients 0.94 for the singlet and 0.95 for the triplet), justifying B3LYP there.
electronic_structure_description: Excited singlet lying at least 10 kcal/mol above the triplet in the gas phase. Its CASSCF wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and cannot be properly represented by a single determinant, so the B3LYP description of this state is not reliable — in contrast to the parent phenyl cation, whose singlet has a reference determinant weight above 90% (eigenvector coefficient 0.94). Geometrically the singlet differs from the planar triplet: the nitrogen is slightly pyramidalized and the divalent carbon C1 is slightly bent out of plane and puckered.
Other: The (8,8) space — six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair, and the sigma orbital on the divalent carbon — is used to answer a single question: can a single-determinant method be trusted for this ion? The answer differs by spin state, and that difference is the paper's finding. For the 3B2 triplet the CASSCF wave function is dominated by one configuration, with the leading coefficient above 0.93 and fractional populations of the eight active orbitals close to 0, 1 and 2 — so B3LYP is adequate there, and indeed the CASSCF and UB3LYP geometries and charges "are in excellent agreement only for the 3B2 state". For the 1A' singlet the wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and "cannot be properly described by a single-determinant" treatment, so the B3LYP singlet results are not reliable. This is a clean case of an active space being used to bound the validity of a cheaper method rather than to produce numbers. The orbital populations also carry chemical content that a single-determinant picture would hide: in the triplet, the sigma and one pi orbital are each singly occupied, with the sigma electron highly localized on C1 but the pi electron delocalized over the ring and onto nitrogen. Combined with UB3LYP spin densities showing nitrogen carrying the second highest spin density (0.35), this makes the triplet "65% diradical, 35% carbene character at divalent C1" — which explains why it does not react with neutral sigma nucleophiles (there is no cation at C1, the largest positive charge being +0.37 on C4) but adds readily to pi nucleophiles as an electrophilic radical. For the parent phenyl cation the same diagnostic gave >90% single-reference character for BOTH states, so amino substitution is what breaks the single-determinant description of the singlet.

notes: Study of the generation and reactivity of the 4-aminophenyl cation by photolysis of 4-chloroaniline. The experimental evidence — reaction quantum yields unchanged by added traps and unchanged in dilute solution where quenching of the short-lived triplet is excluded — indicates the reaction does not proceed by electron-transfer quenching of the excited aniline or by exciplex formation, but by trapping of an intermediate arising directly from the TRIPLET state. B3LYP was chosen for the bulk of the work because it is affordable, has been used for the parent phenyl cation, accounts fairly well for the singlet-triplet splitting, and yields geometries very similar to RCCSD(T)(full)/6-31G(d) and CASSCF(6,7)/6-31G(d). Both CASSCF and B3LYP place the triplet lowest by at least 10 kcal/mol in the gas phase, in accord with a previous evaluation. active_space_protocol: The same space is used for both Jahn-Teller components, each generated from its own open-shell reference configuration: (9a1)2(6b2)2(1b1)2(2b1)1(1a2)2 for one and (9a1)2(6b2)2(1b1)2(2b1)2(1a2)1 for the other. The space was validated by enlarging it with one additional virtual orbital of each of the two symmetries; the resulting optimized geometry was close to the original, and the added orbitals were found to carry occupation numbers below 0.003.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2A2, the upper Jahn-Teller component, lying a few kcal/mol above the 2B1 state. The starting reference configuration is (9a1)2(6b2)2(1b1)2(2b1)2(1a2)1, and the same active space is used as for the lower component. In the optimized geometry only the carbon-carbon bond perpendicular to the binary symmetry axis shows double-bond character, in contrast to the diene-like structure of the lower component. Its total energy is -193.146453 hartree, and in combination with the magnesium cation -392.510536 hartree, giving a binding energy of 74.3 kcal/mol against 74.0 for the lower component. The geometry agrees with previous theoretical work on the same footing as the lower component.
Other: The multiconfigurational treatment here is confined to one species for one reason -- orbital degeneracy -- and the paper says so directly: the main problem in the cyclopentadienyl radical is the degeneracy of the valence orbitals, which produces a Jahn-Teller split of a few kcal/mol between the two components. That is precisely the situation a single-determinant method cannot handle, and it is why this fragment alone is treated multiconfigurationally while everything else in the study, including the magnesium complexes that are its subject, is handled by single-reference perturbation and composite methods. The space is specified by symmetry block rather than by total: five valence electrons distributed over four orbitals of b1 symmetry and two of a2 symmetry. Crucially the same space is used for both Jahn-Teller components, each started from its own open-shell reference configuration, which is what makes the small energy difference between them meaningful -- the two states differ by which orbital carries the single electron, and comparing them across differently constructed spaces would confound the splitting with the reference. The validation is a proper enlargement test with a stated criterion. The space was extended by one further virtual orbital of each symmetry, and the resulting optimized geometry came out close to the original; the authors connect the two observations by noting that the added orbitals carry insignificant occupation numbers, less than 0.003. Reporting the occupation numbers rather than just the geometric agreement is what turns this from an assertion into evidence, since an orbital with occupation below 0.003 cannot be contributing to the wave function regardless of what the geometry does. The geometries the space produces are chemically interpretable in a way that supports the assignment: one component shows a large contribution from a diene-like structure while in the other only the carbon-carbon bond perpendicular to the symmetry axis has double-bond character, and both agree with previous theoretical work to within 3 percent in bond lengths and 1 percent in angles. One limitation of scope worth recording: the multiconfigurational energies enter the reaction thermochemistry only through this fragment, so the computed dissociation energies pair a multiconfigurational description of the radical with a single-reference description of everything else, and the two Jahn-Teller components differ by only 0.0004 hartree in the tabulated total energies.

active_space_protocol: Full valence active space - six electrons in six orbitals - used identically for the state-specific multiconfigurational calculations, for the state-averaged orbitals feeding the configuration-interaction spin-orbit step, and for the coupling calculation inside the functional-based dynamics. Because the program cannot compute spin-orbit coupling from density functional theory, that coupling is obtained from a configuration-interaction calculation in the same space using the high-spin alpha functional orbitals, so the active space is not eliminated even in the nominally functional treatment. No spatial symmetry restrictions are imposed during the simulations.

electronic_structure_description: The 3B1 state, on which every trajectory is initialized and whose lifetime is the quantity being predicted. Its barrier to the crossing point is the one that matters for the rate, and the two methods differ substantially: 1051 reciprocal centimetres by functional against 717 by the multiconfigurational treatment, a difference large enough on its own to change the rate constant appreciably. That it does not is the paper's central observation, because the functional simultaneously overestimates the spin-orbit coupling relative to the multiconfigurational values, and the two errors offset.
Other: The authors give three named reasons for replacing the multiconfigurational treatment with a functional in their dynamics: choosing a space that describes all the geometries accessible during a trajectory is 'a very challenging task'; the multiconfigurational method recovers little dynamic correlation, which 'could result in very inaccurate electronic state energies, and hence in flawed nonadiabatic simulations'; and the functional is a black-box method that 'eliminates the need for constructing the active spaces'. But the elimination is INCOMPLETE, and the reason is a software limitation the authors name: because their program cannot compute spin-orbit coupling with density functional methods, the coupling in the functional-based dynamics is STILL obtained from a configuration-interaction calculation in the SAME six-electron six-orbital space, using the high-spin alpha set of functional orbitals. So the 'active-space-free' method still requires an active space for the very quantity that drives the process being simulated. The headline result is an explicit, quantified error cancellation that the authors identify themselves rather than presenting as agreement. The two methods give excellent agreement on the rate constants, and the explanation is that two effects cancel: the functional gives higher barriers, which would slow the crossing, and stronger spin-orbit coupling, which would speed it up. Both are quantified - the barrier from the triplet to the crossing point is 1051 reciprocal centimetres by functional against 717 by the multiconfigurational method, the barrier from the singlet is 2217 higher, and the singlet-triplet minimum separation is nearly 2000 higher. A reader should not conclude from the agreement that either method has the barrier or the coupling right; the two errors happen to oppose each other for this molecule, and there is no reason to expect the cancellation to survive a change of system. The active space itself is the FULL VALENCE space, six electrons in six orbitals, so it is set by a rule rather than by tuning and is identical between the two treatments and between the multiconfigurational dynamics and the coupling calculation - which is what makes the comparison clean. Geometries and harmonic frequencies from the two methods agree well, so the disagreement is specifically in relative energies and couplings, not structures. The authors also explain a discrepancy with their OWN earlier work: a tighter coupling threshold of 0.1 was used previously against 0.2 here, so the multiconfigurational rates and lifetimes differ slightly between the two papers - a numerical parameter, named, rather than a silent revision. Finally, both dynamics treatments give rate constants about a FACTOR OF TWO larger than the statistical transition-state estimate, which the authors attribute to nonlocal interstate transitions absent from the statistical description - so the dynamical and statistical pictures differ by more than the two electronic-structure methods do.

The lowest two occupied orbitals came out above 1.98 and the highest two unoccupied below 0.02, so those four were dropped, leaving ten electrons in ten orbitals. The crucial detail is that the occupation criterion was checked for all sampled conformations, not just at equilibrium -- a space pruned on occupation numbers at one geometry can easily fail elsewhere on a surface that runs to a conical intersection, and the authors closed that gap explicitly. A second reduction follows for the intersection search alone, down to eight electrons in eight orbitals on the basis of the same preliminary calculation showing that four occupied and four unoccupied pi orbitals suffice where the two states are nearly degenerate. A second appendix defends the basis: polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection at all for this family of molecules, so the intersection geometry is sensitive to the one-electron basis as well as to the space. The decay picture that follows is that the initially populated Spi state relaxes to the lower-lying Sn state and then crosses to T1(3pipi*) through this point.
Other: Two DIFFERENT (8,7) spaces are used for the two crossing points, each built around the orbitals the specific crossing needs, and the substitution is stated explicitly. For the S1(1npi*)/S2(1pipi*) CONICAL INTERSECTION the seven orbitals are one nO, one sigma(C-N), two pi, two pi* and one sigma*(C-N) — the sigma/sigma* pair being included because the intersection involves C-N stretching. For the S1(1npi*)/T1(3pipi*) INTERSYSTEM CROSSING the seven orbitals are instead one nO, three pi, two pi* and one RYDBERG orbital, dropping the sigma/sigma* pair entirely and adding a diffuse function. So the two crossing energies quoted on the same kcal/mol scale relative to S0 — 130 for the conical intersection and 85.5 for the intersystem crossing — come from different orbital selections and are not strictly one surface. The paper is candid about the limit on validating this: "due to the limited computational resources, we are unable to check the Sn/Spi conical intersection point at any higher theoretical level", so no convergence test against a larger space or a correlated method was performed for the intersection that carries the mechanistic argument. Everything else in the study rests on TD-B3LYP rather than CASSCF — the excited-state minima, the vertical excitation energies and the resonance Raman intensity analysis — with CASSCF used only where a single-reference method cannot go, namely at the two crossing points. Note the resulting scale mismatch: the Sn and Spi minima are placed 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0 by TD-B3LYP while the crossings between them are placed at 130 and 85.5 kcal/mol by CASSCF, so the relative ordering of minima and funnels mixes two levels of theory.

notes: Resonance Raman and quantum chemical study of the excited-state structures and decay dynamics of 1,3-dimethyluracil (DMU) and 5-bromo-1,3-dimethyluracil (5BrDMU) in acetonitrile, methanol and water. Computed singlet transitions at 232 nm (f = 0.1495) and 201 nm (f = 0.1273) correlate with the observed A-band at 264 nm (f = 0.2369) and B-band at 206 nm (f = 0.3695). Both molecules have 48 normal modes, and this work provides the first vibrational assignments for either. The Sn and Spi excited-state minima, computed at TD-B3LYP/6-31G(d), lie 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0 and 14.9 and 10.3 kcal/mol below their respective Franck-Condon points; Sn is a relatively pure 1npi* state while Spi is noticeably mixed with Sn.

point_group: Cs, with states classified as A' and A''
geometry_source: Excited state energies computed at B3LYP/6-31G* geometries; a related nitrene geometry was optimized at CCSD(T) in earlier work
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 vertical excitation energies at DFT geometries, with level shifting to remove intruder states; B3LYP and time-dependent B3LYP used alongside
software: MOLCAS 4 for all CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 98 for the DFT work; ACES II for a CCSD(T) optimization
basis_set: ANO-S basis set of Pierloot et al. for the CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G* for the B3LYP geometries; 6-31+G* for the TD-DFT
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals, comprising eight a'' orbitals of pi and pi* type and three a' orbitals: the singly occupied in-plane p orbital of nitrogen and two combinations of the in-plane oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: Three a' orbitals were added to the eight a''-type pi and pi* orbitals specifically because the characteristic triplet nitrene absorption involves excitation from the sp lone pair into the singly occupied in-plane 2p orbital of nitrogen. The total space size is held at (12,11), matching the singlet, so the symmetry composition changes while the size does not. Level shifting was applied in the CASPT2 step as for the singlet, with 0.25 au used for the tabulated energies.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 3A'', with 83 percent of the ground configuration. Table 4 gives vertical excitation energies from CASSCF(12,11)/CASPT2 at the B3LYP/6-31G* geometry: 1 3A' at 0.45 and 1.60 eV, weight 0.76, 775 nm, f 1.3e-4, 80 percent 26a' to 5a''; 2 3A'' at 3.21 and 2.93 eV, weight 0.74, 424 nm, f 1.4e-2, 34 percent 4a'' to 5a'' with 21 percent 4a'' to 6a''; 3 3A'' at 3.76 and 3.04 eV, weight 0.74, 407 nm, f 5.6e-3, 72 percent 23a' to 27a'; 4 3A'' at 3.81 and 3.21 eV, weight 0.74, 386 nm, f 4.6e-3, 44 percent 3a'' to 5a''; 5 3A'' at 4.34 and 3.75 eV, weight 0.74, 330 nm, f 2.6e-2, 36 percent 3a'' to 7a''; 6 3A'' at 4.61 and 4.32 eV, weight 0.74, 287 nm, f 6.4e-3, 37 percent 3a'' to 6a''; 7 3A'' at 4.98 and 4.42 eV, weight 0.74, 280 nm, f 2.2e-2; 2 3A' at 3.38 and 4.48 eV, weight 0.76, 277 nm, f 1.4e-4, 35 percent 27a' to 6a''; and 3 3A' at 4.03 and 5.15 eV, weight 0.76, 241 nm, f 1.2e-5. The triplet is predicted to have several intense absorption bands in the visible and near ultraviolet, a spectrum showing no relation to the experimental one, which the authors take as confirming the absence of the triplet nitrene among the products of photolysis.
Other: The two spin states are treated in spaces of identical size, (12,11), but of deliberately different symmetry composition, and the paper explains why. For the singlet the space contains nine a'' and two a' orbitals -- essentially the pi system. For the triplet the balance shifts to eight a'' and three a', and the reason is stated explicitly: the triplet's characteristic absorption involves excitation of an electron from the sp lone pair orbital into the singly occupied in-plane 2p orbital of nitrogen, a transition analogous to those seen from the triplet ground states of NH at 336 nm, methylnitrene at 315 nm, perfluoromethylnitrene at 354 nm and 1-norbornylnitrene at 298 nm. To describe it, three a' orbitals were added -- the singly occupied in-plane p orbital of nitrogen and two combinations of the in-plane oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs -- to the eight a''-type pi and pi* orbitals. So one orbital was traded out of the pi block to admit the in-plane orbital the transition actually uses. This is a clean example of the space being chosen by which transitions must be representable rather than by a uniform recipe, and of holding the total size fixed so that the two states' reference weights remain comparable: they sit at 0.74 to 0.77 across both tables. The consequence for the paper's conclusion is direct. The computed triplet spectrum shows several intense bands in the visible and near ultraviolet that bear no relation to the experimental spectrum, and that mismatch is what the authors take as confirming the absence of the triplet nitrene among the photolysis products. A negative identification of this kind is only as good as the space's ability to produce those bands in the first place, which is precisely why the in-plane orbitals had to be admitted. A second and independent caveat concerns intruder states rather than orbital selection. To obtain a satisfactory description of all excited states at the CASPT2 level it was necessary to resort to level shifting, and the authors state that they carefully assured no artifacts were introduced, reporting in supplementary tables the results of calculations with level shifts ranging from 0 to 0.3 au; the tabulated energies use 0.25 au. That is the right way to use a level shift -- scanned and reported rather than fixed by default -- but it means the excitation energies carry a chosen parameter, and a few entries show how much CASSCF and CASPT2 can disagree in a single reference: for the triplet the 2 3A' state moves from 3.38 eV at CASSCF up to 4.48 eV at CASPT2, and the 3 3A' state from 4.03 to 5.15 eV, both shifting upward while every other state shifts downward. Finally, note that the multiconfigurational treatment was applied only at geometries obtained elsewhere, at the B3LYP/6-31G* level, and that the electronic spectra of the substituted acetyl derivative were predicted with time-dependent DFT rather than with this space at all.

Other: The subject is a hierarchy of exact-two-component schemes - X2C-1e, X2CAMF built on Dirac-Coulomb, Dirac-Coulomb-Gaunt and Dirac-Coulomb-Breit, X2CMP(DCB), and the new X2Ccorr which adds 'the picture-change correction for the fluctuation potential' - so the size of the neglected term can be read off rather than assumed small. A point-charge-embedded free ion strips the chemistry away to isolate the relativistic physics: 'the Nd(3+) free ion is embedded in point charges with cubic symmetry, using 8 point charges of -1.0 e placed 2.333 angstrom from the Nd(3+) center', and on that model the basis-set effects and relativistic two-electron contributions are studied in isolation. The environment is then grown rather than assumed: from the bare point-charge model to explicit first coordination shells at the two coordination numbers the literature considers likely, eight and nine, then second shells giving systems of 23 and 26 water molecules, with the second shell reported to affect the structures of the first. A two-component CASSCF on twenty-six explicit waters is possible only because of the Cholesky-decomposition and super-configuration-interaction machinery the paper introduces. ligand_set: a triaryl corrole bearing two 4-methylcarboxyphenyl groups at the 5 and 15 positions and a 2-methylcarboxyphenyl group at the 10 position
point_group: saddled, the distortion lowering the symmetry enough to let the singly occupied Cu 3d(x2-y2) orbital mix with the corrole pi orbitals
geometry_source: geometries optimised by DFT at PBE0 with def2-SVP on all atoms and def2-TZVP on copper, for the neutral and charged forms; single-point DFT with PBE0, TPSS, TPSSh and TPSS0 gives the relative energies of the open-shell singlet, triplet and closed-shell singlet states on the closed-shell-singlet optimised structure; crystal structures determined for the two neutral copper corroles
method: single-point CASSCF on the DFT geometries with NEVPT2 energy corrections, used to resolve the oxidation-state description of the metal and the ligand and to simulate the UV/Vis/NIR spectra; broken-symmetry DFT across four functionals for comparison; EPR spectroscopy for the reduced and oxidised species
basis_set: def2-SVP on all atoms with def2-TZVP on copper
active_space_orbital_description: the copper 3d manifold together with the four Gouterman orbitals of the corrole (labelled h-1, h, l and l+1) and three empty meso-aryl centred orbitals
active_space_protocol: CAS(12,9) assembled by the fragment merging procedure, then NEVPT2. Getting the copper 3d_xy orbital into the active space proved hard enough that the authors built the space by hand from fragments: the copper corrole was split into a Cu(III) fragment at charge +3 and a corrole(3-) fragment at the same coordinates, separate CASSCF calculations were run on each - (8e,5o) for the metal and (4e,4o) for the ligand - the resulting wavefunction files were merged with orca_mergefrag, and a (12e,9o) CASSCF with maxiter set to 1 was run on the merged file to inspect the orbitals without optimisation before manually reordering the copper 3d orbitals with the rotate keyword and reconverging. That procedure is the methodological content of the paper as much as the chemistry is: a space that will not form by automatic selection is assembled from pieces whose composition is known. The payoff is a quantitative decomposition of the ground state into metal and ligand oxidation states, which is exactly what the closed-shell versus open-shell controversy in copper corroles needs, and the authors are careful to say the question is not settled in general because substituent electronics and ring distortion both shift the balance.
nroots_per_mult: the ground states of each available multiplicity, singlet and triplet
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a mixture dominated by the open-shell [Cu(II)cor(2-) radical] description at 88 percent, with the closed-shell [Cu(III)cor(3-)] configuration contributing 7 percent. That supports the standard picture of copper corroles as intrinsically non-innocent, with the open-shell configuration carrying the majority weight, while showing that the closed-shell description is not negligible. The saddling distortion is what permits the mixing in the first place, by lowering the symmetry so that the singly occupied Cu 3d(x2-y2) can interact with the corrole pi system - in particular with the orbital that is the HOMO of the free-base corrole.

geometry_source: QUESTDB geometries; theoretical best estimates from QUESTDB as references
method: SA-CASSCF vs XS-CASSCF (globally optimized [0.0,0.5] and molecule-specific [mu,nu]) benchmarked against QUESTDB theoretical best estimates; TDDFT/CAM-B3LYP and MS-CASPT2 for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: per-molecule valence pi/pi* (and lone-pair) active spaces, the same set used in the group's Qat-diagnostic paper
active_space_protocol: the 11-molecule set reuses the per-molecule active spaces of the group's earlier ionic-diagnostic study (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): ethene (2,2), butadiene (4,4), hexatriene (6,6), octatetraene (8,8), naphthalene (10,10) etc. XS-CASSCF is the corrective follow-up to this group's Qat ionic-character diagnostic (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): SA-CASSCF overestimates singlet ionic pi-pi* states by 1-2 eV because the transition-density self-repulsion (two-electron exchange integrals) is not screened by sigma-correlation. XS-CASSCF scales those exchange terms down with two parameters [mu, nu] to mimic sigma-correlation at NO extra cost - mu scales the diagonal exchange (controls the ionic S1), nu the off-diagonal coupling (controls multiconfigurational covalent states). Practical guidance the paper establishes: mu = 0.0 (simply dropping the exchange integral g_pq,qp) is usually optimal and makes the S1 energy independent of the exchange integral, halving the CASSCF singlet-triplet gap to one exchange integral rather than two; nu = 0.0 is best when only the HOMO-LUMO transition matters, but nu = 0.5-0.7 is safer when higher multiconfigurational covalent states are of interest. The recommended default is [0.0, 0.5].

active_space_protocol: The paper's CASVB analysis transforms the canonical single-space CAS(6,6) exactly: all electron distributions and all Rumer spin couplings are retained, so CASVB and canonical CASSCF have identical energy/density. A previously reported double active space CAS(6,12), adding a second/diffuse pi shell, and MRMP on both spaces diagnose polarization/dynamic-correlation errors in ionic states. Nonorthogonal Rumer structures are assigned occupation n_I=C_I* sum_J S_IJ C_J, not naively squared coefficients.
electronic_structure_description: The 1A1g ground state is a covalent minus state dominated individually by Kekule structures, with Dewar and orthopolar/other ionic mixing; CASVB contains 175 structures in 22 D6h bonding classes, including five covalent structures. Covalent excitations rearrange spin coupling: 1B2u is the opposite-sign Kekule combination and 1E2g is predominantly Dewar. Ionic 1B1u and 1E1u states contain polar structures but no covalent structures and require sigma-pi polarization/diffuse active flexibility. CAS(6,6) vertical energies for 1B2u/1B1u/1E1u/1E2g are 4.82/7.91/9.29/8.01 eV; MRMP(6,6) gives 4.71/5.83/6.33/7.73 eV.
Other: CAS(6,12) energies are 4.89/7.57/8.78/8.04 eV and MRMP(6,12) gives 4.67/6.14/6.84/7.71 eV, versus experimental 4.90/6.20/6.94/7.80 eV. Thus enlarging the space barely changes covalent states but is essential for ionic 1B1u/1E1u, while MRMP supplies the missing dynamic sigma-pi response. The CAS(6,6) ground energy is -230.82572 Eh and MRMP(6,6) -231.63073 Eh. Ground-state total occupations for the Kekule and Dewar covalent classes are 0.1565 and 0.0771; the large 0.2528 orthopolar class reflects compensation required by orthogonal, non-reoptimized LMOs. Electronic terms, resonance structures, and polarities remain components of one molecule record rather than separate entries.

electronic_structure_description: TS1 is a five-member-ring C1 doublet transition structure for acidic-H abstraction by proton-coupled electron transfer. The OH lone pair points at the acidic proton while the OH unpaired electron interacts with the carbonyl oxygen. CASSCF wavefunction analysis supports electron transfer from the carbonyl-oxygen lone pair to OH coupled to proton transfer from HCOOH to OH. QCISD spin populations are O1=0.603 and carbonyl O3=0.386; both C-O distances are about 1.258 A at the QCISD geometry, consistent with pi redistribution. TS1 is well characterized by B3LYP, MP2, CASSCF, and QCISD. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical acidic-H abstraction TS2 (conventional H abstraction): TS2 is a planar six-member-ring Cs doublet transition structure for conventional acidic-hydrogen radical abstraction: concerted O5-H6 breaking and H6-O1 formation. CASSCF wavefunction analysis and QCISD spin populations (O1=0.532, O5=0.428) support sharing of the unpaired electron between donor and acceptor oxygens. At the QCISD geometry the transferred H is closer to OH, r(O1-H6)=1.117 A versus r(O5-H6)=1.219 A, and a secondary H2...O3 hydrogen bond is 2.071 A. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical double-proton-transfer TS3: TS3 is a symmetric six-member-ring C2v doublet transition structure for simultaneous double proton transfer: acidic H transfers from formic acid to OH while the OH hydrogen transfers to the carbonyl oxygen, producing no net chemical reaction. Its 2B1 symmetry keeps the unpaired electron in an out-of-plane orbital mainly localized on the hydroxyl-radical oxygen, so the unpaired electron does not participate in the proton transfers. Both C-O distances are equal (about 1.264 A at the non-CASSCF comparison geometry), reflecting pi redistribution.

No spin-orbit coupling, minimum-energy crossing seam, or ISC rate is computed, so the claim that intersystem crossing is impossible follows only from energy differences. active_space_protocol: Present CASVB wave functions are exact transforms of the single active space CAS(4,4). The quantitative excitation benchmarks use a double active space CAS(4,8), adding a second pi set, followed by MRMP; the cis geometry is also optimized with CAS(4,8). Trans/cis isomers and their state-specific roots are consolidated because the paper's central result is their directly paired electronic comparison.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is predominantly the Kekule covalent coupling with smaller Dewar and ionic contributions. The covalent 2 1Ag/2 1A1 state reverses this balance and is predominantly Dewar-like, representing coupled local triplet excitations and bond-order inversion. The bright 1 1Bu/1 1B2 state is purely ionic in CASVB, with no covalent structures. MRMP(4,8) vertical energies are 6.31 eV (trans 2 1Ag), 6.21 eV (trans 1 1Bu), 6.30 eV (cis 2 1A1), and 5.59 eV (cis 1 1B2); corresponding CASSCF(4,8) values are 6.67, 7.73, 6.56, and 6.88 eV.
Other: MRMP predicts trans-butadiene 2.76 kcal mol^-1 below cis. Covalent excitation is essentially isomer-insensitive (6.31 versus 6.30 eV), but folding the chain stabilizes the ionic state by 0.62 eV (6.21 versus 5.59 eV) because oppositely charged termini approach; the leading cis ionic VB combination has occupation 0.2146. Oscillator strengths are 0/0.803 for trans 2Ag/1Bu and 0.004/0.337 for cis 2A1/1B2. Experimental bright-state values are about 5.92-6.25 eV trans and 5.5 eV cis. Ground CASVB occupations quoted in the discussion include Kekule 0.3960 and two major ionic pairs 0.1970/0.1812. These resonance terms are wave-function components, not distinct compounds.

electronic_structure_description: Compact CASSCF-a is unbalanced: four active orbitals are doubly occupied, one singly occupied, and only one antibonding orbital is empty, yielding neutral Re=1.789 angstrom and omega=603 cm^-1. Adding five Br 4d correlators gives CASSCF-b Re=1.740 and 709 cm^-1, close to experiment, because 4d occupations reach about 0.016 and recover d-p/pi-p backbonding. CASMP2/ECT+(2df) gives neutral 1.726 angstrom/720 cm^-1 and BrO- 1.828/598; CASPT2 with Br 3d correlation gives 1.722/715. software: HONDO-95 for CASSCF/CASMP2; Gaussian 94 for MP2/QCI/G2; AIMPAC for topology
basis_set: Stevens ECT(2d) for the multireference geometry comparison; QCISD(T)/ECT+(2df) for the best full property set; systematic all-electron/ECP SV/TZ, polarization, and diffuse-function tests elsewhere in the paper.
relativistic_treatment: ECP/all-electron basis comparisons; explicit relativistic and spin-orbit effects omitted.
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF-a contains the selected valence sigma/pi, lone-pair, and antibonding orbitals needed for the O-Br-O doublet/singlet-anion wave functions. The paper does not enumerate a triatomic electron/orbital count, so no scalar CAS is inferred from the BrO definition.
active_space_protocol: State-specific CASSCF-a references were used for neutral 2B1 OBrO and anion 1A1 OBrO-, followed by Davidson CASMP2. electronic_structure_description: Neutral OBrO has substantial configuration mixing (leading CASSCF coefficient 0.936, close to ozone's 0.903), so HF/MP2 structures and frequencies vary strongly. CASSCF-a/ECT(2d) gives 1.682 angstrom/118.9 degrees and 769/703/282 cm^-1; CASMP2 gives 1.674/117.1. Best QCISD(T)/ECT+(2df) gives 1.659/115.2 and asymmetric/symmetric/bend frequencies 850/786/308 cm^-1, within about 10 cm^-1 of gas/matrix data. The anion is less multiconfigurational; CASMP2 gives 1.756/115.9, while QCISD(T)/ECT+(2df) gives 1.739/112.9 and 698/680/266 cm^-1.
Other: Adding an electron populates an antibonding pi orbital, lengthening both Br-O bonds and lowering critical-point density/ellipticity. MP2/6-311+G(3df) topology gives neutral Br-O rho=0.241, Laplacian=+0.085, H=-0.235, ellipticity=0.188; anion rho=0.201, Laplacian=+0.046, H=-0.162, ellipticity=0.043. Calculated anion-to-neutral energy differences are 47.4 kcal mol^-1 CASMP2, 52.4 QCISD(T), and about 60.1-60.3 G2//QCI. Theory predicts the anion asymmetric stretch above the symmetric stretch, opposite an aqueous assignment.

geometry_source: Ground S0, first singlet S1, and lowest triplet T1 geometries of all three positional isomers were optimized without symmetry constraints at CASSCF(8,7)/6-311G**. method: state-specific CASSCF geometry optimization for S0, S1, and T1; CIS transition electronic dipole moments; crossed-molecular-beam photofragment translational spectroscopy with forward convolution
software: Gaussian 98 revision A.9 for CASSCF and CIS; CMLAB2/KELVIN for beam-spectrum analysis
basis_set: 6-311G** for CASSCF geometries; 6-311G* for CIS geometries and S0-to-S1 transition electronic dipole moments
active_space_orbital_description: All six aromatic ring pi orbitals containing six pi electrons plus one Cl 3p lone-pair orbital containing two electrons; the space therefore permits both ring pi-to-pi* and Cl n-to-pi* configurations.
active_space_protocol: The identical state-specific CAS(8,7) is used to optimize S0, the first singlet excited state S1, and T1 for each meta/ortho/para isomer without symmetry restrictions. The paper reports no state averaging, root weights, or post-CASSCF dynamic-correlation correction. CIS/6-311G* is a separate single-reference calculation for transition-dipole direction, not the source of the recorded CAS.
nroots_per_mult: per isomer: S0, first singlet S1, and lowest triplet T1
electronic_structure_description: For all isomers, S0-to-S1 shortens C-Cl and C-CH3 while lengthening the aromatic C-C framework; orbital analysis assigns the transition predominantly as pi-to-pi*. Meta and ortho T1 retain bound C-Cl bonds (figure values: meta 1.779 angstrom versus S0 1.750; ortho 1.754 versus S0 1.782). Para T1 is qualitatively dissociative: C1-Cl=3.925 angstrom, an alternative C2-Cl contact=3.636 angstrom, and the C1-Cl direction leaves the ring plane by 54.4 degrees, suggesting coupled Cl migration/bond cleavage.
Other: CIS S0-to-S1 transition-dipole/C-Cl angles evaluated at S0/S1/T1 geometries are meta 23.0/22.8/17.8 degrees, ortho 6.1/26.6/25.7, and para 54.3/54.2/63.0, matching positive experimental anisotropy for meta/ortho and negative para anisotropy. At 266 nm, meta has beta=+0.5+/-0.2 and mean translation 3.15 kcal mol^-1 (28% of available energy); para beta=-0.6+/-0.2 and 3.28 (29%). Ortho requires two channels: about 60% slow o-tolyl+Cl with beta=+0.7+/-0.2, 2.06 kcal mol^-1 (18%), and 40% fast proposed benzyl+Cl with beta=+0.1+/-0.1, 5.09 (46%). The source proposes meta predissociation through T1 or internal conversion, direct dissociation on repulsive para T1, and for the ortho fast channel pre-dissociation H transfer to 1-methylene-2-chloro-3,5-cyclohexadiene (MCC) followed by Cl loss. Ortho S0 has a reported intramolecular Cl...H contact of 2.651 angstrom, suggested to facilitate transfer.

method: full-pi CASSCF geometry and Mulliken spin-population calculations, benchmarked against ROHF, UHF, UBLYP, UB3LYP, UQCISD, RCCSD, RCCSD(T), and UCCSD(T) where computationally feasible
software: MOLCAS 4.0 for full-pi CASSCF; Gaussian 98 for ROHF/UHF/DFT/UQCISD; ACES II for coupled-cluster calculations

active_space_protocol: Full-pi CAS(n,n): CAS(3,3) for allyl C3H5, CAS(5,5) for pentadienyl C5H7, CAS(7,7) for heptatrienyl C7H9, CAS(9,9) for nonatetraenyl C9H11, CAS(11,11) for C11H13, and CAS(13,13) for C13H15. electronic_structure_description: The full-pi CASSCF wavefunctions describe alternating positive and negative carbon 2p_pi spin polarization localized most strongly near the radical center, together with increasing C-C bond-length alternation toward the chain ends. Relative CASSCF spin populations (largest positive site normalized to 1) are C3: terminal 1.000, central -0.343; C5: C1 0.75, C2 -0.31, C3 1.00; C7: C1 0.64, C2 -0.30, C3 1.00, C4 -0.42; C9: C1 0.47, C2 -0.24, C3 0.81, C4 -0.39, C5 1.00. The CASSCF distributions are qualitatively close to RCCSD(T) benchmarks, while both DFT functionals delocalize spin too evenly and UHF is severely spin contaminated.
Other: CASSCF/6-31G* optimized unique C-C distances (angstrom) are C3 1.390; C5 1.367/1.421; C7 1.358/1.436/1.394; C9 1.353/1.445/1.379/1.412. For allyl, CASSCF also gives central C-H 1.078 angstrom, averaged terminal C-H 1.074 angstrom, and the tabulated C-C-C angle 124.7 degrees. The authors use experimental EPR hyperfine ratios through the McConnell relationship to benchmark carbon spin-density ratios: full-pi CASSCF is good qualitatively, RCCSD(T)/UCCSD(T) are closest for C3-C7, and absolute ab initio proton hyperfine constants can still be poor. CASSCF C11 and C13 results provide the largest feasible multireference benchmarks; the paper's C41H43 neutral-soliton calculations use only ROHF/UHF/BLYP/B3LYP and are therefore context, not a CAS entry. Those large-chain DFT calculations overestimate the experimental 18-carbon soliton half-width, whereas ROHF makes it too short. No spin-orbit Hamiltonian or spin-spin term is included.

geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G* and ROHF/6-31G* optimize the radical cation to twisted D2 structures with inter-ring torsions of 18.0 and 13.5 degrees; constrained D2h structures have zero torsion. Table 1 gives all symmetry-unique heavy-atom bonds, including B3LYP/ROHF D2 values C1-C2=1.428/1.426, C2-C3=1.374/1.357, C3-C4=1.423/1.423, inter-ring C4-C4-prime=1.448/1.428, C1-N1=1.358/1.334, and N1-C7=1.465/1.460 angstrom. method: B3LYP and ROHF geometry/frequency calculations; CIS screening/assignment of visible doublet excited states; state-specific CASSCF excited-state gradients projected onto ROHF ground-state normal modes to calculate Franck-Condon resonance-Raman intensities; isotope-resolved time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy
software: Gaussian 98 for B3LYP, ROHF, CIS, and CASSCF calculations; REDONG for conversion of Cartesian force constants to local symmetry-coordinate force constants and potential-energy distributions
basis_set: 6-31G* with polarization functions on every C and N atom for all reported electronic-structure calculations
active_space_orbital_description: For the lower visible transition, CAS(3,4) contains 15b3, 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 orbitals in D2, or 4b1u, 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. For the higher transition, CAS(1,3) contains 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 in D2, or 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. These are the smallest converged spaces after progressive expansion through all orbitals of the transition symmetry; the numeric fields record the larger CAS(3,4).
active_space_protocol: CIS first requested four doublet excited states in each D2 model to identify the two lowest transitions with appreciable oscillator strength and their dominant orbitals. Separate state-specific CASSCF gradient calculations were then performed for experimental transition 1 and transition 2 at both D2 and D2h radical-cation equilibrium geometries. Active spaces were progressively enlarged until predicted Raman spectra were stable; the reported CAS(3,4) and CAS(1,3) are the smallest stable choices. The selected configurations have weights close to one.
nroots_per_mult: CIS requested four doublet excited states for convergence; two bright doublet B3 (D2) or B1u (D2h) states were selected and treated in separate state-specific CASSCF calculations.
electronic_structure_description: The open-shell radical cation has 12 pi and two n orbitals, with the two highest-energy orbitals of n type. Both strong visible states are nearly pure one-electron pi-pi* doublet transitions. In D2h, state 1 is chiefly 4b1u(beta)-to-4b2g(beta) and state 2 chiefly 4b2g(alpha)-to-5b1u(alpha); their CIS coefficients are 0.933 and 0.844. The active orbitals and nodal patterns are shown explicitly in Figure 3.
Other: CASSCF energies for the D2 model are 1.79 eV (694 nm) for state 1 and 2.97 eV (418 nm) for state 2; D2h values are 1.83 eV (678 nm) and 3.63 eV (342 nm). CIS predicts 1.97/3.53 eV in D2 and 2.03/3.49 eV in D2h, with oscillator strengths about 0.62/0.32-0.34. Experimental radical-cation bands peak near 900 and 470 nm. Ionization shifts the N-ring and inter-ring stretching fundamentals by +43 and +54 cm^-1. Of the out-of-plane modes activated only by D2 symmetry, ring mode 16a near 415 cm^-1 is predicted to be Raman-intense but is absent at both probe wavelengths, supporting D2h planarity in solution. The four H/D isotopomers are consolidated as isotopic probes, not separate compounds.

electronic_structure_description: Balanced CASSCF/4220/TZ+2d1p gives H2S 1.333 angstrom/92.2 degrees versus experiment 1.328/92.2, though orbital analysis exposes incomplete 1a1 correlation. H2S+ X2B1 is 1.373/94.1 (experiment 1.358/92.5) and A2A1 is 1.370/126.3 (1.369/127). H2S2+ has a strongly bent 1A1 ground state at 1.428/96.6; its 3B1 state is 1.447/131.8 and only about 2.5 kcal mol^-1 higher after CI+ZPVE. H3S+ is pyramidal, while H3S2+ is CASSCF 1.410/118.2.
Other: Neutral->cation CI IPs are H2S MRDCI2 10.0 eV versus 10.56 and SH 9.7 versus 10.46; an enlarged SDCI+modified-Davidson treatment improves H2S to 10.22 versus 10.48. ZPVE-corrected cation->dication values are H3S+ 19.6 versus 21.4, H2S+ 20.8 versus 21.0 and SH+ 21.9 versus 21.2; the most extensive H2S+ calculation gives 21.12 eV. Unlike N/O, sulfur monocation theory shows no systematic offset from charge stripping. ZPVE-corrected deprotonation barriers are substantial: H3S2+ 40.5, H2S2+ 39.3 and SH2+ 36.3 kcal mol^-1, explaining their observed metastability. The SH2+ potential illustrates an attractive neutral-H channel followed by electron transfer onto the repulsive proton-loss asymptote.

Fragment/product spaces are CO and ketene CAS(8,6), acetylene/propyne/allene CAS(4,4), HCO CAS(7,5), propargyl CAS(5,5), CH3 SCF(1,1), and CH4 closed-shell SCF. electronic_structure_description: Furan is closed-shell 1A1. Direct C-O opening gives triplet 3A'' L-furan (structure 4) 322 kJ mol^-1 above furan at CASPT2/0 K and singlet biradical structures near 370-371 kJ mol^-1; the lowest singlet is sigma1pi1 rather than the higher closed-shell carbene-like sigma2 state. The viable minor channel proceeds through 1,2-H-transfer TS20 (280), cyclic singlet carbene 21 (264), ring-opened singlet biradical 23 (309), and C-C fission TS24 (352) to ketene+acetylene (225 kJ mol^-1). The dominant channel proceeds through alternative H-transfer TS25 (288), cyclic carbene 26 (279), formyl-allene intermediates 28/30 (130/118), and concerted TS31 (279) to CO+propyne (129). All values are CASPT2/cc-pVTZ plus CASSCF ZPVE relative to furan at 0 K.
Other: The direct singlet/triplet ring-opening routes have only about 0.1/7.6 s^-1 upper-bound rates at 1400 K and are excluded from the kinetic model. The ketene+acetylene cyclic-carbene route is 234 s^-1 and the formyl-allene route 629 s^-1 at 1400 K; their multistep Arrhenius fits are approximately 1.5x10^15 exp(-344 kJ mol^-1/RT) and 5.94x10^13 exp(-294.1 kJ mol^-1/RT) s^-1. Formyl allene decomposes overwhelmingly to CO+propyne rather than HCO+propargyl. A separate formyl-propyne route has TS34 at 356 kJ mol^-1 and only 2.8 s^-1. Methyl abstraction has 73/76 kJ mol^-1 0-K barriers to 2-/3-furyl, a combined 9.7x10^13 exp(-96.9 kJ mol^-1/RT) rate, and explains methane despite 506/514 kJ mol^-1 furan C-H bond enthalpies. The fitted model uses 82 reactions and reproduces shock-tube furan/major-product profiles; it slightly changes the dominant initiation activation energy from 294.1 to 292.9 kJ mol^-1, lowers the minor-channel A factor from 1.5x10^15 to 9.0x10^14 s^-1, and lowers the abstraction activation energy by 9 kJ mol^-1. CASPT2 underbinds triply bonded products, overestimating CO+hydrocarbon and ketene+acetylene reaction enthalpies by about 25-30 kJ mol^-1 versus experiment, so G2(MP2) is better for those closed-shell thermochemical balances. Conversely, CASPT2 is preferred at biradical/bond-fission structures where Q1 is large and single-reference methods collapse or disagree.

electronic_structure_description: Against experimental transition energies of 19 531, 23 474, 25 707, 28 090 and 33 222 cm-1 from the 6A1g ground term, bare CASSCF with the minimal CAS(5,5) gives 24 968, 28 969, 30 527, 36 137 and 40 044 cm-1; NEVPT2 reduces these to 20 388, 25 248, 27 584, 30 603 and 36 512, and SORCI to 18 064, 23 006, 26 528, 28 995 and 34 389. NEVPT2 on the larger CAS(9,12) gives 19 375, 23 891, 26 638, 29 992 and 36 014 cm-1 - close to the CAS(5,5) NEVPT2 values. The semi-empirical exchange charge model gives 19 718, 23 692, 25 584, 28 748 and 32 626. AILFT parameters: Dq = 814 cm-1 at CASSCF and 796 at NEVPT2 against an experimental 750; Racah B = 1088 and 923 against 820, C = 3933 and 3655 against 3150, with free-ion B0 = 1138 and 978 against 960 and C0 = 4092 and 3696 against 3325, the reduction being the nephelauxetic effect of covalence. The spin-orbit constant, obtainable only from CASSCF, is 314 cm-1 in the crystal and 322 for the free ion against experimental 320 and 335. The g factor is 1.99980 at CASSCF, 1.99972 at NEVPT2, 1.99961 at SORCI, 2.00162 by sum over states and 2.0001 by perturbation theory, against a measured 2.0009.
Other: Enlarging the active space from five orbitals to twelve, in exactly the way the standard prescription advises - adding the ligand eg orbitals and the second d shell - moves the NEVPT2 transition energies hardly at all, and the authors give the reason: the oxide ligands are barely covalent, and ligand orbitals matter most for covalent ligands. The minimal space is not redundant even so, because the spin-orbit coupling constant can be obtained only from CASSCF and not from NEVPT2.

electronic_structure_description: At the DMA-S0 geometry, vertical S1/S2 energies are 3.71/6.24 eV at CASSCF, 3.45/5.73 eV at MS-CASPT2, and 3.50/5.80 eV at MRCI. At the S2/S1 conical-intersection geometry, the S1/S2 energies are 4.02/4.02 eV at CASSCF, 3.60/3.73 eV at MS-CASPT2, and 3.65/3.77 eV at MRCI; at the S1/S0 intersection they are 2.52/2.52, 2.29/2.49, and 2.36/2.42 eV, respectively. The reported MS-CASPT2 stationary-point energies are DMA-S0 0.00, DMA-S1 2.34, S2/S1 intersection 3.67, S1/S0 intersection 2.39, and diazirine 1.73 eV; on the separately referenced N2-loss surface, carbene-I boat is 0.00, chair -0.42, and ketene I -2.06 eV. Among 196 S2-launched trajectories, 135 returned to DMA, 6 formed diazirine, 3 formed ketene concertedly, and 52 formed ketene stepwise through carbene I (35 formed carbene in S1 and 17 in S0). Corresponding branch ratios are 68.9%, 3.1%, 1.5%, 17.9%, and 8.7%. Fitted S2 population-decay components are 17 +/- 2 and 67 +/- 2 fs; S1 components are 62 +/- 6 and 182 +/- 14 fs. Mean pathway times are 200 +/- 50 fs for return to DMA, 120 +/- 70 fs for diazirine, 180 +/- 80 fs for concerted ketene, 500 +/- 120 fs for the S1-carbene stepwise route, and 500 +/- 130 fs for the S0-carbene route.
Other: The active space was chosen mechanistically rather than by a bare size rule: it contains both ring pi channels, the diazo pi bond, and the breaking C-N sigma pair, allowing one SA-CASSCF reference to follow S2-to-S1 relaxation, the extended S1/S0 conical-intersection seam, N2 loss, and product branching. The authors benchmarked the production CAS(12,11) topology against an earlier CAS(10,9) study and checked every key geometry with both MS-CASPT2 and Davidson-corrected MRCI. Those correlated energies generally lower the corresponding CASSCF excitation energies by about 0.25 eV while preserving the relevant gaps, which the authors use to justify CASSCF dynamics; correlated-level trajectories were not run, so that dynamical robustness is inferred rather than directly sampled. CAS(10,8) is used only for the detached-N2 carbene/ketene stationary structures and is not presented as an active-space sensitivity test. The global-switching algorithm uses an improved Landau-Zener probability and avoids explicit nonadiabatic-coupling vectors. The central physical result is that the extended S1/S0 seam, especially whether C2-N9 is longer or shorter than about 1.7 A at hopping, separates excited-state versus ground-state carbene formation and makes the stepwise ketene channel dominant over the synchronous concerted channel.

Structures 2-7 then used electron-count-adjusted CAS(7,10), CAS(6,10), CAS(5,10), CAS(4,6), CAS(6,10), and CAS(6,10), respectively. A CAS(7,7) test for structure 2 removed three nearly empty orbitals and retained the sextet ground-state ordering. MRMP2(7,10) used the corresponding CASSCF wavefunctions and optimized geometries for structure 2.

Other: The orbital analysis identifies ligand participation throughout the PCET cycle. Hydrogen removal in structure 2 promotes one ring-pi orbital to single occupation while a Mn-d orbital drops into the doubly occupied core. Both ring-pi orbitals are singly occupied in structure 3. Structures 4 and 5 exhibit Mn(IV)-O radical, rather than Mn(V)=O, character through singly occupied oxyl-p contributions; structure 5 contains two such moieties. Structure 7 retains the singly occupied O-O pi* orbital during water-assisted Mn-O cleavage. The changing ring-pi occupations correlate with out-of-plane ligand bending and the butterfly-like structure 6. CASSCF total energies of different intermediates are explicitly not compared because their optimized active orbitals differ; the reaction-energy profile shown in the paper is ROHF/ZAPT2 context.

The (522)-2s space correlates the 2s electrons.
active_space_protocol: The principal valence calculations used 7 active/correlated electrons. Equal-weight SA-CASSCF over X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+ was compared with separate state optimizations. Tested spaces were 7e-(322), -(422), -(522), -(333), -(433), and -(344), plus an X-only 7e-(222) test. The 11e-(522)-2s variant included 2s correlation. MRCI reference occupations were selected by maximum spin-coupling coefficient thresholds 0.05, 0.025, and 0.01; final reference lists merged those obtained across r = 1.6-2.4 a0. The avoided crossing at larger r was explicitly outside scope.
nroots_per_mult: two target doublet states: X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+
electronic_structure_description: X 2Pi is the ground valence state and A 2Sigma+ is predominantly Rydberg in the studied region. Increasing diffuse character in X 2Pi at short bond length drives the monotonic increase of the A-X transition moment as r decreases.
Other: The transition-moment function is strongly orbital-basis dependent. Enlarging only sigma space from (322) to (422)/(522) changes little; adding an unbalanced oxygen-centered diffuse pi pair in (333) produces a very small Franck-Condon-region moment, whereas balanced (344), with an added nitrogen diffuse pi pair, restores the magnitude and captures the short-r increase. MRCI removes much but not all CASSCF-space dependence because the selected reference lists are nearly identical and orbital bias remains. The authors identify (344) MRCI(7) as best; its spectroscopic constants are re/omega_e = 2.175 a0/1904 cm-1 for X and 2.009 a0/2421 cm-1 with Te = 42257 cm-1 for A. MRCI(11) closely tracks MRCI(7) with (344), showing 2s correlation is small after accurate valence correlation. At 0.01 threshold, (322) MRCI(11) reached 734395 X-state and 1208479 A-state CSFs, yet transition moments were stable across 0.05-0.01. The computed TMF is nearly linear over the strong-band region and gives A-state v'=0-2 lifetimes of 189.3, 186.1, and 183.1 ns; X-state (344) MRCI(7) gives S(1-0) = 123.9 and S(2-0) = 2.14 cm-2 atm-1, both close to experiment.

method: Full-valence CASSCF correlation-energy decomposition compared with a Hartree-Fock-node/fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC) decomposition. RHF/UHF stability energies supply the spin-symmetry-breaking correction Delta; CCSD(T) extrapolated to the CBS limit approximates exact reference energies. Natural-orbital dynamic/non-dynamic correlation indices were evaluated with CASSCF and FCI, and Slater-Jastrow FNDMC used a single RHF determinant node. Published all-electron FCI and CASSCF energies were shifted to the ccECP energy scale for the cross-method comparison.
software: GAMESS for CASSCF/FCI and natural-orbital indices; Gaussian 09 for RHF/UHF and CCSD(T); QMCPACK for FNDMC
basis_set: CASSCF(14,8) and CASSCF(14,16)/cc-pVQZ; CCSD(T)/CBS extrapolation from cc-pVXZ (X = 3,4,5) with ccECPs; FNDMC RHF orbitals in aug-cc-pVTZ with ccECPs and a 0.0025 au time step. Published all-electron CASSCF/FCI values were adjusted by the all-electron-to-ECP RHF energy difference.
relativistic_treatment: Correlation-consistent ccECPs replaced atomic cores in the CCSD(T)/CBS and FNDMC reference calculations; the paper does not present this as a separate relativistic correction.
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(14e,8o) contains the full F2 valence space. CAS(14e,16o) adds one correlating partner orbital for every orbital in the original eight-orbital valence space.
active_space_protocol: Source-explicit full-valence-versus-extended comparison: CAS(14,8) is crowded, with effectively one empty orbital and maximum excitation degree two for 14 electrons, so it under-recovers non-dynamic correlation toward dissociation. CAS(14,16) adds a complete correlating partner shell and recovers more correlation, but that extra recovery is dominated by unwanted dynamic correlation at shorter distances. The authors judge CAS(14,8) the less inaccurate space for correlation-energy decomposition, not a generally converged electronic-structure space.
nroots_per_mult: Ground-state dissociation/stretching curve only; no state averaging or excited roots are reported.
electronic_structure_description: RHF/UHF instability appears above about 1.4 angstrom, and the HF-node non-dynamic fraction rises toward roughly 50% of total correlation at dissociation. CAS(14,8) follows the qualitative growth but lies below the FNDMC non-dynamic reference in the stretched region because its active space is too restrictive. CAS(14,16) lowers the total energy substantially but exceeds the reference non-dynamic component at all sampled distances, producing non-negligible hidden dynamic correlation, especially at short F-F separations.
Other: F2 shows why lower variational energy is not automatically better for a CASSCF-based dynamic/non-dynamic partition: the double-shell CAS(14,16) is more correlated but less clean as a non-dynamic reference, while CAS(14,8) is undercomplete at dissociation yet less contaminated overall. Both active spaces and the full bond scan are consolidated into one physical-system row.

XMS-CASPT2 overestimates saddling while all the DFT functionals underestimate it. The XMS-CASPT2 dE(S0-T0) computed on TPSSh geometries differs by only 0.1 kcal/mol from that on the XMS-CASPT2 structure Row-specific method, active-space, and result fields were checked without inventing missing values. method: FCIQMC-tailored distinguishable cluster (TDCSD) and tailored coupled cluster (TCCSD, TCCSD(T)), with perturbative F12 basis-set corrections, benchmarked against CASPT2, CCSD(T), DLPNO-CCSD(T1), MC-PDFT, diffusion Monte Carlo and DFT-PBE[U]
