relativistic_treatment: semicore Fe (3s3p) correlation included in the coupled-cluster steps
active_space_orbital_description: largest space CAS(32,34): the entire porphyrin pi system plus the orbitals of CAS(14,18); progression of four spaces detailed in active_space_protocol
active_space_protocol: A four-space progression that is itself the key result. CAS(8,11): five Fe 3d orbitals, five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals and one sigma(Fe-N) bond. CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. Large spaces (over 30 electrons in 30+ orbitals) are built from DCSD natural orbitals whose occupations deviate strongly from 0 and 2, with the explicit requirement that both spin states get a similar space - if an orbital type matters for one spin state it is included for both, so the states are balanced. FCIQMC then supplies the CI vectors inside these large spaces to tailor the distinguishable-cluster/coupled-cluster amplitudes.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3Eg (triplet), stabilized over 5A1g (quintet). Quintet-triplet spin gap dE = E(Q) - E(T), a few kcal/mol with the triplet below the quintet. At CAS(32,34): tailored TDCSD-F12a and TCCSD(T)-F12a both give 5.8 kcal/mol; recent Stochastic-MRCISD on the same CAS(32,34) (correlating 96 electrons in 159 orbitals) gives 6.8 kcal/mol; CCSD(T)-embedded CAS(32,34)+dF12 gives 5.7 and DCSD-embedded 3.6 kcal/mol. Largest doubles amplitude in CAS(32,34): 0.242 (LS/triplet) and 0.221 (HS/quintet) - much more multiconfigurational than the octahedral complexes.
Other: The clearest active-space lesson in the paper: the entire porphyrin pi system must be in the space to stabilize the triplet ground state. Smaller CASs erroneously predict a quintet ground state; only once the full pi system is included (via the Gouterman orbitals and ultimately CAS(32,34)) does the correct triplet-below-quintet ordering emerge, already at the Stochastic-CASSCF level, and tailoring plus F12 enlarges the gap further. Small active spaces demonstrably reduce tailored-method accuracy here - fixed amplitudes in a small space shrink the TCCSD(T) gap far below CCSD(T) - so large active spaces are indispensable when multiconfigurational character is high. All the large-CAS(32,34) tailored methods agree with each other to within a fraction of a kcal/mol.

electronic_structure_description: Singlet ground state with the triplet 17.9 kcal/mol higher (CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)). CASSCF/def2-TZVPP natural occupation numbers of the sigma and sigma* N-X orbitals are fractional, showing partial multireference character; T1 diagnostic only slightly above 0.02.

compound_name: model keto-carotenoids COn with n conjugated double bonds (up to 13), and canthaxanthin in the orange carotenoid protein
geometry_source: ground-state geometries optimized at MP2 for the COn compounds with up to 13 double bonds, chosen after comparing how CAM-B3LYP over-localizes and B3LYP exaggerates the conjugation relative to CC3
method: DMRG-SCF with an NEVPT2 perturbative correction as the multireference route, compared against CC3 and EOM-CC3, time-dependent DFT and semiempirical CI (SECI); DMRG is used precisely because plain CAS-SCF cannot carry the natural active space of the longer chains
active_space_orbital_description: the 'natural active space' of each COn, defined by its n double bonds: n occupied and n virtual pi orbitals plus the two occupied nonbonding lone-pair orbitals - so 2n+2 orbitals for chain length n
active_space_protocol: the space grows with the chain: n occupied pi, n virtual pi and the two lone pairs for a COn with n double bonds. Because CAS-SCF scales exponentially in that space, DMRG-SCF replaces exact diagonalization for the longer chains, with NEVPT2 added for dynamic correlation - a combination previously shown to capture nuclear relaxation effects on the excited-state manifold of extended carotenoids.
electronic_structure_description: The dark Ag- state has strong doubly excited character, so conventional TD-DFT overshoots its transition energy, while the bright Bu+ state is captured reasonably well by TD-DFT. DMRG/NEVPT2 is reliable for the states energetically separated from the others but systematically underestimates the bright Bu+ excitation energy across these systems, so the paper's final benchmark data set is assembled by mixing methods: CC3 for Au and Bg in short systems and NEVPT2 for longer ones, NEVPT2 throughout for Ag, and CC3 for the bright Bu+ in the shorter systems. The practical conclusion is that semiempirical CI is the right accuracy-cost compromise for real xanthophylls in their protein environment, demonstrated on canthaxanthin in the orange carotenoid protein.
reference_short: Bondanza, Jacquemin & Mennucci, Excited States of Xanthophylls Revisited: Toward the Simulation of Biologically Relevant Systems, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2021, 12, 6604-6612
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is defined by a rule that scales with chain length (n occupied pi + n virtual pi + 2 lone pairs for COn) rather than by a fixed pair, and chains up to n = 13 are treated. geometry_source: computational and experimental combined: the Fe-Cb and Fe-CO distances were optimized at the CASPT2 level by stepwise energy scans with 0.01 and 0.02 A steps and parabolic interpolation, with all three Fe-CO distances kept equal and every other parameter fixed at the crystallographic values. Optimized Fe-Cb 1.790 A, 1.783 A with the relativistic correction and 1.82 A with the BSSE correction; Fe-CO 1.797 A and 1.786 A. The BSSE-corrected Fe-Cb distance is about 0.03 A longer than the electron-diffraction value and 0.05 A longer than the X-ray value, while the CASPT2 Fe-CO distance is close to experiment.
software: MOLCAS-3 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 94 and GAMESS for the RHF, UHF and CAS(10,10) geometry optimizations
basis_set: ANO in MOLCAS: (17s12p9d) contracted to [6s4p3d] for iron, (10s4p3d) to [3s2p1d] for carbon and oxygen and (7s) to [2s] for hydrogen, with the carbon 1s and the iron 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals frozen in CASPT2. active_space_orbital_description: twelve electrons in twelve orbitals. Ten of them follow a published general rule for transition metal compounds: the two singly occupied iron 3d(xz) and 3d(yz) orbitals paired with the two singly occupied cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, and the three doubly occupied 3d orbitals - dxy, dx2-y2 and dz2 - each paired with a combination of a 4d correlating orbital and a CO orbital. The remaining two are the lowest and highest cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, added to obtain the correct ordering of the singlet states. CAS(12,12) natural orbital occupation numbers, bonding against antibonding partner: 1.977/0.025 for the cyclobutadiene pair, 1.929/0.070 for dz2 with a CO combination, 1.924/0.073 for dx2-y2, 1.921/0.078 for dxy, and 1.895/0.107 and 1.894/0.107 for the two Fe-Cb pairs.
active_space_protocol: (10,10) following the general transition-metal rule - five 3d orbitals each with a correlating partner - used for the geometry optimization; (12,12) adding the two remaining cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, required for the correct ordering of the singlet states
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet, though the restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction is unstable over a wide range of Fe-Cb distances. The lowest broken-symmetry unrestricted solution dissociates to triplet cyclobutadiene plus triplet Fe(CO)3; higher broken-symmetry solutions break symmetry within the cyclobutadiene ring as well and correspond to excited wavefunctions dissociating to singlet fragments. The CASPT2 binding energy of Fe(CO)3 to cyclobutadiene is 95.7 kcal/mol relative to square triplet cyclobutadiene and 90.3 kcal/mol relative to the rectangular singlet. The rotational barrier of the Fe(CO)3 group against the ring is exactly zero at RHF, UHF and CASSCF, in agreement with experiment and with extended Huckel predictions that such barriers should be very small for M(CO)3 fragments on even-membered carbon rings. The CAS(12,12) occupations show that correlation in the Fe-CO bonds is almost as important as in the Fe-Cb bond, and that correlation within the cyclobutadiene ring is the least important of the three.
Other: The most transferable thing in this paper is a rule for CHOOSING the active space from a broken-symmetry Hartree-Fock calculation. The restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction of the complex is unstable over a wide range of iron-cyclobutadiene distances, and the unrestricted solutions break symmetry in the Fe-Cb bond, localizing electrons on the iron and on the ring. The author's conclusion is stated flatly: the Hartree-Fock orbitals that break symmetry are the ones that should be in the CASSCF active space, and the lowest-energy broken-symmetry solution shows the most important non-dynamical correlation in the molecule. The evidence is that the broken-symmetry natural orbitals and the CAS(10,10) natural orbitals have very similar contours and come out in the same ORDER, and that feeding the broken-symmetry natural orbitals in as CASSCF starting orbitals gives very good convergence - the CAS-UNO procedure. The occupation numbers show the difference between the two descriptions clearly: the broken-symmetry solution over-polarizes, giving 1.595/0.404 for the Fe-Cb pair where the CASSCF gives 1.894/0.107, but it puts the right orbitals in the right order. The space itself follows a published general rule for transition metal compounds - a (10,10) space correlating all five metal 3d orbitals, the empty ones against ligand orbitals that donate an electron pair and the doubly occupied ones against 4d correlating orbitals mixed with empty ligand orbitals - and the paper confirms that rule holds here, with the two singly occupied Fe 3d(xz,yz) orbitals correlating against the two singly occupied cyclobutadiene orbitals and the three doubly occupied 3d orbitals against combinations of 4d with CO orbitals. The 4d orbitals are the second orbitals of a triple-zeta d shell, that is the 3d correlating shell of the double-shell effect. Two orbitals then have to be ADDED beyond that rule: the remaining pair of cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, needed to get the ordering of the singlet states right, giving (12,12) - even though their own correlation contribution is small, with occupations of 1.977 and 0.025. A separate practical warning concerns CASPT2 rather than the space: the potential energy curve of the Fe(CO)3 fragment develops a discontinuity beyond an Fe-CO distance of 1.88 A where the reference weight collapses, an intruder-state artefact, and the minimum had to be found by interpolating over points whose reference weight exceeded 0.58. The paper gives a useful rule of thumb for what reference weight to expect: about (1 + 0.015) to the power -N/2 for N correlated electrons, predicting 0.71 for the 46-electron fragment and 0.61 for the 66-electron complex, against an observed 0.61 to 0.63.
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are arithmetic, treating the complex as iron(0) with a neutral four-electron cyclobutadiene donor and three carbonyls, an eighteen-electron count; the paper does not assign a formal oxidation state. The CASSCF Fe-CO distance is much longer than experiment, which the author attributes to the basis set and to the absence of dynamic correlation; the CASPT2 values are close. formula: O2Ge2Si10H4 quantum region embedded in O2Ge2Si32H32
geometry_source: a hybrid quantum-mechanical / molecular-mechanical cluster representing the reconstructed surface, the two parts joined by the SIMOMM link-atom scheme and the cluster edges saturated with hydrogen; the reaction is followed as a scan in the O-O distance
method: CASSCF on the quantum region of a QM/MM cluster, used because breaking the O-O bond passes through a region of near-degenerate levels that a single-determinant treatment distorts
basis_set: the authors' N21-3** set for the production calculations, with N31-6** used as a check
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in two orbitals - the bonding and antibonding pair of the O-O bond being broken
active_space_protocol: the minimal space for a single bond dissociation, and the paper's justification for it is a convergence test rather than an argument: the barrier and the reaction energy were recomputed for four small bare clusters - the two-atom dimer clusters with each combination of silicon and germanium, and a nine-silicon cluster - at both this space and a four-electron, four-orbital one, and in both basis sets. The barriers move by at most 0.09 eV between spaces in the smaller basis and by 0.04 eV in the larger, except for one mixed cluster where the four-orbital space with the smaller basis is an outlier. The reaction energy is more sensitive, changing sign for the nine-atom cluster. What the test establishes is that the two-orbital space suffices for the barrier, which is the quantity the paper reports.
electronic_structure_description: Chemisorbed dioxygen lying across the addimer, dissociating by O-O bond scission with an activation barrier of 0.18 eV. The three addimer compositions give barriers within 0.04 eV of one another - 0.18, 0.17 and 0.14 eV for the germanium, mixed and silicon dimers - so the composition of the dimer barely matters. On the bare, unembedded dimer clusters the corresponding barriers are 0.39 to 0.49 eV in the same basis and space.
Other: The two-orbital space is doing the one thing a single determinant cannot: following the O-O bond through the region where its bonding and antibonding levels become near-degenerate, which the authors identify as the source of the geometric distortions that uncorrelated calculations produce along this path. What the calculation then shows is that the barrier is not a property of the adsorbate or of the dimer's composition at all - all three compositions give the same value within 0.04 eV - but of the embedding: removing the surface strain by computing the bare dimer cluster more than doubles it. The authors read the composition-independence as evidence that the dissociation is electron-transfer driven.
reference_short: Grynchuk, Koval and Nakhodkin, Surf. Sci. 623, 13 (2014)
notes: The chemisorption step that precedes dissociation releases about 6 eV and is non-dissociative; only the subsequent O-O bond breaking is computed here. The bare-cluster tests in the paper give barriers of 0.35 to 0.54 eV, two to three times the values obtained on the embedded surface clusters, which is the paper's evidence that the low barrier is a consequence of local surface strain rather than of the chemistry of the dimer alone. The quantum region is quoted in the paper only for the germanium case; the corresponding clusters for the other two addimers are not written out. Correlation treatment (moved 2026-10-12 from correlation_correction, which holds only a method name): none - only the static correlation captured by the active space itself

point_group: Oh, with the calculations carried out in the D2h subgroup for technical reasons
geometry_source: the Fe-H distance optimized at each computational level; the rest of the crystal represented by the Madelung field of the infinite Mg2FeH6 lattice, computed by placing the whole negative charge at the metal and then iteratively redistributing it over the complex according to a Mulliken population analysis

basis_set: the SDZC set (1) of Tatewaki and Huzinaga for the metal, with the 3d and 4s shells each split into two functions and one diffuse p (0.09242 for iron) and one diffuse d function added. The metal 1s, 2s, 3s, 2p and 3p core orbitals are frozen in their atomic shape and not optimized in the MCSCF
active_space_orbital_description: two spaces were used. The first has only the bonding and antibonding orbitals of Eg symmetry active - four electrons in four orbitals, specified in D2h as (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0 / 4,0,0,0,0,0,0,0) for inactive and active orbitals per irreducible representation. The second adds the nonbonding d orbitals of T2g symmetry and their d* counterparts, giving ten electrons in ten orbitals, (1,1,1,0,1,0,0,0 / 4,0,0,2,0,2,2,0)
active_space_protocol: the larger space was not planned but diagnosed: the CI calculation on top of the four-electron CASSCF showed that excitations from the nonbonding T2g d orbitals to d* orbitals were important, so a second CASSCF was run with those orbitals active as well. The authors describe this as bringing some pure atomic correlation into the CASSCF itself. Both CI calculations correlated all 18 valence electrons and used four reference configurations
electronic_structure_description: With 18 valence electrons the ion is very likely a closed-shell 1A1g ground state, and the calculations confirm it. The Fe-H distance shortens systematically with correlation: 1.69 A at SCF, 1.63 with the four-electron CASSCF, 1.59 after CI on those orbitals, 1.60 with the ten-electron CASSCF and 1.56 after CI on those - the last identical to the value from neutron diffraction on the Mg2FeH6 crystal. The iron d population rises in parallel from 8.1 to 8.5. The agreement with experiment on both the bond distance and the totally symmetric vibrational frequency supports the model of the crystal as negatively charged metal-hydride complexes in a magnesium ion framework, with the conventional +2 magnesium charge giving the complex a 4- charge.
Other: A textbook instance of letting the CI tell you what the CASSCF space is missing. The first space contains only the Eg bonding and antibonding pairs, the obvious choice for a covalent metal-hydride bond; the CI built on it then reveals large excitations out of the nonbonding T2g d orbitals, so those and their virtual partners are promoted into a second CASSCF. The effect on the answer is not in the CASSCF distance - 1.63 versus 1.60 A - but in what the subsequent CI can do with it: 1.59 A from the small space against 1.56 A from the large one, and only the latter matches neutron diffraction. Note also what carries the crystal here: not a larger cluster but a Madelung field, iterated on the charge distribution, with the same field used for every geometry whenever conformations are compared.

At 90 degrees the 3B3 triplet lies below the planar singlet by 4.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF level. The Ni-H distance is 1.60 A with the four-electron space, unchanged at 1.60 A when the three pairs of bonding and antibonding orbitals involving Ni 4s and 4p are added, 1.57 A after CI on those orbitals, 1.57 A directly from the CASSCF with all five d/d* pairs active, and 1.56 A after CI on those. point_group: Cs (1A' ground PES; N2O itself linear, NNO = 180.0 deg)
geometry_source: optimized in this work at CASSCF (no analytical CASPT2 gradients in MOLCAS 4.1, so CASSCF geometries were made as good as possible); stationary points first located with (14,12) then reoptimized at CASSCF(18,14); transition-state geometries additionally refined at the CASPT2 level to give approximate CASPT2 structures
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF geometries with point-wise CASPT2 single points; transition state theory used for the kinetics
basis_set: Pople Cartesian Gaussian basis sets, chiefly 6-311G(2d) (100 basis functions for the system); 6-311+G(2d) also used for some stationary points
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12)B = all atomic 2p-derived molecular orbitals; (14,12)A = the same but with one 2p-derived MO replaced by one N-2s-derived MO; (18,14)A/B add 4 electrons in two further 2s(N and O)-derived MOs to (14,12)A or B respectively. CI expansion ~85 000 CSFs for (14,12) and ~500 000 CSFs for (18,14) in 1A' symmetry
active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen by a natural-orbital-occupation-number (NOON) criterion — keep as active the MOs with NOONs between 0.02 and 1.98 in the state-averaged first-order density matrix, which is argued to give the lowest energy for a fixed CI expansion size. Applied strictly, this criterion gives a DIFFERENT space per reactive channel — (14,12) for the NO+NO channel and (12,10) for the N2+O2 channel — hence inconsistent at, e.g., reactants; the authors instead adopt a homogeneous space over the whole PES even where NOONs fall outside those limits, accepting spaces that are not strictly homogeneous, and aiming at the lowest-energy ground-PES stationary points (NOONs maximally different from 0.0/2.0). Full valence is not feasible for this system, so trial and error plus comparison with experiment was needed. Sequence: (14,12)B all 2p-derived MOs; (14,12)A swaps one for an N 2s MO — needed because nitrogen is a limiting case for which orbitals to make active; (18,14)A/B add two 2s(N,O) MOs (+4 electrons). (18,14)A partitions as O(2,2)+N2O(16,12), i.e. the full valence space of the N2O fragment is correlated. At CASSCF, space A is clearly favoured for (14,12) and the A/B differences shrink for (18,14); once point-wise CASPT2 is applied all four spaces give similar results. B-type spaces were always used in products and describe some regions better
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A' (lowest singlet PES of the O(1D)+N2O system). Reaction energies, paper's kcal/mol at CASSCF with point-wise CASPT2 in parentheses [eV converted from the CASPT2 values], across the four active spaces: O(1D)+N2O -> NO+NO — (14,12)A -76.1 (-79.7) [-3.456]; (14,12)B -93.1 (-82.4) [-3.573]; (18,14)A -78.3 (-80.5) [-3.491]; (18,14)B -80.0 (-81.0) [-3.513]; experiment -80.4 [-3.486]. O(1D)+N2O -> N2+O2(a 1Dg) — (14,12)A -100.8 (-103.8) [-4.501]; (14,12)B -117.8 (-106.4) [-4.614]; (18,14)A -101.3 (-103.6) [-4.492]; (18,14)B -103.0 (-104.0) [-4.510]; experiment -100.9 [-4.375]
Other: The active-space choice is itself a main result: exoergicities and the N2O geometry vary strongly between the A and B spaces at CASSCF(14,12) (the NO+NO exoergicity swings from -76.1 to -93.1 kcal/mol), the spread narrows at (18,14), and CASPT2 washes out the difference almost entirely — evidence that dynamic correlation compensates an imperfect reference. N2O geometries (RNN / RNO / NNO angle, A and deg) for (14,12)A/(14,12)B and, in parentheses, (18,14)A/(18,14)B: 1.1323/1.1146 (1.1343/1.1339) [expt 1.1273]; 1.1901/1.1949 (1.1931/1.1919) [expt 1.1851]; 180.0 throughout. The 1Dg state of O is five-fold degenerate and resolves in the Cs subgroup into three A' and two A'' components; several 1A' and 1A'' PESs correlate reactants with both product channels. Stationary points reported at CASPT2//CASSCF(18,14)/6-311G(2d) except TS A3 (CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12)/6-311G(2d)); compared with BD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ and earlier CASPT2(10,10)/6-311+G(2d)//CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d) work. The number of active electrons was set to four, corresponding to the two Si-Si bonds of the sigma-conjugated system. All three silicon 1s core orbitals were frozen as determined by the ground-state SCF. The reference wavefunction and orbitals came from an average CASSCF over all the 1A1, 1B2, 1A2 and 1B1 states of interest

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet in C2v. Three states of valence character are found below the first Rydberg state at 7.20 eV - contradicting the previous assignment and meaning the first broad band in the observed spectrum is entirely valence in character. The dipole-forbidden transitions to the 1 1A2 and 4 1A2 states lie at 6.89 and 8.52 eV. The 4s, 4p and 3d members of the Rydberg series converging to the first ionization potential fall between 7.20 and 8.62 eV, and those converging to the second between 7.82 and 9.61 eV. Only MS-CASPT2 reproduced the observed excitations accurately, because only it separated the valence and Rydberg states effectively.
Other: A striking ratio: four active electrons in fifteen active orbitals. The electron count is fixed by the chemistry - the two Si-Si sigma bonds of the sigma-conjugated backbone - while the orbital count is set by what the excited states need to reach, namely the Si-Si sigma*, Si-H sigma* and the whole 4s/4p/3d Rydberg manifold. That asymmetry is the design, not an accident, and it is why the paper can address valence-Rydberg mixing at all. The methodological finding is that having the space is not sufficient: average CASSCF over these states mixes Rydberg and valence character strongly (as it had for n-tetrasilane), single-state CASPT2 does not fix it, and 'only the MS-CASPT2 method gave an accurate description of the observed electronic excitations since it provided an effective separation of the valence and Rydberg states'. The consequence for the chemistry is a reassignment: three valence states lie below the first Rydberg state, so the first broad absorption band is entirely valence, not Rydberg as previously assigned. Two supporting details worth copying - the 2s2p2d Rydberg functions are placed at the charge centroid of the CATION ground state, not the neutral, and a 0.05 level shift removes intruder states at a cost of under 0.1 eV in the excitation energies.

electronic_structure_description: The decay begins in the S2(pi pi*) state. The wavepacket moves first along the S2(pi pi*, A') surface symmetrically, then along the A'' component toward an easily accessible S2(pi pi*)/S1(n pi*) conical intersection reached through an exothermic symmetry-lowering perturbation. At that intersection the -Cbeta-C4=C5 fragment is perpendicular to the CH3O-CO-Calpha fragment, which gives the crossing a bifurcation character: the system has nearly equal probability of reaching the S1(n pi*) state of the parent and the S1(n pi*) state of isomer 1. The two isomers are formed by rotating 180 degrees about the C2=C3 double bond and about the C1-C2 single bond.

Torsion and bending surfaces were computed with state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest seven states - four singlets and three triplets - with equal weights. Vertical excitation energies for S0 to S1 and S0 to T1 agree well with experiment. The lowest S0/S1 crossing point, where excited molecules would internally convert efficiently, is asymmetric: a CNNC dihedral of 92.8 degrees with the two CNN angles unequal at 132.0 and 115.6 degrees. The check that keeps the MRCISD honest is running it on both state-averaged and state-specific CASSCF(6,4) orbitals and confirming they agree - state averaging over seven states is a substantial compromise for any one of them, and this is the evidence it did not distort the energetics. The entrance complex sits at a Be...O distance of 4.602 A on the singlet surface but only 1.818 A on the triplet — a 2.8 A difference between two states described by the same twelve orbitals, which is only possible because the space is defined by orbital index rather than by a fixed chemical picture of the bonding. electronic_structure_description: Spin crossover with 2RT(1/2) = 380 K and essentially no hysteresis; the spin conversion is very gradual. It also localizes the physics outside the coordination sphere, since the active space and the metal environment are unchanged across 1, 2 and 3. geometry_source: Conformational landscape explored at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), with the four most stable conformers retained. For the excitation energies the four conformers were reoptimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ; SA-CASSCF optimizations of the second-root geometries provided the adiabatic S1 energies. method: CASSCF geometry optimization with state-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2); B3LYP, MP2 and TD-OLYP for comparison
software: GAMESS for the DFT and MP2 geometries and frequencies
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 calculations; 6-31+G(d), 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(2d,p) for the DFT and MP2 work; TZ2P(DZP) for TD-OLYP
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals spanning a configuration space of dimension 1764: four orbitals (bonding and matching antibonding) localized chiefly on the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, and four originating from the degenerate e1g and e2u HOMO and LUMO of the benzene ring of the phenylalanine side chain.
active_space_protocol: A single CASSCF(8,8) is used for all four conformers, and its content is stated orbital by orbital: 'Four of the active orbitals (bonding and the matching antibonding interactions) were localized chiefly in the region of the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, whereas the remaining four originate from the benzene degenerate e1g and e2u highest occupied (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied (LUMO) molecular orbitals.' The space spans a configuration space of dimension 1764 and 'effectively encompassed all of the chromophores of interest for describing a few lowest excited states'. Geometries were reoptimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ, then state-averaged CASSCF over the FOUR lowest equally weighted roots was performed at those geometries; SA-CASSCF optimizations of the second-root geometries gave the adiabatic S1 energies. Three separate numerical safeguards were applied at the MS-CASPT2 stage: the C, N and O 1s cores were frozen; an IMAGINARY level shift of 0.10 au removed intruder states 'emerging mostly in the first and the third excited state', after which 'the reference weights in the excited states approached to within 7% of that in the ground state (around 0.60)'; and an IPEA shift of 0.10 au — deliberately BELOW the recommended 0.25 au — was used 'to mitigate the problems of overestimating the stability of open shells in CASPT2'. Oscillator strengths combine CASSCF transition dipole moments in the length representation with MS-CASPT2 energy differences.
nroots_per_mult: 4 equally weighted roots in the state-averaged CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: The extended beta-strand conformer. CASSCF(8,8)/MS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths (length representation, x100, in parentheses): vertical T(v) for state 1 is 4.827 (0.25), state 2 is 5.946 (5.00) and state 3 is 6.809 (88.5); the adiabatic T(0) for state 1 is 4.707. The experimental value for state 1 is 4.650 eV. TD-OLYP/TZ2P(DZP) gives a vertical energy of 5.133 eV (0.64) for the corresponding state. The dominant intensity lies in state 3, whose oscillator strength of 0.885 is more than two orders of magnitude above that of the lowest state. Geometric parameters at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), B3LYP/6-311+G(2d,p) and MP2/6-311+G(2d,p) are tabulated. Amide A band frequencies at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p), harmonic then anharmonic: NH(Phe) 3587/3403, symmetric NH2 3582/3421, antisymmetric NH2 3721/3539 cm-1. Amide I frequencies: amide I(1) harmonic 1729 with intensity 355 and anharmonic 1698 cm-1, dominated by CO(1) stretch (0.76); amide I(2) harmonic 1760 with intensity 269 and anharmonic 1732 cm-1, dominated by CO(2) stretch (0.70).
Other: The beta(a) conformer gives the best agreement with the measured origin, 4.707 eV adiabatic against 4.650 eV observed, a 0.057 eV error that is about as good as MS-CASPT2 on an (8,8) can be expected to deliver for a system this size. What makes the comparison meaningful across conformers is that the eight orbitals — four carbonyl bonding/antibonding pairs from the amide and acetyl groups, four benzene e1g/e2u frontier orbitals — are the same set at every geometry, so conformer-to-conformer differences in excitation energy reflect the hydrogen-bonding environment rather than any change in the correlated space. The spread across all four conformers is only 0.086 eV vertically, which is precisely why a consistent space matters: a differently constructed space per conformer could easily produce artificial differences of that size. The most valuable thing in this paper is that the active space is used to DISPROVE a set of states predicted by another method. TD-DFT with GGA functionals returns 14 of its 15 lowest excited states as charge-transfer states appearing in quasi-degenerate pairs, reflecting quasi-degeneracies among the phenylalanine antibonding orbitals. The authors dismiss these as artefacts with an argument that turns entirely on the space: 'These low-lying CT states must be considered illusive, knowing that the CASSCF active space comprises all of the orbitals necessary for describing them and that they are still absent from the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 spectrum in the 4.8-7.0 eV region.' The state is absent from a calculation whose space contains the orbitals required to build it: the eight orbitals are the amide/acetyl carbonyl set plus the benzene e1g/e2u frontier pair. The reference weight is about 0.60 in the ground state, with the excited states within 7% of it. Achieving that consistency required the imaginary level shift; without it the first and third excited states suffered intruders. The reduced IPEA shift of 0.10 au against the recommended 0.25 au is a second deliberate departure, chosen because the standard value overstabilizes open shells — a reminder that the CASPT2 zeroth-order Hamiltonian is itself a tunable part of the protocol and must be reported alongside the space.
reference_short: Doslic, Kovacevic & Ljubic, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 8650
notes: One of four low-energy NAPA conformers classified by the Ramachandran scheme. The extended beta-strand forms are contrasted with the gamma-L forms supporting a seven-membered C7 ring backbone conformation. Anharmonic corrections of -2.01, -1.92, -1.86 and -1.70 kcal/mol were computed for the four conformers. Conformer-specific experimental data come from R2PI and IR spectroscopy. correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 with the C, N and O 1s cores frozen, an imaginary level shift of 0.10 au and an IPEA shift of 0.10 au (reduced from the recommended 0.25 au).

The isomerization is mediated by a DOUBLY EXCITED state S(DE), built on the configuration pi(NN) pi(NN) to pi*(NN) pi*(NN) — 'this state is the necessary intermediate in promoting the conversion from the bright S(pi-pi*) to the S1(n-pi*) state, thereby ensuring that the photoisomerization process occurs.' Those are different wave functions, so an intersection located under one average is being described energetically under another. That is standard practice and the paper is explicit about it, but it means the degeneracy at a CI structure is not guaranteed to be exactly reproduced in the tabulated nine-root energies — and indeed several tabulated S1/S0 pairs at the CItors structures differ by 3-7 kcal/mol.

active_space_protocol: Treated by the same CASSCF/CASPT2 protocol as the two Dewar benzene species. The paper does not separately restate the active space for this compound, and its computed transition energies are shown only as bars in Figure 3 rather than in a table.
nroots_per_mult: lowest three roots in each symmetry (state-averaged)

The lowest 2A1 state in this cation lies so high that it cannot contribute to the visible part of the spectrum.
Other: The paper gives the active space twice and the two statements do not agree, which is worth knowing before reusing these numbers. The Results section says that increasing the active space to (13,12), and thus including a degree of dynamic electron correlation in the CASSCF wave function, moves the two transitions to higher energies, although still not into satisfactory agreement with experiment. The Computational Details section says instead that for some exploratory calculations up to 13 electrons were correlated in 14 orbitals, but this hardly affected the results. The electron count matches, the orbital count does not, and the verdicts point in opposite directions -- one says enlargement changed the transitions, the other says it hardly mattered. Both are reproduced here verbatim rather than reconciled. The substantive active-space lesson is separate and clear. The (5,6) reference space gives a 2B2 ground state that suffers severe symmetry breaking at the CASSCF level for the parent radical cation but not for the hexamethyl or norbornadiene analogues: the CASSCF-optimized geometry localises the SOMO, and hence spin and charge, in one of the two double bonds, which stretches to 1.406 Angstrom while the other stays at 1.348 Angstrom, close to the neutral value, and that broken-symmetry structure lies 7.9 kcal/mol below the C2v-constrained one. That is the diagnosis for why a method giving excellent spectra for the two analogues is off by 0.36 eV on the first band of the parent and places the second band where the spectrum has a minimum. Enlarging the space is the direct test of that diagnosis, and it pushed the transitions the right way without closing the gap. A second, non-active-space factor was also identified: the visible band position is exceedingly sensitive to the dihedral angle between the two cyclobutene moieties, and CASPT2 or CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ single points on geometries with the dihedral fixed between 96 and 108 degrees put the minimum near 102 degrees rather than the B3LYP value near 104; at 98 degrees, a distortion costing only 0.5 kcal/mol at CCSD(T), the bands come out at 2.13 and 3.57 eV, in good accord with experiment. So the residual error is attributed to a combination of adverse circumstances rather than to the active space alone.

geometry_source: Geometries optimized with the B3LYP and BPW91 density functionals and, for the hydride, by full CASPT2 optimization both with linear symmetry imposed and without any symmetry constraint
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 to describe the multiconfigurational nature of the molecules and analyse the U-N bonding, alongside hybrid B3LYP and pure BPW91 density functional calculations; matrix infrared spectroscopy of laser-ablated uranium atom reaction products
software: MOLCAS 7.2 for the CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 09 for the density functional calculations

active_space_protocol: A bond-inventory space covering every U-N sigma and pi bonding orbital together with its antibonding partner, so that the multiconfigurational character of the two equivalent triple bonds is captured symmetrically.
electronic_structure_description: The uranium-nitrogen bonds are equivalent by symmetry. Mulliken bond orders based on the CASSCF orbitals are N-2.89-U-2.89-N, and the CASSCF Mulliken partial charges are -0.25 on each nitrogen and +0.50 on uranium. The molecule is formed directly from the reaction of a laser-ablated excited uranium atom with molecular nitrogen; this requires electronically excited uranium, since annealing does not increase the yield but ultraviolet irradiation to excite U increases the signal threefold, consistent with a separate CASSCF/CASPT2 study of the reaction path that found a 25 kcal/mol barrier for this 59 kcal/mol exothermic reaction. Infrared spectra of laser-ablated uranium with nitrogen in excess argon at 5 K gave strong NUN and weak UN absorptions.

For NUNH one electron in a hydrogen 1s orbital is added, giving (13,13): the same bonding and antibonding orbitals as in NUN plus one nonbonding orbital localized on uranium. Because nothing else changes, the differences in Mulliken bond orders read off the CASSCF orbitals -- N-2.89-U-2.89-N for the symmetric molecule against N-2.91-U-2.19-N-1.05-H for the hydride -- reflect the chemistry rather than a re-tuned reference, and the conclusion that the two N-U bonds in NUNH differ by nearly a bond order rests on that. What the space then reveals is a piece of orbital anatomy that a bond-counting picture would miss: the sigma bonding orbital for the inside U-N bond is extended substantially to include the N-H bond, so it makes little contribution to the inside U-N bond, which is instead a double bond formed from the contribution of the four pi bonding orbitals spanning both N-U-N bonds. CASPT2 frequencies were first computed for a structure optimized with linear symmetry imposed; that structure had an imaginary frequency and is therefore not a minimum. A full CASPT2 geometry optimization without symmetry constraints then gave a slightly bent structure with all real frequencies, lying just 0.2 kcal/mol below the linear one -- a difference the authors describe as well within CASPT2 error. Crucially, the qualitative appearance of the orbitals does not change when symmetry is removed, and the orbital occupation numbers and bond orders remain the same, which is what licenses their conclusion that the molecule is pliable rather than genuinely bent. That is the right test: an imaginary frequency at a constrained geometry matters only if relaxing the constraint changes the wave function, and here it does not. The practical consequence is in the spectrum, since the bent minimum has two distinct UNH bending frequencies at 519 and 303 per cm where the symmetric structure has one degenerate mode, against a single observed argon matrix absorption at 433.0 per cm. A final caveat on charges: the hydrogen carries a slight positive Mulliken charge of 0.06 at both CASSCF and CASPT2, whereas B3LYP gives about 0.24. The authors attribute the gap to the different basis sets and to Mulliken analysis being very sensitive to basis, but also to a real difference in density -- CASSCF describes systems in a more covalent manner because of the presence of bonding and antibonding pairs of orbitals in the wave function, so it is not unexpected that it makes the system more covalent than a single determinant method. geometry_source: structures first located by DFT (PBE/TZVP and PBE/TZVPP with Turbomole 6.0, B3LYP/6-31+G(d) with Gaussian 03), then treated at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d); all stationary points checked by frequency analysis
method: CASSCF(6,6) for both the open-shell and closed-shell species, with CCSD(T)/6-31+G(d) single points used to verify the CASSCF results; DFT for the initial structure location
software: Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF and the B3LYP work; Turbomole 6.0 for the PBE calculations
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF; 6-31+G(d) for B3LYP and the CCSD(T) single points; TZVP and TZVPP for the PBE calculations
active_space_orbital_description: for the singlet azirine the six correlated orbitals are the sigma and pi bonds of the three-membered ring together with their antibonding counterparts. For the triplet vinyl nitrene the same six-orbital space is rebuilt from the sigma and pi bonds of the C-N part of the molecule, their antibonding combinations, and the formally singly occupied lone-pair orbitals left by the broken sigma molecular orbital
active_space_protocol: (6,6) held at constant size but recomposed between species: ring sigma/pi and their antibondings for the closed-ring azirine, C-N sigma/pi plus antibondings plus the two singly occupied lone pairs for the ring-opened triplet nitrene
electronic_structure_description: The five-membered-ring azirine is a minimum on the singlet hypersurface, taken as the zero of energy, with the open-shell vinyl nitrene 3.7 kcal/mol above it at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d) and 5.1 kcal/mol at CCSD(T). The transition state for the ring opening lies about 7 kcal/mol up. The bridgehead azirine with a five-membered ring could not be characterized by low-temperature NMR even when kinetically stabilized, whereas the six-membered-ring homologue could - and ring opening to the vinyl nitrene is identified as the key step behind the observed photoreactivity. For the six-membered system two energy-rich triplet azirine conformers lie at 59.9 (62.0 at CCSD(T)) and 60.2 kcal/mol.

That is what allows a closed-shell heterocycle and an open-shell nitrene to be put on one energy scale, and the authors' stated reason for going multireference at all is exactly this: to 'appropriately treat both open-shell as well as closed-shell species'. The validation is external rather than internal - CCSD(T)/6-31+G(d) single points were run to verify the CASSCF results, and the DFT, CASSCF(6,6) and CCSD(T) relative energies are reported to agree reasonably well qualitatively. The residual disagreement is small but systematic: the singlet nitrene sits 3.7 kcal/mol above the azirine at CASSCF and 5.1 at CCSD(T), so the small space slightly favours the open-shell species.

software: GAUSSIAN (MP2 geometry, conical-intersection search); GAMESS (CASSCF paths)

active_space_protocol: one ten-orbital space per state character: all pi for ground and pi-pi* states; swap the lowest pi for a lone pair to reach n-pi*; swap the highest pi* for a sigma* to reach pi-sigma*

notes: The three ten-orbital spaces are kept in one row because they are the same size and differ only by which single orbital is swapped for the state being described.

electronic_structure_description: The ground-state g tensor and the energies of a series of electronically excited doublet and quartet states were computed for this cation. The g tensor of the lowest Kramers doublet was obtained from the spin-orbit mixed states. For comparison the g tensors of all the paramagnetic species in the study were also computed by a density functional method with the same relativistic Hamiltonian.
Other: The multiconfigurational treatment is used here because the cheaper alternative demonstrably failed, and the paper says so plainly. For the anion-cation pairs the authors were unable to obtain the correct broken-symmetry solutions at all, and for a related salt studied earlier the exchange couplings from that approach came out nonrealistically large; the multiconfigurational route was adopted in its place. That is the clearest kind of justification for a multireference calculation -- not that it might be better, but that the single-determinant description does not exist for the states in question. Two quite different spaces then serve two quite different purposes. For the exchange couplings between radical pairs the space is minimal, two electrons in two orbitals, one singly occupied orbital per radical, representing the singlet and triplet combinations whose splitting is the quantity wanted. For the metal cation the space is nine electrons in nine orbitals built by chemical composition: the five metal d orbitals together with two pi bonding and two pi antibonding orbitals of the arene ligands, chosen because those ligand orbitals mix with the metal d orbitals. Admitting the mixed ligand orbitals rather than the metal d set alone is what makes the description of a formally 3d5 centre in a sandwich environment meaningful. The consequence of the small pair space is visible in the tables and worth flagging. For the radical-radical pairs the three methods disagree by more than a factor of two on the largest coupling -- minus 8.25, minus 3.70 and minus 7.45 per cm from density functional, multiconfigurational and perturbatively corrected treatments respectively -- and the multiconfigurational value without correction is the outlier, closer to zero than either of the others. At longer contact distances the uncorrected values collapse to exactly zero while the corrected ones retain small residual couplings. For the anion-cation pairs, where only the multiconfigurational route was available, the correction changes the sign of the largest coupling, from plus 1.00 to minus 1.55 per cm, so whether that interaction is ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic depends entirely on the dynamic correlation added after the space. Given that these couplings are then used to interpret magnetic susceptibility data, that sign change is the whole result. A note on the spin-orbit treatment for the metal cation: one sextet, twenty-four quartet and seventy-five doublet states from the multiconfigurational calculation were mixed to give two hundred fifty-two spin-orbit states, so the state manifold entering the property calculation is far larger than the space itself suggests.

geometry_source: Minima, conical intersections and reaction paths optimized at state-averaged CASSCF; all energies re-evaluated by multistate CASPT2 at those geometries
method: State-averaged CASSCF over the lowest five roots with equal weights for all optimizations, with multistate CASPT2 in a larger common active space to re-evaluate every energy
basis_set: 6-31G* for all computations, with Cholesky decomposition and unbiased auxiliary sets for the two-electron integrals
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals at the reference level, composed differently per state: five occupied pi and three unoccupied pi antibonding orbitals for the bright state, with one occupied pi orbital replaced by the carbonyl oxygen lone pair for the dark state. The perturbative step uses the union of these, twelve electrons in nine orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Two-tier design: state-specific composition at the reference level so each state has its best small space, and a common union space at the correlated level so that energies compared across states share one description. Five roots averaged with equal weights, an imaginary shift of 0.2 against intruder states, and no IPEA shift.
electronic_structure_description: The bare chromophore. Vertical excitation energies are 4.32 eV to the bright state and 4.74 eV to the dark state, a gap of 0.42 eV. Because the two states are close, the predominant relaxation route from the bright state is state-switching to the dark state; photoisomerization is the minor channel.
Other: The space is two-tier: at the reference level the space is ten electrons in eight orbitals whose composition depends on the state -- five occupied pi and three unoccupied pi antibonding orbitals for the bright state, with one occupied pi orbital swapped for the carbonyl oxygen lone pair when the dark state is treated -- while the perturbative step uses a larger twelve-electron nine-orbital space that is the UNION of the two. Each state therefore gets its best small space for geometry work, and every energy compared across states comes from one common space. State averaging is over the lowest five roots with equal weights. What the numbers show is a case where the environment does most of the work the active space is usually blamed for: a single water molecule stabilizes the bright state by 0.41 eV and simultaneously destabilizes the dark state by 0.43 to 0.55 eV, so the gap between them widens from 0.42 eV in the bare chromophore to 1.26 and 1.38 eV in the two hydrated forms. That is a differential shift of roughly one electronvolt from one hydrogen bond, and it inverts the mechanism -- internal conversion to the dark state dominates in the isolated molecule and is heavily suppressed on hydration, so photoisomerization takes over. Equally instructive is what the water does not change: the authors state that the effect on the ADIABATIC excitation energies is much smaller than on the vertical ones. Vertical energies are evaluated at a geometry the excited state did not choose, so they are sensitive to how the environment tilts the ground-state structure; adiabatic energies let each state relax and largely absorb that. Reporting both and noting the contrast is what makes the mechanistic claim credible rather than an artifact of where the energies were evaluated. One parameter choice deserves a flag for cross-study comparison: the IPEA shift is not APPLIED here, whereas the same group used the default value of 0.25 in closely related work on a methoxy-substituted analogue of this very chromophore, where that parameter moved the two excited states by different amounts and changed their gap by 0.33 eV. Two studies of near-identical molecules from the same authors therefore sit on different sides of a parameter that is known to shift exactly the quantity both papers depend on, and their excitation energies should not be compared directly. An imaginary shift of 0.2 guards against intruder states and Cholesky decomposition handles the integrals; a single split-valence polarized basis is used throughout.

notes: Part of a study of a sunscreen-related cinnamate chromophore and its two most stable one-water complexes. compound_name: hydrazoic acid, HN3, dissociating to N2(X 1Sigma_g+) + NH(X 3Sigma- or a 1Delta)
point_group: Cs; the equilibrium HN3 geometry is planar and no non-planar geometries were computed
geometry_source: transition states for both the singlet and the triplet dissociation channels located by CASSCF and MCSCF; the singlet-triplet crossing seam mapped as a function of the N2-NH distance and the NNH angle
method: CASSCF and MCSCF to locate the transition states, with the largest configurations from the CASSCF calculations then used as the reference for MCSCF-CI calculations
basis_set: 94 contracted Gaussian-type functions, of s, p and d symmetry on N and s and p on H
active_space_orbital_description: the 4a' to 12a' and 1a'' to 3a'' orbitals - nine orbitals of a' and three of a'' symmetry - holding either all 16 valence electrons or the 10 valence electrons exclusive of the N 2s electrons
active_space_protocol: a fixed twelve-orbital window (4a'-12a', 1a''-3a'') with two electron counts: all 16 valence electrons, or 10 valence electrons with the N 2s electrons left out. Running both is the point - it tests whether the nitrogen 2s correlation affects the location of the singlet-triplet crossing seam that the whole spin-selectivity argument rests on.
nroots_per_mult: the lowest singlet (1A') and lowest triplet (3A'') surfaces of HN3 and the seam between them
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1A', planar at equilibrium. At the point of lowest singlet-triplet crossing the N2 and NH bond distances are identical to those in the isolated N2 and NH molecules in both X 3Sigma- and a 1Delta, so the dissociation is vibrationally adiabatic; the seam lies nearly perpendicular to the direction of steepest descent on both sides, so little rotational torque is exerted on the NH fragment, as observed. The terminal N-N and N-H bonds are nearly perpendicular at the crossing, making the energy almost independent of the dihedral angle and so preserving planarity. A barrier in the singlet channel was located at a trans HN3 geometry with angle HNN = 90 degrees and angle NNN = 165 degrees at an interior N-N distance of about 4.5 bohr, beyond the singlet-triplet crossing; it lies about 2000 cm-1 above the crossing and about 1000 cm-1 above the N2 + NH(a 1Delta) asymptote, and arises from electronic constriction - at long range the 10a' and 2a'' orbitals are equally occupied by the NH 2p electrons, but the 10a' orbital becomes unfavourable in the presence of N2 through Fermi repulsion with the N2 2p_sigma orbitals.
Other: The active space exists to locate a crossing seam, not to get an energy right, and the symmetry argument built on it is what the paper is really for: because the HN3 ground-state wavefunction and the I_z S_z term of the spin-orbit Hamiltonian are both symmetric under reflection in the molecular plane, only NH product states whose total electronic-plus-rotational wavefunction is also symmetric can be formed, so only the F1 and F3 multiplets of NH(X 3Sigma-) are populated - exactly as the infrared multiphoton dissociation experiments find. The two electron counts on the same twelve orbitals are a built-in check that the seam location does not depend on correlating the nitrogen 2s shell.

basis_set: cc-pVDZ; aug-cc-pVDZ; cc-pVTZ; aug-cc-pVTZ (trajectory level: aug-cc-pVDZ)

active_space_protocol: (2,2) N-N pi/pi* baseline used for the production trajectories; (6,4) adds both N lone pairs to test active-space adequacy. Both spaces were mapped with four basis sets and received matching-space CASPT2/aug-cc-pVTZ single points. The authors selected CAS(2,2)/aug-cc-pVDZ for dynamics because its profile is close to CAS(6,4)/aug-cc-pVDZ and it is small enough for 100 on-the-fly trajectories.
electronic_structure_description: The paper does not state a multiplicity or root count. ZPE-corrected relative energies (trans, cis, inversion TS, torsion TS; kcal/mol) are: CASSCF(2,2)/aug-cc-pVDZ 0.0, 5.9, 52.9, 58.0; CASSCF(2,2)/aug-cc-pVTZ 0.0, 5.7, 52.1, 58.5; CASPT2(2,2)/aug-cc-pVTZ//CASSCF(2,2) 0.0, 5.5, 51.9, 55.6; CASSCF(6,4)/aug-cc-pVDZ 0.0, 5.8, 53.4, 58.0; CASSCF(6,4)/aug-cc-pVTZ 0.0, 5.7, 52.2, 58.6; CASPT2(6,4)/aug-cc-pVTZ//CASSCF(6,4) 0.0, 5.6, 52.0, 53.6. The torsion TS breaks the N-N pi bond and is biradical. SI imaginary frequencies are -1706 cm-1 for inversion and -2954 cm-1 for torsion.
Other: CAS(2,2) and CAS(6,4) give nearly identical CASSCF/aug-cc-pVDZ barriers (52.9/58.0 versus 53.4/58.0 kcal/mol for inversion/torsion), supporting the small-space dynamics choice. At aug-cc-pVTZ, CASPT2 changes the CAS(2,2) inversion/torsion barriers from 52.1/58.5 to 51.9/55.6 kcal/mol and the CAS(6,4) values from 52.2/58.6 to 52.0/53.6; dynamic correlation affects torsion much more than inversion. Nevertheless, dynamics overrides the lower static inversion barrier: all 100 4-ps reactant trajectories isomerized exclusively by torsion, and 20 trajectories launched at the inversion TS immediately entered cis/trans wells and then isomerized only by torsion because centrifugal force blocks inversion. The trajectory decay rate 1.99 ps-1 is close to the torsional RRKM rate 1.55 ps-1, while the faster inversion RRKM prediction 3.60 ps-1 is dynamically inaccessible.

electronic_structure_description: The lowest singlet CH2OO state is planar 1A' and its CAS(4,4)/cc-pVTZ association curve is barrierless and long-range attractive; singlet CH2OO is bound by 53.2 kcal/mol (51.2 with ZPE). CAS(18,14)/AVDZ gives triplet binding 36.9 kcal/mol (31.5 with ZPE), a 3A'' barrier of 6.0 (7.1 with ZPE), and a 3A' electronic barrier of 11.1 kcal/mol. CAS(12,11)/6-31+G(d) gives triplet binding 27.0 (22.4 with ZPE) and barrier 7.3 (8.7 with ZPE) kcal/mol. CASPT2(4,4) gives singlet/triplet binding 52.7/27.8 and a 7.1-kcal/mol triplet barrier; MRCI(4,4) gives 47.6/18.6 and 4.2 kcal/mol, respectively (all electronic magnitudes relative to separated reactants).
Other: At equilibrium, MRCI gives singlet Psi(1A') approximately 0.898|pi1^2 pi2^2> - 0.531|pi1^2 pi3^2>, biradical character beta = 0.517, and bond order 1.241; triplet Psi(3A'') = 0.988|pi1^2 pi2^1 pi3^1>, beta = 0.988, and bond order 1.006. The triplet transition state has beta = 0.878. At triplet C-O distances 1.70, 2.70, 3.70, and 4.70 angstrom, beta is 0.980, 0.567, 0.968, and 0.990. The 3A'' route passes through CH2OO, whereas 3A' leads directly to H2CO + O(3P). The current work does not calculate spin-orbit coupling; it cites an earlier SOC-matrix result finding negligible intersystem crossing, so the SOC field is left empty. The singlet is about 16.5 kcal/mol more stable at primary CASSCF, consistent with its stronger C-O bond; the barrierless singlet path should have little temperature dependence, whereas the triplet path becomes relevant at higher temperature.

compound_name: the CH3SO + O3 reaction system and its CH3SO(O3) adduct, methylsulfinyl radical plus ozone
geometry_source: density-fitted MP2 saddle-point structures with 6-311++G(2df,2p), cc-pV(T+d)Z and Def2-TZVPP, and omegaB97X-D3/6-31+G* and M06-2X stationary points, in ORCA 4.x; two-dimensional relaxed scans of the S-OOO and SO-OO bond lengths at omegaB97X-D3/6-31+G*; the CASSCF and CASPT2 work consists of single points on these structures and of two-dimensional single-point scans over the same coordinates
method: CASSCF with an active space built from the restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock frontier orbitals and systematically enlarged, followed by CASPT2 single-point two-dimensional scans; compared against DF-MP2, omegaB97X-D3 and M06-2X treatments and a CFOUR Hartree-Fock stability analysis
software: Molpro (MULTI program) for the CASSCF and CASPT2; ORCA 4.x for the DFT and DF-MP2; CFOUR for the Hartree-Fock stability analysis
basis_set: cc-pV(T+d)Z and cc-pV(D+d)Z for the CASSCF and CASPT2 work and 6-31G* for the larger-space scan; the +d tight-d correction is used throughout on sulfur
active_space_orbital_description: spaces built from the ROHF frontier orbitals and enlarged systematically from five electrons in four orbitals up to thirteen electrons in twelve orbitals: half of each space is the highest doubly occupied orbitals, one orbital is the singly occupied orbital, and the remainder are the lowest virtuals. The CASPT2 scans used (11e,8o) with cc-pV(D+d)Z and (13e,10o) with 6-31G*.
active_space_protocol: (5e,4o) then (9e,8o) at CASSCF/cc-pV(T+d)Z to diagnose static correlation, enlarged systematically as far as (13e,12o); CASPT2 single-point scans at (11e,8o)/cc-pV(D+d)Z and (13e,10o)/6-31G*. The enlargement is the diagnostic itself - the leading CI coefficient is what the authors read off it.
nroots_per_mult: the doublet ground state of the radical-plus-ozone system
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: doublet. The key result is negative: the CASPT2/cc-pV(D+d)Z (11e,8o) and CASPT2/6-31G* (13e,10o) two-dimensional scans over the S-OOO and SO-OO coordinates, covering exactly the region where the DFT adduct and saddle point sit, show smooth curvature and no evidence of either an adduct or a transition state - so ozone reacts with the methylsulfinyl radical barrierlessly and without intermediate stationary points. A CASSCF transition-state search found none. The DFT picture, by contrast, gives a [CH3S(O3)O] addition adduct in a deep 37 kcal/mol well whose O-O bond dissociates over a flat 1 kcal/mol barrier (0.4 kcal/mol electronic, and 0.2 kcal/mol below the adduct once zero-point energy is included, with a 454i cm-1 imaginary mode at omegaB97X-D3/6-31+G* and 1177i cm-1 at DF-MP2) to give CH3SO2 + O2. Those products lie about 60 kcal/mol below the reactants, far more than the 14 kcal/mol measured barrier for CH3SO2 to dissociate to CH3 + SO2, so CH3SO2 should decompose immediately.
Other: This paper is a worked lesson in using an active-space series as a diagnostic rather than as a production calculation. A CASSCF(5e,4o)/cc-pV(T+d)Z calculation gives a leading CI coefficient of 0.99 and would have licensed a single-reference treatment; enlarging to (9e,8o) gives coefficients of 0.955, 0.219 and 0.102, revealing static correlation that the small space had hidden. The trap being diagnosed is severe: the published MP2/6-311++G(2df,p) barrier of 66 kcal/mol for this reaction comes from an unrestricted Hartree-Fock reference whose <S2> values are 1.35 and 1.36 for a doublet, and a CFOUR stability analysis turned an <S2> of 0.768 into 3.42 on orbital rotation - the authors call UHF wholly inappropriate here. The multireference scans then overturn the DFT mechanism as well, finding no adduct and no barrier where DFT places a 37 kcal/mol well. The honest limitation the authors state is that their results cannot conclusively prove the adduct dissociation is barrierless, only that any barrier is too small to matter at marine-boundary-layer temperatures.

compound_name: FeGe anion, the iron-germanium diatomic anion
d_electron_count: Formally d6 s2 iron in the free atom; no ionic d count is assigned for these covalent clusters
ligand_set: Germanium atoms only; no ancillary ligands
point_group: C2v used for computational convenience; the molecule itself is linear
geometry_source: Optimized in this work at the CASPT2 level with the [11; 14] space
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 for the diatomics and RASSCF/RASPT2 for the larger clusters, with geometries optimized at the correlated level rather than borrowed - FeGe(-/0) and FeGe2(-/0) optimized at CASPT2, FeGe3(-/0) relaxed at RASPT2. Default IPEA shift of 0.25 and an imaginary level shift of 0.1 au, both stated explicitly. In the perturbation step the Fe 3s and 3p and the Ge 3d electrons are also correlated, so semicore correlation is included rather than frozen. Density functional theory with BP86, TPSS, B3LYP and TPSSh is run alongside and benchmarked against the RASPT2 results. Multidimensional Franck-Condon factor simulations convert the computed geometries and frequencies into vibrational band profiles for comparison with the measured photoelectron spectrum.
software: OpenMolcas for all CASSCF/CASPT2 and RASSCF/RASPT2 calculations; ORCA 4.0 for the density functional calculations; MOLFC 2.3 for the Franck-Condon factor simulations
basis_set: aug-cc-pwCVTZ-DK on iron - a core-valence correlating set, consistent with correlating the Fe 3s and 3p in the perturbation step - and aug-cc-pVTZ-DK on germanium. The density functional calculations instead use def2-TZVPP on both elements.
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian for scalar relativistic effects, applied consistently in both the multireference and the density functional calculations, with Douglas-Kroll-recontracted basis sets to match. No spin-orbit coupling is reported.
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen orbitals: the Fe 3d and 4s, the Ge 4p, and the Fe 4d second shell, holding eleven electrons. This is the CASPT2(I) space; the paper also runs the identical space stripped of the Fe 4d, as CASPT2(II), and four RAS variants.
active_space_protocol: A targeted rule, itemized by orbital type and then tested. The space is built from 'the valence 3d and 4s of Fe and 4p of Ge', and then, 'in order to include the important double-shell effect of Fe, the 4d orbitals were incorporated'. Every space in the paper is stated with its composition, not merely its size. For the diatomics two complete spaces are compared head to head: CASPT2(I) uses [11 (10); 14], eleven electrons for the anion or ten for the neutral in fourteen orbitals comprising Fe 3d and 4s, Ge 4p and Fe 4d; CASPT2(II) uses [11 (10); 9], the same space with the five Fe 4d orbitals removed, and exists purely to isolate the double-shell contribution. Four restricted spaces are then calibrated against CASPT2(I): RASPT2(I) is [11 (10), 0, 2; 0, 9, 5] with nine orbitals in RAS2 and the five Fe 4d in RAS3 at a maximum of two excitations; RASPT2(II) and (III) raise that maximum to four and six; RASPT2(IV) is [11 (10), 0, 2; 0, 9, 8], adding the Ge 5p orbitals to RAS3. For the larger clusters only RAS is affordable, and the reason is quantified: full spaces would reach seventeen and twenty orbitals, whereas 'most of the computers can handle CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations with an active space around 14 orbitals'. FeGe2 uses [13 (12), 0, 2; 0, 12, 5], Fe 3d/4s and Ge 4p in RAS2 and Fe 4d in RAS3. FeGe3 uses [15 (14), 0, 2; 0, 10, 10], and its RAS3 is different in kind - alongside the Fe 4d it holds five antibonding 4p orbitals of the Ge3 ligand, so the space is extended toward the ligand as the cluster grows rather than only toward the metal.
multiplicities_studied: Doublet, quartet and sextet manifolds are all computed
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 2-Delta, with a bond length of 2.232 Angstrom and a vibrational frequency of 280 per centimetre. Its leading configuration is 13-sigma(2) 14-sigma(2) 15-sigma(0) 6-pi(4) 7-pi(0) 2-delta(3) with a reference weight of only 35 percent, which the authors read as 'strong multireference character'. The orbitals are identified individually: 13-sigma and 15-sigma are the bonding and antibonding combinations of Fe 3d(z2) with Ge 4p(z), 14-sigma is mainly Fe 4s, 6-pi and 7-pi are bonding and antibonding between Fe 3d(xz)/3d(yz) and Ge 4p(x)/4p(y), and 2-delta is predominantly Fe 3d(x2-y2) and 3d(xy). A dense manifold of nearly degenerate states sits above it: 4-Pi at 0.13 eV, then 6-Sigma(+) and the first 4-Sigma(-) both at 0.39, 2-Pi at 0.47, the second 4-Sigma(-) at 0.55, 6-Pi at 0.57 and 6-Sigma(-) at 0.89 eV. Doublet, quartet and sextet states all lie within 0.9 eV. Detaching an electron from the 2-delta orbital gives the neutral ground state, with an adiabatic detachment energy of 0.96 eV at CASPT2 and 0.91 eV at RASPT2.
Other: Four enlargement axes are varied separately and exactly one of them matters. The decisive axis is the iron double shell, and it does not merely shift energies - it inverts a ground-state assignment. With the Fe 4d orbitals in the space, CASPT2(I) puts the FeGe(-) quartet 4-Pi 0.13 eV above the 2-Delta doublet; with those five orbitals removed, CASPT2(II) puts the quartet 0.03 eV below it. The adiabatic detachment energy moves in step, from 0.96 eV to 0.74 eV, an error of 0.22 eV against the better calculation. The authors conclude 'the double-shell effect of Fe is really important to get the true relative energy order of the nearly degenerate electronic states'. The other three axes are all null, and each null is stated as a conclusion rather than buried. (i) Restricting the space: RASPT2(I) through (IV) 'provide almost the same relative energy order ... as that of the CASPT2(I) method', which licenses RASPT2 for this class of cluster. (ii) Excitation level into RAS3: raising the maximum from two to four to six electrons leaves the relative energies 'almost the same', so 'the single and double excitations of electrons from RAS2 to RAS3 are enough'. (iii) Further orbital addition: RASPT2(IV) adds the Ge 5p shell and changes nothing, so 'the 5p orbitals of Ge are not important enough to include in the active space'. One addition reverses a state ordering; three others do nothing measurable. Note finally that multireference character varies sharply across the series: the FeGe(-) 2-Delta ground state has a leading configuration carrying only 35 percent, which the authors call 'strong multireference character', whereas the cyclic FeGe2(-) states carry 80 to 92 percent.
reference_short: Tran & Tran, J. Phys. Chem. A 2020, 124, 4095
notes: A dedicated multireference study of iron-doped germanium clusters, and unusually self-contained: there is no supporting information, and every active space, basis set, shift parameter and geometry level appears in the main text. Two authors. The density functional benchmark is the arbitrating-among-functionals flavour, run in the correct direction with the multireference as reference: BP86, TPSS, B3LYP and TPSSh all agree with RASPT2 that the CYCLIC FeGe2 isomer is more stable than the linear one, so the qualitative verdict survives, but 'the relative energies of density functional theory are somewhat lower than those of RASPT2' in every case - the cyclic-linear separation in the anion comes out at 1.24, 1.24, 0.86 and 1.10 eV for the four functionals, with B3LYP the furthest off. The functionals are therefore licensed for the isomer question and not for the energetics. What the calculations are ultimately for is an experimental spectrum this paper does not measure: the anion photoelectron spectrum of FeGe3(-), taken from earlier work, whose four bands at 2.26, 3.00, 3.35 and 3.86 eV are all assigned to detachments from a single anionic ground state, with computed vertical detachment energies of 2.89 and 2.93 eV for the second band and 3.14 and 3.43 eV for the third. The experimental spectrum and the earlier density functional studies of FeGe(n) clusters are other groups' work and get no rows. metal_ox_state: Not assigned; these are gas-phase clusters with covalent Fe-Ge bonding rather than ionic oxidation states. nroots_per_mult: Not given as a root count; the paper reports the individual states it located in each symmetry and multiplicity.
correlation_correction: Second-order perturbation theory on the CASSCF or RASSCF reference, with the parameters disclosed - a default IPEA shift of 0.25 and an imaginary level shift of 0.1 au. Semicore correlation is included at the perturbation step (Fe 3s and 3p, Ge 3d), matched by a core-valence correlating basis on iron. The paper does not tabulate bare CASSCF or RASSCF relative energies against the perturbed ones, so the magnitude of the dynamic-correlation correction cannot be read off; instead it holds the correction fixed and varies the reference space. The two multireference routes agree closely on the one quantity computed both ways - the FeGe(-) adiabatic detachment energy is 0.96 eV at CASPT2 and 0.91 eV at RASPT2, a 0.05 eV spread - which is the internal cross-check that makes the RASPT2 licence credible for the larger clusters where CASPT2 is unaffordable.

d_electron_count: Formally d6 s2 iron in the free atom; no ionic d count is assigned for these covalent clusters
ligand_set: Germanium atoms only; no ancillary ligands
point_group: C2v used for computational convenience; the molecule itself is linear
geometry_source: Optimized in this work at the CASPT2 level with the [10; 14] space
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 for the diatomics and RASSCF/RASPT2 for the larger clusters, with geometries optimized at the correlated level rather than borrowed - FeGe(-/0) and FeGe2(-/0) optimized at CASPT2, FeGe3(-/0) relaxed at RASPT2. Default IPEA shift of 0.25 and an imaginary level shift of 0.1 au, both stated explicitly. In the perturbation step the Fe 3s and 3p and the Ge 3d electrons are also correlated, so semicore correlation is included rather than frozen. software: OpenMolcas for all CASSCF/CASPT2 and RASSCF/RASPT2 calculations; ORCA 4.0 for the density functional calculations; MOLFC 2.3 for the Franck-Condon factor simulations
basis_set: aug-cc-pwCVTZ-DK on iron - a core-valence correlating set, consistent with correlating the Fe 3s and 3p in the perturbation step - and aug-cc-pVTZ-DK on germanium. The density functional calculations instead use def2-TZVPP on both elements.
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian for scalar relativistic effects, applied consistently in both the multireference and the density functional calculations, with Douglas-Kroll-recontracted basis sets to match. No spin-orbit coupling is reported.
active_space_orbital_description: The same fourteen orbitals as the anion - Fe 3d and 4s, Ge 4p, Fe 4d - holding ten electrons.
active_space_protocol: A targeted rule, itemized by orbital type and then tested. The space is built from 'the valence 3d and 4s of Fe and 4p of Ge', and then, 'in order to include the important double-shell effect of Fe, the 4d orbitals were incorporated'. Every space in the paper is stated with its composition, not merely its size. For the diatomics two complete spaces are compared head to head: CASPT2(I) uses [11 (10); 14], eleven electrons for the anion or ten for the neutral in fourteen orbitals comprising Fe 3d and 4s, Ge 4p and Fe 4d; CASPT2(II) uses [11 (10); 9], the same space with the five Fe 4d orbitals removed, and exists purely to isolate the double-shell contribution. Four restricted spaces are then calibrated against CASPT2(I): RASPT2(I) is [11 (10), 0, 2; 0, 9, 5] with nine orbitals in RAS2 and the five Fe 4d in RAS3 at a maximum of two excitations; RASPT2(II) and (III) raise that maximum to four and six; RASPT2(IV) is [11 (10), 0, 2; 0, 9, 8], adding the Ge 5p orbitals to RAS3. For the larger clusters only RAS is affordable, and the reason is quantified: full spaces would reach seventeen and twenty orbitals, whereas 'most of the computers can handle CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations with an active space around 14 orbitals'. FeGe2 uses [13 (12), 0, 2; 0, 12, 5], Fe 3d/4s and Ge 4p in RAS2 and Fe 4d in RAS3. FeGe3 uses [15 (14), 0, 2; 0, 10, 10], and its RAS3 is different in kind - alongside the Fe 4d it holds five antibonding 4p orbitals of the Ge3 ligand, so the space is extended toward the ligand as the cluster grows rather than only toward the metal.
electronic_structure_description: The neutral ground state is 3-Sigma(-), with a bond length of 2.180 Angstrom - 0.05 Angstrom shorter than the anion - and a vibrational frequency of 341 per centimetre, stiffened from the anion's 280. The assignment of a triplet ground state agrees with earlier density functional work. The excited states are 3-Delta at 0.21 eV, 5-Pi at 0.57, 5-Sigma(-) at 0.67 and 3-Pi at 0.78 eV, so the neutral manifold is somewhat less congested near the ground state than the anion's, whose first excited state lies at only 0.13 eV.
Other: Four enlargement axes are varied separately and exactly one of them matters. The decisive axis is the iron double shell, and it does not merely shift energies - it inverts a ground-state assignment. With the Fe 4d orbitals in the space, CASPT2(I) puts the FeGe(-) quartet 4-Pi 0.13 eV above the 2-Delta doublet; with those five orbitals removed, CASPT2(II) puts the quartet 0.03 eV below it. The adiabatic detachment energy moves in step, from 0.96 eV to 0.74 eV, an error of 0.22 eV against the better calculation. The authors conclude 'the double-shell effect of Fe is really important to get the true relative energy order of the nearly degenerate electronic states'. The other three axes are all null, and each null is stated as a conclusion rather than buried. (i) Restricting the space: RASPT2(I) through (IV) 'provide almost the same relative energy order ... as that of the CASPT2(I) method', which licenses RASPT2 for this class of cluster. (ii) Excitation level into RAS3: raising the maximum from two to four to six electrons leaves the relative energies 'almost the same', so 'the single and double excitations of electrons from RAS2 to RAS3 are enough'. (iii) Further orbital addition: RASPT2(IV) adds the Ge 5p shell and changes nothing, so 'the 5p orbitals of Ge are not important enough to include in the active space'. One addition reverses a state ordering; three others do nothing measurable. Note finally that multireference character varies sharply across the series: the FeGe(-) 2-Delta ground state has a leading configuration carrying only 35 percent, which the authors call 'strong multireference character', whereas the cyclic FeGe2(-) states carry 80 to 92 percent.

point_group: Td at the reference geometry, distorting to D2d minima; the surfaces also carry C2v orthorhombic and C3v trigonal saddle points

method: state-averaged CASSCF for the surfaces, with CASPT2 (level shift 0.2 hartree against intruder states) used to check them; spin-orbit coupling by the state-interacting approach with the one-electron spin-orbit operator of the Nb pseudopotential in the CASSCF state basis; multi-configuration time-dependent Hartree for the vibronic spectra and nonadiabatic population dynamics on the fitted surfaces

basis_set: cc-pwCVTZ-PP on Nb for the CASPT2 (cc-pVTZ-PP for the CASSCF) with a 28-electron relativistic pseudopotential, and all-electron aug-cc-pVTZ on F
