active_space_protocol: the space is as small as the problem allows - the single d electron in the five metal 4d orbitals - and everything else is pushed into the correlation treatment: the CASPT2 step correlates the Nb outer-core 4sp electrons together with the F 2sp and Nb 4d, 5s valence electrons. That minimalism is deliberate and is justified afterwards rather than assumed: CASSCF stationary-point energies come within 7.3 +/- 3.2 per cent of CASPT2 and the geometries within 0.002 A and 3 degrees, so dynamic correlation barely reshapes the surfaces and the cheap CASSCF method can be used to generate the thousands of points the fitted five-dimensional surface needs.
electronic_structure_description: Both states are strongly Jahn-Teller distorted from Td to D2d, with stabilization energies of about 2200 cm-1 for E x e and 6400 cm-1 for T2 x e at CASPT2 (1990 and 6734 at CASSCF). The A 2T2 state lies 1.657 eV above X 2E vertically at CASPT2 (1.708 at CASSCF). Barriers between the D2d minima on the lower E x e sheet are only 761 cm-1 (CASSCF) and 1075 cm-1 (CASPT2), so pseudorotation in the ground state is only partly hindered. On the A 2T2 surface the C2v orthorhombic saddle points, arising from T2 x (e + t2 + t2) coupling, sit 1779 cm-1 above the D2d minima at CASPT2, while the C3v trigonal saddle points from t2 modes alone are far higher at 4947 cm-1. The strong e-mode splitting of both surfaces creates a low-lying A/X conical intersection seam; the minimum-energy point has D2d symmetry and sits only 62 cm-1 above the A 2T2 minimum at CASPT2 (S2a = -2.52 bohr). Spin-orbit coupling splits A 2T2 by 363 cm-1 at the reference geometry but changes the E x e stabilization energy by 1 cm-1 and the pseudorotation barrier by -7 cm-1, and shifts stationary-point energies on the A surface by at most 6 per cent, so it is treated as negligible.
Other: The two t2 modes divide the labour in a way that only emerged from comparing them: stretching and bending give nearly equal Jahn-Teller stabilization of the C2v saddle points, but the bending mode dominates the pseudo-Jahn-Teller coupling between the two states, which is what selects it for the reduced-dimensionality dynamics. The e mode acts as the tuning mode that brings the surfaces into degeneracy and the t2 modes as coupling modes, as Td selection rules require. A further methodological finding is that the standard second-order Jahn-Teller model cannot reproduce this topography at all - the polynomial expansion has to be carried to fourth order. Against VF4, treated identically in earlier work, every coupling is much stronger here: 2000 and 6700 cm-1 of Jahn-Teller stabilization at CASSCF against 400 and 3600 in the vanadium compound. The dynamics on the fitted surfaces show ultrafast, complex nonadiabatic decay of the 2T2 population into 2E through the pseudo-Jahn-Teller coupling, with extra spectral bands appearing by intensity borrowing.

compound_name: a tetracoordinate cobalt(II) complex with two 2-amino-1-methylbenzimidazole ligands and two Cl ligands, one of a series of six studied for its zero-field splitting
ligand_set: two 2-amino-1-methylbenzimidazole ligands bound through nitrogen and two Cl ions, giving a distorted four-coordinate CoN2X2 core
point_group: nominally tetrahedral but distorted to a flattened bisphenoid, so the true symmetry is low - D2d, C2v, Cs or C1 depending on the complex
geometry_source: experimental single-crystal X-ray geometries used without optimization
method: state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field with N-electron valence second-order perturbation theory and spin-orbit coupling, from which zero-field splitting parameters and g-tensors are extracted via an effective Hamiltonian
basis_set: DKH-cc-pVTZ on cobalt, nitrogen and the halide, DKH-cc-pVDZ on carbon and hydrogen, with the resolution-of-identity and chain-of-spheres approximations and decontracted auxiliary sets
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian with matching basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: the seven d electrons in the five metal-based 3d orbitals
active_space_protocol: Seven electrons in the five metal d orbitals, with all ten quartet and forty doublet states of the d7 configuration equally weighted in the state average. Averaging over the whole manifold rather than a few roots is what the zero-field splitting requires, since the splitting is built by spin-orbit mixing of the ground quartet with excited states across the configuration, and truncating the set would bias it. The same space and the same state set are used for all six complexes, which is the basis for the magnetostructural comparison the paper is after. Spin-orbit coupling is applied through a mean-field operator and the splitting parameters extracted by constructing an effective Hamiltonian.
nroots_per_mult: all ten quartets and forty doublets of the d7 configuration, equally weighted
electronic_structure_description: The computed g-tensor components are 2.267, 2.296, 2.514. CASSCF/NEVPT2 (SOC, effective Hamiltonian): D = -13.67 cm-1, E/D = 0.06. The spin-Hamiltonian estimate lambda(gz-gx)/2 from those computed g-values gives -21.24 cm-1 (Table 2, D_SH). Measured (fit of susceptibility and magnetization, Table 4): D = -14.44 cm-1, E = 0.431 cm-1. The first excited Kramers doublet lies 3062 cm-1 above the ground one. The distortion from tetrahedral is to a flattened bisphenoid, which lifts the orbital degeneracies, the ground term being labelled according to whichever low symmetry the complex retains.
Other: The point of the series is the sign and size of the splitting across a systematic ligand variation - two nitrogen-donor heterocycles crossed with the three heavier halides. Only one of the six complexes has a positive axial parameter, and the paper's structural recipe for predicting the sign, based on which axis the largest g component lies along, picks out exactly that one. The computed and magnetically fitted parameters agree in sign and order of magnitude throughout but differ by up to about 8 cm-1, the calculation consistently the smaller in magnitude for the chloride and iodide complexes.

geometry_source: stationary structures on the ground state and the three low-lying excited singlets optimized at the CASSCF level; the conical intersection located with state-averaged CASSCF

active_space_protocol: the space is built reaction by reaction rather than by a general rule, and the authors say why: a full valence space is unaffordable, so which orbitals go in is a choice, and they justify each inclusion against a specific process. The O-H bonding and antibonding pair and the carbonyl lone pair are there because a proton has to move; the ring pi and acetyl pi* orbitals because the excited state is a charge transfer between those fragments; the remaining pi orbitals purely to balance the correlation. Carbon dioxide is not released on the excited surface at all - it forms in the ground state after passage through a charge-transfer/ground-state conical intersection. active_space_orbital_description: ten electrons in seven orbitals - the five ring pi orbitals plus two nitrogen lone pairs - with one auxiliary 3s Rydberg orbital restricted to single excitations
electronic_structure_description: Excitation energies at MR-CISD+Q in eV. The first two 3s Rydberg states are degenerate at 6.97 eV, inside the 6.44 to 7.06 eV window predicted by the Rydberg formula, and the next Rydberg state is at 7.46 eV, inside its predicted 7.28 to 7.90 eV window. No experimental absorption spectrum exists for this molecule, so it was included purely as a consistency check before the method was applied to 2H-tetrazole.
Other: This paper argues, and demonstrates across five azoles, that Rydberg states do not require a large active space if the one-particle basis is diffuse enough. The construction is a small valence CAS built from the ring pi orbitals plus the relevant nitrogen lone pairs, augmented by a single AUXILIARY Rydberg orbital into which only single excitations out of the CAS are permitted. The authors state the principle explicitly: as long as the basis is diffuse enough - and they identify d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ as about the minimum doubly augmented basis that will do - one does not need much larger active spaces to get a good partition between valence and Rydberg orbitals, and the payoff is that very little valence-Rydberg mixing appears even at the MCSCF level. That is the opposite trade-off from the more common approach of enlarging the space with a full 3s and 3p Rydberg set, and it is worth knowing that both routes work. The paper also bounds its own error: 0.55 eV, on the second Rydberg state of pyrrole, is the maximum error over all states of all the azoles tested, and that particular error falls below 0.2 eV if the auxiliary space is expanded from 3s alone to 3s plus the three 3p orbitals. Two technical notes transfer. First, the reference space must be a good representation of the final CI expansion, which the authors call a crucial requisite. Second, the averaged quadratic coupled cluster treatment developed intruder-state problems in several excited states - at most two configuration state functions outside the reference space acquiring unreasonably large weight - and the fix was simply to move those individual configurations into the reference space. CI dimensions run from about 67 million configuration state functions for the valence space alone to about 263 million once the auxiliary orbital is added. This molecule carries no experimental data at all and was included solely to check internal consistency, which it does in the only way available: both computed Rydberg energies fall inside the windows predicted by the Rydberg formula for plausible quantum defects. It is also the closest structural analogue of the target molecule, differing from 2H-tetrazole by one ring nitrogen, so its agreement is what licenses the extrapolation.

The neutral reference calculations place six pi electrons in the same six orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Neutral equilibrium geometry/normal modes and trajectory initial conditions use CAS(6,6); the X+/A+ cation surfaces use CAS(5,6). Away from small gaps, the occupied state is optimized state-specifically. Below a 0.05-Eh gap the root weights change in 0.1 increments over five steps to equal-weight (0.5,0.5) SA2-CASSCF and reverse smoothly after leaving the interaction region. The five-mode Hamiltonian was refitted to 106 CAS(5,6)/3-21G* points with a 0.06-eV RMS deviation.

electronic_structure_description: The A+ Franck-Condon point is 9.449 eV (244.896 kcal mol-1) above neutral butatriene. The lowest D2h X+/A+ conical intersection is barrierlessly accessible and lies 2.467 kcal mol-1 below that point; the A+ minimum is 3.756 kcal mol-1 below it. The two symmetry-equivalent D2 X+ minima lie 24.462 kcal mol-1 below Franck-Condon and are separated through a planar transition structure at -24.077 kcal mol-1. A second D2d Jahn-Teller seam at 90-degree torsion lies at -7.220 kcal mol-1 and is absent from the reduced model.
Other: Eighty trajectories sampled the neutral normal modes with half a quantum in every mode and were propagated for 100 fs from A+. Electronic propagation starts below a 0.04-Eh gap; a hop occurs when the occupied-state population falls below 0.65, followed by derivative-coupling momentum correction and a 5-fs no-hop interval. More than half hop within 10 fs; 39 show a single direct hop, 30 a double hop, 5 multiple crossings, and 6 no crossing. Eight later recross through the D2h seam and five through the D2d seam. Direct dynamics and the five-mode wavepacket agree well through roughly 50 fs, but only the coherent quantum calculation shows pronounced approximately 50- and 100-fs recurrences; the trajectory upper-state population instead stabilizes near 15%. electronic_structure_description: For conversion of the Dewar-type isomer to 1,4-disilabenzene, the symmetry-allowed conrotatory ring opening has an activation energy of 34.6 kcal/mol at B3LYP and 47.7 at CASSCF, while the symmetry-forbidden disrotatory opening costs 36.6 and 54.3 respectively. Both methods put the conrotatory barrier 2.0 to 6.6 kcal/mol below the disrotatory one, so the conrotatory pathway is preferred. 1,4-disilabenzene is distorted to D2h, which lifts the orbital degeneracy of benzene: one component of the pi HOMO rises from -6.719 to -5.037 eV (b2g) and the other falls to -7.297 eV (b1g), while the degenerate pi* LUMO splits from -0.072 eV to -0.809 eV (au) and -1.143 eV (b3u). Those splittings account for the high reactivity - the b2g HOMO and b3u LUMO carry large amplitude on the silicon atoms, unlike benzene where one member of each degenerate pair has no amplitude at the 1 and 4 positions, so the frontier orbital interactions with a dienophile are much stronger. The Diels-Alder addition of acetylene has a barrier of only 4.2 kcal/mol at B3LYP.

For the quartets the active orbitals did not come out corresponding to the Fe 4s, 4p and 3d - the pi active space contained a 3d_pi and a 3d_pi correlating orbital, which treats 3d_pi differently from 3d_sigma and 3d_delta and leaves states with 4p_pi character inadequately represented, a problem given that the 3d6 4s1 4p1 occupation is fairly low-lying in the Fe atom. active_space_protocol: A methodological study in which the active space is a controlled VARIABLE rather than a modelling choice: CASSCF(2,2), CASSCF(4,4) and CASSCF(6,6) are each used as the reference for the same set of correlated methods, so the active-space dependence of every method can be read directly down the columns of Tables 2-4. compound_name: CH2CH2O biradical from O(3P) + ethylene — singlet-triplet spin-orbit coupling at crossing geometries
geometry_source: Spin-orbit matrix elements evaluated at selected singlet-triplet crossing point geometries detected in sample trajectories from the direct-dynamics trajectory surface hopping simulation; the underlying potential energy surface was generated on the fly at unrestricted B3LYP/6-31G(d,p). Six different crossing point geometries were sampled.
method: Twelve-state state-averaged CASSCF used to generate orbitals for Breit-Pauli spin-orbit coupling matrix elements; the reaction dynamics themselves use quasiclassical trajectory surface hopping on UB3LYP/6-31G(d,p) surfaces
software: GAMESS, using the Breit-Pauli spin-orbit implementation of Fedorov and Gordon
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF; 6-31G(d,p) for the B3LYP dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight active orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: A single (8,8) space used purely to generate orbitals for the spin-orbit coupling evaluation, with a TWELVE-STATE state average. The state list was chosen from the states actually involved in intersystem crossing: 'the states that are close in energy and thus are actively involved in ISC processes are the first 6 triplet states 1(3A) (Ms = 0, +/-1), 2(3A) (Ms = 0, +/-1), and the first 2 singlet states 1(1A) (Ms = 0), 2(1A) (Ms = 0)'. Because the singlet-triplet matrix elements are complex, the three components of each triplet were combined into symmetry-adapted triplet wave functions following Hoffmann and Schatz, making all elements real.
nroots_per_mult: 12 states in the average: the first 6 triplet states (two 3A states with Ms = 0 and +/-1) and the first 2 singlet states
electronic_structure_description: In the symmetry-adapted triplet representation the singlet-triplet spin-orbit matrix elements are all real and range from 0 to 70 cm-1. Close inspection of the coupling matrix shows the triplet wave functions can be further linearly combined so that the first singlet 1(1A) couples strongly to only three of the six triplets and the second singlet 2(1A) couples to the other three. An average spin-orbit coupling was defined by summing the squares of the twelve singlet-triplet coupling elements and dividing by six, the number of nonzero elements after this decoupling; calculations at six different crossing point geometries give an average SOC of about 35 cm-1. Rather than use that value directly, the dynamics were run with SOC values of 70, 50 and 30 cm-1 to test sensitivity, with 70 cm-1 producing excess singlet formation. For the CH2CH2O biradical the triplet and singlet relative energies are -30.4 and -33.7 kcal/mol on the B3LYP surface but -24.0 and -25.9 kcal/mol at the CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q level of an earlier study, i.e. B3LYP stationary points are lower by up to 8 kcal/mol, an especially prominent discrepancy for the saddle points and reaction intermediates on the triplet surface. The triplet and singlet curves lie very close over a wide range of C-O distances (1.3-1.7 A) in the biradical region, so there are numerous singlet-triplet surface crossings after the biradical forms and the overall ISC probability for a long-lived intermediate can be large even though each individual hop probability is small. Unlike the multireference CASPT2 curves of the earlier work, the barrier to O addition is barely visible on the B3LYP surface.
Other: The active space here is doing an unusual job: it is not used for energetics at all, only to supply orbitals of sufficient quality for a Breit-Pauli spin-orbit calculation, and the design constraint is therefore not correlation recovery but BALANCED description of all the states that participate in the crossing. Hence the twelve-state average over the six triplet components and two singlets rather than a state-specific calculation — with singlet and triplet manifolds nearly degenerate over C-O distances of 1.3 to 1.7 A, a state-specific (8,8) would describe one manifold better than the other and bias the very couplings being measured. The paper also demonstrates why this matters quantitatively: individual matrix elements span the full range 0 to 70 cm-1 depending on which pair of states is taken, and only after the triplets are linearly recombined does the structure become clear (each singlet couples to just three of the six triplets), giving a meaningful average of about 35 cm-1. Quoting any single element would have been arbitrary. The corresponding caution about the surfaces is that the B3LYP energetics used for the dynamics differ from the earlier CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q values by up to 8 kcal/mol in the biradical region and, more seriously, the B3LYP surface loses the O-addition barrier that the multireference CASPT2 curves show — the paper accepts this because 'the relative significance of the primary reaction pathways is largely preserved'.
reference_short: Hu, Lendvay, Maiti & Schatz, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 2093
notes: The main study is a quasiclassical trajectory surface hopping simulation of O(3P) + C2H4 with the potential generated on the fly at UB3LYP/6-31G(d,p); nonadiabatic transitions were only considered where the singlet surface intersects the triplet. The CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q and CASPT2 comparisons are taken from reference 16 of the paper and are not this work's own calculations. Two transition states exist for direct H abstraction, TS1a of 3A'' and TS1b of 3A' symmetry, within 5-6 kcal/mol at B3LYP. A single fixed SOC value was used throughout the trajectories, an approximation justified on the grounds that most T-S crossings occur near the CH2CH2O biradical where the SOC matrix elements vary little with geometry. correlation_correction: None on the CASSCF used for the spin-orbit couplings; the cited CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q energetics are from an earlier study.

compound_name: Phenol blue (PB) — ultrafast photochemical reaction dynamics
geometry_source: S0 minimum optimized at SA2-CASSCF(2,2) and, for comparison, at MP2 and B3LYP. The S1/S0 conical intersection was optimized at SA2-CASSCF(2,2) and characterized by the topography in its branching plane. Minimum energy paths were computed on the S1 surface from the Franck-Condon point and on the S0 surface from the conical intersection minimum. Because no experimental structure of phenol blue exists, an indoaniline-derived calix[4]arene containing the phenol blue skeleton (Cambridge Structural Database refcode TEYGOT), whose X-ray structure is known, was computed at HF, MP2 and B3LYP as a structural benchmark.
method: State-averaged CASSCF over two states, with multistate multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MS-CASPT2) on that reference; trajectory surface hopping nonadiabatic molecular dynamics driven by ab initio CASSCF energies, gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors; TD-DFT(B3LYP) and SAC-CI for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G*, with a 6-31G(d on N/O) variant giving no significant differences in vertical excitation energies or oscillator strengths
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals: the HOMO, which is clearly localized on the aniline ring, and the LUMO, localized on the quinoneimine ring. The HOMO-to-LUMO excitation is therefore an electron transfer from the aniline to the quinoneimine ring.
active_space_protocol: A minimal two-electron, two-orbital space averaged over two states (S0 and S1) with equal weights, denoted SA2-CASSCF(2,2), is used for EVERY calculation in the study — the ground-state minimum, the conical intersection optimization, the minimum energy paths, and the trajectory surface hopping dynamics. The choice is dictated by the dynamics: nonadiabatic trajectories require energies, gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors on the fly, which restricts the affordable space. Its accuracy was checked separately rather than assumed: MP2 and B3LYP were used for the S0 geometry, and MS-CAS(2,2)PT2, TD-DFT(B3LYP) and SAC-CI for the vertical excitation energies and dipole moments. The equal-weight two-state average is what makes the S0 and S1 surfaces balanced enough for the conical intersection and the surface hops.
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies from S0 in vacuum, in eV with oscillator strengths in parentheses, at the 6-31G* level. S1, of pi(HOMO) to pi*(LUMO) character: SA2-CASSCF(2,2) 3.38 (f 0.89); MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 2.15 (0.57); TD-DFT(B3LYP) 2.33 (0.39); SAC-CI(level2) 2.27 (0.34); experimental absorption maximum 2.16 eV in benzene and 2.25 eV in cyclohexane. The bare SA2-CASSCF(2,2) value is more than 1 eV above experiment. TD-DFT and SAC-CI assign S1, S2 and S3 as pi(HOMO) to pi*(LUMO), n(O) to pi*(LUMO) and n(N) to pi*(LUMO) respectively, with transitions to S1 and S3 allowed and that to S2 almost forbidden. Averaged permanent dipole moments: MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 and TD-DFT(B3LYP) values are about 1.0 D LARGER for S0 and 2.0-3.0 D SMALLER for the S1 Franck-Condon state than the SA2-CASSCF(2,2) values, meaning dynamical correlation mixes the quinonoid (Q) character of S0 with the zwitterionic (Z-like) character of S1 and vice versa. The experimental S0 dipole moment in benzene is 5.8 D, about 2 D below the MS-CASPT2 and B3LYP values, with the caveat that B3LYP may overestimate charge-transfer dipole moments through self-interaction error. The ground state has two equivalent mirror-image minima distinguished by the sign of the C5-N8-C9-C10 dihedral. The S1/S0 conical intersection minimum is a branching point, as established by computing minimum energy paths away from it. Trajectory surface hopping from the S1 Franck-Condon point gives nonadiabatic transitions to the ground state mostly at 110-120 fs, reaching the vicinity of the S0 minimum at 200-300 fs, in good agreement with the fast ground-state recovery component seen by pump-probe spectroscopy in solvents. After decay the trajectories show a coherent bending vibration between the quinoneimine and aniline rings at 43 cm-1, matching a low-frequency coherently excited mode observed experimentally.
Other: This paper is an unusually clear case of a minimal active space being wrong about energies and right about dynamics, with the authors quantifying both. The bare SA2-CASSCF(2,2) vertical excitation energy is 3.38 eV against an experimental 2.16-2.25 eV — an error exceeding 1 eV — and MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 on the same two orbitals brings it to 2.15 eV, essentially exact. So the (2,2) contains the right two orbitals; what it lacks is dynamical correlation, and adding it perturbatively suffices. The dipole moments show the physical content of that correction precisely: correlation raises the S0 dipole by about 1 D and lowers the S1 dipole by 2-3 D, i.e. it mixes quinonoid character into the zwitterionic excited state and vice versa, which a two-configuration wave function cannot do on its own. The consequence for reuse is sharp — the excited-state charge separation is OVERESTIMATED at bare CASSCF, and since the trajectory surface hopping dynamics run on uncorrected SA2-CASSCF(2,2) surfaces, the simulated trajectories evolve on a surface whose excited state is too ionic and too high by over 1 eV. That the resulting 110-120 fs hopping times and the 43 cm-1 coherent bending mode nonetheless match experiment suggests the TOPOGRAPHY around the conical intersection is captured even where the energetics are not, which is the usual justification for minimal-space dynamics and here is supported by direct comparison rather than assumed.
reference_short: Kobayashi, Shiga, Murakami & Nakamura, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, 6405
notes: Phenol blue consists of an electron-donor dimethylaniline moiety linked to a quinoneimine acceptor. The Q (quinonoid) and Z (zwitterionic) resonance structures are the two limiting descriptions of its ground state. Cis and trans forms are defined by the C4-C5-N8-C9 dihedral and R/L forms by the C5-N8-C9-C10 dihedral; because C4 and C6 are equivalent in reality, the cis and trans labels are a bookkeeping convenience. No experimental structure of phenol blue itself is available. Pump-probe measurements in solvents report fast and slow decay components, with reported fast time constants of about 200 fs and of 30 fs in two separate studies.

method: CASSCF with MCQDPT second-order perturbative correction (a multireference perturbation approach similar to CASPT2 but using a different zeroth-order Hamiltonian); spin-orbit coupling added afterwards by computing and diagonalizing the matrix representation of the SOC Hamiltonian using the CASSCF wave function, with one-electron terms only

active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals: four Fe 3d orbitals (all but the Fe dz2 orbital, which test calculations with larger active spaces gave an occupation of 1.99 electrons, suggesting it should be moved to the core), the two occupied pi orbitals from each Cp fragment that can interact with the dxz and dyz orbitals of Fe, and the SOMO of the TCNE fragment.
active_space_protocol: Three different active spaces are used for three kinds of radical pair, each sized so that the high- and low-spin states of that pair are properly described and so that the quality is comparable across pairs. That comparability is the design constraint, since the magnetic topology is assembled from J values computed for different pair types. Two of the three choices are justified by explicit tests: the Fe dz2 orbital was excluded from the (8,7) space because test calculations with larger spaces gave it an occupation of 1.99 electrons, so it belongs in the core; and the (2,2) space for the anion-anion pairs was validated against CASSCF(6,6), whose six active orbitals came out at occupations 1.93, 1.93, 1.00, 1.00, 0.07 and 0.07, with both spaces giving the same J of -0.16 cm-1. The largest pairs, cation-cation with about 540 basis functions and no symmetry, could only be run at CASSCF(14,12) with no perturbative correction. All calculations used the crystal geometry of each pair.

Pair 3: CASSCF 0.0, 26.99, 0.17, 27.15; MCQDPT 0.0, 54.52, 0.34, 54.84. Pair 4: CASSCF 0.0, 7.05, -0.02, 7.04; MCQDPT 0.0, 6.46, -0.07, 6.39. Pair 5: CASSCF 0.0, 22.64, 0.0, 22.65; MCQDPT 0.0, 54.47, 0.0, 54.48. Pair 8: CASSCF 0.0, 31.72, -0.02, 31.73; MCQDPT 0.0, 70.05, -0.09, 70.04. Exchange couplings in cm-1 as isotropic JAB(1), JAB(2), then anisotropic JAB-parallel and JAB-perpendicular: pair 1 +45.25, +46.84, +30.6, +1.6; pair 2 +27.93, +23.60, +17.04, +3.78; pair 3 +0.17, +0.16, +0.12, +0.01; pair 4 -0.04, -0.03, -0.03, -0.08; pair 5 0.00, +0.01, 0.00, 0.00; pair 8 -0.05, -0.01, -0.03, -0.02. No single isotropic JAB Hamiltonian fits the whole energy spectrum, so two coupling constants are used, defined as JAB(i) = [ES(i) - ET(i)]/2. Center-to-center distances are 5.209, 5.323, 7.804, 8.278, 8.097 and 7.408 A for pairs 1-5 and 8, with nearest Fe-N distances of 5.582, 5.600, 5.042, 5.311, 5.594 and 5.563 A. The dominant interaction JAB(1) is ferromagnetic with a triplet ground state; the CASSCF(8,7) wave function has three SOMOs with occupations 1.5, 1.5 and 1.0, the two at 1.5 being nonbonding Fe dxy and dx2-y2 orbitals and the one at 1.0 a bonding combination, with all other orbitals close to 2.0 or 0.0. Interchain interaction 3 is also ferromagnetic, coupling the chains into (101) sheets, while interactions 4, 6 and 8 between the sheets are antiferromagnetic. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling does not affect the order of magnitude of the interactions, their relative strength, or their strong anisotropy. All JAB interactions were computed with an expected error smaller than +/- 0.01 cm-1.
Other: The Fe dz2 orbital was removed from the space on the strength of an occupation number: test calculations with larger active spaces gave it 1.99 electrons, so it was demoted to the core, yielding (8,7) rather than a larger space that would have carried a doubly occupied passenger. The resulting wave function has exactly three partly occupied orbitals -- 1.5, 1.5 and 1.0 -- with everything else at 2.0 or 0.0, which is the internal confirmation that the space is neither too small nor padded. The perturbative correction matters enormously for the energies but much less for the couplings: MCQDPT roughly doubles most of the excitation energies relative to CASSCF (pair 1 goes from 17.31, 53.34, 71.07 to 40.15, 90.51, 133.82 cm-1) yet the sign and relative ordering of every JAB survive, which is what the magnetic topology actually depends on. A structural limitation is stated rather than solved: the CASSCF energies alone do not fit a single isotropic Hamiltonian, so two coupling constants per pair are needed, and the spin-orbit correction is applied after the fact using only one-electron terms, on the grounds that including two-electron terms by modifying nuclear charges does not change the exchange couplings. Note the space differs from those used for the other pair types in the same study -- (14,12) for cation-cation and (2,2) for anion-anion -- so cross-pair comparability rests on each space being separately validated rather than on uniformity.

compound_name: Acetamide (CH3CONH2), mechanistic photochemistry and dissociation pathways
point_group: The x-y plane is the molecular symmetry plane in the planar structures; the T1 equilibrium structure is pyramidal
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at the CASSCF level with cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ basis sets; harmonic frequencies examined at each converged point to confirm it as a true minimum or first-order saddle point. Optimization was terminated when the maximum force and its root-mean-square fell below 0.00045 and 0.0003 hartree/bohr. DFT (B3LYP) and MP2 calculations were carried out alongside.
method: CASSCF for the excited-state surfaces and conical intersections, with B3LYP and MP2 for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals. Six of the active orbitals are the C=O pi and pi*, the oxygen nonbonding orbital and the nitrogen 2pz atomic orbital (a six-electron, four-orbital set for the equilibrium geometries of the low-lying valence states), together with the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-C or C-N bond being cleaved. The seventh active orbital is a valence orbital with antibonding character mainly localized on the C-C, C-O and C-N regions, determined by test calculations.
active_space_protocol: The paper states plainly that choosing the active space is a crucial step that cannot be regarded as completely solved and that most applications still involve trial and error, then documents its own trial explicitly. A four-orbital, six-electron set describes the low-lying valence states at equilibrium, but the dissociation involves C-C or C-N cleavage, so the corresponding sigma and sigma* orbitals must be active; (8,7) is adopted as the compromise giving a balanced description of both equilibrium and transition state structures. The seventh orbital was fixed by a lowest-energy criterion: for the T1 equilibrium geometry three different antibonding candidates localized on the N-H, C-H and C-CO-N regions were each tried as the seventh orbital, giving CAS(8,7)/cc-pVDZ energies of -207.92067, -207.92410 and -207.93051 hartree, so the third was chosen. The one-electron densities on those three orbitals, 0.003, 0.01 and 0.04, track the energy ordering, and the authors note that an antibonding orbital giving relatively low energy generally carries relatively large one-electron density. Similar test calculations were performed for the other stationary structures.
electronic_structure_description: No potential barrier above the endothermicity exists on the S0 dissociation pathway. The C-C and C-N dissociations are endothermic by 86.9 and 88.3 kcal/mol, becoming 80.5 and 82.2 kcal/mol with zero-point correction; the C-N bond dissociation energy is close to the 90 kcal/mol enthalpy change measured for C-N dissociation of N,N-dimethylformamide. A transition state TS1(S0) on the H9 transfer pathway has a barrier of 40.5 and 42.5 kcal/mol at the two levels. The barrier on the second step is 70.9, 69.5 and 71.2 kcal/mol relative to the ground-state reactant and 54.6, 54.2 and 54.9 kcal/mol relative to the intermediate, from three levels of calculation. A value of 24.1 kcal/mol is obtained at MP2/cc-pVDZ and B3LYP/cc-pVDZ against an experimental 12.9 kcal/mol from heats of formation at 0 K. The barrier to decarbonylation to CH3NH2 + CO is 107.2 kcal/mol at B3LYP with both basis sets, 8.2 kcal/mol lower than the MP2 value, and 107.5 kcal/mol by another estimate; a related value of 23.8 kcal/mol is quoted for comparison. Perpendicular (D2d) with 1 2A as reference at zero: 1 2B1 at 0.63 eV, 1978 nm, f = 0.066; 1 2E at 2.61 eV, 475 nm, f = 0.002; 2 2E at 3.59 eV, 346 nm, f = 0.002; 2 2B1 at 4.80 eV, 258 nm, f = 0.365. The most prominent absorption of the planar form is in the near infrared, close to the experimental maximum, with no further intense absorptions predicted up to the ultraviolet apart from the weak 524 nm transition that may correspond to the observed hump at 660 nm; the observed 373 nm band probably corresponds to the predicted 395 nm transition, while the intense predicted 243 nm transition may be masked by the large excess of neutral precursor in the matrix. The near infrared transition corresponds largely to promotion of an electron from the b1g singly occupied orbital to the au lowest unoccupied orbital, that is from the positive to the negative combination of the nonbonding allylic orbitals, making it a charge-resonance transition of the kind seen in dimer radical cations. Such transitions usually show no vibrational fine structure, but here a progression of about 400 per cm is discernible. A separate DFT calculation on the 2Au state at the geometry of the 2B1g ground state puts this charge-resonance excitation at 0.45 eV, in excellent accord with the CASPT2 value, dropping to 0.42 eV on twisting by 10.3 degrees. Optimizing the excited state in D2 symmetry collapses it to a perpendicular structure stabilized by spiroconjugation between the two allylic moieties, whose own near infrared charge-resonance transition corresponds to promotion from the spiro-bonding to the spiro-antibonding combination of allyl nonbonding orbitals. The two forms differ in the nature of the singly occupied orbital but have a similar disposition of excited states, and apart from the dihedral angle their geometries are nearly the same, which is why the authors call them electromers, or lumomers. Their Mulliken spin populations at the allylic termini are identical to within 0.005 electrons, so the two forms are not expected to give distinguishable ESR spectra even though the optical spectra separate them.

The authors set out explicitly why they did not attempt the localized-versus-delocalized question computationally at all, and the argument is about what a reference wave function can support. B3LYP is ruled out because it artifactually overstabilizes delocalized structures, through incomplete cancellation of the self-interaction energy of the unpaired electron by current exchange functionals. Hartree-Fock SCF is ruled out because an accurate account of the subtle balance of forces favouring localization or delocalization requires proper treatment of dynamic electron correlation, and because such methods are prone to artifactual symmetry breaking. Adding correlation perturbatively is ruled out too, and this is the part that bears directly on active-space practice: a localized Hartree-Fock wave function is such a poor zero-order approximation to a correlated delocalized wave function, or the reverse, that perturbation theory is bound to fail in such cases. So the group that is otherwise applying CASSCF/CASPT2 throughout the paper declines to use it on the one question where the reference itself would prejudge the answer, and instead restricts CASPT2 to excited-state energies at fixed geometries where that risk does not arise. The reference quality is nevertheless checked and reported: all excited states are described to more than 70 percent by the CASSCF wave function in the CASPT2 calculation, which is the relevant sanity test given that the whole assignment rests on perturbation theory being applicable. Two further practical points. The 11-electron, 12-orbital space is held identical between the planar D2h and perpendicular D2d geometries, so the two electromers are compared on the same footing and the change in the charge-resonance energy from 0.49 to 0.63 eV reflects the geometry rather than the reference. And the excited-state calculations were performed at the exactly planar geometry for reasons of computational economy, whereas the real product is twisted by about 10 degrees with almost no barrier to planarization; the DFT check quantifies what that costs, moving the charge-resonance excitation from 0.45 to 0.42 eV on twisting by 10.3 degrees, so roughly 0.03 eV.

method: CASSCF and CASPT2, with DFT-PBE natural bond orbital and natural population analyses alongside

active_space_protocol: The initial space comprised all fourteen actinide 5f orbitals with their ten electrons. electronic_structure_description: The An 5f orbitals are localized on the metal site with no evident interaction with any coordinating oxygen atoms of the phosphonate ligands, and the An 6p orbital admitted by expanding the space likewise shows no interaction with the coordinating ligands. Natural population analysis gives Pu 5f5.38 and Pu 6d0.79, and Mulliken gives Pu 5f5.04 and Pu 6d0.54. Atomic populations from the total density at DFT-PBE give, by Loewdin, Pu 6s 4.185, 6p 12.440, 5d 11.467 and 5f 5.895; by natural population analysis 4.165, 11.994, 10.844 and 5.423; by Mulliken 4.267, 12.301, 10.906 and 5.404. point_group: D3h at the planar reference geometry, with no symmetry imposed in the calculations
geometry_source: no optimization; energies computed along one-, two- and three-dimensional radial cuts in symmetry-adapted internal coordinates, about 6000 points up to 7 eV above the planar reference, and fitted to a diabatic three-by-three potential matrix
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by multireference configuration interaction, used to generate the data that a diabatic Jahn-Teller and pseudo-Jahn-Teller Hamiltonian is fitted to; the fitted surface then carries nuclear wave-packet propagation by the multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree method. The first vertical ionization energy comes separately from restricted coupled cluster with perturbative triples.
active_space_orbital_description: a full valence space of seven orbitals - the phosphorus 3s and 3p orbitals and the three hydrogen 1s orbitals - holding the seven valence electrons of the cation; the five core orbitals on phosphorus are frozen and doubly occupied in the correlated step
active_space_protocol: full valence, so the same space applies unchanged at every one of six thousand nuclear configurations, which is what the fit requires - the surface is only as smooth as the orbitals behind it. The three lowest states are averaged together, which is not an option here but a necessity: two of them are the components of a degenerate pair at the planar geometry and the third crosses them, so no state-specific treatment could follow all three through the intersections. No symmetry was imposed anywhere.
electronic_structure_description: Three doublet sheets, the ground X 2A''(2) state and the two components of the first excited degenerate state. The ground state has two equivalent pyramidal minima separated along the umbrella coordinate by a barrier of only 0.099 eV, lower than earlier calculations had found. Two symmetry-allowed three-state conical intersections sit near plus and minus 0.9 radian in that coordinate, and when displacements in all three bending modes are allowed they are joined by a hyperline of two-state intersections. Reproducing the data required expanding the Jahn-Teller and pseudo-Jahn-Teller coupling to eighth order in the bending modes - 208 coefficients in all. The simulated first photoelectron band is a single extended progression reflecting how far the umbrella angle moves on ionization, and the second band is nearly structureless, matching experiment, its diffuseness caused by the exceptionally strong coupling. Dynamically, the Jahn-Teller motion within the excited state finishes in about 5 fs, roughly 80 percent of the excited-state population reaches the ground state within about 10 fs, and after 20 fs the wave packets are so delocalized that no further population transfer occurs out to 100 fs.
Other: The active space is doing something a static calculation never asks of one: it has to remain the same object across six thousand geometries spanning three intersecting sheets, two of them degenerate at the reference point, because the entire result is a fitted analytic surface and any discontinuity in the orbitals would appear as a spurious feature in the dynamics. Averaging the three states together is what makes that possible. The payoff is that an eighth-order coupling expansion - unusually high, and needed because of how anharmonic the surface is around the intersections - can be fitted to data that is internally consistent, and the resulting 10 fs decay and structureless second photoelectron band both follow from the coupling rather than being put in by hand.
reference_short: Bhattacharyya, Dai and Domcke, J. Chem. Phys. 143, 194301 (2015)
notes: The symmetry-adapted expansion of the coupling Hamiltonian is what makes the six-dimensional surface affordable, by removing thousands of redundant nuclear configurations from the set that has to be computed. The 208 fit coefficients were determined by Marquardt-Levenberg optimization carried out in three stages following the hierarchical form of the expansion. The kinetic energy operator uses Wilson G-matrix elements frozen at their values at the planar reference geometry.

ligand_set: para dimethylamino donor and nitrile acceptor on a benzene ring
point_group: C1 for unconstrained optimizations; a previously proposed C2-constrained partially twisted ICT structure was specifically tested and rejected as a likely constraint artefact
geometry_source: Ground, LE, PICT, RICT, TICT(Q) and TICT(AQ) geometries are the CASSCF geometries of ref. 4 (energies recomputed here at MS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ); the LE/S0 and CT/S0 conical intersections and the transition state were optimized here at CASSCF/6-31G* without symmetry constraints. The ground state is untwisted with a 43.0 degree amino wag, the LE structure is near-planar, and TICT is amino-twisted/pyramidal. The six-page ESI gives selected bond lengths and rendered structures but no complete Cartesian or full internal-coordinate block, so no XYZ is fabricated.
method: MS-CASPT2(12,11)/cc-pVDZ single-point energies recomputed at the CASSCF critical-point geometries of ref. 4; new CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G* optimization of the LE/S0 and CT/S0 conical intersections and the transition state on the radiationless-decay path, with MS-CASPT2 energies; pTICT minimum search; CASSI transition moments from perturbed-modified CAS-CI wavefunctions
basis_set: 6-31G* for CASSCF geometry optimizations and MS-CASPT2 energy paths; cc-pVDZ for MS-CASPT2 single-point energies at CASSCF critical geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Six benzene pi/pi* orbitals, the dimethylamino nitrogen lone pair, and four cyano-group pi/pi* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The common CAS(12,11) was used for ground, LE, ICT(Q), ICT(AQ), and ICT(CN) surfaces, minima, crossings, and paths. At TICT(Q), PM-CAS-CI mixes the ICT(Q) and LE CASSCF functions with nearly equal weights; a reported CAS(14,13) test adding the ring-amino sigma/sigma* pair decoupled those states without materially changing the energy, supporting retention of CAS(12,11). An exhaustive pTICT search varied active-space size/composition, basis, and geometric constraints but found no unconstrained minimum.

electronic_structure_description: At the Franck-Condon geometry, MS-CASPT2 vertical energies relative to S0 are 93.3 kcal mol^-1 for LE (dipole 6.01 D, f=0.006) and 102.7 for bright ICT(Q) (13.80 D, f=0.608), versus experimental nonpolar-band maxima 92.2 and 101.9. active_space_protocol: A single eight-electron seven-orbital space maintained across the whole path, with its orbital composition changing so that it always contains the orbitals and electrons that change along the pathway; state-averaged orbitals throughout because the reactions pass between open- and closed-shell singlet states. Where no compatible space existed, the vinylnitrene space was carried over to keep energies comparable, and where a genuinely incompatible space was required, the common reference species was recomputed in both spaces.

electronic_structure_description: A closed-shell planar molecule of A-prime symmetry, the reference point for all relative energies. Its pyrolysis begins by breaking the ring nitrogen-oxygen bond to give a carbonylvinylnitrene. Because the lowest singlet of that nitrene is of A-double-prime symmetry, having one electron in a sigma and one in a pi orbital, the reaction cannot proceed adiabatically in planar symmetry and a conical intersection must be circumvented by out-of-plane distortion. The transition state for this step is accordingly slightly nonplanar with a wave function mixing closed- and open-shell configurations, and the barrier is just under 50 kcal/mol.
Other: This is one of the clearest published treatments of active space consistency along a reaction path, and the selection criterion is stated as a principle: in studies of chemical reactions it is very important to choose a space containing all the orbitals and electrons that change along the considered pathways, both to avoid discontinuities in the potential surfaces and to make energies comparable. Eight electrons in seven orbitals proved sufficient -- provided it contained the right orbitals, which is where the interest lies, because the composition of that fixed-size space changes identity three times along the path. In the heterocyclic reactant it is the five pi and pi* orbitals holding the six pi electrons plus the sigma and sigma* of the ring N-O bond. In the vinylnitrenes those N-O orbitals are replaced by the singly occupied in-plane p orbital on nitrogen and the in-plane p lone pair on oxygen. In the azirine one of the pi/pi* pairs turns into the sigma and sigma* of the newly formed C-N bond. Same seven slots throughout, three different sets of orbitals, chosen so that what enters and leaves the space is exactly what the chemistry changes. Because the reactions pass between open- and closed-shell singlet states, state-averaged orbitals were used throughout; a space optimized for either state alone would not permit a smooth passage. No compatible space could be found for four of the primary products, so the vinylnitrene space was used for their transition states instead, justified by those transition states being very early since the reactions are exothermic by 55 to 70 kcal/mol, and adopted explicitly because a consistent space was needed for comparability. The cost is stated: that space does not contain the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the reactive X-H bonds being broken, because those could not be included in the vinylnitrenes. Separately, the transition states leading out of the azirine to the nitrile ylide and to another product required the sigma and sigma* of the ring C-C bond rather than of the C-N bond, a genuinely incompatible space, and the authors' response was to recompute the azirine geometry and energy in that second space as well so that all the relative energies remain comparable. Recomputing a common reference in each of two incompatible spaces is the correct fix and is almost never done. The multiconfigurational treatment also overturns two single-reference results. A transition state found at the density functional level for a direct concerted rearrangement, with a stable wave function, could not be located at all with the active space -- attempts either failed or collapsed onto the open-shell transition state leading elsewhere -- from which the authors conclude that the lower-lying concerted path is an artifact of constraining the system to the closed-shell surface. At another transition state the closed-shell reference is outright unstable, and the multiconfigurational wave function confirms significant open-shell character. Conversely the space corrects a prior multiconfigurational result too: on an earlier four-electron four-orbital surface the parent vinylnitrene was reported as a transition state for azirine interconversion, whereas with the larger consistent space three of the four planar structures are shallow minima. A symmetry argument constrains everything: the closed-shell species are of A-prime symmetry while the lowest singlet nitrene has one electron in a sigma and one in a pi orbital and is therefore A-double-prime, so the reaction cannot proceed adiabatically in planar symmetry and a conical intersection must be circumvented by out-of-plane distortion. The computed transition state is indeed slightly nonplanar with a wave function mixing closed- and open-shell configurations, while the transition state for the lowest hydrogen shift is almost planar and solidly closed shell, meaning the surface crossing has already happened before it is reached. One caution for anyone reusing the numbers: the authors note that relative energies of closed-shell and open-shell transition states are affected to surprisingly different extents by the Davidson correction for quadruple excitations, defer the analysis of why to a separate paper, and state that their chemical conclusions do not depend on which set is used.

electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a 3A'' triplet, essentially a single configuration with weight 0.925. The lowest excited state is a 1A' singlet at 10841 reciprocal centimetres, strongly two-configurational with weights 0.686 and 0.242 for configurations differing by a double excitation between the 14a' and 7a'' orbitals. All three of these singlets have oscillator strengths below 1e-10. Higher triplet and singlet states at 27710 and 28110 reciprocal centimetres carry oscillator strengths of 0.004 and 0.002 and show a much longer N-C bond, 1.643 and 1.652 Angstrom against 1.438 in the ground state. The 14a' and 7a'' orbitals are described as almost degenerate in the two 1A' states. Vertical absorption maxima are computed at 336 and 340 nanometres and emission at 383 and 392 nanometres. C-N hyperconjugation shortens the N-C bond, and increased s character along that axis strengthens the bonding interaction.
Other: This paper is an unusually clear case of a space whose NECESSITY varies from state to state within the same molecule, and the configuration weights make the point quantitatively. The triplet ground state is essentially a single configuration, weight 0.925 to 0.934, so a single-determinant method would describe it adequately. The low-lying closed-shell singlets are not: for the tert-butyl species the lowest 1A' state splits 0.686 against 0.242 between two configurations that differ by a double excitation between the two frontier orbitals, and the second 1A' state splits 0.388 against 0.515 -- meaning the configuration listed as leading is not the one with the largest weight. Two configurations of comparable weight, with the ordering flipping between two states of the same symmetry, is exactly the situation that no single-reference method can represent, and the authors trace it to a physical cause: the two frontier orbitals are described as almost degenerate in these states. So the space is doing real work for half the states studied and almost none for the other half, and a reader comparing this study to a single-reference one should expect agreement on the triplet and disagreement on the singlets. The space itself is chosen by an explicitly stated trade-off between cost and precision, with a chemical rationale for what is left out -- the methyl groups are described as stable, so their orbitals stay inactive -- giving eight electrons in eighteen orbitals for the tert-butyl nitrene, itemized as eleven orbitals of one symmetry and seven of the other, and eight electrons in fifteen orbitals, nine and six, for the isopropyl nitrene. geometry_source: Optimized by density functional theory in TURBOMOLE V7.0, with the triplet-singlet stability of the reference wave function tested and, where unstable, the spin and spatial symmetry constraints released for a broken-symmetry reoptimization of the singlet
method: CASSCF used to determine multiconfigurational character and to test whether single-reference wave functions suffice, on density functional geometries; nonresonance Raman spectra computed for both spin states
software: Gaussian 09 for the CASSCF calculations; TURBOMOLE V7.0 for the density functional work
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, described by the authors as a modest space, held fixed across the whole size series.
active_space_protocol: The space is deliberately kept constant across clusters spanning one to forty-two fused rings so that the leading configuration coefficient is comparable along the series; it therefore samples a shrinking fraction of the valence manifold as the clusters grow, and the authors present the result as detection of multiconfigurational character rather than its quantification.
electronic_structure_description: A rectangular cluster with 1 units along the zigzag edge and 1 along the armchair edge, comprising 1 fused rings. The squared coefficient of the leading configuration is 0.78 for the singlet and 0.56 for the triplet, and the triplet lies 33.019 kcal/mol from the singlet, so the singlet lies lower.
Other: Space fixed at ten electrons in ten orbitals, which the authors call modest, and held constant across clusters from one fused ring to forty-two, so the squared leading configuration coefficient is a like-for-like measure across the series. For the singlet it falls from 0.78 in the smallest cluster to 0.33-0.40 in the larger ones; for the triplet it stays between 0.49 and 0.77. Relative energies collapse from 33 kcal per mole in favour of the singlet at one ring to within a few hundredths of a kcal per mole, changing sign to favour the triplet past roughly a dozen rings. The space does not grow with the pi system it samples, so it covers a shrinking fraction of the valence manifold as the series extends, and the authors present the coefficient as detection rather than quantification. Workflow: density-functional geometries were tested for triplet-singlet instability of the reference wave function first, and where instabilities appeared the spin and spatial symmetry constraints were released and the geometry reoptimized with a broken-symmetry treatment before the multiconfigurational step. Reported spin contamination grows about 1.2 times faster along one edge direction than the other, more in the singlet than the triplet.
reference_short: Pablo-Pedro, Lopez-Rios, Fomine & Dresselhaus, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2017, 8, 615
notes: One of a series of rectangular hydrogen-passivated silicene nanoclusters indexed by the number of units along the zigzag and armchair edges. electronic_structure_description: The parent nucleobase cation. Its four lowest cationic states arise from removing an electron from the highest pi orbital, the two oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs, and the next pi orbital down, giving the 2pi+HOMO ground state and 2nO+, 2piHOMO-1+ and 2nN+ excited states. Vertical ionisation potentials come out at 7.62, 8.63, 8.67 and 9.08 eV from CASSCF and 8.82, 9.68, 9.77 and 10.14 from XMS-CASPT2, with the averaged CASPT2 values of 8.74, 9.44, 9.59 and 9.94 carrying standard deviations of 0.16 to 0.28 eV from the choice of zeroth-order Hamiltonian alone; the ground-state vertical and adiabatic values fall within the measured range. Geometrically the ground cationic state shows only a 0.03 angstrom C5-C6 elongation from the neutral, while the first excited state distorts strongly around the carbonyl where its hole localizes - C2-O lengthening by 0.09 angstrom with N1-C2 and C2-N3 shortening by 0.07 and 0.08. Three crossings were located: the D3/D2 and D2/D1 intersections sit essentially at the Franck-Condon geometry, distorted by only 0.02 angstrom, reflecting an effective THREE-STATE near-degeneracy right at the point of ionisation; the D1/D0 intersection is far more distorted, mirroring the excited-state minimum. The decisive result is that the path from the first excited minimum to that lowest crossing is BARRIERLESS at XMS-CASPT2 but carries 'a sizeable energy barrier at CASSCF' - the correction converts a trapped excited state into an ultrafast one. Decay is therefore predicted to be prompt, and the ground state surface then funnels the population to the cationic ground-state minimum rather than toward fragmentation, which is the paper's explanation for the photostability of the ionised base.
Other: The headline finding is that dynamic correlation changes the mechanism, not merely the numbers, and the paper is built around demonstrating it. For the parent cation the decay from the first excited doublet minimum to the conical intersection with the ground state is BARRIERLESS at XMS-CASPT2 while 'presenting a sizeable energy barrier at CASSCF'; for the methylated derivative the corrected barrier is 0.03 electronvolts against 0.22 at CASSCF. In both cases the uncorrected surface would predict a trapped, long-lived excited state and the corrected one predicts ultrafast depopulation. Bare CASSCF is not a neutral reference here: for barrier heights on decay pathways it errs systematically toward too much barrier. A protocol the authors tried and threw away, with the failure mode named: 'additional computations on top of the CASSCF geometry optimisations employing the SS-CASPT2//CASSCF protocol were carried out but were discarded as the system presented strong differential correlation effects leading to the appearance of artificial crossings along the decay pathways, thus discouraging its use.' That is the single-state perturbative energy on multiconfigurational geometries, and here it manufactures conical intersections that do not exist: where differential correlation between states is strong, single-state corrections on a common geometry can produce spurious crossings. Four zeroth-order Hamiltonians are benchmarked and the spread is reported as a standard deviation. On identical geometries and an identical space, the four lowest vertical ionisation potentials come out at 7.62, 8.63, 8.67 and 9.08 electronvolts from CASSCF; 8.54, 9.06, 9.31 and 9.66 from single-state CASPT2; 8.61, 9.26, 9.44 and 9.79 from the multistate variant; and 8.82, 9.68, 9.77 and 10.14 from the extended multistate one. The authors average over the formulations and quote standard deviations of 0.16 to 0.28 electronvolts. The extended multistate values sit systematically 0.3 to 0.5 electronvolts above the single-state ones - a shift comparable to the differences between the electronic states being assigned. An empirical parameter is used outside the regime it was calibrated for, and the authors say so plainly. Both IPEA values of 0.0 and 0.25 atomic units were tested, and the paper notes that 'the IPEA shift described above was calibrated for the single-state formulation of CASPT2, 0.25 a.u. therefore being possibly a non-optimal value for correcting MS-/XMS-CASPT2 energies. We made use of this value due to its wide use in the literature ... and to roughly estimate its effect in its multistate formulations.' A shift parameter fitted for one variant of a method carries no guarantee for another variant of it, and the multistate formulations are noted to reach the experimental range already at zero shift, so applying the standard value may double-count. An imaginary level shift of 0.2 atomic units was used throughout to suppress intruder states. The space is specified in the exemplary form - requirement first, orbital list second - and is held fixed across charge states. It comprises 'the full pi valence occupied and virtual space PLUS the two occupied n lone pair orbitals to INCLUDE the 2n+ states', giving fourteen electrons in ten orbitals for the neutral and thirteen in the same ten for the cation. So the pi system enters by a rule that scales with the molecule, and the two lone pairs enter for a NAMED PURPOSE - to make two specific cationic states representable at all. Since the ionisation potentials are differences between neutral and cation, holding the orbital set fixed and changing only the occupancy is what makes those differences meaningful; this is the same discipline recorded for redox series elsewhere here. Five doublet states were state-averaged. The correction matters for energies but not for geometries, and the split is demonstrated rather than assumed. Comparing CASSCF against XMS-CASPT2 optimized structures, the excited-state minimum differs by bond shortenings of only 0.02 to 0.03 angstrom and the two sets are 'shown to be qualitatively [similar], validat[ing] the use of CASSCF as a potential cost-effective alternative' for structures. The authors are careful to note this does not generalize, citing prior work 'where XMS-CASPT2 geometries were shown to deviate more prominently from CASSCF estimates, particularly at conical intersections' - which is precisely where this study needs them. So the licence granted to CASSCF here is for geometries only, on this system, and the paper says as much. How much dynamic correlation matters varies between two nearly identical molecules treated with the same space: the authors 'conclude that dynamic electron correlation in 5-methyl-cytosine [plays a lesser role] compared to cytosine', the correction removing a barrier entirely in one case and reducing it from 0.22 to 0.03 electronvolts in the other. A single methyl group changes not the answer but the size of the correction needed to get it - which means a protocol validated on one member of a family is not automatically licensed for its close analogue. Finally, note what the multireference work does not supply: the connection to photostability is an argument from surface topography - 'the shape of the ground state potential energy surface strongly directs the decaying excited state population towards the cationic ground state minimum' - rather than from dynamics, since no trajectories were run. The 'ultrafast' timescale is inferred from barrierless topology and proximity of crossings to the Franck-Condon region, not computed. Basis ANO-L at valence double-zeta polarised quality; resolution of identity by Cholesky decomposition used for energies, analytical gradients and non-adiabatic couplings, with second nuclear derivatives taken numerically.

notes: One of two DNA nucleobase cations whose radiationless excited-state decay is mapped, motivated by the role of photoionisation in genetic damage - a process the authors note has been 'scarcely studied' relative to neutral nucleobase photophysics. formula: C2H4O, the adduct of triplet atomic oxygen with ethylene
point_group: C1 along the reaction paths; individual stationary points such as oxirane carry higher symmetry and their states are labelled accordingly, for instance the 1B1 transition
geometry_source: All geometry optimizations performed at the CASSCF level, with the reason for not going further stated precisely: 'CASPT2 optimizations using a CAS(12,12) active space was not possible with our computational resources', because although CASPT2 single points cost about the same as CASSCF ones, the energy gradients and derivative couplings do not. Reaction paths are followed by intrinsic reaction coordinate analysis where a transition state can be located.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with multi-state CASPT2 on top, applied across the whole reaction surface rather than at selected points, with CCSD(T) single points as an independent check. The parameters are disclosed and some are justified: a standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au, and a level shift of 0.3 au that was 'carefully chosen in order to avoid intruder states'. The Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian and Cholesky decomposition at a 1e-6 threshold are used throughout. Separate MS2-CASPT2 calculations are run for each multiplicity. Biradical character is quantified from the natural orbital occupation number of the LUMO-like orbital, which is itself identified by inspecting the CASSCF configurations to find the orbital each excitation targets.
software: OpenMolcas for all CASSCF and CASPT2 work; ORCA 4.1.2 for the CCSD(T) single points
basis_set: ANO-L-VTZ all-electron on oxygen and carbon with ANO-L-VDZ on hydrogen for the multireference work, chosen after testing: 'some tests with a larger basis set did not show any notable change in the energies', so the smaller combination was kept as 'a good compromise between accuracy and computational cost'. The CCSD(T) comparison uses aug-cc-pVTZ on all atoms.
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian applied in all CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; CASSCF wave functions also serve as the basis for a spin-orbit Hamiltonian, since the reaction proceeds by intersystem crossing
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, itemized in the text and chosen 'in view of the reactive scattering process, which mainly involves the O and C atoms, with C-C and C-O bond breaking and bond formation': the sigma/sigma-star and pi/pi-star pairs for the carbon-carbon bond, the 2s and all three 2p orbitals of oxygen, the pi orbital for the C-H bond, and the pair of virtual 3p(x) and 3s orbitals. The two Rydberg-like virtuals were added for a stated double purpose, 'to stabilize the active space and to recover some dynamic correlation'; 3p(x) proves 'essential to capture the C-H bond breaking' on three of the five channels, and 3p(z) is the acceptor orbital of the experimentally validated first singlet excitation.
active_space_protocol: A rule stated in terms of the jobs the space must do, and then checked at every point: the orbitals are chosen from the bonds that break and form in the scattering process, and 'the active space has been carefully checked after every single-point calculation to ensure the stability and reliability of the CASSCF wave function'. The design goal is consistency along the whole surface rather than accuracy at any one point, and the trade-off is spelled out: the authors 'opt toward identifying a stable and smoothly varying active space that is able to capture the majority of the reaction channels - about 70 percent - rather than adapting the active space to the various reaction channels, which would prevent from a straightforward application in on-the-fly dynamics'. State averaging over two states per multiplicity is justified twice, both because 'this number of states stabilizes the active space' and because only the lowest two singlets and triplets are energetically accessible in this collision.
multiplicities_studied: Singlet and triplet, two states of each - S0, S1, T1 and T2 are analysed at every stationary point, with separate state-averaged CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 runs per multiplicity
nroots_per_mult: Two roots per multiplicity, denoted SA2-CASSCF(12,12) and MS2-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: A scattering reaction of atmospheric and interstellar relevance that proceeds on both singlet and triplet surfaces via intersystem crossing. The paper characterizes minima, transition structures and a conical intersection on the lowest singlet and triplet surfaces, analysing S0, S1, T1 and T2 at every geometry, and quantifies the biradical character of each from the occupation number of the LUMO-like natural orbital on a scale where 100 percent denotes a pure biradical. For oxirane, MS-CASPT2 places the first singlet excited state at 7.18 eV against a measured 7.24 eV, an error of 0.06 eV. The character of that state is contested: the multireference assigns it as a 1B1 transition from the oxygen 2p(x) lone pair into the virtual 3p(z) orbital, and this 'is in disagreement with the earlier TD-DFT calculations, using different functionals, at the same geometry, which predict a contribution from an s-like virtual orbital'. Along the reaction paths the active orbitals acquire 'atom-like' character at the later transition structures, reflecting the partial dissociation of the system.
Other: Consistency of the reference along the reaction paths is the stated design objective: the authors set out to identify 'an active space that changes smoothly along several reaction paths', and the space is 'carefully checked after every single-point calculation'. It fails on one channel while the energy profile still looks well behaved. Of the five reaction pathways the space handles four, but 'the same active space, however, rotates along pathway (5), and while the energy profiles look smooth, we cannot conclude on the reliability of this active space to describe correctly pathway (5)'. The authors decline to report it: 'therefore, we will not describe in detail this low-probability reaction pathway'. Rather than switch spaces per channel they keep one space covering about seventy percent of the reactive flux, because 'adapting the active space to the various reaction channels would prevent from a straightforward application in on-the-fly dynamics'. The space is also validated externally, with the licence limited in the same sentence: CCSD(T) single points on the CASSCF geometries lead the authors to conclude that 'the CASSCF/CASPT2 computational procedure and the chosen active space are accurate enough to describe the electronic structure of the system in the relevant regions visited along the reaction'.
reference_short: Talotta, Morisset, Rougeau, Lauvergnat & Agostini, J. Phys. Chem. A 2021, 125, 6075
notes: A dedicated electronic-structure study, five authors with two corresponding, explicitly framed as preparatory work for on-the-fly nonadiabatic dynamics rather than as an end in itself - 'the results presented in this work shall be intended as a preliminary study for dynamics on-the-fly simulations'. That framing accounts for the premium on a single smoothly varying space, the willingness to sacrifice one reaction channel, and the note that the chosen orbitals 'could also serve as the starting point' for larger spaces later. No trajectories are run here; the product is a validated protocol and a characterization of the stationary points and their multiconfigurational character. The one experimental comparison available, the oxirane first singlet excitation, is met to 0.06 eV. Earlier surface-hopping simulations by others on fitted surfaces with a spatially constant spin-orbit coupling, and crossed-molecular-beam branching ratios, are cited as context and are other groups' work, so they carry no rows. Only one chemical system is treated, so this is a single-row entry; its several stationary points and four electronic states belong to that one reaction surface. Spans oxirane, acetaldehyde, the transition structures connecting them and a singlet-triplet crossing, on the lowest two singlet and two triplet surfaces. Multi-state CASPT2 was run with a standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au and a level shift of 0.3 au chosen specifically against intruder states, separately for each multiplicity on the lowest two states. No bare-CASSCF versus CASPT2 comparison is tabulated in the passages examined, so the size of the correction is not directly readable; instead the corrected result is validated against an independent single-reference method, CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ single points on the CASSCF-optimized geometries computed in a different code 'to give further support to the MS-CASPT2 results'. Two of the twelve active orbitals, the 3p(x) and 3s virtuals, were included partly 'to recover some dynamic correlation' at the CASSCF level, with the perturbative correction then applied on top.
