geometry_source: Ground-state geometry optimised at B3LYP/6-31G(d) in GAUSSIAN 09 and used for the vertical excitation energies; 1000 single-point geometries sampled from it to simulate the absorption band; both S1/S0 conical intersection minima optimised at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* and re-confirmed at MRCIS(8,8)/6-31G*; linear interpolations in internal coordinates run between the Franck-Condon point and each intersection. Trajectory geometries are generated on the fly, so most structures in the study are dynamical rather than stationary.
method: two-state state-averaged CASSCF(8,8) with Tully fewest-switches trajectory surface hopping; MRCIS(8,8) single points for validation; B3LYP and TD-B3LYP
basis_set: 6-31G* for all CASSCF and MRCIS work; 6-31G(d) for the B3LYP optimisation; 6-31+G* used only in the basis-set comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Eight orbitals shown explicitly in Fig. 1: the sigma and sigma* orbitals of both C-N bonds, the pi and pi* orbitals localised on the N=N bond, two non-bonding orbitals n1 and n2 built mainly from the two nitrogen lone pairs, and the two lowest Rydberg orbitals R1 and R2. The set is chosen to contain every bond that can dissociate after excitation to S1.
active_space_protocol: Unusually explicit for a dynamics paper. Five active spaces - (8,8), (8,9), (10,10) and (10,8) - were compared at both CASSCF and MRCIS with 6-31G* against the experimental S1 excitation energy of 3.71 eV: CASSCF gives 4.292 (8,8), 4.476 (8,9), 4.290 (10,10) and 4.406 eV (10,8), and MRCIS 4.168, 4.381, 4.168 and 4.286 eV, so enlarging the space does not move the excitation energy toward experiment and (8,8) is kept. The basis was tested the same way: 6-31+G* gives no improvement over 6-31G*, and product energies for the dissociation channels differ by at most 8.0 kcal/mol between the two, so 6-31G* is used. The number of averaged states was also justified rather than assumed: two-state averaging with equal weights is adopted because S2 lies about 51 kcal/mol above S1 in the Franck-Condon region, and a four-state average (S0-S3) along a representative trajectory confirms that S2 and S3 never approach S1 over the whole propagation. The CASSCF surfaces are then validated against MRCIS(8,8) single points both at the critical points of the mechanism (largest discrepancy 9.7 kcal/mol, at the trimethylene biradical) and along a complete trajectory. The one weakness the authors acknowledge is that CASSCF overestimates the excitation energy, which blue-shifts the simulated absorption maximum.
nroots_per_mult: singlet: 2 states (S0 and S1) averaged with equal weights for the trajectory propagation; a 4-state average over S0-S3 was run only as a check on that choice
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state. The S0 -> S1 excitation is n -> pi* on the N=N group, computed at 4.292 eV with oscillator strength 0.0107 by CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* and 4.168 eV with f = 0.004211 by MRCIS(8,8)/6-31G*, against the experimental 3.71 eV (334 nm); a two-root calculation puts S2 at 6.626 eV (CASSCF) or 6.740 eV (MRCIS) with f below 0.0005, i.e. about 51 kcal/mol above S1. TD-B3LYP/6-31G* places the same transition, mainly HOMO -> LUMO, at 3.95 eV. Two distinct S1/S0 conical intersection minima are located. In CI-I the intact C-N=N group lies out of the three-carbon plane, with C3-C4-C5-N1 at 62.0 degrees, N2-C3 stretched to 3.67 angstrom and N1-N2 at 1.185 angstrom; in CI-II the same group is coplanar with the carbon skeleton, C3-C4-C5-N1 at 177.0 degrees, N2-C3 at 4.807 angstrom and N1-N2 at 1.206 angstrom. The CI-I seam is much more steeply sloped than CI-II, and the interpolated S1 path from the Franck-Condon point is barrierless to CI-I but carries a barrier to CI-II, which the authors could not refine into a transition state.
Other: Dynamics: 363 trajectories propagated from S1 at 334 nm with a 2000 fs maximum propagation time and a 0.1 fs integration step, reduced to 0.05 fs where energy conservation demanded it; hopping decided by comparing the computed transition probability against a random number at each step. Four-fifths of the trajectories break one C-N bond promptly in S1 and then hop; the remaining fifth break it more slowly before hopping. Hopping times span 60-450 fs with a few out to 720 fs, and 78% of trajectories decay through CI-I against 22% through CI-II, matching the barrierless-versus-barriered interpolated paths. Hopping geometries separate cleanly: C3-C4-C5-N1 between -100 and 100 degrees with C3-N2 under 4 angstrom funnel to CI-I, while dihedrals near +/-180 degrees with C3-N2 beyond 4 angstrom correlate with CI-II. After the hop a second C-N bond breaks on S0 to give trimethylene biradical plus N2. Continuing the trajectories on S0 gives three secondary channels: cyclopropane + N2 at about 77.8% (barrierless ring closure), propene + N2 at about 12.5% through a [1,2]-hydrogen shift with a barrier of 17.8 kcal/mol at CASSCF(8,8) but only 4.8 kcal/mol at MRCIS(8,8), and CH2 + C2H4 + N2 at about 9.7%, endoergic by 30 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 27.6 kcal/mol at MRCIS relative to the biradical. The simulated absorption band spans 220-340 nm with its maximum at 290 nm, against an experimental band of 280-340 nm peaking near 318 nm.
reference_short: P. Mahata, A. K. Rauta, B. Maiti, J. Chem. Phys. 157, 194302 (2022)
notes: The sequential mechanism found here - one C-N bond breaking on S1, nonradiative decay through a conical intersection, then the second C-N bond breaking on S0 - reproduces the earlier experimental inference, and the three secondary product channels match those reported from 333 nm photolysis. The new structural result is CI-I: only the planar CI-II had been reported for the three-membered analogue diazirine, so the non-planar funnel appears to be specific to the five-membered ring. Two internal inconsistencies are worth noting for anyone reusing the numbers. The propene barrier is quoted as 17.8 kcal/mol in the mechanism discussion but as 17.0 kcal/mol, attributed to a different reference, in the branching discussion; and the branching ratios are given as 77.8 / 12.5 / 9.7 percent in one paragraph and as about 78 / 12 / 10 percent in the next, where the three latter figures sum to 100 only by rounding. Table I also lists two different (8,8) entries, 4.292 and 4.372 eV for the same transition, without explaining what distinguishes them beyond the second row carrying an S2 root, so the (8,8) excitation energy is effectively state-averaging dependent at the 0.08 eV level.

active_space_protocol: CAS(n,5) with n the number of 3d electrons in the five 3d orbitals - the paper's own prescription, 'an active space of CAS(n,m) is considered where n number of 3d electrons are considered in m number of 3d orbitals, i.e., 5 to account for the ligand field excitation energies' - applied unchanged across the whole Sc to Cu series in both oxidation states, with dynamic correlation added afterwards by NEVPT2. What varies between members is the state averaging, specified per d configuration in the paper's Table 1 so that high-lying excited states influence the spin-Hamiltonian parameters, and recorded per row in nroots_per_mult
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: the high-spin 3d8 configuration, which the paper finds lowest in energy for every member of the series. D = 26.562 cm-1 at CASSCF and 56.030 cm-1 at NEVPT2, with E/D of 0.001 and 0.000 respectively. The effective spin-orbit coupling constant zeta is 740.4 cm-1. CASSCF g values (g_x, g_y, g_z): 2.333, 2.333, 2.622 (g_iso 2.429); NEVPT2: 2.070, 2.070, 2.072 (g_iso 2.071). Positive D, so easy-plane anisotropy, with the g tensor becoming almost exactly isotropic under the correction. Because the AILFT ligand-field splitting is large for this complex, the geometry was also optimised in the low-spin S = 0 state, but the high-spin S = 1 state is more stable by 11 kcal/mol - consistent with the NEVPT2 transition energies, which give a triplet ground state with a first excitation energy of 25 kcal/mol. The D_zz axis superimposes on the C3 axis and is perpendicular to the plane of the metal and the three nitrogen donors. The AIM analysis shows non-covalent interactions between the methyl hydrogens to be prevalent, and EDA-NOCV shows the amide ligand bonding to the metal through both sigma and pi interactions with a substantial dispersion contribution.
Other: The one member whose spin state the authors felt obliged to check, and the check is the useful part: because the AILFT d-orbital splitting is largest here, a low-spin singlet was a real possibility, and both the DFT optimisation (high spin favoured by 11 kcal/mol) and the NEVPT2 spectrum (triplet ground state, first excitation 25 kcal/mol) were used to rule it out. That is the right order of operations when a CAS(n,5) ligand-field space is to be applied under the blanket assumption of high spin that this paper makes for the whole series. The NEVPT2 correction more than doubles D here (26.562 to 56.030 cm-1) while flattening the g tensor to isotropy, which is the same pattern of large unpredictable shifts seen for the d2 and d3 members.

electronic_structure_description: Ground state: triplet, 99.996% in the leading 2222222211 configuration. Its two unpaired natural orbitals mix Cu3 dx2-y2 and Cu2 dz2 character (72% combined contribution). The first singlet is an equal multireference mixture of [20] and [02] occupations in the top e-double-prime pair. The singlet lies 5.8 cm-1 above the triplet at CASSCF and 3.8 cm-1 after NEVPT2, versus the experimental ferromagnetic J = +4.50 cm-1 under H = -J S1·S2. The effective-Hamiltonian g values are (2.099179, 2.228293, 2.275021), giso = 2.200831.
Other: NEVPT2 reduces the singlet-triplet gap from 5.8 to 3.8 cm-1, improving agreement with the experimental 4.50 cm-1 despite the authors' warning that CAS(18,10) omits external excitations and normally underestimates exchange. State averaging produces two pairs of near-degenerate orbitals and a lower group of six nearly degenerate orbitals. The multireference first singlet exposes the failure of broken-symmetry DFT: B3LYP predicts J = 56.86 cm-1 and tested functionals span roughly 39.9-114.92 cm-1, while the CASSCF/NEVPT2 gap remains near experiment.

reference_short: Conical Intersection Induced Valley-Ridge Inflection Drives Chemiluminescence in the SO 2 Afterglow Reaction (2026)
notes: A barrierless T1 pathway reaches a valley-ridge inflection created by the T1/T2 conical-intersection seam and branches toward 3B1 and 3A2 SO2 minima; the resulting vibronic manifold rationalizes broad UV-to-visible chemiluminescence. Forty-nine trajectories propagated for 100 fs show frequent T1/T2 exchange and hops in both reactant and CI-induced-VRI regions, establishing dynamical accessibility without claiming quantitative branching ratios or lifetimes. Rigid scans varied the incoming S-O distance from 3.0 to 1.2 A and the angle from 60 to 160 degrees; the grid was interpolated to 150 by 120 points. Row-specific method, active-space, and result fields were checked without inventing missing values. Source-text MD5 b03220d0028e6baede2be6906749ba61. The paper's methodological point: an ordinary microcanonical (uniform-weight) SA-CASSCF cannot self-consistently resolve all six CSF energies/couplings for this 'more diabatic than adiabatic' problem (the solution does not persist beyond 3 states), whereas the proposed canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF puts weight self-consistently on the full 6-dimensional CAS-CI Hilbert space, enabling the complete diabatic decomposition - a strategy for including more adiabatic states in the ensemble without convergence collapse.

The two bridge states are quasi-degenerate and weakly coupled; the bonding channel has the larger energy dispersion. Both contribute to S2/S3 (not S1 by symmetry, nor S4); the ionic bridge state 202 contributes significantly to the ground state. Michler's hydrol blue is an important reference cyanine and an amyloid-sensitive fluorogenic stain.

point_group: C-infinity-v; orbitals classified in the C2v subgroup
geometry_source: No fixed geometry: potential energy curves are scanned from 0.08 to 1.10 nm with a 0.02 nm step, reduced to 0.002 nm near each equilibrium separation, for every Lambda-S and every Omega state. Curves are fitted by cubic splines, the rovibrational Schroedinger equation is solved by Numerov's method, and spectroscopic parameters come from fitting the first ten vibrational levels where available.
method: state-averaged CASSCF; internally contracted MRCI with Davidson modification (icMRCI+Q); Breit-Pauli spin-orbit state interaction
basis_set: aug-cc-pV6Z for the reference curves, with two-point aug-cc-pV5Z / aug-cc-pV6Z extrapolation to the complete basis set limit (exponents 3.4 for Hartree-Fock and 2.4 for the correlation energy, the result denoted 56); aug-cc-pV5Z-DK against aug-cc-pV5Z for the scalar relativistic correction; aug-cc-pCV5Z for the core-valence correlation correction; all-electron cc-pCV5Z for the spin-orbit calculations
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic correction from the third-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian (DKH3), taken as the difference between aug-cc-pV5Z-DK with DKH3 and aug-cc-pV5Z without it at icMRCI level; spin-orbit coupling from the state-interaction method with the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian at icMRCI level with the all-electron cc-pCV5Z basis, the bra and ket states assigned by MOLPRO with no manual adjustment. Both corrections are applied across the whole curve of every state, and the final Omega-state curves are icMRCI+Q/56+CV+DK+SO.
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence space: the 8 outermost MOs 3sigma, 1pi, 4sigma, 5sigma, 2pi, 6sigma (4a1 + 2b1 + 2b2 in C2v), in that computed energy order, holding the three 2s2p valence electrons of boron and the four 2s2p valence electrons of carbon, i.e. 7 electrons in 8 orbitals (the article writes this as CAS(8,7), orbitals first). The remaining 4 inner electrons occupy the 2 closed-shell MOs 1sigma and 2sigma (2a1), and 244 external orbitals (86a1, 60b1, 60b2, 38a2) complete the basis, so 10 MOs (6a1, 2b1, 2b2) carry the correlated wavefunction. The 1s pairs of boron and carbon are frozen in the frozen-core calculations and released as the core electrons for the core-valence correction.
active_space_protocol: The space is fixed by the full-valence criterion, not by selection, and the same CAS(8,7) serves as the state-averaged CASSCF orbital space and as the icMRCI reference space for all 21 Lambda-S states across the whole internuclear range. The authors state explicitly that no additional MOs were added to the active space, and justify the choice only by the smoothness and convergence of the resulting curves; the same 10 correlated MOs are used for the core-valence and scalar relativistic corrections. Convergence is instead demonstrated in the correlation treatment: Table 4 tracks Te, Re, omega_e and De of a 2Pi and A 4Pi at icMRCI and icMRCI+Q through aug-cc-pVTZ, aug-cc-pVQZ, aug-cc-pV5Z, aug-cc-pV6Z and the CBS limit, and Table 3 separates the DK and CV shifts for a 2Pi, b 2Sigma-, A 4Pi and B 4Sigma- (CV dominates, changing Te by 111-316 cm-1 and Re by about 0.0005 nm, while DK changes Te by at most 45 cm-1 and Re by 0.00003 nm). No calculation with a different active space is reported, so the adequacy of the full valence space is assumed rather than tested.

notes: Agreement with the sparse gas-phase measurements is close where they exist: X 4Sigma- Re 0.14913 vs 0.14912 nm and Be 1.31959 vs 1.32041 cm-1, omega_e 1170.44 vs 1170.18 cm-1, De 4.4623 eV vs the mass-spectrometric 4.5966 +/- 0.3035 eV; a 2Pi omega_e 1396.32 vs 1394.5 cm-1 (neon matrix); A 4Pi Te 8627.55 vs 8604.5 cm-1 (neon matrix); B 4Sigma- Te, Re and omega_e within 6.59 cm-1, 0.00004 nm and 0.26 cm-1 of the gas-phase values. The one state singled out as discrepant is d 2Sigma+, whose Te departs strongly from the matrix measurement when the a 2Pi Te is fixed at the value computed here, and the authors offer no explanation; the computed omega_e for that state does match. The omega_e values of 3 2Pi (2636.37 cm-1 with omega_e x_e 279.2) and 5 2Pi (2233.11 cm-1 with omega_e x_e 420.8) are far outside the range of the other states and sit on wells distorted by the avoided crossings, so these two harmonic constants should be read as fitting artefacts of strongly anharmonic double-well curves rather than as physical vibrational frequencies - a caveat the article does not state. The methodology section mistakenly refers to the 1s core pair of a nitrogen atom where carbon is meant.

compound_name: NV- , the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy point defect in diamond, modelled by the C19NVH28 cluster
ligand_set: a nitrogen atom adjacent to a lattice vacancy, the three vacancy-related carbon atoms carrying the non-bonding electrons, with the cluster boundary terminated by 28 hydrogens
point_group: C3v in the ground state; the excited-state relaxation lowers it
geometry_source: ground-state geometry from B3LYP with the B1 basis (6-31+G* on the first shell around the vacancy, 6-31G* on the second, 6-31G elsewhere), optimized with the boundary atoms frozen at positions taken from optimized defect-free clusters; excited-state geometries optimized at CASSCF with the B2 basis. Ground-state frequencies computed at the same B3LYP level in Gaussian
method: CASSCF geometry optimization of the lowest excited states, with CASPT2 used in the authors' earlier work for the vertical transition energies. Vibrations activated by the electronic transition are identified by projecting the calculated excited-state atomic displacements onto the ground-state normal-mode vectors. The barrier for nitrogen migration through the vacancy is evaluated separately at TD-B3LYP
software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF; Gaussian for the B3LYP geometries and frequencies
basis_set: B2, which is the B1 set (6-31+G* on the atoms of the first shell around the vacancy, 6-31G* on the second shell, 6-31G on the rest) augmented by diffuse s functions with the 6-31+G exponent on the second-shell atoms
active_space_orbital_description: Two spaces, (8,11) and (4,11), eight or four electrons in eleven active molecular orbitals. The (8,11) space covers orbitals with occupation numbers from 1.98 down to 0.002. The (4,11) space covers only the occupied MOs built from the broken bonds of the vacancy-related carbon atoms, together with empty MOs down to occupation 0.0001.
active_space_protocol: the active window is positioned on the occupation-number spectrum rather than by orbital count: shifting it down by several MOs pulls the N-C and C-C bonds around the vacancy into the space in non-equivalent amounts and does not improve the result, so both spaces are anchored on the vacancy-related non-bonding orbitals. Both were established as the most suitable for this excited state in the authors' earlier study
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 3A2 and the first triplet excited state 3E. The transition involves only the non-bonding electrons of the vacancy-related carbon atoms; the electrons in the C-C and N-C bonds do not participate, which is why excitation cannot be expected to lower the nitrogen-migration barrier appreciably. The zero-phonon line is observed at 1.945 eV with a photoluminescence progression spaced by about 0.07 eV; the computed activated frequencies come out around 600 cm-1. The ground-state barrier for N migration through the vacancy is about 5 eV and no significant reduction of it is found on excitation, which argues against the nitrogen-tunnelling explanation of the doublet splitting in the absorption band.
Other: The two spaces are a deliberate pair rather than a refinement of one another - (8,11) reaches down to orbitals with occupation 1.98, (4,11) keeps only the broken-bond orbitals of the vacancy carbons and their empty partners - and the selection criterion is stated in terms of occupation numbers and of which bonds would enter the space if the window moved. That the same eleven orbitals serve with either four or eight electrons is the practical point: the states of interest live entirely in the dangling-bond manifold, so the additional four electrons buy correlation rather than new physics. Only the C19NVH28 cluster could be used for the excited states at all, on computer-time grounds, so the size of the model rather than the space is the binding constraint here.

notes: metal_center, metal_ox_state and d_electron_count empty: the defect has no metal. The cluster is written NC19H28 in the abstract and C19NVH28 in the computational section, V denoting the vacancy rather than an atom, so the formula here records the 19 carbons, the nitrogen and the 28 terminating hydrogens. compound_name: NV0, the neutral nitrogen-vacancy point defect in diamond, modelled by the C19NVH28 cluster
ligand_set: a nitrogen atom adjacent to a lattice vacancy; here the nitrogen lone pair as well as the vacancy-related carbon non-bonding electrons take part in the lowest transitions
point_group: C3v nominally; the optimized first excited state distorts away from it, one vacancy-related carbon shifting away from the vacancy
geometry_source: B3LYP/B1 ground-state geometry with frozen boundary atoms; the 3 2A'' state geometry optimized at CASSCF(9,6) with the B1 basis
method: CASSCF geometry optimization of the excited state, with CASPT2 needed to get the state ordering right. The first excited state is defined here as the first state above the two 1 2A' and 1 2A'' components of 1 2E, and reproducing its excitation energy and wave function requires selecting from the initial CASSCF the state involving electron transfer from the two highest doubly occupied orbitals HOMO-1 and HOMO into the SOMO
basis_set: B1: 6-31+G* on the vacancy-related atoms only, 6-31G* on the second shell, 6-31G on the rest - a deliberately moderate amount of diffuse character
active_space_orbital_description: nine electrons in six orbitals, a limited space built so that the state corresponding to the HOMO-1/HOMO to SOMO transition is actually present among the CASSCF roots
active_space_protocol: chosen against a failure mode rather than for completeness. A larger basis with more diffuse functions produces a dense set of states involving transitions to diffuse orbitals, which crowds out the state of interest; the space is limited to (9,6) and the diffuse functions restricted to the vacancy-related atoms specifically to keep the required state available in the CASSCF calculation
electronic_structure_description: Accounting for dynamic correlation lowers the relative energy of the 1A2 state substantially, and for the neutral defect this changes the order of the electronic states between CASSCF and CASPT2. The resulting CASPT2 wave function for the first excited 1 2A2 state is genuinely multireference, its largest coefficient of about 0.7 corresponding to the 3 2A'' state of the CASSCF wave function - which is why the geometry relaxation was evaluated by optimizing 3 2A'' at CASSCF(9,6). The relaxed geometry breaks C3v symmetry, one vacancy-related carbon moving away from the vacancy, and since the two components of 1 2E should be roughly equally populated the mean geometry in that state is expected to look C3v.
Other: A blunt illustration of the active space and the basis being chosen to keep a particular state visible rather than to converge an energy. The physically wanted state - HOMO-1/HOMO to SOMO - is not among the low CASSCF roots when diffuse functions let Rydberg-like states intrude, so the authors restrict both the space and the diffuse set until it reappears, then take the CASSCF root that carries the largest weight in the CASPT2 wave function as the one to optimize. It also shows CASSCF and CASPT2 disagreeing about state ordering for this defect, so the CASSCF ordering alone would have led to the wrong state being followed.
reference_short: Zyubin, Mebel, Chang and Lin, Chem. Phys. Lett. 462, 251-255 (2008)
notes: The (9,6) space and the B1 basis here differ from the (8,11)/(4,11) spaces and the B2 basis used for NV- in the same paper, which is why the two defects are separate rows. Activated vibrational frequencies across both defects are evaluated at about 600 cm-1. metal_center, metal_ox_state and d_electron_count empty: no metal.

active_space_protocol: A fine two-dimensional grid varied the pyridyne-H and methanol C-H distances while all other coordinates relaxed without symmetry; no state averaging, root count, or orbital threshold was reported.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet hydrogen-abstraction surface. The CASMP2/6-31G** barrier is 13.80 kcal mol-1 at the grid saddle near r(pyridyne-H) = 1.45 Angstrom and r(methanol C-H) = 1.275 Angstrom; the main text reports approximately 1.45/1.28 Angstrom.
Other: Reactant-reference grid point (pyridyne-H = 10, methanol C-H = 1.1 Angstrom): CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G** E = -360.462672 Eh and CASMP2 E = -361.571051 Eh. At 1.45/1.275 Angstrom the energies are -360.431070 and -361.549064 Eh (relative 19.83 and 13.80 kcal mol-1). The CASMP2 barrier is 4.3 kcal mol-1 above the analogous p-benzyne/methanol value. Approach at the carbon end nearer N was slightly higher and not pursued. The ionic protonated surface was rejected in vacuo because ion-dipole attraction dominated; no SCRF calculation was performed.
reference_short: Hoffner et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 120, 376-385 (1998)
notes: Comprehensively mined from all 10 main-article pages and both official SI files (50 PDF pages, comprising 48 source SI pages plus two ACS terms pages); the complete two-page numerical grid was visually inspected. compound_name: the CH + NO reaction on the singlet surface: HCNO, HNCO, HOCN and related C,H,N,O isomers and transition states
point_group: Cs for the planar species and C1 for several transition states
geometry_source: computational: CASSCF(12,11) optimizations in both basis sets, starting from B3LYP/cc-pVDZ structures. Bond lengths from the two basis sets differ by less than 0.04 A and angles by less than 4 degrees, the only exception being the N-O bond of one transition state, so basis-set effects on the geometry are small.
method: CASSCF relocation of every stationary point starting from B3LYP/cc-pVDZ geometries, with vibrational frequencies computed for all of them; then internally contracted multireference configuration interaction including all single and double excitations relative to a reduced reference, with a Davidson correction. Only the singlet surface was considered. Both approach modes were followed - the oxygen end of NO attacking the CH carbon, and the nitrogen end attacking it.
software: MOLPRO and DALTON for the multireference calculations; Gaussian 98 for the B3LYP starting geometries
basis_set: cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF work; cc-pVDZ for the multireference CI
active_space_orbital_description: twelve electrons in eleven orbitals, defined by exclusion: everything except the 1s orbitals of carbon, nitrogen and oxygen and the 2s orbitals of nitrogen and oxygen. For the multireference CI the reference had to be reduced to ten electrons in ten orbitals, because CI on the twelve-electron reference was not feasible.
active_space_protocol: (12,11) full valence minus the C, N and O 1s orbitals and the N and O 2s orbitals, used for all geometry optimizations and frequencies; (10,10) as the reduced reference for the internally contracted multireference CI, chosen for feasibility rather than on physical grounds
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol from separated CH(2Pi) plus NO(2Pi), given as CASSCF(12,11)/cc-pVDZ, CASSCF(12,11)/aug-cc-pVTZ, MRCI/cc-pVDZ and MRCI with the Davidson correction. Intermediates: A -4.75, -6.67, -10.83, -11.26; B -17.90, -21.19, -24.13, -26.93; C -93.23, -95.61, -98.88, -99.15; D -155.69, -159.28, -156.95, -158.69; E -177.38, -182.37, -180.39, -181.20; F -95.36, -99.44, -98.10, -100.89; G -71.97, -75.37, -77.33, -78.20; H -110.74, -115.83, -111.27, -112.38. Asymptotes: H + c-NOC -1.43, 0.70, 2.20, 2.26; N(4S) + HCO 11.39, 9.62, 13.88, 15.27; H + CNO -13.55, -14.43, -11.71, -13.05; O(1D) + HNC -18.11, -20.16, -19.05, -10.96; O(1D) + HCN -36.67, -35.64, -35.58, -26.68. The two entrance transition states TS1 and TS2 sit at 9.10 and 8.77 kcal/mol above the reactants at CASSCF but go NEGATIVE at the correlated level, -2.51 and -1.79 and, with the Davidson correction, -5.70 and -5.18, so the barriers that CASSCF predicts vanish once dynamic correlation is added. The formation of intermediates A and B from the reactants is therefore essentially barrierless, as is the further conversion to C. The main products are H + NCO and NH + CO when the oxygen end of NO attacks the carbon; when the nitrogen end attacks, the reaction is expected to stop at fulminic acid.
Other: Two active-space observations here, and one of them is the paper's most consequential result. First, the space is defined by EXCLUSION rather than by construction: everything is active except the three 1s core orbitals and the nitrogen and oxygen 2s orbitals, giving twelve electrons in eleven orbitals. That is a clean recipe for a small reactive system and it makes the space transferable across every stationary point of a complicated multi-channel surface without re-selection. Second, and inevitably, the CI could not be run on that reference: the authors state flatly that multireference CI with the twelve-electron reference is not feasible and reduce it to ten electrons in ten orbitals for that step. So the geometries come from one space and the energies from a smaller one, and the reduction was made for cost rather than physics. The consequence is visible in the entrance channel and it changes the chemistry: at CASSCF(12,11) the two transition states leading to the first intermediates lie about 9 kcal/mol ABOVE the reactants, whereas at the correlated level they lie 2 to 6 kcal/mol BELOW them. A CASSCF-only reading of this surface would predict an activation barrier for a reaction that is in fact barrierless. Anyone using CASSCF stationary-point energies for radical-radical addition should expect exactly this sign of error. A reassuring result on the other axis: enlarging the basis from cc-pVDZ to aug-cc-pVTZ at fixed active space changes the geometries by under 0.04 A and 4 degrees.
notes: This is a metal-free system, so metal_center, metal_ox_state, d_electron_count and ligand_set are left empty. The formula CHNO is that of the reacting complex and of all its isomers; the individual intermediates are labelled A through H in the paper and are not all identified by chemical name in the extracted text, so the row covers the surface as a whole. Only singlet surfaces were computed, although the reactants CH and NO are both doublets and one product asymptote involves quartet nitrogen. Relative energies are electronic energies without zero-point correction.

compound_name: ammonia NH3 dissociation to NH + H2
point_group: Planar C2v and Cs cuts; D3h/C3v correlations analyzed
geometry_source: More than 400 state-averaged CASSCF geometries sample planar NH + H2 dissociation cuts. In C2v, one NH bond is fixed at 2.0 bohr while H-H and NH-to-H2-center-of-mass distances vary; Cs cuts use the NH/H2-center angle and separation. No complete Cartesian coordinates are reported.
method: State-averaged CASSCF potential-energy surfaces and conical-intersection/dissociation-path analysis
basis_set: basis set A (65 contracted Gaussian functions)
active_space_orbital_description: All eight NH3 valence electrons distributed without restriction among 10 orbitals: 8 a-prime + 2 a-double-prime in Cs, or 5 a1 + 2 b1 + 3 b2 in C2v.
active_space_protocol: State-specific symmetry blocks were averaged: in C2v, the three lowest singlet states were optimized together and the two lowest triplets were averaged; for singlet Cs cuts, two 1A-double-prime roots and three 1A-prime roots were optimized together. The paper maps only planar cuts because a full six-dimensional excited-state mapping was considered impractical.
nroots_per_mult: C2v: three singlets and two triplets state averaged; Cs singlets: two 1A-double-prime and three 1A-prime roots averaged within their symmetry treatments
electronic_structure_description: The mapped states are X 1A1-prime, A 1A2-double-prime, and a 3A2-double-prime ammonia, with higher B 1E-double-prime and b 3E-double-prime states entering conical-intersection correlations. On the constrained planar C2v ground-state NH+H2 path, a 68,500 cm^-1 barrier occurs at r(NH)=2.0, NH-to-H2 center=2.9, and r(HH)=1.6 bohr relative to equilibrium NH3; the A singlet and a triplet cuts have no analogous barrier. The A state primarily dissociates to NH2(X 2B1)+H, whereas the a triplet preferentially reaches NH(X 3Sigma-)+H2(X 1Sigma-g+).
Other: The X/A/B singlet surfaces and a/b triplet surfaces form common conical intersections under symmetry reduction, providing vibronic-coupling channels. Product correlations depend strongly on whether C2v, Cs with a bisecting plane, or coplanar Cs symmetry is enforced; lowering symmetry can remove avoided-crossing barriers. point_group: D2d (minimum), C2v(planar), C2v(bent) and D2h — four symmetry-distinct critical points on the same surface
geometry_source: CASSCF gradient optimization of each structure with the (14,10) space; CASPT2 single points at those CASSCF-optimized geometries. DFT (LSD/DZVP, and LANL2DZ ECP) optimizations performed for comparison with B3LYP, BLYP and BP86.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single points (Andersson et al. multireference perturbation approach)
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis of Bauschlicher et al. for nickel and Dunning cc-pVDZ for carbon and hydrogen: primitives (Ni 20s15p10d6f), (C 7s6p4d2f), (H 4s1p) contracted to [Ni 7s6p4d2f], [C 3s2p1d], [H 2s1p)
active_space_orbital_description: (14,10) for the CASSCF geometry optimizations: the pi and pi* orbitals of the two ethylene moieties plus the 4s and 3d orbitals of the nickel atom — all the orbitals required to describe the forming Ni-C bonds and the low-lying states of the metal atom. The space is ENLARGED for the CASPT2 single points by adding a correlating 4d orbital for each doubly occupied 3d orbital not taking part in the bonding, following Pierloot, Persson and Roos: this gives 14 electrons in 12 orbitals for the D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) structures and 14 electrons in 13 orbitals for the D2h structure.
active_space_protocol: Two-stage: a (14,10) space carries the geometry optimizations, then the space is extended with 3d-correlating 4d orbitals for the single-point CASPT2 energies. The number of added 4d orbitals is structure-dependent, because it is set by how many 3d orbitals remain doubly occupied and non-bonding in each symmetry — hence (14,12) for three structures and (14,13) for D2h. The adequacy criterion is stated numerically: with this extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol".
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet d10 nickel(0) complex. Four critical points, with relative energies in kcal/mol at CASSCF and (in the CASPT2 column E(2)) at CASPT2: D2d 0.00 / 0.00, C2v(planar) 6.89 / 5.07, C2v(bent) 18.05 / 17.31, D2h 36.56 / 18.96. Absolute energies of the D2d structure are -1663.01454 (CASSCF) and -1664.27375 (CASPT2) hartree. D2d is the only genuine minimum (all real frequencies); C2v(planar) is a saddle point of index 1 connecting two equivalent D2d structures, C2v(bent) has index 2 and D2h index 3. Geometrical parameters are barely affected by structure: Ni-C distances 2.021 A (D2d) lengthening to 2.121 A (D2h), C=C 1.399 A (D2d) shortening to 1.373 A (D2h), and the ethylene pyramidalization angle epsilon 18.8 deg in D2d, 18.5/20.2 deg in C2v(planar), 18.7 deg in C2v(bent), falling to 11.6 deg in the planar D2h form.
Other: A textbook double-shell case with a structure-dependent twist. The (14,10) space that suffices for geometries does not suffice for energies: for every 3d orbital that stays doubly occupied and out of the bonding, a correlating 4d orbital must be added for the CASPT2 step (the Pierloot-Persson-Roos prescription), and because the count of such orbitals depends on symmetry the extended space is (14,12) for D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) but (14,13) for D2h. The payoff is quantified — with the extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol" — and the effect on the answer is highly non-uniform: adding dynamic correlation barely moves the D2d-C2v(planar) and D2d-C2v(bent) gaps (6.89 -> 5.07 and 18.05 -> 17.31 kcal/mol) but nearly HALVES the D2d-D2h gap, from 36.56 to 18.96 kcal/mol. So a (14,10) CASSCF number for the planar D2h form is wrong by 17.6 kcal/mol, while the same space is good to ~2 kcal/mol for the other two — the structure needing the extra 4d orbital is exactly the one whose energy is most wrong without it. The DFT comparison lands closer to CASPT2 than to CASSCF for the D2d-C2v(planar) gap (5.03-5.64 kcal/mol across B3LYP, BLYP and BP86 against 5.07 at CASPT2) but spreads widely for the D2h gap (12.84 kcal/mol at B3LYP/DZVP, 14.53 at BLYP, 15.94 at BP86).

basis_set: 6-31G* for both the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: (8,8): the four sigma and pi bonding orbitals involved in the rearrangement together with their four antibonding counterparts.
active_space_protocol: A single (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals is used for every stationary point on the surface, so reactant, both transition structures, the diradical intermediate and the product are directly comparable. The paper notes explicitly that structures 10, 11 and the diradical intermediate 12 were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was verified rather than assumed at each optimization. Dynamic correlation enters as (8,8)CASPT2 single points at all stationary points, and reported enthalpy differences are zero-point corrected using the CASSCF numerical frequencies.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reactant of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement, optimized as an energy minimum at (8,8)CASSCF/6-31G* with the correct active space orbitals. It rearranges to triene 11 through either of two transition structures — 13 and 15 — which differ by 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy and both lead to the common diradical intermediate 12. Passing through the lower-energy structure 13, the terminal methylene group rotates in only one direction, whereas through 15 it appears free to rotate either way; this asymmetry is consistent with the 90% stereoselectivity observed in the thermal rearrangements of the dimethyl derivatives. A separate structure lies 32.7 kcal/mol above 10 with a large associated H term.
Other: A uniform (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals across every stationary point, which is what allows a two-transition-state mechanism to be established at all — the two structures 13 and 15 differ by only 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy, a margin that would be meaningless if the two had been computed in differently composed spaces. The paper also records that the reactant, product and diradical intermediate were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was checked at each optimization rather than assumed to persist — the failure mode being that an (8,8) optimization can converge onto a different set of eight orbitals at a distant geometry and silently break the comparison. The mechanistic conclusion depends on dynamic correlation being added on top: an earlier study at CASSCF level alone gave a different picture for the parent system, and it was "the inclusion of dynamic electron correlation at the (8,8)CASPT2/6-31G* level" that located allylic-stabilized structures and changed the pathway. The result here — two separate transition structures both leading to a common diradical intermediate — differs substantially from the parent 1,2,6-heptatriene rearrangement, which has a single transition structure that either proceeds to the diradical or bypasses it entirely. That contrast between a conformationally restricted system and its flexible parent, computed with the same space and the same correction, is the paper's central point.

geometry_source: State-specific (14,12)CASSCF optimization of the S0 geometry, then phenyl torsional potentials in S0 and S1 scanned under C2 and/or Ci symmetry constraints, with C2h-constrained optimizations for comparison
method: State-specific CASSCF for geometry optimization and global potential energy surface scanning, with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP2) corrections including all valence and virtual orbitals; preliminary CI up to triple excitations used to select the active space
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta augmented by polarization functions: alpha_d = 0.75 for C, 0.55 for P, 0.80 for N
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12): the highest five occupied pi orbitals, the lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals, and the two nonbonding orbitals on the P atoms (for t-DPP) or N atoms (for t-AZB). The symmetric combination of the lone pairs is denoted n+; the antisymmetric combination n- is described as much less important.
active_space_protocol: The full space is defined first and then explicitly rejected on cost grounds. DPP has seven pi-type occupied orbitals with their corresponding pi* partners plus two phosphorus nonbonding orbitals, so allowing all excitations from the nine occupied into the lowest seven unoccupied orbitals would be an (18,16) CASSCF — 'quite unrealistic to scan the global potential energy surfaces', and the paper states plainly that 'reduction of active space is important'. The reduction is guided by a SEPARATE preliminary calculation rather than by inspection: configuration interaction including up to triple excitations from the closed-shell Hartree-Fock configuration was run first, and on that basis the highest five occupied pi, the lowest five pi*, and the two phosphorus nonbonding orbitals were judged 'enough to describe our present interest of S0 and S1 states at any geometries which possibly contribute to the photochemistry' — the qualifier AT ANY GEOMETRIES being the important one for a global surface scan. That gives (14,12), used for all surface scanning, with S0 geometries optimized by a STATE-SPECIFIC (14,12) CASSCF. MRMP2 corrections including all valence and virtual orbitals are applied to each electronic state where needed. The identical space and protocol are applied to t-AZB so the two molecules are directly comparable.
electronic_structure_description: At the S0 geometry: S0 at 0.0 eV with a dipole moment of 0.025 D and a leading closed-shell configuration of coefficient 0.897; S1 at 3.544 eV CASSCF (2.759 eV with MRMP2), dipole 0.088 D, leading n+ to pi* configuration of coefficient 0.901. The experimental n+ to pi* absorption maximum is 2.695 eV (about 460 nm), well reproduced by MRMP2. Key geometric parameters, S0 then S1: P-P 2.056 then 2.153 A; P-C1 1.834 then 1.821 A; C1-P-P angle 103.1 then 109.0 degrees; C1-P-P-C1' dihedral -177.9 then -179.1 degrees; and the phenyl torsion phi 30.3 then 89.6 degrees. The S0 torsional potential has DOUBLE MINIMA at nonplanar conformations, phi = phi' = 30.3 degrees (C2) and phi = -phi' = 30.0 degrees (Ci). On excitation to S1 the phenyls twist to nearly perpendicular. Electron populations at phi = 30 degrees show that on n to pi* excitation the in-plane 3s, 3px and 3py populations fall from 0.936, 1.065 and 1.058 to 0.891, 0.828 and 0.963 while the out-of-plane 3pz rises from 0.994 to 1.398, and that 3pz population stays almost constant in S1 regardless of phi — the pi electron is localized on the P=P unit.
Other: This is a clean case of a reduced space being justified for a GLOBAL surface scan rather than for a single point, and the justification procedure is worth copying: a preliminary CI including up to triple excitations was run first, and the (14,12) subset was selected on the criterion that it describe S0 and S1 'at any geometries which possibly contribute to the photochemistry'. That geometry-independence requirement is exactly what a torsional scan from planar to perpendicular demands, and it is a stronger condition than adequacy at the Franck-Condon point. The full (18,16) was defined and rejected purely on the cost of scanning global surfaces, not on any claim that it would give the same answer. The compensating check is external: MRMP2 on this reference reproduces the observed 2.695 eV absorption to within 0.06 eV, whereas bare CASSCF is 0.85 eV too high. Note that the S1 phenyl torsion result — twisting to 89.6 degrees — is driven by an electron-population redistribution into the out-of-plane 3pz orbital, a property the active space must contain the relevant pi* orbitals to describe at all; the paper notes explicitly that P-C bond-length change alone 'is not persuasive enough' to explain the torsion. The general lesson is that the reduced space was validated against EXPERIMENT rather than against the larger space it replaced. Bare (14,12) CASSCF overestimates the n+ to pi* excitation energy substantially — 3.544 eV for t-DPP against an observed 2.695 eV, and 3.277 eV for t-AZB against 2.412 eV — while MRMP2 on the same reference gives 2.759 and 2.412 eV, essentially exact in both cases. The CASSCF error is nearly identical for the two molecules (0.85 and 0.87 eV), so the reduced space is BALANCED across the P/N comparison even though it is quantitatively poor on its own; that constancy is what makes the t-DPP versus t-AZB contrast trustworthy at the CASSCF level while the absolute energies are not. Both states are strongly single-configurational at the S0 geometry (leading CI coefficients 0.897-0.907 for S0 and 0.896-0.901 for S1), so the multiconfigurational treatment is needed for the surface topology and the excited-state ordering rather than for near-degeneracy at any one point.

notes: An analogue of trans-azobenzene with P=P in place of N=N. compound_name: Pyrene radical cation (Py+) — photostability via sloped conical intersections
point_group: D2h for all CASSCF geometry optimizations, matching the planar-constrained MMVB structures
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations within D2h symmetry for the D0, D1 and D2 minima. Conical intersections optimized at CASSCF in a REDUCED (13e,14o) active space, with full (15e,16o) CASSCF energies then computed at the resulting crossing structures. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries. MMVB structures optimized with planar constraints.
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 as benchmarks for a hybrid QM/MM molecular mechanics-valence bond (MMVB) force field, for which an analytical energy gradient for cations was implemented in this work
basis_set: 6-31G*, including polarization d functions on the carbon atoms
active_space_orbital_description: The FULL pi active space: 15 pi electrons distributed in 16 valence pi orbitals. A reduced (13e,14o) space is used for conical intersection optimization and as the CASPT2 reference.
active_space_protocol: Three distinct uses of two spaces, each forced by a stated computational limit. The full (15e,16o) pi space is used for minima and for single-point energies, and the paper quantifies why it cannot be used everywhere: 'CASSCF presently has a practical limit of around 10^7 configuration state functions (e.g., Py+ with 15 electrons in 16 active orbitals and D2h point group symmetry)' — this molecule sits AT that limit. Conical intersections therefore had to be optimized in a reduced (13e,14o) space 'as computationally expensive orbital state-averaging procedures are required for such calculations', with full-space energies recomputed at the resulting geometries. For CASPT2 'we also had to reduce the reference space to (13e,14o), keeping the CASSCF optimized orbitals frozen with the (15e,16o) active space' — so the CASPT2 reference orbitals come from the large space while the reference configurations come from the small one. The choice of a multiconfigurational method is argued from first principles: the one-electron approximation 'is unreliable, because so many problems involve interaction of many configurations', and CASSCF 'fully accounts for configuration interactions within a pi-electron system'.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (D0, D1, D2); state averaging required for the conical intersection optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in kcal/mol as CASSCF / CASPT2 / MMVB: D1 at 22.9 / 23.7 / 21.5; D2 at 39.9 / 36.2 / 47.0, against an experimental D2 value of about 36 kcal/mol. At the D1 minimum the D0-D1 energy gap is 7.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 11.9 at CASPT2 (1.9 at MMVB). The D0/D1 conical intersection lies 1.9 kcal/mol above the D1 minimum at CASSCF (0.1 at MMVB). The D1/D2 conical intersection lies 8.1 kcal/mol above the D2 minimum at CASSCF and 7.9 at MMVB. Both conical intersections are SLOPED, with parallel gradients on the upper and lower states and equivalent gradient difference vectors at CASSCF and MMVB. Root-mean-square deviations of MMVB from CASSCF bond lengths over six distinct bonds are 0.006, 0.009 and 0.011 A for the D0, D1 and D2 minima (maximum errors under 0.01, 0.015 and 0.02 A), 0.010 A for the D0/D1 CI (maximum 0.015 A) and 0.017 A for the D1/D2 CI (maximum 0.030 A). The mechanism proposed is photoexcitation to an absorbing Dn state, rapid decay to D1 consistent with Kasha's rule, then ultrafast nonradiative decay to D0 at an easily accessible sloped D0/D1 conical intersection — accounting for the observed photostability.
Other: The most important caveat is one the authors state against their own conical intersections: 'at the CASSCF D0/D1 CI and D1/D2 CI optimized geometries, the two respective electronic states split by over 6 kcal/mol at the CASPT2 level, indicating that differential dynamic electron correlation is not negligible. We therefore do not know the real crossing energy and geometry at the CASPT2 level.' The crossings were located where the CASSCF space makes two states degenerate, and adding dynamic correlation lifts that degeneracy by more than 6 kcal/mol — so these are CASSCF crossing points, not true conical intersections of the correlated surface, and the paper says the same effect was seen for the naphthalene cation. It cannot be fixed here because CASPT2 geometry optimization is not available at this size. The second point concerns how the reduced space is used: conical intersections need state averaging, which is expensive enough that the space had to drop from (15e,16o) to (13e,14o) for those optimizations, and the CASPT2 reference is a hybrid — orbitals frozen from the large-space CASSCF, configurations from the small space. That is a defensible compromise but means the CASPT2 energies do not correspond to any single self-consistent active space. Finally, pyrene sits exactly at the stated practical CASSCF ceiling of about 10^7 configuration state functions even with D2h symmetry, so this molecule marks the size boundary for full-pi treatment of PAH radical cations — which is the whole motivation for benchmarking the cheaper MMVB force field against it.
reference_short: Tokmachev, Boggio-Pasqua, Bearpark et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 10881
notes: MMVB is a hybrid QM/MM method parameterized to reproduce CASSCF calculations, not experimental or CASPT2 results — a point the authors make explicitly before comparing. Its analytical energy gradient for cations was implemented for this work. MMVB reproduces the CASSCF geometries well (RMS deviations 0.006-0.017 A) and the sloped topology of both conical intersections, but overestimates the D1-D2 gap: its D2 vertical excitation of 47.0 kcal/mol against an experimental 36, which is the origin of its larger error in the D1/D2 CI geometry. It also brings the D0/D1 CI too close to the D1 minimum (0.1 against 1.9 kcal/mol). A previous study of the naphthalene radical cation had shown that CASSCF alone cannot be completely adequate and that CASPT2 may be needed to reproduce experimental excited states. Absolute CASSCF and CASPT2 energies are in Tables S3 and S4; CASSCF bond lengths in Table 1. The CASSCF derivative coupling vector was not computed. correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF-optimized geometries, using a reduced (13e,14o) reference space with the CASSCF orbitals from the full (15e,16o) space held frozen.

active_space_protocol: the oxygen virtual p orbitals are in the space deliberately: the authors note that including them brings the correlation energy closer to the full-CI result than a single-reference CISD achieves. Low NO-bond rotation and NN inversion interconvert trans/cis isomers before a rectangular H-N-N-O saddle leads to closed-shell N2+H2O. Any HNNOH isomer can instead dissociate without an additional barrier to spin-coupled HN2+OH.

compound_name: Glyoxal (S1) with argon — collision-induced intersystem crossing
point_group: C2h (planar in the S0, S1 and T1 states)
geometry_source: Geometries of the S0, S1 and T1 states optimized with the eight-in-six CASSCF method, with zero-point energies from the same level. For the interaction calculations the glyoxal geometry was FIXED at the isolated-molecule S1 optimized structure, since the region of interest is where the interaction energy is sufficiently low. Roughly 150 points were sampled over a quarter sphere by symmetry: r from 3.0 to 6.0 A in 0.5 A steps, theta from 0 to 90 degrees and phi from -90 to 90 degrees, both in 30 degree steps.
method: CASSCF with multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) including Davidson and Pople corrections; full CI within the same active space for the T1 interaction energies; Breit-Pauli spin-orbit interaction calculations on the resulting CI wave functions
basis_set: Gaussian basis sets of double-zeta plus polarization quality: Dunning-Raffenetti [9s5p1d/3s2p1d]/(3s1p/2s1p) for glyoxal and [12s8p/5s3p] for the argon atom
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in six orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: A single eight-in-six CASSCF space is used for the geometries, frequencies and vibrational basis sets of both the S1 and T1 states. For the glyoxal-argon interaction energies the S1 orbitals were computed at this level and then a FULL CI was carried out within the same active space to obtain the T1 interaction energies — the paper notes 'the results for S1 by the full-CI calculations are identical as those by the eight-in-six CASSCF', so the full CI is exact within the space and serves to put both spin states on precisely the same orbital footing. The resulting CI wave functions for S1 and T1 were used directly in the spin-orbit interaction calculations. Separately, MRCI with Davidson or Pople corrections was used to improve the S0/S1/T1 energy differences.
electronic_structure_description: Optimized geometries (bond lengths in angstroms, angles in degrees), calculated then experimental: S0 r(C-H) 1.088 vs 1.132, r(C-C) 1.508 vs 1.526, r(C-O) 1.208 vs 1.212, angle CCH 116.2 vs 112.2, angle CCO 121.1 vs 121.2; S1 r(C-H) 1.077 vs 1.115, r(C-C) 1.419 vs 1.460, r(C-O) 1.281 vs 1.252, angle CCH 121.1 vs 114.0, angle CCO 120.4 vs 123.7; T1 r(C-H) 1.076, r(C-C) 1.435, r(C-O) 1.265, angle CCH 120.9, angle CCO 119.8. Adiabatic energy differences including zero-point corrections in kcal/mol (CASSCF, MRCI, MRCI+Davidson, MRCI+Pople, experiment): E(S1)-E(S0) 79.79, 74.05, 70.49, 70.07, 62.8; E(T1)-E(S0) 73.69, 65.64, 61.68, 61.83, 54.9; E(S1)-E(T1) 6.10, 8.41, 8.82, 8.24, 7.9. CASSCF overestimates the adiabatic excitation energies to S1 and T1 while underestimating the S1-T1 gap; MRCI improves both because the dynamical correlation lowers S1 and T1 more than S0. The MRCI+Pople S1-T1 gap of 8.24 kcal/mol agrees excellently with the experimental 7.9 and was adopted for the dynamics. The T1 optimized geometry is very close to that of S1, so intersystem crossing is intrinsically slow because the Franck-Condon factors between the initial S1 vibrational state and the numerous isoenergetic T1 vibrational states are small. Normal mode frequencies agree with experiment in the low-frequency region but differ substantially at high frequency, with the C=O stretching (bu) mode particularly discrepant. A lifetime of 5.3 ps is quoted for a state at a given energy in the collision dynamics analysis.
Other: This paper records a specific pathology of excited-state CASSCF: symmetry breaking. The discrepancy between calculated and experimental S1 geometries is 'attributed to the instability problem, i.e., the symmetry-broken solutions with a lower symmetry than the C2h nuclear framework exist in the CASSCF wave functions for the excited states. It seems that the excited-state CASSCF wave function overemphasizes the O-C=C-O resonance structure.' The consequence propagates into the vibrational analysis — the C=O stretching bu mode is singled out as badly wrong and explicitly linked back to the same symmetry-breaking problem — and matters here because those frequencies build the vibrational basis sets for the collision dynamics. An eight-in-six space is not large enough to prevent one resonance structure dominating the excited-state wave function. The energetics show the complementary limitation: CASSCF overestimates both excitation energies by 17-19 kcal/mol and simultaneously UNDERestimates the S1-T1 gap (6.10 against 7.9 experimental), because dynamic correlation stabilizes the two excited states more than the ground state. MRCI with the Pople correction repairs the gap to 8.24 kcal/mol but leaves the absolute excitation energies still 7 kcal/mol high. A neat methodological detail worth carrying: the T1 interaction energies were obtained by full CI within the same active space using the S1 orbitals, and the authors verify that this reproduces the CASSCF S1 result exactly — so both spin states are described in an identical orbital basis, which is what makes the computed spin-orbit matrix elements between them meaningful.
reference_short: Nakajima & Kato, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 10657
notes: The study computes cross sections for the S1 to T1 transition in glyoxal induced by collision with argon, combining the interaction potential with the spin-orbit interaction. Vibronic basis sets were constructed from the CASSCF vibrational analysis, and Franck-Condon factors between the S1 and T1 manifolds were required. The MRCI+Pople S1-T1 difference was the value adopted for all subsequent dynamics. correlation_correction: MRCI with Davidson or Pople energy corrections; full CI within the active space for the T1 interaction energies.

method: restricted active space MCSCF (in place of a full CASSCF) followed by higher-order CI
software: a modified version of ALCHEMY II
active_space_orbital_description: in both the CASSCF and the higher-order CI, all sixteen 4s and 4p orbitals were kept inactive - no excitations from these shells were allowed, though the orbitals were allowed to relax - leaving twenty-four orbitals for the active space in both the C2v and D2h point groups. active_space_protocol: restricted active space MCSCF: 4a1 + 3b2 + 3b1 = ten orbitals for the tetrahedron in C2v, with a separate selection for the rhombus and square structures; all sixteen 4s and 4p orbitals inactive but relaxed
electronic_structure_description: Electronic states of the yttrium clusters Y2, Y3 and Y4 in tetrahedral, rhombus and square geometries.

method: CASSCF as reference for valence internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q), plus core-valence and scalar relativistic corrections and total-energy extrapolation to the complete basis set limit; the best level is denoted MRCI+Q/CV+DK+56

active_space_protocol: the space was enlarged for a specific diagnosed reason rather than for accuracy: with the valence-only eight-orbital space every curve carried a visible bump, which the authors traced to the calculation skipping from one state's curve to another's, and adding three orbitals made all four curves smooth across the whole 0.05-1.52 nm range. geometry_source: All geometrical optimizations performed at the CASSCF/6-31G* level, with energies of all critical and nonstationary points, including Franck-Condon points and dissociation fragments at the asymptotic limit, recalculated at CASPT2/CASSCF/ANO-L. active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in ten valence orbitals: 2sO, 2sN, sigma-NN, pi-NO, sigma-NO, np-N, np-O, pi*-NO, sigma*-NN and sigma*-NO. For the tautomerization study a sigma-CH orbital and its corresponding virtual orbital were added, giving 16 electrons in 12 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is inherited from the authors' previous work on NH2NO and enumerated orbital by orbital. It is enlarged to (16,12) by adding a sigma-CH orbital and its virtual counterpart when tautomerizations are studied, since hydrogen migration cannot be described without them. Fragment spaces are derived from this parent space by reduction rather than being constructed independently, so that dissociation asymptotes connect properly. Geometries use 6-31G* on grounds of molecular size, while energies are recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L to make the vertical transitions and excited-state relative energies quantitative.
electronic_structure_description: The S0 to S1 transition occurs at 3.29 eV with an oscillator strength of 0.003 au and the S0 to S2 transition at 5.30 eV with an oscillator strength of 0.17 au; the second singlet state (2 1A') has np-N to pi*-NO character. Changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, and both sets of values agree well with experiment and with MS-CASPT2 results. Experimentally the first band shows a vibrational progression with an oscillator strength of 0.009 and the second band an oscillator strength of 0.12. Excitation at 363.5 nm corresponds to the S0 to S1 transition and gives the dimethylamino radical with a lifetime above 0.5 s, while excitation at 248 nm implies a different mechanism. Experimentally, after dissociation the fragments carry 18.4 kcal/mol and the dimethylamine radical the remaining 23.0 kcal/mol. A surface crossing point occurs at 75.9 kcal/mol (3.29 eV) above the ground-state minimum. Dissociation after excitation at 363.5 nm deviates from planarity, whereas at 250 nm NDMA exhibits planar character. MS-CASPT2 vertical transitions were also computed with PCM in cyclohexane, benzene, methanol and water in increasing order of dielectric constant, and the resulting solvent shifts are small.
Other: Four different spaces are used across one study and their relationships are stated explicitly. The parent (14,10) is inherited from the authors' earlier work on NH2NO and lists its orbitals individually: 2sO, 2sN, sigma-NN, pi-NO, sigma-NO, np-N, np-O, pi*-NO, sigma*-NN and sigma*-NO. Studying the tautomerizations required adding a sigma-CH orbital and its virtual partner, giving (16,12) -- the space grows to accommodate a hydrogen migration that the original set could not represent. The dimethylamine radical fragment gets its own (11,10) built for the two extrusion channels it participates in, and that space is described as obtained by reduction of the parent space, so the fragment and parent descriptions are nested rather than independent. The NO fragment was optimized at yet another level, CASSCF(11,8). Nesting is what makes the dissociation energetics meaningful, since the asymptotic limits and the parent molecule must be described consistently. The basis strategy is split deliberately for the same reason: geometries at 6-31G* justified by the size of the molecule, energies recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L specifically to make the vertical transitions and excited-surface energies quantitative. That split is validated by the observation that changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, so the smaller basis is adequate for the geometry-dependent quantities and the larger one is needed only for energies. Core orbitals were frozen in CASPT2 as optimized at the CASSCF level, and imaginary modes at the Franck-Condon geometries were characterized separately at CASSCF/ANO-L with gradients, rotations and translations projected out.

d_electron_count: 5d10 in the 2A1 state; the gold atom valence space is 5d10 6s1
point_group: C2v; the ground state is X 2B2 and the bent HAuH structure was studied on a bending potential energy surface
geometry_source: Bending potential energy surfaces computed in two and three dimensions for the 2A1 and 2B2 states. Dissociation energies computed by a supermolecular calculation with the Au-H distances set to 10 A, because MRSDCI is not size consistent. Vibrational frequencies computed at the coupled cluster (CCD) and MP2 levels in the same gold basis with aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen, and compared with experiment and with DFT.
method: CASSCF followed by multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI); CCD and MP2 for frequencies; matrix isolation infrared spectroscopy in solid hydrogen for comparison
software: Balasubramanian's programs for all CASSCF and MRSDCI computations
basis_set: Extended (3s3p4d1f) basis for gold with a relativistic effective core potential of Ermler and co-workers replacing 68 electrons and leaving the 5d10 6s1 shells as the valence space; triple-zeta plus polarization for the hydrogens; aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen for the frequency calculations
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potential on gold, replacing 68 electrons; relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital are noted as essential for gold
active_space_orbital_description: Five a1 orbitals, three b2 orbitals, two b1 orbitals and one a2 orbital, holding all 13 valence electrons of AuH2, distributed in all possible ways among the active orbitals. The space was chosen to include all 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals of gold.
active_space_protocol: The space is dictated by the atomic spectroscopy of gold rather than by the molecular bonding: because the first excited state of the gold atom arises from 5d9 6s2 and the second from 5d10 6p1, all of the 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals must be active if the molecular states correlating with those atomic limits are to be described. Listing the space by symmetry block -- five a1, three b2, two b1 and one a2 -- makes the composition explicit rather than leaving it to a bare count. The MRSDCI built on it correlates the same 13 electrons and takes as references all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients at or above 0.01, which typically gave 65 reference configurations and up to 3.4 million total configurations. Because MRSDCI is not size consistent, dissociation energies were obtained from a supermolecular calculation at 10 A rather than by subtracting fragment energies.
electronic_structure_description: The gold atom 2D state from the 5d9 6s2 configuration lies 1.7 eV above the ground state while the corresponding state from 5d10 6p1 lies 4.9 eV higher, a consequence of relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital. The barrier to insert Au(2D) into H2 is 53 kcal/mol, but the 2P state of gold lies considerably above this barrier and is very reactive because it also yields a 2B2 state which undergoes an avoided crossing with the 2B2 state arising from Au(2D); the barrier appears to arise from that avoided crossing. The barrier for formation of the lowest 2A1 state from Au(2S) + H2 is 95 kcal/mol. Once the X 2B2 state is formed through excitation of gold to the 2P state it remains in its potential well, since dissociating back to Au(2D) + H2 requires surmounting a large barrier. The 2B2 and 2A1 surfaces cross at a bond angle of 65 degrees, about 25 kcal/mol above the X 2B2 minimum, and that 25 kcal/mol barrier must be overcome before decomposition to Au(2S) + H2. Spin-orbit coupling between the two states cannot be large because the 2A1 state has predominantly Au(5d10 6s1) character; the 2B2 state has a larger spin-orbit effect but its coupling to 2A1 should be negligible because of the closed 5d10 shell in the latter. X 2B2 is therefore a long-lived ground state, 27 kcal/mol more stable than Au(2D) + H2. A zero-point correction of 6.4 kcal/mol is applied. The computed 2A1 bending surface is close to a previous study but the 2B2 surface differs, especially near the dissociation limit and the minimum. Adding an f function gives unrealistic infrared intensities. The AuH2 anion has also been observed, with a related energy of 68 kcal/mol from DFT.
Other: The composition of the active space is fixed by where the atomic excited states come from, not by which orbitals form bonds: since gold's first excited state is 5d9 6s2 and its second is 5d10 6p1, the 5d, 6s and 6p sets all have to be active for the molecular states correlating with those limits to exist in the wave function at all. That matters directly for the physics being reported, because the barrier to insertion is attributed to an avoided crossing between two 2B2 states arising from the 2D and 2P atomic asymptotes -- a feature that simply cannot appear if the 6p orbitals are outside the space. compound_name: H2 formation inside the T8 polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane cage, [HSiO1.5]8
geometry_source: Structures optimized at the Hartree-Fock level with the 6-31G(d) basis and characterized by frequency analyses, with single-point MP2 energies on those geometries; transition-state structures for hydrogen insertion into each cage located and used as trajectory starting points
method: Ab initio molecular dynamics at the CASSCF level, with Hartree-Fock geometry optimization and MP2 single-point energies for the reaction energetics
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF dynamics and the Hartree-Fock optimizations; 6-31+G(d,p) used additionally at the MP2 level and to test the CASSCF dissociation curve
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals, being the two electrons and the two orbitals of the colliding hydrogen atoms. The silsesquioxane host is entirely outside the active space.
active_space_protocol: A minimal two-electron two-orbital space confined to the colliding hydrogen atoms, chosen so that the formation and dissociation of the H-H bond is described correctly across the whole trajectory while the cage is treated at the mean-field level. The two-electron two-orbital dissociation curves for the hydrogen molecule were compared between the 6-31G(d) and 6-31+G(d,p) basis sets and found essentially indistinguishable, which justified running all the dynamics in the smaller basis.
electronic_structure_description: Trajectories were started by inserting a second hydrogen atom into the hydrogen-encapsulated cage, and in many cases the gradual formation of a hydrogen molecule was observed after frequent collisions of the two hydrogen atoms within the cage. Two sets of initial conditions were used: inserting the second hydrogen with a small kinetic energy of 0.5 kcal/mol starting from the transition state for the insertion reaction, and inserting it with a kinetic energy larger than the insertion barrier, starting 2.5 Angstrom above a cage face; the latter used 60 kcal/mol of kinetic energy for this cage. The face through which insertion occurs is expanded relative to the other faces, as previously seen for direct H2 insertion. The binding energy of a hydrogen molecule in the gas phase is calculated to be 94.0 kcal/mol at the CASSCF(2,2) level. Of the three reactions considered, insertion of an H atom and insertion of an H2 molecule into the empty cage are endothermic while the stepwise route through the mono-hydrogen adduct is exothermic, and the MP2 stabilization energy of the product relative to the two separated reactants is only slightly smaller than the gas-phase hydrogen binding energy. Both cages expand on including the impurities.
Other: The active space here is as small as a multiconfigurational treatment can be -- two electrons in two orbitals -- and the paper is explicit that those are the orbitals of the two colliding hydrogen atoms and nothing else. The whole silsesquioxane cage, dozens of Si-O and Si-H bonds, is outside the space and described only at the mean-field level. That is a defensible choice for the specific question being asked, because the process under study is the making of a single sigma bond between two hydrogen atoms, which is exactly the textbook case a two-orbital space describes and a single determinant cannot: at large separation the two-electron two-orbital wave function goes correctly to two neutral atoms where a restricted single determinant would not. The cost is that nothing about the cage's own electronic structure can respond multiconfigurationally, so any polarization or charge transfer between the encapsulated hydrogens and the host is only present through the orbital optimization, not through the configuration expansion. Two checks are reported that bear on how much the choice constrains the result. The basis set dependence of the space's central quantity was tested directly: the two-electron two-orbital dissociation curves for the hydrogen molecule in the 6-31G(d) and the larger 6-31+G(d,p) basis sets are described as essentially indistinguishable, which is what justified running the whole dynamics in the smaller basis. Separately, diffuse and polarization functions were found to change inclusion energies by 1.9 to 9.8 kcal/mol and barrier heights by 1.3 to 4.2 kcal/mol at the perturbative level, so the basis matters for the host-guest energetics even though it does not matter for the bond the active space describes. That asymmetry is the practical lesson: the space was validated on the quantity it governs, while the quantities it does not govern were left to a different method. Note also that the energetics quoted for the inclusion reactions come from second-order perturbation theory on Hartree-Fock geometries, not from the multiconfigurational calculation, which supplies only the dynamics and the reference hydrogen binding energy of 94.0 kcal/mol in the gas phase. Anyone reusing these numbers should keep the two levels apart.

geometry_source: Optimized at the CASSCF level with a correlation-consistent double-zeta basis, with frequency analyses confirming the transition states
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequency analysis, with multireference configuration interaction including single and double excitations used to refine the energetics at those geometries and zero-point corrections taken from the CASSCF frequencies; vertical excitation energies additionally computed with time-dependent density functional theory and equation-of-motion coupled cluster
software: GAUSSIAN03 for the density functional and CASSCF calculations; GAUSSIAN09 for the coupled cluster calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the carbonyl group, two lone-pair orbitals on the two oxygen atoms, and the sigma and sigma* orbitals of both the carbon-chlorine and the carbon-oxygen bonds that can undergo alpha cleavage.
active_space_protocol: Both competing alpha-cleavage channels are represented in the same space so that their barriers can be compared on a common footing. The authors state explicitly that CASSCF cannot provide sufficient correlation energy, so the space serves to generate geometries and a reference wave function while all energies are refined by configuration interaction.
electronic_structure_description: The first excited singlet minimum arises mainly from an n to pi* excitation. On excitation the carbonyl bond lengthens from 1.193 Angstrom in the ground state minimum to 1.380 Angstrom, and the carbon rehybridizes from sp2 to sp3, converting the planar ground state structure into a pyramidal excited state one; the adiabatic energy difference between the two minima is 102.2 kcal/mol. Two transition states for alpha cleavage were located and confirmed by frequency analysis, one for carbon-oxygen fission and one for carbon-chlorine fission. The carbon-oxygen barrier is 9.7 kcal/mol on the refined electronic energies and 15.6 kcal/mol once zero-point energy is included, the increase arising because the transition state has one fewer real vibrational mode than the minimum and so a smaller zero-point energy. The carbon-chlorine barrier is 1.5 kcal/mol, with the corresponding bond significantly elongated at its transition state.
Other: The authors say the space selection 'requires some details' and then supply them, orbital class by orbital class, which is the level of specification that makes a space reusable. Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the pi and pi* of the carbonyl, two lone-pair orbitals on the two oxygen atoms, and the sigma and sigma* pairs of both bonds that can undergo alpha cleavage. Both competing dissociation channels are therefore represented in the same space, which is what allows their barriers to be compared on one footing -- the central quantitative claim of the paper is that one barrier is 9.7 kcal/mol and the other 1.5, and that comparison would be worthless if each channel had been given its own tailored space. Including the sigma manifold of a bond that stays intact in one channel is the price of that comparability. The paper is unusually blunt about what the space alone cannot do, stating flatly that the CASSCF calculations cannot provide sufficient correlation energy and using configuration interaction with single and double excitations on the reference geometries to refine every energy. So the space is treated as a geometry and reference generator rather than as an energy method, with the division of labour stated rather than implied. A subtle trap is documented in the process. The barrier for one channel is 9.7 kcal/mol on the refined electronic energies but 15.6 kcal/mol once zero-point energy is included, and the authors explain the direction: the transition state carries one fewer real vibrational mode than the minimum because one has become imaginary, so its zero-point energy is smaller and the correction raises rather than lowers the barrier. A 6 kcal/mol swing on a 10 kcal/mol barrier from a bookkeeping effect, moving in the counterintuitive direction, is worth carrying generally -- zero-point corrections at transition states are not small and are not signed the way one expects. The wave function analysis at the excited minimum shows what the space buys structurally: the carbonyl bond lengthens from 1.193 to 1.380 Angstrom on excitation and the carbon rehybridizes from sp2 to sp3, turning a planar structure pyramidal, with an adiabatic excitation energy of 102.2 kcal/mol. A space containing the carbonyl pi system and the oxygen lone pairs is exactly what is needed to describe an n to pi* state that rehybridizes the carbon, and a space built only from the breaking bonds would have missed it. Vertical excitation energies were cross-checked against time-dependent density functional theory and equation-of-motion coupled cluster as well as the configuration interaction treatment, so the state characters do not rest on the active space alone.
reference_short: Cui, Sun & Fang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2011, 115, 10146
notes: The two alpha-cleavage channels differ in barrier by more than a factor of six on the refined energies, which is the paper's central comparison and depends on both channels sharing one active space. The study frames the mechanism in both adiabatic and nonadiabatic terms, the latter being the less commonly examined picture for Norrish type I reactions.
