active_space_protocol: CAS(7,5) over the Co(II) 3d manifold, state-averaged, then NEVPT2, with the ZFS extracted by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory over the spin-orbit-coupled excited states
electronic_structure_description: Static and dynamic magnetic properties were measured for a series of four pentacoordinate [Co(L3A-D)Cl2] complexes and supported by the ab initio zero-field-splitting parameters. The multireference calculations cover the four complexes of this work together with five further compounds (I-V) taken for comparison.
Other: The same minimal CAS(7,5) recipe as the other Co(II) anisotropy studies, and the point of interest here is the machinery layered on top rather than the space: the zero-field splitting is extracted by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory over the spin-orbit-coupled excited states, using the SOMF approximation to the Breit-Pauli operator and effective Hamiltonian theory, with scalar relativity carried in the basis. A five-orbital space determines which excited states exist to contribute; everything about how much each contributes is decided by that perturbative apparatus. Extending the calculation across nine compounds - the four new ones plus five from the literature - is what gives the comparison its force, since the space is identical for all of them and only the ligand field differs.

ligand_set: one Terp aryl substituent on each bismuth; 64 atoms in the molecule
point_group: given as "C2d" in the paper, alongside C2 for P=P, Cs for the As/Sb/Bi heteronuclear pairs and C1 for the phosphorus-containing heteronuclear ones; the three phenyl rings of each Terp are rotated out of plane, so there is no significant conjugation along them

method: CASSCF followed by multireference MP2 (MR-MP2) on the CASSCF reference, used for the bond order and the singlet-triplet transition; TDDFT with B3LYP, BLYP and M06 for the allowed bands
software: Firefly 8.1.1, which is based partly on the GAMESS (US) source; GAMESS for the M06 calculations
basis_set: def2-TZV on the pnictogens, all-electron for P and As and with a relativistic effective core potential for Sb and Bi; 6-311(d) on C and H
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic effects for Sb and Bi enter through the relativistic effective core potential in the def2-TZV basis; spin-orbit coupling is invoked qualitatively, as the reason a singlet-triplet band becomes weakly allowed in bismuth compounds, but is not computed
active_space_orbital_description: HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1, which are the n+ and pi orbitals of the Bi=Bi bond and their antibonding counterparts. A larger (10,10) space was also used for this molecule alone, adding pi orbitals of the Terp groups and their antibonding partners
active_space_protocol: the author reports the space as a compromise: a common space for all ten dipnictenes was wanted, but the molecules have 64 atoms, different point groups, and the low-symmetry cases such as P=Bi were reluctant to converge, so (4,4) was used for every Bi-containing compound and the (10,10) space was run only for dibismuthene as a check. The check holds: the CASSCF(10,10) reference gives almost the same singlet-triplet energy and almost the same bond order as (4,4), and its leading configurations, Psi = 0.91|2222200000> - 0.28|2222020000> - 0.10|2220202000>, are dominated by the HOMO-to-LUMO and HOMO-1-to-LUMO+1 excitations that already lie inside the (4,4) space.
multiplicities_studied: singlet ground state and the lowest triplet
electronic_structure_description: The singlet-triplet band is calculated at 1174 nm with CASSCF and 886 nm with MR-MP2, against an observed weak band at 970 nm, or a band split into 913 and 1025 nm; the DFT functionals put it at 900-1100 nm. The TDDFT n+-to-pi* band (lambda2) comes at 549 nm against experimental values of 660 or 670 nm reported for other dibismuthenes, which is the discrepancy that prompts the reassignment: the long-wavelength weak features previously taken for n+-to-pi* are proposed to be the singlet-triplet band instead, spin-orbit coupling making it weakly allowed only in the bismuth compounds. The pi-bond is weaker than a formal double bond: DFT gives a bond order of 1.84 with B3LYP, BLYP and M06, but with either the (4,4) or the (10,10) CASSCF reference for MR-MP2 the bond order drops to 1.49, the pi orbital occupation being 1.80 and the pi* occupation about 0.20. The second configuration, with coefficient -0.28, is a double excitation from pi to pi*, and that is what cuts the bond order.
Other: This is a case where the multireference treatment changes a chemical conclusion rather than a number: the closed-shell DFT description gives an almost classical Bi=Bi double bond, and the correlated pi/pi* occupations of 1.80/0.20 reduce it to about one and a half. The (10,10) test also shows what the extra six orbitals buy - the Terp pi system contributes nothing essential, so the four frontier orbitals carry the non-dynamical correlation of the double bond by themselves.

method: RASSCF/RASPT2 with a highly-excited-state (HEXS) core-hole projection, plus a displaced-harmonic-oscillator (DHO) vibronic model for line shapes, to simulate XPS and XANES (K-edge) soft X-ray spectra to sub-eV accuracy

active_space_protocol: A detailed, transferable RAS active-space-selection recipe for core (X-ray) excitation/ionization, tested on 1,1-difluoroethene at the C K-edge. The space must contain: (i) the core orbital(s) of interest, placed in the subspace to which the HEXS core-hole projection is applied; (ii) virtual orbitals, chosen deliberately by the user - more virtuals give a more complete spectrum, since they are the arrival orbitals of the excited 1s electron and enable multiple-excitation intensity; (iii) occupied valence orbitals for correlation and shake-up states, where often just the highest occupied (HOMO) suffices. Key finding: even a MINIMAL active space of just the core orbital + HOMO(pi) + LUMO(pi*) reproduces the strongest pre-edge pi*-resonances accurately in energy, relative intensity and line shape; missing correlation from excluded occupied orbitals is recovered by the PT2 step, which stays stable as long as the HOMO is in the space. The paper gives an iterative algorithm (minAS + n virtuals per step) to systematically grow the virtual set and add core-excited states while keeping cost low. No molecular symmetry was imposed, to keep the recipe general.
Other: Applications: N/C/O K-edge XPS and XANES spectra of the two most stable glycine conformers (the three edges ~100 eV apart allow unique conformer identification), C K-edge of formaldehyde and the fluoroethane/ethene series. Sub-eV accuracy against high-resolution experiment, with the DHO vibronic treatment quantitatively reproducing line shapes. The core-hole formation modulates (weakens or strengthens) bonds, rationalized via an ESCA-potential/chemical-shift picture.

compound_name: Ta2, the tantalum dimer, low-lying electronic states
geometry_source: potential energy curves and equilibrium bond lengths obtained for each electronic state at the CASSCF level; spin-orbit splittings not computed directly but estimated by scaling
method: CASSCF with relativistic effective core potentials, followed by relativistic CI for the states where it was run; spin-orbit splittings estimated by scaling variational CASSCF/MRSDCI/RCI results for Pt2 as Z^3.7
software: the author's modified version of ALCHEMY II, a quadratically convergent direct MCSCF and symbolic CI package
basis_set: valence (5s5p4d) contracted to [5s3p3d] on Ta, augmented with two sets of 4f functions with exponents 0.45 and 0.72
relativistic_treatment: relativistic effective core potentials with (1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 4f14) in the core and 13 electrons (5s2 5p6 5d3 6s2) in the valence
soc_included: not computed for this molecule; spin-orbit splittings are estimated by scaling variational results for Pt2 as Z^3.7
active_space_orbital_description: ten active electrons distributed in all possible ways among twelve active orbitals
active_space_protocol: the dimer is treated multiconfigurationally because dimers of heavy metals carry genuine multireference character in their low-lying states, while the larger clusters in the same paper are handled by B3LYP - so the CASSCF calculation here also serves to justify the cheaper treatment used elsewhere. A basis-set test showed the two 4f function sets change bond lengths by no more than 0.01 A, which is why they were dropped for the larger clusters.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 3Sigma-g at Re 2.166 A, dominated (77 per cent) by sigma_g2 delta_g2. Low excited states follow closely: 1Gamma_g at 0.136 eV (2.176 A), 5Sigma-u at 0.189 eV (2.264 A), 3Delta_u at 0.228 eV (2.251 A), 3Gamma_u at 0.281 eV (2.270 A), 1Delta_u at 0.356 eV, 5Pi_g at 0.556 eV, 3Delta_g at 0.675 eV and 1Sigma+g at 1.5 eV. Leading configurations carry weights of 71 to 85 per cent for most states, but higher states are genuinely mixed - 3Phi_g at 0.711 eV has two configurations contributing 25 and 24 per cent - so a single-configuration treatment is adequate only for the lowest states and the high-spin ones. The estimated 0g+ to 1g spin-orbit splitting of the 3Sigma-g ground state is 6500 cm-1, scaled from the computed 8252 cm-1 for the corresponding splitting in Pt2.
Other: That estimated 6500 cm-1 splitting is roughly 0.8 eV, larger than the entire spread of the eight lowest electronic states - which is the paper's central point. In clusters of these very heavy metals spin-orbit stabilization can exceed Jahn-Teller stabilization, so the symmetric structure survives rather than distorting, the opposite of the behaviour in lighter clusters. The estimate is obtained by scaling rather than computed for Ta2 itself, and the author notes that such scaled splittings come out considerably larger than the perturbative ones used for the bigger clusters, so the two treatments in this paper are not on the same footing.

notes: Ta2 is the only system in this paper treated by CASSCF. compound_name: iodobenzene, C6H5I, examined for its ability to phosphoresce through the heavy-atom effect
point_group: C2v state labels are used throughout - A1, B1 and B2 - with the z axis taken collinear with the C-I bond
geometry_source: ground-state geometry optimized by restricted Kohn-Sham DFT with the wB97X functional and D3 dispersion with Becke-Johnson damping, verified by a nuclear Hessian; the multireference calculations are single points on it, with an unrelaxed scan along the C-I coordinate for the dissociation curves
method: state-averaged CASSCF with four different active spaces compared head to head, followed by three post-CASSCF corrections - strongly contracted NEVPT2, its quasi-degenerate extension with a Van Vleck effective Hamiltonian, and spectroscopy-oriented MRCI with singles and doubles plus the Davidson correction (SORCI+Q) - all in multi-state formulation and all built on the corresponding state-averaged CASSCF densities. Real-time TDDFT with Ehrenfest nuclear dynamics run separately in CP2K to demonstrate dissociation explicitly
software: ORCA 5.03 for all static multireference work; CP2K for the real-time TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics
basis_set: segmented all-electron relativistically contracted SARC-DKH-TZVP on iodine and relativistically recontracted def2-DKH-TZVP on all other atoms; a mixed Gaussian and plane-wave dual-space basis for the CP2K dynamics
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess one-particle Hamiltonian with a finite-size Gaussian-like nucleus model
soc_included: yes, and it is the entire subject: spin-orbit coupling matrix elements and SOC-corrected transition moments from the DKH2-transformed spin-orbit mean-field operator including spin-other-orbit and spin-own-orbit terms with a DFT-like local correlation term, treated throughout in a quasi-degenerate perturbation theory framework
active_space_orbital_description: the recommended space is ten electrons in nine orbitals: the six benzene pi orbitals, the occupied and virtual sigma orbitals of the C-I bond, and the out-of-plane pz lone pair of iodine. Three other spaces were run for comparison - (8e,8o) with benzene pi plus the C-I sigma/sigma* pair only; (10e,9o)-LP with the in-plane px/y iodine lone pair added instead of the pz; and (12e,10o) with both iodine lone pairs - and a six-orbital benzene-pi-only space was tried and rejected
active_space_protocol: A stepwise enlargement in which every step is justified by a named failure of the previous one. The six-orbital benzene pi space suggested by TD-DFT was rejected because it gives an almost zero spin-orbit coupling matrix; the C-I sigma and sigma* pair was added because the dissociation cannot be described without it, giving (8e,8o); the iodine lone pairs were added because (8e,8o) misses low-lying states carrying very large couplings to the ground state. The paper states explicitly that these orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage'. State averaging is over six low-lying singlets and nine low-lying triplets, the number 'chosen based on level spacing to include all near-degenerate energy states and provide efficient mixing in spin-coupling'
nroots_per_mult: 6 low-lying singlet roots and 9 low-lying triplet roots in every space compared
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell aromatic iodide whose ground state is dominated by a single CAS-CI configuration with weight above 0.99 regardless of the active space chosen. With the recommended (10e,9o) space the lowest six triplets lie at 3.752, 4.876, 4.884, 5.035, 6.982 and 7.068 eV above the ground state, with averaged spin-orbit coupling matrix elements to the ground state of 0.926, 6.63, 0.106, 1286.754, 4.571 and 0.122 reciprocal centimetres - the fourth triplet, T4 of B2 symmetry, carrying a coupling three orders of magnitude larger than any other. That state is dissociative along the C-I coordinate. It cannot be reached directly from S1 B1 by intersystem crossing because of spin-orbit selection rules, but is easily populated by coupling from other triplets, the squared matrix element from T1 A1 being 4965.7 reciprocal centimetres squared. T1 A1 is stable near equilibrium but dissociative at long range. The conclusion is that iodobenzene cannot phosphoresce because every strongly spin-orbit coupled triplet sublevel leads to dissociation - confirmed by explicit Ehrenfest dynamics
Other: Four active spaces are run at fixed root set on the same molecule. Across them the excitation energy of the strongly coupled triplet moves by about half an electronvolt while its spin-orbit coupling moves by a factor of six hundred. Across the four post-CASSCF treatments at fixed space the energy moves 5.035 to 4.523 eV while the coupling moves only 1287 to 1160 reciprocal centimetres, about ten percent. Two spaces of identical size differ in one orbital: (10e,9o)-LP, which adds iodine's in-plane px/y lone pair, gives a coupling of 2.085 reciprocal centimetres for the fourth triplet, while (10e,9o)-Pi, which adds the out-of-plane pz orbital that can mix with the benzene pi system, gives 1286.754 for the same state, at the same electron count, orbital count, root set and code. Adding the second lone pair on top of the pz, to reach (12e,10o), then changes that coupling by only four percent. The space also decides which state carries the coupling: the very large matrix element sits on T4 in the (8e,8o) and pz-containing spaces but moves to T5 in the in-plane-lone-pair space, so the state ordering itself is active-space dependent. The six-orbital benzene pi space that linear-response TD-DFT points to 'leads to an almost zero-defined SOC matrix in CASSCF and all post-CASSCF methods', which would leave phosphorescence available only through spin-vibronic Herzberg-Teller coupling. Strongly contracted NEVPT2 returns spin-orbit coupling matrix elements identical to CASSCF to every printed digit - 1286.754 and 635.898 reciprocal centimetres - because a non-quasi-degenerate perturbative correction shifts state energies without touching the wavefunctions the coupling is built from; only the quasi-degenerate variant, which rotates the states, and SORCI+Q, which rebuilds the wavefunction, move those numbers at all. The ground state is over 99 percent one configuration in every one of the four spaces. On procedure, the extra orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage' - enlarging the CI expansion after the orbitals are fixed is not the same thing as enlarging the active space.
reference_short: Rublev, Boldyrev & Scheiner, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 4927-4933
notes: The heavy-atom effect does deliver a very large spin-orbit coupling here, but every triplet sublevel that carries it is dissociative along the C-I coordinate, so the molecule cannot phosphoresce. The argument is a composite of three independent pieces - multireference vertical energies and couplings, an unrelaxed potential energy scan showing the dissociative character, and RT-TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics in a different code showing the dissociation explicitly - and the paper is clear about which piece does what. Intersystem-crossing accessibility is argued through Fermi golden rule proportionality to squared coupling matrix elements together with spin-orbit selection rules, not by computing rates. Note a printing artefact in Table 1: the row labelled S0 to T7 in the two pz-containing columns repeats the T1 values exactly and should not be read as a seventh state. The recommended production protocol is QD-SC-NEVPT2 on the (10e,9o) space with the benzene pi system, the C-I sigma and sigma*, and the pz lone pair. Three corrections are compared at fixed active space: SC-NEVPT2, QD-SC-NEVPT2 and SORCI+Q. For the strongly coupled triplet they give excitation energies of 4.966, 4.694 and 4.523 eV against 5.035 eV at bare CASSCF, and couplings of 1286.754, 1299.534 and 1159.658 reciprocal centimetres against 1286.754 - the SC-NEVPT2 value being numerically identical to CASSCF because that correction cannot alter the wavefunction from which the coupling is computed. QD-SC-NEVPT2 is the one the authors recommend.

For 3B1: re 2.4955 a0 and alpha_e 126.571 degrees with TZ, Te 12 165.341, T00 11 834.295 against 11 695 +/- 15 empirical, nu1 874.077, nu2 514.574, nu3 748.155 cm-1 against empirical 1090 +/- 80 and 555 +/- 15. The two states interact only in Cs - in C2v they belong to different irreducible representations - so the off-diagonal diabatic coupling is nonzero only when the antisymmetric mode nu3 is excited, and their surfaces cross at alpha between 115 and 120 degrees. The diabatization is the other half of the construction - the states cross, and only the diabatic representation is smooth enough to fit with a Partridge-Schwenke-type expansion.

The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.

point_group: C2v (with Cs calculations for the A' and A'' roots)
geometry_source: minima and transition states located with analytic CASSCF gradients and numerical Hessians; intrinsic reaction coordinate and approximate minimum energy path calculations used to verify connectivity; intersection seams located by fitting diabatic surface regions with bicubic splines and minimizing the surface difference
method: CASSCF with analytic gradients for stationary-point optimization and numerical Hessians for characterization, refined by CASPT2 (standard correction and the G1/G2/G3 variants)

active_space_orbital_description: full valence, the same space as in Part I
active_space_protocol: Full valence CAS(17,12) throughout, matching Part I so the two mechanisms are directly comparable. Two-state-averaged CASSCF was used for the lowest two roots of each Cs symmetry (A' and A''); in C2v the first root of each of A1, B1, A2 and B2 was taken, except at the I2 intersection where the first and second roots were needed because two states of the same symmetry are involved. Dynamic correlation from CASPT2 using the G2 variant. A deliberately reduced CAS(7,6) with 6-31G(d) was used in GAUSSIAN 98 purely to identify the two coordinates defining each conical intersection - a cheap auxiliary space for a topological question rather than an energetic one
nroots_per_mult: two state-averaged roots per Cs symmetry; first root of each C2v irreducible representation
Other: High barriers were found for the direct C2v-insertion mechanism: 3.11 and 2.54 eV. These are much higher than the barriers for the indirect Cs-insertion mechanisms reported in Part I, so the direct C2v insertion is not competitive. The authors note they did not rigorously verify the conical nature of each located intersection and use the term loosely throughout.

geometry_source: Active-site cluster models built from the CPD and (6-4) photolyase crystal structures, with hydrogens added in HyperChem and the sugar-phosphate part of the FADH- cofactor omitted; geometries optimized at B3LYP/6-31G(d) and found to agree well with the parent PDB models, with a planar flavin ring system in every case. software: Firefly (partially based on the GAMESS US source code)
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the excitation-energy calculations; B3LYP/TZVP for the separate two-base photoproduct models

active_space_protocol: State-averaged CASSCF with EQUAL weights for all roots, using the second-order MCSCF optimization implemented in Firefly and the POCAS (principal orbital CASSCF) orbital-selection scheme. The two-electron/two-orbital space is used specifically so that closed-shell singlet and biradical states can be put on one energy scale; the corresponding broken-symmetry U-B3LYP calculations of the (6-4)II and (6-4)Int models describe the same HOMO-LUMO biradicals. nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over all roots with equal weights

compound_name: BeBr, 14 Lambda-S states and the 30 Omega states they generate
point_group: Cinfv, replaced by C2v for the calculations
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed point by point and fitted; spectroscopic parameters from the vibrational levels
method: CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (icMRCI+Q), with core-valence and scalar relativistic corrections and CBS extrapolation; spin-orbit coupling by the state-interaction approach with the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ (AVQZ) for all the potential energy curves - (22s,17p,13d,3f,2g) contracted to [8s,7p,5d,3f,2g] on Br and (13s,7p,4d,3f,2g) to [6s,5p,4d,3f,2g] on Be - with AVTZ/AVQZ CBS extrapolation (denoted TQ); cc-pVTZ for the scalar relativistic correction and all-electron cc-pCVTZ for both the core-valence and the spin-orbit calculations

active_space_orbital_description: nine outermost MOs (five a1, two b1, two b2) holding two valence electrons from the Be 2s orbital and seven from the Br 4s4p orbitals; the inner 30 electrons occupy fifteen closed-shell MOs (eight a1, three b1, three b2, one a2) corresponding to the 1-7 sigma, 1-3 pi and 1 delta MOs

The first well of A 2Pi sits at Te 26703.56 cm-1 (Re 1.9760 angstrom, measured 1.9765; omega_e 704.12, measured 702; De only 4503.80 cm-1) and its second well at 26776.43 cm-1 with Re 4.2907 angstrom and De 96.79 cm-1. Higher states: 2 2Pi 33726.89, 2 2Sigma+ second well 35284.57 and first well 47663.16, 1 4Sigma+ 45371.55, 1 4Delta 46691.25, 1 4Sigma- 47322.24, 1 2Delta 47367.01, 1 2Sigma- 47752.41, 1 4Pi 48721.17, 2 4Sigma+ 48791.18 and 3 2Sigma+ 48845.36 cm-1. Without spin-orbit coupling 3 2Pi and 2 4Pi are repulsive; with it 1 4Pi, 2 4Pi, 3 2Pi and 2 4Sigma+ are repulsive instead, A 2Pi and 2 2Sigma+ keep their double wells either way, and 1 4Sigma+, 1 4Sigma-, 1 2Pi and 2 2Pi are inverted.
Other: Two findings a reader choosing this space should carry away. First, the ninth active orbital exists only to keep the curves from breaking down at long range - the space was sized by dissociation behaviour rather than by energy accuracy, and the paper shows in supplementary figures what the A 2Pi, 1 4Pi and 2 4Sigma+ curves look like without the core-valence correction to make the same point. Second, which states are repulsive changes when spin-orbit coupling is switched on: the spin-free calculation calls 3 2Pi and 2 4Pi repulsive, the spin-orbit one calls 1 4Pi, 2 4Pi, 3 2Pi and 2 4Sigma+ repulsive, so a CAS(9,9) result read without spin-orbit coupling would misclassify two states. Basis convergence on the fixed space: AVDZ to AVTZ to AVQZ raises Te of A 2Pi by 736 cm-1, CBS adds 242 more, and the Davidson correction lowers it by up to 979 cm-1.

compound_name: s-indacene, S0 and S1 minima and the S0/S1 conical intersection
point_group: D2h; all geometry optimizations were constrained to the D2h framework symmetry
geometry_source: optimized in this work: S0 and S1 minima at CAS12/cc-pVDZ, and the same minima plus the S0/S1 conical intersection at CAS6/6-31G*, all under D2h constraint. The S0 minimum has transannular bonds of about 1.448 A; on excitation to S1 those lengthen to about 1.51 A while the 7-7a bond linking the central benzene to the outer allyl fragments compresses from about 1.42 to 1.40 A, and continuing along that coordinate reaches the conical intersection. The S1 structure has two long transannular bonds near 1.5 A and a uniform perimeter near 1.4 A. For comparison, a low-temperature X-ray structure of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative gives ring bond lengths of 1.394-1.395 and 1.434 A with no significant deviation from D2h, against MP2/6-31G* values of 1.397 and 1.429 A.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with two active spaces, plus CASPT2 single points at the CAS12 geometries correlating all electrons with no frozen core; conical intersection searches carried out at the smaller space only, since they are impractical with the full pi space. State-averaged orbitals were used for the S1 minimum and the intersection at the CAS6 level. The hybrid MMVB method - an MM2 sigma framework with the active conjugated electrons in a Heisenberg Hamiltonian over neutral valence-bond configurations, parametrized against CASSCF/4-31G - was run in parallel for comparison.
software: Gaussian for the CAS6 calculations, MOLPRO for the CAS12 calculations, and MOLCAS for the CASPT2
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CAS12 and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G* for the CAS6 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: CAS12 is the full pi valence space, twelve electrons in twelve pi molecular orbitals. CAS6, six electrons in six pi orbitals, is the smallest space found capable of describing S0 and S1 simultaneously, and it was selected by inspecting the CAS12 natural orbital occupation numbers and keeping the orbitals with fractional occupations.
active_space_protocol: (12,12) the full pi valence space, used for the S0 and S1 minima and as the CASPT2 reference; (6,6) the six pi orbitals of most fractional CAS12 occupation, selected as the smallest space describing both states at once and used for the surface exploration and the conical intersection search, which is impractical with the full space
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0 (1Ag); the excited state is B3g. Total energies in Eh at the D2h optimized geometries, given as CAS6/6-31G* / CAS12/cc-pVDZ / CASPT2/cc-pVDZ (the last at the CAS12 geometries) for S0 then S1: at the S0 minimum -459.03542 / -459.18834 / -460.62604 and -459.00339 / -459.16651 / -460.59399; at the S1 minimum -459.02292 / -459.17929 / -460.62039 and -459.00936 / -459.17657 / -460.60331; at the S0/S1 intersection, located only with CAS6, -458.99790 and -458.99658 (state-averaged orbitals). The 0-0 excitation energies come out at 16.4 kcal/mol (CAS6) and 7.4 kcal/mol (CAS12), both below the experimental near-infrared transition of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative at about 9270 cm-1, i.e. 26.5 kcal/mol; adding dynamic correlation through CASPT2 raises every computed energy difference, bringing the 0-0 value to 14.3 kcal/mol. The intersection lies about 5 kcal/mol above the S1 minimum and about 4 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon point on S1. The S0 structure has pronounced open-shell character - four allyl radical units coupled to an overall singlet - with HOMO and LUMO occupations of 1.59 and 0.45 at CAS12 and 1.79 and 0.22 at CAS6, close to a previously published 1.60 and 0.45; the S1 structure has singly occupied B2g and B1g orbitals. Experimentally the S1 lifetime of the tetra-tert-butyl derivative is 18 +/- 4 ps with a fluorescence quantum yield below about 1e-4.
Other: The active-space reduction here is done by an explicit and reusable criterion rather than by intuition: a conical intersection search with the full twelve-orbital pi space is impractical, so the CAS12 natural orbital OCCUPATION NUMBERS at the D2h structures are inspected, and the smallest space that still describes S0 and S1 simultaneously turns out to be the six orbitals carrying fractional occupations - six electrons in six pi orbitals. The reduction is then validated rather than assumed, by comparing CAS6 and CAS12 geometries and relative energies at the S0 and S1 minima before trusting CAS6 for the intersection search. What the comparison shows is that the reduction is safe for geometry and character but expensive in energy: the 0-0 excitation is 16.4 kcal/mol with the small space against 7.4 with the full one, a factor of more than two, and CASPT2 on the CAS12 reference moves it back up to 14.3, all against a measured 26.5 kcal/mol for the tetra-tert-butyl derivative. So both spaces underestimate the gap badly and the small space happens to land closer for the wrong reason. The deeper finding concerns the character of the states, and it is a warning about method rather than about space: MMVB and CASSCF both predict a conical intersection at a comparable place, but they assign S0 and S1 OPPOSITE character, disagreeing by nearly 100% in relative energies where the same comparison on styrene agreed to within 10%. The authors argue the CASSCF ordering is right but concede that with energy differences of a few kcal/mol a definitive answer needs a multireference treatment beyond what they did. The underlying reason the system is hard is visible in the occupations: the S0 minimum is not a closed shell at all but four allyl radicals singlet-coupled, with a HOMO occupation of 1.59 and a LUMO occupation of 0.45, which is also the accepted explanation for s-indacene's extreme reactivity.
reference_short: Bearpark, Blancafort, Robb and co-workers, Mol. Phys. 96, 645 (1999)
notes: The active-space columns record CAS12, the full pi valence space and the CASPT2 reference; CAS6, used for the intersection search, is in active_space_protocol. The natural orbital occupation tables (Tables 1 and 2) are misaligned in the extracted text, so only the HOMO and LUMO occupations the running text states in words are recorded. The experimental transition energy, lifetime and fluorescence yield are for the tetra-tert-butyl derivative (TTBI), not for the parent s-indacene, and the X-ray bond lengths are likewise for that derivative. The author list is taken from a running header in the extracted text and should be checked against the original if cited precisely. formula reflects the compound's identity; the paper states only the name.

point_group: C2h for the s-trans ground state; lower symmetry at excited-state minima, transition states and surface crossings
geometry_source: CASSCF(14,11)/cc-pVTZ optimized stationary points with zero-point energies at the same level; surface crossing points optimized with the reduced CASSCF(10,8)/cc-pVTZ space; minimum energy pathways computed at the CASSCF level, with B3LYP and MP2 as a complement on the lowest triplet surface
method: State-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2; conical intersection and intersystem crossing point optimization; spin-orbit coupling evaluated at the ISCs with the atomic mean field integral (AMFI) approximation and an effective one-electron Fock-type spin-orbit operator
software: MOLCAS 6.2 (CASSCF, CASPT2, SOC); Gaussian 03 (conical intersection optimizations, B3LYP, MP2)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(14,11) for the stationary points, built from the C2h ground-state configuration by taking (5ag)2, (5bu)2, (6ag)2, (1au)2, (6bu)2, (7ag)2, (1bg)2, (2au)0, (7bu)0, (8ag)0, (2bg)0. The four orbitals 1au, 1bg, 2au and 2bg all have pi character and are labelled pi1, pi2, pi3* and pi4*. A reduced CASSCF(10,8) space was used for the surface crossings, containing all the pi-type orbitals, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the N-N bond, and the two nitrogen lone-pair orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens the point with 'the selection of the active space is a crucial step for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations' and then writes the ground-state configuration out orbital by orbital before naming which entries enter the space, so the choice is fully auditable. TWO spaces are used for two purposes: the larger (14,11) for stationary points and vertical excitations, and a smaller (10,8) 'in order to get a balance between the precision and the computational cost' for locating the conical intersections and intersystem crossing points, that smaller space being defined by chemical function (all pi orbitals, the N-N sigma/sigma* pair that breaks, and both nitrogen lone pairs) rather than by energy window. The (14,11) choice is then validated against measured structure: the optimized bond parameters agree with experiment, which the authors state 'means that our selection of the active space is reliable'.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 1(1)Ag. Vertical excitations at SA-CASSCF(14,11)/cc-pVTZ then MS-CASPT2: 1(1)Au 4.01 then 3.62 eV (f = 0.00506), 1(1)Bg 5.90 then 5.46 eV (f = 0), 1(1)Bu 8.54 then 6.40 eV (f = 0.76518), 1(3)Au 3.69 then 3.39 eV, 1(3)Bu 3.25 then 3.70 eV. The 34500 cm-1 band is assigned to 1(1)Au from 1(1)Ag, principally a nitrogen lone pair to pi3* promotion; the 44150 cm-1 band to the symmetry-forbidden 1(1)Bg transition, whose observed oscillator strength of about 0.003 comes from vibronic interaction. Natural orbital occupations for 1(1)Bg are 1.97, 1.99, 2.00, 1.95, 1.78, 1.21, 1.83, 0.44, 0.03, 0.01, 0.78, from which the authors conclude the CASSCF wavefunction has multireference character. Critical points relative to the S0 minimum (CASSCF then CASPT2, eV): S1 minimum 3.02/2.32, T1 minimum 3.06/2.16, T1-NNTS 6.76/5.79, T2 minimum 2.57/2.64, T2-NNTS 3.26/3.12, two H2CN(1(2)B2) fragments 1.80/2.28, H2CN(1(2)B2) plus H2CN(1(2)B1) 6.34/5.81, and the crossings S1/S0(1) 6.51/6.14, S1/S0(2) 6.42/5.99, S1/S0(3) 3.58/2.45, S1/T1/T2 3.26/3.18. Ground-state N-N is 1.398 A, shorter than a typical 1.45 A N-N single bond, and C-N 1.288 A, slightly longer than a typical 1.25 A double bond, reflecting conjugation between the two H2CN moieties.
Other: Two things here should stop anyone reusing these numbers uncritically. First, dynamic correlation REORDERS the two lowest triplets: at SA-CASSCF T2 (1(3)Bu) lies at 3.25 eV BELOW T1 (1(3)Au) at 3.69 eV, but MS-CASPT2 pushes T2 up to 3.70 eV and T1 down to 3.39 eV, swapping them. The labels T1/T2 in Table 2 are therefore assigned on the CASSCF ordering, and the T1/T2 minima at 3.06/2.16 and 2.57/2.64 eV cross the same way. Any mechanistic statement about which triplet is reached first depends entirely on which level is trusted. Second, the largest correlation correction of all is on 1(1)Bu, which falls from 8.54 to 6.40 eV — a 2.14 eV shift, against 0.39-0.44 eV for the other singlets — so the bright state is precisely the one the CASSCF space describes worst. Reference weights are uniformly healthy (0.82-0.86), so this is a genuine correlation effect and not an intruder problem. Note also that the CASPT2 level shift is not the same across the paper: 0.2 hartree for the vertical excitations in Table 1 but 0.0 hartree for the critical points in Table 2, so the two tables are not on a common footing and their energies should not be mixed. Finally, the surface crossings were located in the smaller (10,8) space while the stationary points come from (14,11), so the crossing energies in Table 2 rest on a different space from the minima they are compared against.
reference_short: Luo, Duan, Liu & Li, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 8979
notes: Photodissociation mechanisms starting from the excited states are mapped, with the dominant channel giving two H2CN radicals. A three-surface intersection S1/T1/T2 was located where all three states meet, but the intersystem crossing route through it is found not to be energetically competitive. Spin-orbit coupling constants between singlet and triplet states were computed at the ISC geometries. Figure 1 shows stationary points with CASSCF(14e,11o) bond parameters and crossing points with CASSCF(10e,8o) parameters, with experimental values in parentheses. correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 with the same (14,11) space; level shift 0.2 hartree for the vertical excitation energies of Table 1 and 0.0 hartree for the critical point energies of Table 2.

point_group: Cs(2) ground/excited minima with comparison to Cs(1) and C1 bond-fission paths; neutral singlet reactant
geometry_source: CASSCF stationary points were optimized for S0/S1 Franck-Condon minima, three excited-state bond-fission transition states, the N-H and C-N minimum-seam crossings, and separated-product limits. Hondo 8.4 handled Franck-Condon minima, transition states, and seams; Molpro 92 handled product minima, with three unoptimizable excited products estimated from related structures. Tables 1-3 provide complete internal parameters and frequencies but no Cartesian coordinates; no XYZ is attached rather than risk an underdetermined reconstruction from the paper's specialized delta/gamma conventions.
method: CASSCF S0/S1 stationary points and seam-of-crossing optimization; MRSDCI single/double correlation with Davidson correction; one-dimensional CASSCF scans for three photodissociation channels
software: Hondo 8.4; Molpro 92; locally written Seam 1.0 driver coupling seam updates to external energy/gradient programs
basis_set: 6-31++G** stated for all calculations; Table 2 alone prints 6-31++G* in its heading, while the methods text and Tables 1/3 specify 6-31++G**
active_space_orbital_description: Franck-Condon CAS(2,5): the nitrogen lone pair plus diffuse Rydberg s, px, py, and pz orbitals. Each dissociation CAS(4,6) adds the two electrons and bonding orbital of the particular N-H, C-N, or C-H bond being ruptured. The formally preferred CAS(8,8) would include all three relevant bonds simultaneously but was computationally too large.
active_space_protocol: Ground and first excited singlet Franck-Condon structures used CAS(2,5); each bond-fission coordinate used its own CAS(4,6), adding the relevant sigma bond. Separate MRSDCI expansions built on the three CAS(4,6) references and Davidson corrections provide comparable energetics. At Franck-Condon geometries, CAS(2,5)+MRSDCI+DC closely matches CAS(4,6)+MRSDCI+DC, supporting the cross-channel comparison. All conformations, channels, S0/S1 states, seams, and estimated product geometries are consolidated in one chemical-system row; numeric fields carry the production bond-breaking CAS(4,6).
nroots_per_mult: Ground and first excited singlet surfaces; two same-spin states coupled at N-H and C-N seams
electronic_structure_description: The bright S1 state is nitrogen-lone-pair to diffuse 3s-Rydberg excitation, leaving singly occupied N lone-pair and Rydberg orbitals. Along a cleavage coordinate the Rydberg orbital mixes with the corresponding sigma* orbital. N-H and C-N channels develop S0/S1 crossings and conical intersections; the C-H channel has no such intersection. Fragment doublet states are spin-coupled on the total singlet surfaces.
Other: MRSDCI+Davidson gives a 129.8 kcal mol^-1 (5.64 eV) vertical excitation, essentially the 130.0 kcal mol^-1 experimental band maximum. N-H transition states lie below 222-nm excitation; inaccessible excited products funnel trajectories through the minimum seam (rNH=1.938 A) to ground H + CH3NH, predicting 27.5 kcal mol^-1 maximum kinetic energy versus 27 observed. C-N transition states become 2.4/4.6 kcal mol^-1 below the photon energy after ZPE; accessible excited CH3 + NH2 products mean most trajectories stay on S1, with 11.1 kcal mol^-1 predicted versus 15 observed and a residual 1-4 kcal mol^-1 MRSDCI error. The C-N seam has rCN=2.498 A. C-H S1 transition/product structures are inaccessible (TS about 21.3 kcal mol^-1 above 222 nm) and no conical intersection exists on that coordinate, so observed low-translation H + CH2NH2 arises indirectly after internal conversion to a hot S0 molecule. Calculated ground bond energies are 101.6, 85.4, and 97.2 kcal mol^-1 for N-H, C-N, and C-H, versus 102.6, 79.5, and 94.6 experiment.

geometry_source: All eight CN3- minima and key transition states were optimized/frequency-classified at B3LYP/6-311+G(d), then all minima and important transition states were reoptimized at CASSCF(12,12) with 6-311+G(d) and aug-cc-pVTZ. method: CASSCF(12,12) geometry optimization/frequencies and RS2C-CASPT2(12,12) energetics; CASSCF(8,8) minimum-energy crossing and Pauli-Breit SOC; CCSD(T)/DFT comparisons; 300 K BOMD stability test
basis_set: 6-311+G(d) and aug-cc-pVTZ for CASSCF/CASPT2; 6-311+G(d) for crossing/SOC calculations; B3LYP/6-31G(d) for BOMD
relativistic_treatment: Pauli-Breit Hamiltonian for spin-orbit coupling, including rigorous one- and two-electron terms
active_space_orbital_description: All MOs arising from the valence carbon and nitrogen p orbitals. For chain 3NCNN- in Cs, the explicitly selected orbitals are 8 a' orbitals (9a'-16a') and 4 a'' orbitals (1a''-4a''); eight lower orbitals are inactive and doubly occupied.
active_space_protocol: A common CAS(12,12) treats every singlet/triplet isomer and important transition structure equivalently, with CASSCF geometries/frequencies and modified-CASPT2 (Molpro RS2C) dynamic correlation at both basis levels. The leading triplet CI coefficient is 0.96 near equilibrium. A reduced CAS(8,8)/6-311+G(d) locates the singlet-triplet crossing and evaluates SOC; its orbital membership is not separately enumerated. The chain and connectivity-distinct tetrahedral stable candidates are separate rows, while other minima, TSs, product limits, basis variants, and dynamics frames are consolidated.
nroots_per_mult: Lowest singlet and triplet surfaces for crossings; exact root averaging/weights not stated
electronic_structure_description: The global isomer is an open-shell 3A'' chain resonating between N=C-N=N- and N=C=N-N- valence patterns, with two delocalized pi sets over internal C-N bonding and localized p orbitals on C-N/N-N. B3LYP Wiberg indices are 2.544, 1.331, and 1.427 for terminal C-N, internal C-N, and N-N; the corresponding B3LYP distances are 1.182, 1.301, and 1.292 A.
Other: CASPT2(12,12)/aug-cc-pVTZ sets 3NCNN- at -201.94196493 Eh and zero relative energy. Direct triplet dissociation to 3CN-+1N2 is endothermic by 87.4 kcal mol^-1 and has no triplet TS. A lower spin-change route reaches a CASSCF(8,8) crossing about 20.6 kcal mol^-1 above the chain; the crossing has C-N 1.191/1.256 A, N-N 1.367 A, angles 179.8/120.2 degrees, and only 23.9 cm^-1 SOC, making ISC unlikely. A 300 K B3LYP/6-31G(d) BOMD trajectory retains the chain for at least 100 ps. Of five triplet minima and three singlet minima found globally, most alternatives have <5 kcal mol^-1 rearrangement barriers or sub-0.2-ps lifetimes and are not split into durable compound rows. Carbon doping reverses the instability of the isoelectronic chain N4 triplet.

method: CASSCF(12,12) geometry optimization/frequencies and RS2C-CASPT2(12,12) potential energies; CASSCF singlet-triplet crossing and CAS(8,8) Pauli-Breit SOC; CCSD(T)/DFT comparison; 300 K BOMD

relativistic_treatment: Pauli-Breit Hamiltonian for SOC with rigorous one- and two-electron terms

active_space_protocol: Common CAS(12,12) CASSCF geometries and RS2C-CASPT2 energies treat the entire singlet/triplet PES consistently at 6-311+G(d) and aug-cc-pVTZ. The leading CI coefficient is 0.94, supporting a multireference treatment. The 1A'/3A'' crossing uses CASSCF(12,12) geometry/energy, while SOC at that geometry is reported from CAS(8,8); the smaller orbital list is not specified. One tetrahedral connectivity row consolidates singlet isomerization, fragmentation, crossings, method variants, and dynamics frames.

electronic_structure_description: This high-energy C3v isomer is analogous to tetrahedral N4 but contains a carbon vertex and triangular N3 base. Its reactant configuration differs from the 1CN-+1N2 product configuration, and the spin-allowed dissociation TS mixes the two, making two-bond fragmentation orbital-symmetry forbidden. The equilibrium leading CI coefficient of 0.94 confirms non-negligible multireference character.
Other: Best CASPT2(12,12)/aug-cc-pVTZ energy is -201.83967532 Eh, 64.2 kcal mol^-1 above triplet chain 3NCNN-. Concerted dissociation through 1TS6/P1 lies at -201.77237323 Eh (106.4 relative to the triplet ground), hence a 42.2 kcal mol^-1 barrier; ring isomerization via TS5/6 is about 45 kcal mol^-1. Fragmentation releases 136.8 kcal mol^-1 at the CCSD(T) comparison level. The CASSCF(12,12) singlet-triplet crossing lies only 1.3 kcal mol^-1 above the singlet dissociation TS but is off the minimum-energy path; its geometry has C-N 1.381/1.581/1.581 A and N-N 1.293 A, and CAS(8,8) SOC is only 18.5 cm^-1, so ISC does not lower the operative barrier. A 300 K BOMD trajectory retains the structure for at least 25 ps. Carbon doping therefore leaves a ~42 kcal mol^-1 effective barrier, larger than the ~28 kcal mol^-1 ISC-limited stability of tetrahedral N4.

geometry_source: Potential curves giving Re, De, omega_e, the dipole moment and its derivative
method: State-averaged CASSCF, then MRCI(SD) with single and double excitations from all CASSCF configurations, with the Langhoff-Davidson size-consistency correction (+Q) estimating quadruple excitations
basis_set: the WB-MEFIT and HF-MEFIT pseudopotentials with their optimized (8s7p6d)/[6s5p3d] GTO valence basis sets, and the Hay-Wadt and LaJohn relativistic effective core potentials with their uncontracted optimized (5s5p4d) sets; all augmented with a single f function of exponent 3.0
relativistic_treatment: 16-electron energy-adjusted pseudopotentials, quasirelativistic (WB-MEFIT) and nonrelativistic (HF-MEFIT), compared with the Hay-Wadt and LaJohn relativistic effective core potentials
active_space_orbital_description: the molecular orbitals derived from the metal nd and (n+1)s atomic orbitals - 4d and 5s for Ru, 5d and 6s for Os - together with the hydrogen 1s; the same space is used for the CASSCF and for the subsequent correlation treatment
nroots_per_mult: seven low-lying states: 4Sigma-, 4Pi, 4Delta, 4Phi, 6Sigma+, 6Pi and 6Delta. The CASSCF expansions run to about 120 configurations; the MRCI(SD) expansions to 580000-770000 configurations for the quartets and 96000-170000 for the sextets
electronic_structure_description: Seven low-lying states computed - 4Sigma-, 4Pi, 4Delta, 4Phi, 6Sigma+, 6Pi and 6Delta - with term energies compared at CASSCF, MRCI(SD) and MRCI(SD)+Q levels for each pseudopotential. All three relativistically corrected pseudopotentials give a qualitatively similar picture with only minor differences, and both the nonrelativistic HF-MEFIT pseudopotential and the relativistic effective core potentials give 4Sigma- as the ground state, agreeing with the experimental assignment.
Other: The state ordering is the quantity of interest and it moves between CASSCF, MRCI(SD) and MRCI(SD)+Q on the same seven-orbital space, which is why all three levels are plotted rather than the last alone. That the ground state comes out 4Sigma- with a nonrelativistic pseudopotential as well as with three relativistic ones means the assignment is not being carried by the relativistic treatment. State averaging is used here for a specific structural reason rather than for balance alone: it allows the pi orbitals of Pi states and the delta orbitals of Delta states to be treated under an equivalence restriction in C2v, where the two components would otherwise be inequivalent. The space itself is the minimal chemically meaningful one - metal nd and (n+1)s plus the hydrogen 1s, seven orbitals - and it is kept identical across every pseudopotential being compared, which is what makes the comparison a test of the potentials rather than of the reference. The accuracy limits are stated at the atomic level: with the quasirelativistic WB-MEFIT pseudopotential the Ru 4d7 5s1 5F to Ru+ 4d7 4F ionization potential comes out 6.73 eV against a spin-orbit-averaged experimental 7.37, and the Os 5d6 6s2 5D to Os+ 6s1 6D ionization potential 7.57 eV against 8.77.
reference_short: Andrae, Haussermann, Dolg, Stoll & Preuss, Theor. Chim. Acta 77, 123-141 (1990)
notes: Active electron count is arithmetic from the stated composition: the metal nd and (n+1)s valence electrons - eight for both Ru (4d7 5s1) and Os (5d6 6s2) - plus the hydrogen 1s electron. d_electron_count reflects the free-atom configuration; the paper assigns no formal oxidation state. CASSCF over-stabilizes DIR-11 below reactant and underestimates the barrier by about 15 kcal/mol; CASPT2 dynamic correlation raises it and gives near-degenerate one- and two-step barriers, slightly favoring the two-step route. Planar excited states, with P-P and P-H bond lengths in angstrom, HPP angle in degrees and MRD-CI energy relative to trans 1Ag in kJ/mol, and 0 or 1 marking an energy minimum or maximum along the torsion - cis: 3B2 (pi-pi*) 2.284 / 1.408 / 97.8 / 191 (max), 3A2 (n+-pi*) 2.228 / 1.408 / 99.8 / 314 (min), 3B1 (n--pi*) 1.987 / 1.397 / 121.5 / 354 (min), 1A2 (n+-pi*) 2.248 / 1.408 / 101.0 / 368 (min), 1B1 (n--pi*) 2.000 / 1.417 / 117.7 / 417 (max), 1B2 (pi-pi*) 2.216 / 1.406 / 98.7 / 486 (max); trans: 3Bu (pi-pi*) 2.272 / 1.408 / 94.3 / 182 (max), 3Bg (n+-pi*) 2.094 / 1.398 / 105.6 / 236 (min), 1Bg (n+-pi*) 2.118 / 1.401 / 105.6 / 298 (max), 3Au (n--pi*) 2.123 / 1.406 / 104.9 / 471 (min), 1Bu (pi-pi*) 2.207 / 1.406 / 94.7 / 470 (max), 1Au (n--pi*) 2.130 / 1.419 / 105.0 / 479 (min). point_group: D2h for the computation, with D_infh symmetry imposed on the orbitals

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by MRCI using all the CASSCF configurations as references; Einstein coefficients and radiative lifetimes derived from the transition moments

active_space_protocol: the doublets and quartets listed were averaged separately, with equal weight given to every state in the CASSCF except the 2Delta_g state, which is doubly weighted because it appears in two D2h irreducible representations. Imposing D_infh on the orbitals while computing in D2h keeps the degenerate components equivalent
electronic_structure_description: The states studied lie below about 40,000 cm-1 and include those dissociating to the ground-state asymptote, the quartets dissociating to Al 4P(3s1 3p2) at 29,000 cm-1, and doublets and quartets dissociating to Al+ 3P(3s1 3p1) near 37,000 cm-1. The D 2Delta_g, E 2Pi_g, F 2Sigma_u- and H 2Sigma_u- states come from the same excited asymptote as G 2Sigma_u+, differing only in how the two 3p electrons are distributed among the 3p orbitals: D, E and F have both in bonding orbitals and are more strongly bound than H, which has one bonding and one antibonding electron. Einstein coefficients are given for the A 2Pi_u to X 2Sigma_g+, E 2Delta_g to A 2Pi_u, G 2Sigma_u+ to X 2Sigma_g+ and H 2Sigma_u- to A 2Pi_u systems. None of the transitions involving X 2Sigma_g+ is ideal for experimental observation. Radiative lifetimes are of order 0.1 microseconds and increase slightly with v', because the transition moment falls rapidly with increasing r.
Other: The doubled weight on 2Delta_g is the detail worth carrying: a Delta state splits across two irreducible representations in D2h, so equal per-representation weighting would silently give it half the weight of every Sigma state in the average and bias the orbitals. Imposing D_infh on the orbitals while working in the Abelian subgroup is the other half of the same fix. Both matter here because the object of the calculation is transition probabilities between state pairs, which are only as balanced as the common orbital set they are computed from.

active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals, the full valence space made up of the valence atomic sp orbitals of the two carbons and the nitrogen plus the hydrogen 1s, comprising ten a' and three a'' orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A full-valence complete active space: the wave function includes all excitations of the valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals corresponding to the valence atomic sp orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms and the 1s orbital of hydrogen, namely ten a' and three a'' orbitals. The same active orbitals were used for all three charge states, with the active electron count increased by one for the anion and decreased by one for the cation. Oscillator strengths are defined as f = 2(TDM)^2 dE/3, with transition dipole moments computed at CASSCF and the excitation energies, described as very sensitive to dynamic correlation, computed at CASPT2.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 3A''. Table 1 gives geometries, leading configurations and adiabatic energies at CASSCF and CASPT2 for ten states. X 3A'': R(CH) 1.063, R(CC) 1.372, R(CN) 1.184 Angstrom, angles 175.6 and 137.5 degrees, coefficient -0.939, 0.000 and 0.000 eV. 1A': 1.114, 1.413, 1.173, 174.1, 107.6, coefficient 0.930, 0.702 and 0.738 eV. 1A'': 1.057, 1.319, 1.203, 176.2, 155.6, -0.940, 1.365 and 0.932 eV. 2 1Sigma+ (2 1A'): 1.054, 1.293, 1.219, both angles 180.0, 0.936, 2.041 and 1.556 eV. 2 1A'': 1.063, 1.350, 1.304, 168.4, 135.4, three configurations with coefficients -0.435, -0.428 and 0.504, 3.822 and 3.315 eV. 2 3A'': 1.098, 1.366, 1.300, 161.6, 121.5, 0.821, 4.071 and 3.579 eV. 3A': 1.102, 1.377, 1.288, 167.7, 116.6, 0.930, 4.204 and 3.896 eV. 2 3A': 1.080, 1.322, 1.296, 173.2, 144.8, coefficients 0.448 and 0.833, 4.750 and 4.252 eV. 3 1A': 1.099, 1.403, 1.305, 119.6, 129.4, coefficients 0.341 and 0.809, 5.307 and 4.824 eV. 3 1A'': 1.097, 1.381, 1.202, 166.2, 119.7, -0.904, 5.487 and 5.074 eV. Every state shares a common core configuration not tabulated. Table 3 gives CASPT2 vertical energies at the ground-state geometry with oscillator strengths for eleven states: 1A' 0.938 eV, 1A'' 1.113, 2 1A' 2.329, 2 1A'' 3.850, all with f below 1e-10; 2 3A'' 4.179 eV with f 0.0148; 3A' 4.395 with 0.000180; 3 3A'' 4.579 with 0.0143, assigned to 7a' to 9a'; 2 3A' 4.727 with 0.000908; 3 3A' 5.056 with 0.00597, assigned to 1a'' to 9a', 2a'' to 11a' and 8a' to 2a''; 3 1A'' 5.274 and 3 1A' 5.397, both below 1e-10. The singlet-triplet splitting is calculated at 17.0 kcal/mol, 0.738 eV, compared with the experimental value and with the much smaller triplet-singlet gap of CH2 carbene at 0.392 plus or minus 0.002 eV.
Other: The active space is a full-valence space, defined once and then carried unchanged across all three charge states -- the same active orbitals were chosen for the anion and cation as for the neutral radical, with the active electron count simply increased or decreased by one. That is the cleanest possible arrangement for the quantities this paper reports, because ionization potentials and detachment energies are differences of total energies between charge states, and any change in the orbital set between them would contaminate those differences with a change of reference rather than a change of physics. The space is fourteen valence electrons in thirteen molecular orbitals for the neutral, corresponding to the valence atomic sp orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms plus the hydrogen 1s, comprising ten a' and three a'' orbitals under the assumed planar Cs symmetry; the anion carries fifteen electrons and the cation thirteen in the same thirteen orbitals. Because it is the full valence space, no orbital-selection judgement is involved and there is nothing to converge -- the only remaining question is dynamic correlation, and the paper is explicit that comparing the CASSCF and CASPT2 energies shows the dynamical correlation effect must be considered. The magnitude is large and state-dependent, which is the substantive active-space-related finding here: for the neutral, CASSCF and CASPT2 adiabatic energies are 0.702 against 0.738 eV for the 1A' state, essentially agreeing, but 2.041 against 1.556 eV for the 2 1Sigma+ state, 3.822 against 3.315 for 2 1A'', and 5.307 against 4.824 for 3 1A' -- shifts approaching half an electronvolt that reorder nothing but change every transition energy well beyond spectroscopic tolerance. So a full valence space is a necessary but not sufficient reference here; the authors correspondingly compute transition moments at CASSCF but excitation energies, which they describe as very sensitive to dynamic correlation, at CASPT2, mixing the two levels within a single oscillator strength. A second point concerns what the space has to accommodate. The states are far from uniformly single-reference: for the neutral, 2 1A'' is described by three configurations with coefficients -0.435, -0.428 and 0.504, 2 3A' by 0.448 and 0.833, and 3 1A' by 0.341 and 0.809, while the ground state sits at -0.939. For the cation the authors state the criterion explicitly, noting that the leading-configuration coefficients for X 2A', 2Pi(2A''), 4Pi(4A') and 4A' are all above 0.90, indicating single-reference character, while the other states show obviously multireference character. A space that could not have carried those multiple configurations would have failed selectively, on exactly the excited states the paper is about. Finally, a caveat on the geometries the space was optimized under: all states of all three species were assumed to have planar Cs symmetry, and several stationary points turn out not to be minima under that assumption. The 2 2A' state of the anion has an imaginary frequency of 474.3i and is unstable, and linear configurations of both ions carry imaginary bending frequencies that resolve into Renner-Teller pairs -- for the cation, X 2A' and 2Pi(2A'') are separated by only 0.009 eV, degenerate at linearity. Energies read from this table are therefore tied to a symmetry assumption that the vibrational analysis partly contradicts.

point_group: D2d minimum and D2h conformer (D2d treated in the C2v Abelian subgroup for CASSCF/CASPT2)
geometry_source: CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations used TPSS-optimized geometries from Gaussian 03. TPSS employed an SDD small-core pseudopotential/basis for Ce and cc-pVDZ for C/H. The D2-constrained optimization relaxed to D2d and was a minimum; D2h had one imaginary frequency (i35.9 cm^-1) and lay 0.13 eV above D2d at TPSS. Reported D2d metrics are Ce-C(br) 2.50 A, Ce-C(alpha) 2.72 A, Ce-C(beta) 2.86 A, mean Ce-C 2.70 A, ligand fold 25.6 degrees, and twist 90.04 degrees.
method: CASSCF(12,16) followed by CASPT2 energies for the two lowest singlet and triplet roots of every working-point-group irrep; IVO-RHF input orbitals; natural-orbital occupation and f-density analysis; transition oscillator strength at CASPT2
basis_set: All-electron ANO: Ce (25s22p15d11f)/[9s8p5d4f], approximately cc-pVQZ quality; C and H ANO sets of cc-pVDZ quality
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian with all-electron ANO basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: The active space contains six initially occupied and ten initially virtual IVO-RHF orbitals. It extends the earlier cerocene CAS(8,14) by adding the higher-lying ligand pi1 level because the pi2-pi1 gap falls to 1.17 eV (D2d) or 1.06 eV (D2h). It explicitly includes the relevant ligand pi1/pi2 manifold and permits occupation of any of twelve Ce 4f/5d levels. D2d/C2v active occupied counts are A1=2, A2=2, B1=1, B2=1 and active virtual counts 2,2,3,3. D2h active occupied counts are Ag=1, B1g=1, B2g=1, B3g=0, Au=1, B1u=1, B2u=0, B3u=1 and active virtual counts 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2.
active_space_protocol: For D2d, MOLCAS calculations used C2v while orbital mixing newly allowed by symmetry reduction was monitored and eliminated. For both conformers, compact input virtuals came from the improved-virtual-orbital RHF procedure. The two lowest singlet and triplet roots of each irrep were computed: 16 states for D2d/C2v and 32 for D2h. Ground-state state-average sizes from one through six were tested; natural occupations were substantially more stable than configuration weights. CASPT2 frozen-orbital counts were D2d/C2v A1=17, A2=4, B1=9, B2=9 and D2h Ag=11, B1g=3, B2g=4, B3g=4, Au=1, B1u=6, B2u=5, B3u=5. Spin-orbit coupling was explicitly neglected as expected to be weak from prior CeCOT2 work.
nroots_per_mult: D2d/C2v: 8 singlet and 8 triplet roots; D2h: 16 singlet and 16 triplet roots; two roots per irrep and multiplicity (24 roots per multiplicity across both conformers)
electronic_structure_description: The D2d conformer has a strongly multiconfigurational 1A1 ground state. Conical intersections between the bright excited singlet and the ground state were located at both multireference levels. Two hundred trajectories were launched from the bright state, with maximum simulation times of 300 femtoseconds in vacuum and 350 femtoseconds in water, using 821 explicit water molecules in the solution simulations and a 0.5 femtosecond time step. In the gas phase the excited state is completely depopulated within 225 femtoseconds, and fitting gives a latency of 49.5 femtoseconds before decay begins, a decay constant of 55.2 femtoseconds and a total excited-state lifetime of 104.7 femtoseconds, comparable to the 85.5 femtoseconds of the hypoxanthine keto-N9H analogue. In water the corresponding fit gives a fractional weight of 0.291, a latency of 217.6 femtoseconds, a decay constant of 25.2 femtoseconds and a total lifetime of 242.8 femtoseconds. The decay constant is therefore larger in the gas phase than in solution, 55.2 against 25.2 femtoseconds, while the latency increases substantially from 49.5 to 217.6 femtoseconds on going into water. Of the trajectories run in water only 59 return to the ground state within the 350 femtosecond simulation. Both computed lifetimes are consistent with the experimental observation of sub-200 femtosecond decay in aqueous solution.
Other: The authors state the ideal space and then explain exactly what they gave up and why, which is the most useful form this information can take. Ideally the space should include all p orbitals perpendicular to the molecular plane, requiring twelve electrons in ten pi orbitals; to reduce cost they used ten electrons in eight orbitals instead, on the stated grounds that the two electrons and two pi orbitals omitted have the least effect on the conjugation interaction and on the selected low-lying states. So the truncation is justified by an argument about which orbitals matter for the specific states being followed, not by a general claim of adequacy, and the reader is told precisely which orbitals were dropped. The space that is used comprises the oxygen lone pair of the carbonyl moiety together with pi orbitals, which is what allows both the bright pi-pi-star state and the nearby n-pi-star state, predicted to lie 0.24 eV higher, to be represented in the same reference. What makes this record more than a truncation note is that the reduced space carries the entire dynamical result. Two hundred surface-hopping trajectories were propagated on a two-state averaged reference with this space, in vacuum and embedded in 821 explicit water molecules, and the excited-state lifetimes extracted from them are the paper's principal quantity. Those lifetimes are 104.7 femtoseconds in the gas phase, decomposing into a 49.5 femtosecond latency before decay begins and a 55.2 femtosecond decay constant, against 242.8 femtoseconds in water with a 217.6 femtosecond latency and a much shorter 25.2 femtosecond decay constant. The solvent thus more than quadruples the latency while halving the decay time, and the two effects are separately resolved only because the same space was used in both environments. Any error the truncation introduces sits in the surface topography that determines those numbers, and it cannot be corrected afterwards the way an energy can. Consistent with that, the perturbative correction is applied only to gas-phase excitation energies and not to the dynamics, so the trajectories run on uncorrected surfaces throughout. The conical intersection between the bright state and the ground state was optimized both at the multiconfigurational level and with a single-excitation multireference configuration interaction treatment, giving an independent check on the crossing geometry that the dynamics depends on. And in solution the multiconfigurational region is embedded in a molecular mechanics environment, so the active space describes a solute inside a classical bath rather than a supermolecular cluster, with the geometry optimization in solution performed at a density functional level instead.

compound_name: parent Diels-Alder reaction system: 1,3-butadiene + ethylene -> cyclohexene, with vinylcyclobutane side channel
ligand_set: 1,3-butadiene + ethylene reactant pair; concerted and anti-/gauche-diradical pathways to cyclohexene plus diradical side pathway to vinylcyclobutane
geometry_source: Reactants, products, minima, and transition states were optimized on the unmodified PES and force-modified G-FMPES at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** using custom FIRE optimization and climbing-image NEB. The article provides labeled molecular drawings and selected C-C bond lengths but no complete Cartesian coordinates, so no structure file is claimed.
method: CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** generalized force-modified potential-energy surfaces with FIRE geometry optimization, climbing-image nudged elastic band minimum-energy paths/transition states, Hessian/ZPE analysis, and harmonic transition-state-theory yield estimates
software: AIMS-MOLPRO for all electronic-structure calculations, using MOLPRO version 2012.1; custom Python routines coupled to MOLPRO for G-FMPES structure optimization
basis_set: 6-31G** for CASSCF; 6-311++G** for the parallel B3LYP comparison
active_space_orbital_description: The source specifies CASSCF(6,6) but does not identify or plot the six active orbitals; an orbital assignment is therefore not inferred.
active_space_protocol: The same CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G** model was used for the concerted path, the open-shell anti- and gauche-diradical paths, and the vinylcyclobutane side path. The paper explicitly invokes singlet<->triplet switching for diradical mechanisms, but does not report root counts, state-average weights, occupation restrictions, or state-specific/state-averaged implementation details. External force on atom j was defined as f_ext(j)=P_HP[r(j)-c], with negative P_HP compressive and c the geometric centroid; this places all atoms in a common three-dimensional parabolic potential. Stationary points were optimized by FIRE and paths/transition states by CI-NEB. Hessians gave six numerical zero modes at minima and one imaginary frequency at each saddle. ZPE is included in tabulated activation/reaction energies unless the figure caption explicitly says otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: At zero external force, the CASSCF concerted route has ZPE-corrected activation/reaction energies of 45.5/-21.2 kcal/mol (B3LYP comparison 24.3/-27.6; experiment 27.5+/-2/-40.0). For the anti-diradical route, the zero-force barriers are 44.0 kcal/mol for diradical formation and 3.9 kcal/mol from anti-diradical to cyclohexene; anti is 0.4 kcal/mol below gauche. The overall gauche route is 46.3 kcal/mol: first-step barrier 41.4, intermediate only 0.9 below that transition state, and second-step barrier 5.8. Anti-route overall activation energies at P_HP=0,-0.31,-0.63,-1.25 kcal mol^-1 A^-2 are 44.0,43.6,43.0,44.3 kcal/mol. At P_HP<=-2.51 the anti minimum catastrophically merges toward cyclohexene; at the smallest tested compression (-0.31), the gauche minimum instead disappears toward vinylcyclobutane. The CASSCF concerted barrier falls with compression but does not vanish over the tested range, unlike B3LYP below -3.45.
Other: For the vinylcyclobutane side path, exact CASSCF activation/reaction energies (kcal/mol) at P_HP=0,-0.31,-0.63,-0.94,-1.25 are 42.4/+2.0, 38.1/-4.0, 35.8/-7.8, 48.4/-9.4, and 46.3/-11.9. The nonmonotonic barrier accompanies a switch in which C-C bond forms first; a persistent path kink was not removed by varying NEB spring constants over an order of magnitude, and its origin remained unknown. Under simplifying hTST assumptions (irreversible reactions, unit reactant concentration, equal prefactors, no cyclohexene<->vinylcyclobutane interconversion), the predicted vinylcyclobutane/cyclohexene yield ratios at P_HP=0,-0.63,-1.25 are 13.18,1.95,6.34e-12 at 300 K and 3.78,1.49,1.87e-7 at 500 K. Converting the force model by mean force divided by mean enclosing-sphere area gives about 68-1410 MPa for P_HP=-0.31 to -5.02. For the concerted CASSCF path, estimated reactant/TS/product pressures (MPa) are 68.4/81.7/83.4, 150.6/164.5/167.9, 230.6/248.8/252.5, 314.3/332.5/338.5, 484.8/504.4/511.6, 659.0/678.4/686.8, 838.0/856.2/864.2, 1022.8/1037.0/1043.7, and 1397.6/1406.6/1409.1 at the nine listed compressions. The authors emphasize trends rather than benchmark absolute energies: compression lowers the desired concerted barrier, generally raises exothermicity, and at high force suppresses the vinylcyclobutane yield. Spin crossing is described at the PES/path level; no SOC or spin-spin calculation is reported.

method: embedded-cluster CASSCF followed by CASPT2 and then a spin-orbit treatment, giving the 4f and 5d level structure and the relative oscillator strengths of the transitions between them. The cluster's surroundings are represented out to 10 A by several hundred ab initio model potentials and beyond that by tens of thousands of point charges at lattice sites generated by Lepetit's method.
relativistic_treatment: not stated beyond the spin-orbit treatment and the model potentials used for the embedding
soc_included: yes, applied on top of the correlated wavefunctions; it raises every 5d level by about 1000 cm-1 and splits the 4f manifold into the two expected multiplet groups
active_space_orbital_description: the cerium 4f, 5d and 6s shells - thirteen orbitals holding the single 4f electron
active_space_protocol: the space is the whole one-electron manifold the spectroscopy lives in, so every 4f and 5d level appears on the same footing and none is privileged; with one electron there is nothing to select and the space is fixed by the ion rather than by judgement. What is judged is what surrounds it - the cluster boundary, the model potentials and the point-charge field - and what is correlated afterwards: the cerium 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the oxygen 2s and 2p electrons.
electronic_structure_description: With spin-orbit coupling the seven 4f levels split into two groups about 2400 cm-1 apart, at 0, 642, 1416, 2290, 2772, 3336 and 3931 cm-1, matching the 2F(5/2) and 2F(7/2) multiplets; without it they span only 0 to 2153 cm-1. The five 5d levels fall at 30901, 33234, 37736, 41157 and 53388 cm-1 - 324, 301, 265, 243 and 187 nm - with relative oscillator strengths of 1.00, 0.18, 0.32, 0.02 and 0.12; without spin-orbit coupling each sits about 1000 cm-1 lower. The lowest 4f-to-5d transition is 18439 cm-1 below the free-ion value of 49340 cm-1. compound_name: Tetrachloridodioxidouranate(VI) ion, [UO2Cl4]2-, the complex anion of cesium uranyl chloride
ligand_set: two axial oxido ligands forming the linear uranyl unit and four equatorial chlorides
geometry_source: Geometries imposed by hand rather than optimized - the U-O distance is scanned sequentially over 1.75-1.80 angstrom and the U-Cl distance over 2.40-2.68 angstrom, the ranges expected under the applied pressures; the experimental crystal structure is used for the one validation point against measured charge density
method: CASSCF wave functions used to generate electron densities for a quantum-theory-of-atoms-in-molecules topological analysis, and to produce molecular orbital plots for comparison against density functional ones; scalar-relativistic PBE0 supplies the starting orbitals
software: ORCA 4.0 for the electronic-structure calculations; AIMAll for the topological analysis
basis_set: SARC-TZVP on uranium and def2-TZVP on all other atoms, as stated for the density functional step that supplies the starting orbitals; the text does not separately state the basis for the correlated step
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by a criterion rather than a count: the f and d orbitals of uranium 'that had significant bonding with the O atoms'. No number of electrons or orbitals is given anywhere in the body text, nor which specific f and d orbitals qualified. Orbitals from a preceding scalar-relativistic hybrid density functional calculation are used as the starting wave function. Note that the selection criterion references the U-O bond while the conclusion concerns U-Cl covalency, so the space is aligned with one side of the comparison. No perturbative correction, no root count, no multiplicities, no state averaging, no IPEA or level shift is reported. The resulting wave functions are used solely to generate densities for a topological atoms-in-molecules analysis and to produce orbital plots.
electronic_structure_description: The uranyl(VI) ion with four equatorial chlorides, formally 5f0 and closed shell, whose short strongly covalent axial U-O bonds dominate its chemistry. The question addressed is how those axial bonds respond to compression of the equatorial U-Cl bonds. Covalency is quantified by the covalency degree, the total energy density per electron at the bond critical point. Validating against experiment at the crystal geometry gives -0.92 hartree/angstrom for the calculated U-O covalency degree against -0.93 from the measured charge density. Across the scans, shortening U-O makes the U-O covalency degree linearly more negative, while shortening U-Cl changes the U-O covalency degree only very slightly - the basis for the claim that the uranyl bond is almost unaffected by the equatorial bond and that earlier density functional work overestimated the coupling. The orbital comparison behind that claim is qualitative: density functional orbitals show significantly more chloride involvement than the CASSCF ones, attributed to the known tendency of density functional methods to overdelocalize.
Other: What the multireference calculation actually produced is far less than the abstract implies. The abstract credits 'ab initio wave function methods (CASSCF)' with supporting the claim that the uranyl bond is sensitive to its own length but negligibly affected by the U-Cl length. In fact the CASSCF supplies no energies, no excited states and no spectroscopy. Its entire output is a set of wave functions handed to a topological electron-density analysis, plus orbital pictures compared side by side against density functional ones. Every quantitative result in the paper - the Raman shift with pressure, the linear fall in fluorescence intensity, the lifetime dropping from 627 to 137 microseconds, the separated radiative and nonradiative rates, the quantum yield - is measured. The multiconfigurational calculation contributes exactly one negative claim: that the earlier published density functional work overestimated the influence of the U-Cl bond on the U-O bond. Nothing about the pressure behaviour itself is computed. The active-space issue is that the selection criterion is tied to one of the two bonds being compared. The space is specified by a procedure rather than a count: 'the active spaces selected included the f and d orbitals of the U atom that had significant bonding with the O atoms.' The orbitals were therefore chosen for their U-O bonding significance, and the conclusion drawn is about U-Cl covalency. A space assembled from uranium f and d orbitals selected by their overlap with the oxo oxygens is not one in which U-Cl bonding is guaranteed to be representable, so the observation that CASSCF orbitals show less chloride involvement than density functional orbitals partly reflects what the space was allowed to contain rather than an independent verdict on covalency. What may legitimately be inferred is that the two methods place different amounts of chloride character in the frontier orbitals; what may not be inferred without the missing details is that the CASSCF value is the converged one. And the missing details are extensive. Pressure cannot enter such a model at all; it enters only as the hand-chosen bond lengths. The proposed physical explanation for the quenching - increased nonradiative relaxation through phonon modes - is by construction outside anything the molecular calculation can address, and is offered as inference from the measured rates. active_space_orbital_description: the minimal space holds the two singly occupied d-x-squared-minus-y-squared-based magnetic orbitals. The six-electron eight-orbital space adds the two doubly occupied d-z-squared-based orbitals and four virtual 4d-based orbitals.
