active_space_protocol: The paper is a systematic study of how the active space and the orbitals chosen for it control a computed exchange coupling, and it is worth recording in detail. The minimal space is two electrons in the two singly occupied metal-d-based magnetic orbitals. Three enlargements were tested on the first complex: adding the two doubly occupied and four virtual d-z-squared- and d-based orbitals gives six electrons in eight orbitals - and the paper notes the d-z-squared orbitals must be included or the calculation will not converge to the intended solution; adding four acetate pi orbitals gives ten in twelve; adding four acetate sigma orbitals instead gives a different ten in twelve. Equally important is the choice of orbitals within the minimal space: state-specific and 50/50-averaged orbitals give couplings far too small, while orbitals from a 70/30 average of the two lowest singlets, which have substantially larger delocalization tails onto the bridging ligands, do much better and are cheaper than any enlargement. electronic_structure_description: The ground state is the singlet of an antiferromagnetically coupled copper pair. point_group: C-infinity-v, treated in the C2v subgroup

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by MRCI with the Davidson correction, for doublet and quartet states; the same curves were then recomputed by the R-matrix scattering method for comparison
software: MOLPRO, driven through the GABEDIT interface; Quantemol-EC, built on UKRmol+, for the R-matrix calculations; LEVEL 8.2 for Franck-Condon factors
basis_set: all-electron cc-pV5Z (s, p, d) on Li and the Ahlrichs-Cfit set (s, p, d) on H
active_space_orbital_description: 32 orbitals distributed over the C2v irreducible representations as [16, 7, 7, 2] - 16 sigma (Li 2s, 2p0, 3s, 3p0, 3d0, 3d+2, 4s, 4p0, 4d0, 4d+2, 5s, 5p0, 6s and H 1s, 2s, 2p0), 7 pi (Li 2p+/-1, 3p+/-1, 3d+/-1, 4p+/-1, 4d+/-1, 5p+/-1 and H 2p+/-1) and 2 delta (Li 3d-2, 4d-2)
active_space_protocol: the space is built by listing atomic orbitals rather than by an electron count, and it is very large relative to the number of electrons - a deliberate consequence of the problem, since an anion this weakly bound needs diffuse orbital space to be described at all. That same generosity is what creates the difficulty the paper is really about: with enough diffuse orbitals a bound-state calculation will produce curves that are not bound states of the anion but the neutral molecule plus a free electron, and the active space cannot distinguish them.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state X 2Sigma+ with Re 1.664 A, omega_e 1223.8 cm-1, Be 6.929 cm-1, De 19,464 cm-1 and dipole moment 1.213 a.u.; literature values for Re span 1.594 to 1.772 A and for De 15,146 to 16,647 cm-1, so the dissociation energy here is high by an average of 17.4 per cent while the bond length agrees to within 0.1 to 6.1 per cent. The electron affinity of 0.244 eV is positive, confirming the ground state is stable, and the equilibrium dipole moment reaches 5.10 D, well above the 2.5 D threshold for dipole binding of an excess electron. The percentage ionic character of the ground state is 38 per cent, so the bond is predominantly covalent.
Other: The paper's headline finding is a warning about its own method as applied to this molecule. Comparing the bound-state curves against R-matrix resonance curves taken from the literature shows that the MCSCF/MRCI excited states of LiH- may be spurious - representations of the neutral-molecule-plus-free-electron continuum rather than genuine anion states. The diagnostic offered is that a resonance curve following the avoided crossings of the adiabatic curves, and adiabatic curves that approach the neutral ground state as the basis is enlarged, both signal continuum contamination. Only the ground state escapes this doubt, which is why it alone carries tabulated constants here while the sibling anions get full state manifolds.

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCI, with spin-orbit coupling included by diagonalizing the SO Hamiltonian in the basis of MRCI eigenstates; vibronic spectra simulated from the SO-coupled curves. TD-DFT (CAM-B3LYP) for comparison
basis_set: Au 19-electron relativistic MDF60 effective core potential with a (12s12p9d3f2g)/[6s6p4d3f2g] basis; MDF60 SO-pseudopotentials for the SO operator; 5s/5p cores frozen
relativistic_treatment: scalar-relativistic 19e MDF60 ECP plus explicit spin-orbit coupling (omega-omega coupling regime)
active_space_orbital_description: the ten orbitals derived from the atomic Au 5d orbitals plus two valence orbitals derived from the 6s atomic orbitals (12 active orbitals); 5s/5p cores frozen
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF active space = the 10 Au-5d-derived orbitals + 2 Au-6s-derived valence orbitals (12 orbitals total), spanning both gold atoms' 5d and 6s manifolds; followed by ic-MRCI and SO coupling. The paper's central lesson: this seemingly H2+-like one-electron-bond diatomic ACTUALLY requires a full multireference + relativistic + spin-orbit treatment - d-orbital bonding contributions, omega-omega (not L-S) coupling, and strong SO coupling all matter, and standard DFT/TD-DFT fails completely.
nroots_per_mult: ~36 SO-coupled electronic states contribute to the two band systems
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2Sigma_g+ (ground state). Ground-state MRCI-SO equilibrium bond length Re = 2.64 A. Two experimental band systems: BS1 near 440 nm (origin 2.79 eV / 22520 cm-1, strongest peak 2.81 eV) with an irregular structure and a 182 cm-1 progression implying an excited-state Au-Au bond of 2.48 A; BS2 near 325 nm (3.63-4.03 eV) with ~60 peaks, ~20x the integrated intensity of BS1. Multiple closely-spaced SO-coupled states underlie each band system, so no clean one-state assignment is possible.
Other: A benchmark case that even a simple gold diatomic cation is electronically complex: strong vibronic and spin-orbit coupling produce irregular, congested band systems that require relativistic multireference (CASSCF-MRCI) + SO to reproduce, while TD-DFT and even non-SO MRCI fail to predict the spectrum. Relevant as the fundamental building block for understanding gold-cluster catalysis. The neutral Au2 dissociation energy is D0 = 2.290 eV for reference.
reference_short: The Optical Spectrum of Au2+, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2020)
notes: Gold dimer cation (metal_center = Au); homonuclear so ligand_set = none. compound_name: BN- anion, the three low-lying doublet states X 2Sigma+, A 2Pi and B 2Sigma+
point_group: C-infinity-v, treated in the C2v subgroup because of the program's symmetry limitation
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed as a function of internuclear distance; the one-dimensional nuclear Schroedinger equation solved on them by discrete variable representation to get vibrational levels and wave functions, with omega_e and omega_e x_e fitted to those levels
method: state-averaged CASSCF providing the multireference wave function for internally contracted MRCI with Davidson correction, followed by a three-term exponential extrapolation over aug-cc-pCVQZ, 5Z and 6Z to the complete basis set limit; Franck-Condon factors, Einstein A coefficients and radiative lifetimes derived from the resulting curves and transition dipole moments
basis_set: aug-cc-pCVQZ, aug-cc-pCV5Z and aug-cc-pCV6Z on both atoms, extrapolated to the basis set limit
active_space_orbital_description: ten active molecular orbitals built from the 2s, 2p and 3s shells of boron and nitrogen, distributed as (6a1, 2b1, 2b2) in C2v; the 1s inner shells of both atoms are frozen
active_space_protocol: the space takes the whole valence manifold of both atoms and adds the 3s shells on top, which matters because the states of interest involve promotion into sigma orbitals that acquire diffuse character in the anion. Freezing only the two 1s shells keeps the core-valence basis sets meaningful for the subsequent MRCI. The quartet and sextet states that the same space would also describe were checked and found to lie above B 2Sigma+ - the first 4Sigma+ by about 1.1 eV and the first 6Sigma+ by about 4.1 eV - and then dropped.
multiplicities_studied: doublet, with quartet and sextet states checked and found to lie higher
electronic_structure_description: Ground state X 2Sigma+ with the configuration ...4sigma2 5sigma1 1pi4: Re 1.289 A, omega_e 1658.79 cm-1, omega_e x_e 11.25 cm-1, against measured 1.284 +/- 0.005 A, 1660 +/- 40 and 12 +/- 4. A 2Pi (1pi to 5sigma) at Te 0.8837 eV with Re 1.355 A, and B 2Sigma+ (4sigma to 5sigma) at 2.6137 eV with Re 1.281 A; neither has experimental data. The valence orbitals are strongly localized - 3sigma is an sp hybrid on boron, 5sigma and 1pi are built from nitrogen p orbitals, and only 4sigma is genuinely B-N bonding - so the attached electron sits mainly on nitrogen, giving B(delta+)N(1+delta)-. The anion at equilibrium lies 25,306 cm-1 (3.138 eV) below neutral BN, close to the 3.16 eV from photoelectron spectroscopy. Permanent dipole moments at Re are -4.6, -0.95 and -1.5 Debye for X, A and B.
Other: The whole case for laser cooling rests on the accident that X 2Sigma+ and B 2Sigma+ have nearly the same bond length - 0.008 A apart here - which makes the Franck-Condon array highly diagonal: f00 = 0.9898, f11 = 0.9727, f22 = 0.9612, with diagonal Einstein coefficients two orders of magnitude above the off-diagonal ones. The proposed scheme needs one pump at 474.67 nm and two repumps at 514.64 and 514.90 nm, with decays to v'' of 3 or more below 2.8e-6. Two potential leaks are checked and dismissed: the intermediate A 2Pi state drains to X about a thousand times faster than B feeds it, so no population accumulates there, and the B state minimum lies below the X and A dissociation limits, so predissociation cannot occur. The B(v'=0) radiative lifetime of 72.4 ns gives an optical cycling rate around 1.3e7 per second. That lifetime is notably shorter than Mawhinney's 101.7 ns, and the authors trace the difference to the bond-length change between X and B - 0.008 A here against 0.019 A there - which is exactly the quantity the diagonal Franck-Condon factors depend on.
reference_short: Liu, Wang, Li, Li, Huang and Feng, Spectrochim. Acta A 255, 119670 (2021)
notes: The active-electron count is not stated in the paper; nine follows from the valence electrons of B and N plus the extra electron, with the two 1s shells explicitly frozen. Rotational effects were neglected in the Einstein coefficients. See the sibling row for neutral BN, computed first as a check on the method.

compound_name: Complex 3a, cerium-rhodium heterometallic cluster with multiple Ce-Rh bonds
metal_center: Ce, together with three Rh centres
metal_ox_state: Not a single number: CASSCF gives a multiconfigurational ground state that is 68 percent Ce(III) and 32 percent Ce(IV), so the cerium is intermediate-valent rather than one or the other. The rhodium centres are assigned as Rh(I) with one Rh(0).
d_electron_count: For cerium the relevant count is the 4f occupancy, which is fractional here - between the 4f1 of Ce(III) and the 4f0 of Ce(IV)
ligand_set: A tripodal triamido-phosphine framework, N[(CH2CH2NPiPr2)]3, bridging the cerium to three rhodium centres, with cyclooctadiene on the rhodium in the precursor. The reduction removes the chlorides and forms direct Ce-Rh and Rh-Rh bonds.
geometry_source: Optimized in this work with the B3PW91 density functional, and validated against the single-crystal structure: computed against experimental metal-metal distances are 2.85 against 2.8360(4), 3.14 against 3.1553(4), 2.85 against 2.8068(4), 2.67 against 2.6871(4) and 2.96 against 2.9345(4) Angstrom for the five Ce-Rh and Rh-Rh contacts. No geometry is optimized at the multiconfigurational level.
method: B3PW91 density functional theory for geometries, spin densities and natural bond orbital analysis, with CASSCF called in specifically to settle the cerium oxidation state. The effective-core-potential strategy runs two ways: small-core relativistic effective core potentials keep the 4f shell in the valence and let the calculation decide the occupancy, while large-core potentials are, in the authors' words, 'dedicated to a given oxidation state' and so must be run twice, once assuming Ce(III) and once Ce(IV). The two treatments were first benchmarked against the precursor complexes where the oxidation states are unambiguous. Experimental support comes from X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, XANES, single-crystal diffraction and SQUID magnetometry.
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on the rare earth centres, used in both small-core and large-core forms as a deliberate probe of the oxidation state. No treatment is described for the CASSCF step specifically.
active_space_orbital_description: Only counts are given, never compositions. Three spaces were tried - CAS(3,3), CAS(3,7) and CAS(7,7) - and no orbital is named or depicted for any of them in the article. The adopted minimal space is recorded here as (3,3).
active_space_protocol: An enlargement test was run, varying both axes, though reported in a single sentence: 'Several active spaces were considered to compute the ground state in order to define the most appropriate one. The small CAS(3,3) was found to be leading to similar results than larger CAS(3,7) or even CAS(7,7), and all are giving a doublet ground state for complex 3a with a multiconfigurational ground state formed by 68% Ce(III) and 32% Ce(IV).' Going from (3,3) to (3,7) adds orbitals at fixed electron count, and from (3,7) to (7,7) adds electrons at fixed orbital count, so the two directions of enlargement are probed separately. All three agree. Not given: any composition for any space, a root count, a basis set, software, a perturbative correction, or a statement of how the 68/32 weights were extracted from the wave function.
multiplicities_studied: Doublet ground state, obtained consistently from all three active spaces
electronic_structure_description: An intermediate-valence cerium problem in which two independent structural readings contradict each other. On one side, the unpaired spin density shows depletion at cerium and accumulation at rhodium, and large-core calculations assuming Ce(IV) give a doublet with 0.84 unpaired electrons on one rhodium and reproduce the metal-metal distances better than the Ce(III) assumption does, so 'one can therefore conclude that there is a Ce(IV) center present with one Rh(0)'. On the other, 'the RE-N bond distances in complex 3a are found to lie in between the bond distances found for the La(III) and Nd(III) complexes, so that one may conclude that this is compatible with a Ce(III) center'. The CASSCF ground state is a doublet whose wave function is 68 percent Ce(III) and 32 percent Ce(IV), so both structural signatures are partly right. The calculation was triggered by an experimental anomaly: among all the complexes measured, the cerium one alone has a chi-T versus temperature curve that 'is not smooth and is the only one to exhibit a change in slope, indicative to some extent of temperature independent paramagnetism and of a multiconfigurational ground state'. The multireference result accounts for that slope change and matches the Ce(IV) fingerprints seen in XANES. The effect is specific to cerium: the singly occupied orbital of the neodymium analogue and the highest occupied orbital of the lanthanum one show no such delocalization toward rhodium. Bonding indices give a strongly polarized Ce-Rh bond at 0.51 with Rh-Rh values of 0.40, 0.37 and 0.18.
Other: A null result from a test that varies both axes separately, licensing a minimal space for this property. CAS(3,3), CAS(3,7) and CAS(7,7) all return the same doublet ground state and the same 68 to 32 mixture of Ce(III) and Ce(IV). The progression is well chosen: (3,3) to (3,7) adds four orbitals while holding the electron count, and (3,7) to (7,7) adds four electrons while holding the orbital count, so orbital-space and electron-count enlargement are probed independently and neither moves the answer. The qualification is how little else is disclosed. No orbital is named for any of the three spaces, so a reader cannot tell what the (3,3) contains, nor what the four added orbitals in (3,7) were. No basis set, no software, no root count and no perturbative correction are given, and the article does not say how the 68 to 32 weights were extracted. The agreement across three spaces is an internal consistency check on a calculation whose setup is not documented.
reference_short: Shi, Douair, Feng, Wang, Zhao, Maron & Zhu, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2021, 143, 5998
notes: A synthesis and characterization Article reporting the first molecule with multiple rare-earth to rhodium bonds, seven authors across two groups with two corresponding. The multireference supplies the 68 to 32 mixture that reconciles two structural observables pointing to different cerium oxidation states, which a single-determinant calculation cannot do, since such a calculation must place the 4f electron either on cerium or not. It also accounts for an experimental magnetic anomaly, the slope change and temperature-independent paramagnetism unique to the cerium member, and agrees with the Ce(IV) fingerprints in XANES. The multireference covers only the cerium complex. The neodymium and lanthanum analogues 3b and 3c are computed by density functional theory alone, and their frontier orbitals show none of the delocalization toward rhodium that the cerium complex does; they receive no rows. The entry is marked partial on several counts. Compound 3a is identified only by its label - no molecular formula is given in the text and the authors describe its formation mechanism as 'ambiguous' - so the row is written under the paper's own label with no structure guessed. Beyond that, no basis set, no software, no root count and no active-space composition appear anywhere in the article, with computational details listed among the Supporting Information contents. On the density functional side, small-core effective core potentials keep the 4f shell in the valence so the calculation can decide its occupancy, whereas large-core potentials are 'dedicated to a given oxidation state' and must be run twice under opposite assumptions. The two were benchmarked against the precursor complexes, where the oxidation states are unambiguous and the computed spin densities of 1.02 for cerium and 3.06 for neodymium confirm the expected assignments. Complex 3a was obtained by reducing the chloride-bridged precursor 2a, Ce{N[(CH2CH2NPiPr2)RhCl(COD)]3}, with potassium graphite. The paper states that 'the detailed mechanism for the formation of complex 3a is ambiguous' but probably involves reduction of two Rh(I) to Rh(0), oxidative addition of two C-H bonds on the cyclooctadiene, and reductive elimination. The density functional side is described only in terms of its effective core potentials - small-core for cerium and neodymium, and eleven-electron large-core potentials in the comparison runs - with no orbital basis specified. No CASPT2, NEVPT2 or any other correction is applied on top of the CASSCF, so the 68 to 32 configuration weights come from a bare multiconfigurational wave function; the three-space agreement tests the reference space rather than what a correction would do to it.

compound_name: trans-nitrofurantoin, a widely used urinary-tract antibiotic and an environmental contaminant, studied for the channels open after photoabsorption
geometry_source: ground-state minimum from a hybrid functional; conical intersections optimized multiconfigurationally starting from geometries where trajectories actually hopped; reaction pathways built from the vertical region to those crossings
method: a staged protocol: state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field with a small space and basis to drive exploratory surface-hopping dynamics, then the hopping geometries clustered by unsupervised machine learning, then conical intersections optimized and reaction paths built with a larger space, more states and a better basis at both the self-consistent-field and multistate perturbation levels
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-31G for the exploratory dynamics; 6-31G* for the production conical-intersection optimizations and pathway calculations
active_space_nel: 12 in the exploratory dynamics, 16 in the production calculations
active_space_norb: 9 in the exploratory dynamics, 11 in the production calculations
active_space_orbital_description: the production space comprises six pi orbitals, three pi-star orbitals and two n orbitals; the smaller exploratory space is not broken down by type
active_space_protocol: Two spaces used in sequence, and the paper is unusually explicit about why a single space would not do. The difficulty it states is real: the bright state is neither the first nor the second excited state, so many states must be carried, and convergence of smooth surfaces demands averaging over still more states than the mechanism itself needs - all of which is unaffordable at the production level across thousands of trajectory steps. The resolution is to use a twelve-electron nine-orbital space with a minimal basis and only two or three averaged states to find where the molecule actually goes, then rebuild the important geometries and paths in a sixteen-electron eleven-orbital space with six averaged states and a polarized basis. The number of averaged states is varied deliberately within the production space too - three for the ground-to-first-excited crossings, four for the first-to-second, six for the higher ones - matched to which states are degenerate at each crossing. The authors also concede the compromise in the dynamics: trajectories were launched only from low-lying states and higher-energy channels reached by scaling the initial velocities, because starting from the genuinely relevant high states was not affordable.
nroots_per_mult: two or three states averaged in the exploratory dynamics; three to six in the production calculations depending on which crossing is being optimized
electronic_structure_description: Four reaction channels emerge. The first is photolytic: one N-O bond of the nitro group breaks, and the dissociation limit is strongly multireference because of near-degenerate states there. The second is a large-amplitude isomerization about the central C-N bond. The third combines pyramidalization at the nitro nitrogen with internal rotation of the nitro group about the C-N bond. The fourth is governed by bending of the O-N-O angle. Crossings were located between the ground and first excited state, between the first and second, between the second and third, and between the third and fourth.
Other: The machine-learning step is what makes the protocol work rather than an ornament: every geometry at which a trajectory hopped from the first excited state to the ground state was collected, then reduced in dimension and clustered, and the distinct clusters identified which conical intersections were worth optimizing. That replaces guessing the reactive coordinates in advance, which the authors note they had no basis for - the system is too large and its transitions too tangled for chemical intuition to supply the relevant coordinates.
reference_short: Lin, Hu, Peng, Xu, Gu and Lan, Chemosphere 281, 130831 (2021)
notes: The compound is studied as an environmental pollutant rather than as a drug - the question is what it does when sunlight reaches it in water. A flow chart of the staged protocol is given in the paper, and the active-space orbitals in the supporting information. One test finding worth noting: when the initial velocities were scaled by a factor of three, every trajectory gave oxygen-atom detachment, so the higher-energy channels are reachable but only by supplying energy the thermal sampling does not provide.
correlation_correction: multistate second-order perturbation theory on the production reference, used for the vertical excitation energies and for the reaction pathways

Other: The benchmark turns on where a correction can act, stated explicitly: for a free atom every state arising from one term receives the same amount of external correlation from CASPT2, so a non-state-specific perturbative correction cannot alter a within-term fine-structure splitting at all, however large it is, while pair-density functional theory evaluated on the state's own density and on-top pair density is state-specific and can. Where CASPT2-SO nevertheless agrees well, the paper credits the active space rather than the correction, attributing its good group-13 numbers to a much larger active space than the valence s and p set used here. compound_name: gauche-1,3-butadiene closing to bicyclobutane, the parent electrocyclization, studied for how the substituent reshapes the conical intersection that controls the photocyclization
geometry_source: reactant and product minima optimized multiconfigurationally with frequencies confirming them; conical intersections optimized at the same level; ground-state transition states optimized with a dispersion-corrected hybrid functional after the perturbative treatment validated its barrier
method: state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field for ground and excited state geometries, minimum-energy conical intersection optimization and excitation energies, with extended multistate second-order perturbation theory as a benchmark on the same reference, and surface-hopping dynamics on the resulting surfaces
active_space_orbital_description: two pi-bonding orbitals and two pi-antibonding orbitals - the two highest occupied and two lowest unoccupied orbitals of the diene
active_space_protocol: Four electrons in the four frontier pi orbitals - the minimal space for a diene electrocyclization, spanning exactly the orbitals whose occupations change as the ring closes. The same space is used for the parent and both substituted systems, which is what makes the substituent comparison meaningful: any change in the crossing topography is then a property of the substituent and not of the description. Two states are averaged with equal weights. The paper does not stop at the reference level for the quantities that matter - the topography parameters and the excitation energies are recomputed with the perturbative treatment at the same geometries, so the sensitivity of the conclusions to dynamic correlation can be seen directly.
nroots_per_mult: the two lowest singlet states, averaged with equal weights

active_space_protocol: (6,4): pi, pi* and the two nitrogen lone pairs, used identically for XMS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF so the methods are compared on equal footing. The reference XMS-CASPT2 used no level shift and had IPEA deactivated. Note the independent convergence on this same (6,4) space for azomethane in 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00917 and 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00137, though those papers do not all spell out the orbital composition
Other: Reference XMS-CASPT2 dynamics resolves four time regimes: (I) about 30 fs during which all molecules stay cis on S1; (II) crossing of a first conical intersection region up to about 60 fs, giving 20-25 percent nonadiabatic S1-to-S0 decay and complete cis-to-trans isomerization; (III) a roughly 40 fs plateau with most molecules trans; (IV) a second strong-coupling region with further decay, during which some molecules return to cis. The 90 degree conical intersection is reached after about 40 fs and the 270 degree one from about 120 fs. The end of regime II appears at about 60 fs regardless of electronic structure method. Method verdict: multireference methods are the preferred choice. CC2, TD-PBE, TDA-PBE, TD-PBE0 and TD-CAM-B3LYP are too unstable near electronic degeneracies to give trustworthy statistics. ADC(2) with local diabatization, TDA-PBE0 and TDA-CAM-B3LYP reproduce the timescale (despite up to 40 percent of trajectories crashing) but predict almost total decay through the first crossing and so badly describe the 'rotator' trajectories. CIS additionally fails to reproduce the population plateau. The authors' most transferable caution: which methods would succeed could hardly be predicted from a static analysis of the potential energy surfaces, so the usual practice of validating an electronic structure method on static energetics before running dynamics may not be sufficient.

That is an objective and reproducible selection rule, and it is the kind of procedure the database is short of - most papers assert a space, this one derives it. The renormalization-group step exists precisely because it can handle a larger orbital space than the complete-active-space method can, so it is used to decide which orbitals matter and the smaller method is then run on the selection. The crossing moves outward as the cluster grows, which the paper traces to the falling ionization potential of larger clusters through a near-linear relationship between the two, while the bond energy stays essentially constant across the whole series so that 'the energy of the bond is quite local'. The diabatic coupling behaves in two opposite ways depending on where it is evaluated: measured AT the crossing it falls exponentially with cluster size, because the crossing itself recedes; measured at its maximum along the coordinate it 'does not change dramatically'. Beyond these two states lies a manifold of bath states from single excitations, whose coupling to the charge-transfer state sets a resonance width and hence a lifetime
Other: The default active space fails the spanning test outright, and the paper states the failure in one sentence: 'for a standard CASSCF(2,2) calculation, both active orbitals would be located on the lithium cluster'. An unconstrained two-electron, two-orbital space on a chlorine-plus-lithium-cluster system puts everything on the metal, so it cannot describe the transfer of an electron between the two fragments at all - the quantity the whole study is about would be identically absent. The variational principle actively drives the space onto one site, and the paper's entire methodological contribution exists to prevent that. THE REMEDY is A new kind of selection rule: A constraint on the active space's population rather than on the identity or count of its orbitals. Since the calculation 'must be sure that the active space spans both the molecule and the metal', the authors 'enforce the constraint that the total population on the molecule for the active space' takes a chosen value, implemented after symmetric orthogonalization of the atomic basis and expressed through a projector. The constraint is weaker than the outcome it produces: 'the space of active orbitals must contain the same total projected magnitude onto the lithium orbitals and chlorine orbitals, but there is no reason to assume that one active orbital must be localized on the chlorine and the other on the lithium cluster. Nevertheless, for the most part... we do find that one active orbital is located on the lithium cluster and the other is localized on the chlorine.' A condition on the SUM delivers a one-orbital-per-fragment arrangement without demanding it, so the donor-acceptor picture emerges from the calculation rather than being imposed on it. The paper also states plainly the principle this whole collection depends on: 'within a CASSCF calculation, the results depend only on the active space and are invariant to the choice of individual orbitals'. The active orbitals are then localized by diagonalizing the projector onto the molecule purely so that they can be looked at - an analysis step with no effect on any energy. The one empirical parameter is sensitivity-tested over A fortyfold range and the two observables respond differently. The dynamic-weighting parameter was 'chosen empirically to match the energy gap of the crossing as well as provide appropriate weights to ensure convergence', which is frank about its arbitrariness. Varying it from 0.037 to 1.47 leaves the crossing position essentially fixed - 'for all values, the crossing sits around 7.7 angstrom' in the three-lithium case - while 'the diabatic coupling strength does depend on the weighting parameter, but the change is no more than 50 percent'. The geometric conclusion is therefore independent of the fitted parameter while the magnitude of the coupling is not. The size dependence differs with where the coupling is measured: 'the strength at the crossing decreases exponentially with the increase of the lithium atom number while the maximum coupling does not change dramatically'. The two are not in conflict - the crossing point itself moves to larger separations as the cluster grows, so an exponentially decaying coupling evaluated at a receding point falls exponentially while its peak value barely moves. Anyone quoting 'the diabatic coupling versus cluster size' from this system must say which of the two they mean. The physical effect usually invoked turns out to be the weak one: delocalization of the metal orbital over a larger cluster does reduce the overlap and hence the coupling, 'but this effect is weak (scaling as the square root of the cluster volume) and can easily be overshadowed by other geometric features that are accentuated in a cluster of a finite number of atoms'. The same conclusion returns for the state lifetime: it 'fluctuates for different clusters, indicating that the geometry of the cluster (and the position of Cl relative to the cluster) is just as important (if not more so) as the total number of atoms'. Geometry beats size, twice over. The rate-like quantity is A composite and the approximations are named. The resonance width is obtained from a golden-rule expression fed by constrained-CASSCF couplings and state densities, with the delta function replaced by a Gaussian of 0.14 electronvolts, and the authors immediately caution that 'approximating a delta function cannot be terribly reliable until the cluster size is quite large'. Cluster geometries and all ionization potentials come from Hartree-Fock, and a local density of states is separately built from Hartree-Fock orbital energies specifically to connect with solid-state practice, where 'multireference calculations are rare and lifetimes are calculated (almost by default) using local densities of states'. The paper limits itself explicitly: 'in principle, Gamma must converge to a fixed value as we increase the cluster size, but clearly we have not yet reached the bulk limit (and reaching such a limit will require a more optimized code implementation on our end)'. A study whose stated purpose is the transition from homogeneous to heterogeneous electron transfer, saying openly that it has not reached the heterogeneous end, is reporting its own incompleteness rather than extrapolating past it

Six systems carry constrained-CASSCF potential energy surfaces and each gets a row: the odd-numbered lithium clusters from one to eleven atoms, each paired with a chlorine, scanned along the distance between chlorine and its nearest lithium. Odd cluster sizes are used throughout so that the combined system can pair its electrons. electronic_structure_description: A closed-shell hydrogen-bonded dimer whose structural hallmark the valence CASSCF gets BACKWARDS. Experiment and CCSD(T) agree that hydrogen bonding lengthens the donor O-H bond by about 0.01 angstrom and redshifts its stretch by about 100 wavenumbers - CCSD(T) placing the donor stretch at 3756 per centimetre against a monomer average of 3866, a shift of -110. Restricted Hartree-Fock, with no correlation at all, gets the sign right, lengthening the donor bond from 0.9410 to 0.9450 angstrom. The valence CASSCF shortens it, from a monomer 0.9641 to a dimer 0.9448 angstrom, a change of -0.0193. Its dimer donor bond length of 0.9448 is within 0.0002 angstrom of the Hartree-Fock value, showing the bond receives no left-right correlation at all. The acceptor bond also shortens, by -0.0011 angstrom, where RHF and CCSD(T) lengthen it by +0.0006 and +0.0008. The oxygen-oxygen separation comes out at 3.0848 angstrom against 2.9133 at CCSD(T), yet the interaction energy of -19.16 kcal/mol OVERBINDS the CCSD(T) value of -5.22 by a factor of 3.7
Other: The full valence active space fails, and it fails by composition despite having no choice about its size. The valence CASSCF space here is not a truncation anyone selected - it is every valence orbital of every atom, the largest space the concept admits short of full configuration interaction. And yet 'one of the active weakly occupied dimer orbitals correlates electrons in the acceptor lone pairs, not the donor bond, which is left without left-right correlation'. The orbitals are all present and the optimizer sends the correlating power to the wrong place. Size cannot fix this, because the space is already maximal by construction; only the orbital optimization decides where within it the correlation goes, and here it decides wrongly. The failure is diagnosed by a numerical coincidence: 'the RHF and vCAS bond lengths of the donor OH bond in (H2O)2 are nearly identical, 0.9450 angstrom and 0.9448 angstrom, respectively. Together, these two results strongly suggest that the OH donor bond in the vCAS calculations is described without any left-right correlation.' A multiconfigurational calculation reproducing a Hartree-Fock bond length to two ten-thousandths of an angstrom shows the correlated method has added nothing where it was needed. The sign of the structural effect is wrong, and Hartree-Fock gets it right. Hydrogen bonding lengthens the donor bond by about 0.01 angstrom and redshifts its stretch by about 100 wavenumbers. Restricted Hartree-Fock, with no correlation whatever, reproduces the lengthening at +0.0040 angstrom; coupled cluster with singles, doubles and perturbative triples gets it right; and the valence CASSCF shortens the donor bond by 0.0193 angstrom. A method built to add correlation to Hartree-Fock here produces a worse answer than Hartree-Fock, with the opposite sign on the structural hallmark the whole field uses to identify hydrogen bonding. The acceptor bond behaves the same way, shortening by 0.0011 angstrom where RHF and CCSD(T) both lengthen it by about 0.0007. And the energetic error runs the opposite way from the structural one. The valence CASSCF oxygen-oxygen separation is 3.0848 angstrom against 2.9133 at CCSD(T), 0.17 angstrom too long, 'suggesting an underestimation of the attractive interaction'. Yet 'paradoxically, despite the overly long O-O distance, the vCAS/aVTZ interaction energy of -19.16 kcal/mol considerably overestimates the CCSD(T)/aVTZ value (-5.22 kcal/mol)' - overbinding by a factor of 3.7 while simultaneously placing the monomers too far apart. The authors name the cause: 'this overbinding is a result of the inconsistent treatment of the electronic structure of the dimer relative to the two monomers'. A space that correlates different things in the complex than in its fragments does not cancel errors on subtraction, and an interaction energy is a subtraction. The monomers are fine, which localizes the failure precisely. For isolated hydrogen fluoride the valence CASSCF lengthens the bond from the Hartree-Fock 0.8991 angstrom to a value 'that deviates from the CCSD(T) result by only 0.0034 angstrom'. The method works on the fragments and breaks on the complex, so the defect is not in the valence-space concept but in what the optimizer does with it once a second molecule is present to offer competing orbitals. The consequence for everything built on such a reference is stated in the abstract: 'this has significant implications for subsequent treatments of dynamical correlation that are based on a vCAS reference wave function'. Perturbation theory repairs a reference; it does not repair a reference that has correlated the wrong electrons. The paper is titled a cautionary tale and is entirely a negative result. Valence CASSCF is described as having 'been applied successfully to countless' systems; the contribution here is to bound that success by exhibiting a common, chemically central class of system where it fails qualitatively and to explain why
reference_short: Nguyen, Dunning & Xantheas, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2026, 22, 6283-6289
notes: The system carrying the paper's full numerical case, and the one where two errors point in opposite directions at once - the monomers held too far apart and the binding overestimated nearly fourfold. The authors attribute the overbinding to 'the inconsistent treatment of the electronic structure of the dimer relative to the two monomers', which is the general hazard of any interaction energy computed as a difference between a complex and its fragments when the active space correlates different things in each. A purpose-built negative result. The paper's entire content is the demonstration that valence CASSCF fails qualitatively on hydrogen-bonded dimers and the orbital analysis explaining why. Split by source: all geometries are optimized at each level of theory being compared - restricted Hartree-Fock, valence CASSCF and CCSD(T) - with harmonic frequencies computed at those optimized geometries, so structures and frequencies are internally consistent within each method and the comparison is genuinely method-against-method. Cs symmetry constraints were applied during the optimizations, using the previously known dimer geometries as the guide. The aug-cc-pVTZ basis is used throughout, with the 1s electrons of the heavy atoms kept doubly occupied. Calculations were carried out with GAMESS and MOLPRO. CCSD(T) serves as the accuracy reference, with the experimentally established hallmark - about 0.01 angstrom of donor bond lengthening and about 100 wavenumbers of redshift - as the external anchor. Marked extracted_partial because the paper states the active-space RULE rather than printing explicit electron and orbital counts for each dimer, because the full geometry and frequency tables and the optimized Cartesian coordinates live in tables and the supporting information, and because the orbital plots underlying the central diagnosis are likewise supporting material. A perturbative correction built on a reference that has correlated the acceptor lone pairs instead of the donor bond inherits that choice. CCSD(T) is used as the accuracy reference and is a SINGLE-reference method built on the Hartree-Fock determinant, which here has the correct structural behaviour.

method: SA-CASSCF for geometry optimization and conical-intersection searches, with MRCI (with and without Davidson correction), MS-CASPT2 (0.2 level shift) and EOM-CCSD single points for the vertical excitation energies; natural population analysis and Wiberg bond indices for the electronic structure characterization

active_space_protocol: A worked example of choosing an active space under a cost ceiling, with the reasoning spelled out. The chemically correct space is (20,16): eight pi plus two nO lone-pair orbitals on uracil, and six pi orbitals on benzene. That space generates 14 158 144 CSFs and 64 128 064 determinants and is affordable only for single points, not for geometry optimization or conical-intersection searches. Dropping the highest unoccupied orbital gives (20,15), 2 186 184 CSFs and 9 018 009 determinants, which the authors identify as the best compromise for vertical excitation energies - explicitly better than the alternative of transplanting the previously used reduced spaces for the separate fragments, (12,9) for uracil plus (6,6) for benzene, which would give (18,15). All geometry optimizations were then done at (20,14), the largest space they could afford for optimization, and MRCI and MS-CASPT2 single points were computed on top of it. 5BU has 106 electrons in 53 doubly occupied orbitals; during MCSCF optimization the lowest 43 orbitals were closed but still fully optimized, and for the correlated single points those same 43 were frozen.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. Vertical excitation energies in eV, S1 (n-pi*) then S2 (pi-pi*), in the printed order of Table 2: SA-CASSCF(20,14) 4.85 / 7.92; SA-CASSCF(18,14) 4.94 / 5.34; SA-CASSCF(20,15) 5.02 / 7.02; SA-CASSCF(18,15) 4.94 / 5.21; SA-CASSCF(20,16) 4.94 (f = 0.003) / 7.10 (f = 0.571); MS-CASPT2(20,13) 5.02 / 6.83; MS-CASPT2(20,14) 4.93 / 6.28; MRCI(20,14) 5.08 / 7.12; MRCI+D(20,14) 5.11 / 6.90; EOM-CCSD 5.13 / 5.44; LT-DF-LCC2 4.94 / 5.07
Other: The active space controls S2 far more than S1. Removing two active electrons at fixed orbital count collapses S2 from 7.92 to 5.34 eV at (20,14) versus (18,14), and from 7.02 to 5.21 eV at (20,15) versus (18,15), while S1 moves by only 0.01-0.09 eV. Enlarging the virtual space from (20,15) to (20,16) shifts S2 only from 7.03 to 7.10 eV and leaves S1 unchanged, so the virtual orbitals matter much less than the occupied ones. Dynamic correlation then brings the CASSCF values of 6.93 and 8.48 eV down to 5.83 and 6.93 eV at MS-CASPT2. Because the saturated methylene bridge blocks pi communication between the two rings, the 5BU excited states track the isolated fragments closely: the first two excited states at 5.13 and 5.44 eV match isolated uracil (5.17 eV) and isolated benzene (5.30 eV), and the third and fourth lie at 5.78 and 6.55 eV. At the correlated level the uracil-benzene difference falls below 0.02 eV.

active_space_protocol: Full valence for ethane is 14 electrons in 14 orbitals, which produced a prohibitively large CASSCF-CI expansion, so a (10,10) was used instead by demoting the totally symmetric CH-bond combinations and their antibonding partners. The authors state they expect MRCI on (14,14) and on (10,10) to give very similar results. The paper's central and directly transferable active-space result: MRCI based on a CASSCF that puts only the electrons of the C-C or N-N bond itself in the active space reproduces full-valence CASSCF/MRCI very well. This worked because the bond orbitals could be cleanly distinguished from those involved in the C-H or N-H bonds. There is in fact more variation among full-valence MRCI results with the reference-selection threshold than between the two choices of active space. The small space carries a second practical advantage: full-valence MRCI and ACPF expansions were prohibitively long and required reference selection (keeping occupations whose spin-coupling coefficients exceeded about 0.05), whereas with the smaller spaces the entire CASSCF could be used as the reference with no selection at all. The authors judge their best numbers to be the ACPF values on the smaller active space, precisely because it avoids reference-selection error.
Other: Single-bonded reference case. The discrepancy between the single-reference MCPF and the multireference ACPF dissociation energies is only 0-1 kcal/mol for single bonds, rising to 3-4 kcal/mol for double bonds and about 6 kcal/mol for triple bonds - consistent with higher excitations mattering more as bond multiplicity increases. All electrons except the 1s on carbon were correlated in the MCPF, MRCI and ACPF steps. The numerical De values are in the paper's Table I, which did not survive PDF text extraction.

compound_name: He...He van der Waals dimer ground state (with He...H2 excited-state and hydrogen-bonded dimers as further tests)
geometry_source: interaction energy curves versus interatomic distance; van der Waals minimum near 5.6 bohr
method: supermolecular CASSCF interaction energies analyzed for their dispersion content, with a derived closed-form CAS dispersion energy (Edisp_CAS) from CAS transition density matrices; benchmarked against SAPT dispersion at the FCI level and an exact reference potential
software: Molpro (integrals, CASSCF 1- and 2-RDMs and the supermolecular CASSCF calculations); in-house code for the CAS dispersion energy
basis_set: aug-cc-pV5Z for the interaction curves; aug-cc-pVTZ for the long-range C6 analysis
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4) for the dimer, dissociating to a product of CAS(2,2) monomers; larger dimer spaces up to CAS(4,28) also tested
active_space_protocol: A quantitative warning about active-space size and intermolecular dispersion. CASSCF itself recovers a PORTION of the dispersion energy, and that portion GROWS with active-space size, so naively adding a dispersion correction to a supermolecular CASSCF interaction energy double-counts intermonomer correlation by an amount that increases with the space. For He...He: CAS(4,4)+dispersion deviates from the benchmark by only 6.6% at the vdW minimum, but CAS(4,28)+dispersion OVERestimates by 72% and shifts the minimum from 5.6 to 5.3 bohr. The paper's fix (CAS+DispCAS, subtracting the dispersion already in the CASSCF energy) keeps errors under 2% at any active-space size. The complementary limitation: even CAS(4,18) recovers only about 50% of the He...He C6 coefficient (0.735 vs the reference 1.461 a.u.) and no higher Cn, because only p orbitals are in the active space. He...H2 excited-state dimers used CAS(2,5)/CAS(2,4) for the 1Sigma_u+ state and CAS(2,2) on He with CAS(2,10) on H2 for the 1Pi_u state.
Other: The study also decomposes interaction energies of hydrogen-bonded dimers (H2O...H2O, HCN...HCN and others). The overarching message for anyone choosing a CASSCF active space for intermolecular interactions: enlarging the active space captures more dispersion inside the CASSCF energy, so dispersion corrections must be made active-space-consistent or they will double-count - a counterintuitive direction, since bigger is not automatically safer here.
reference_short: How Much Dispersion Energy Is Included in the Multiconfigurational Interaction Energy? J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2020)
notes: Metal-free rare-gas/model dimers (metal_center = none). Recorded for the transferable and counterintuitive active-space caution: CASSCF partially and size-dependently recovers dispersion, so a larger active space makes naive dispersion-corrected interaction energies WORSE (He...He CAS(4,4) 6.6% error -> CAS(4,28) 72% overestimate). active_space_nel/norb hold the CAS(4,4) dimer case; the larger and He-H2 spaces are in the protocol field.

software: locally modified Arrow (multicomponent heat-bath CI) for the CI step; locally modified PySCF for the orbital update

active_space_protocol: largest electronic space (16,48); the reported series is (12,11), (12,17), (12,27), (12,46) at a fixed 13-orbital protonic space, (1,13). Multicomponent (nuclear-electronic orbital) CASSCF, in which a proton is treated quantum-mechanically alongside the electrons; active spaces are written (n,m)/(k,l) for n electrons in m electronic orbitals and k protons in l protonic orbitals. A heat-bath-CI solver enables far larger spaces than the ~1e5-configuration limit of the previous GAMESS implementation. Two active-space lessons transfer even to single-component work. First, LARGE electronic active spaces are essential for a qualitatively correct protonic density: the density error decreases monotonically as the electronic space grows, and even the largest spaces here still trail NEO-CCSD. Second, and newly shown, the PROTONIC active space can be truncated substantially with negligible loss - not all protonic orbitals need be active - which contradicts prior multicomponent CASSCF practice.
Other: Protonic density RMS error (a.u.) versus electronic active space, showing the monotonic improvement: (12,11) 0.695 (E -199.6047 Ha); (12,17) 0.560 (-199.6796); (12,27) 0.328 (-199.7879); (12,46) 0.190 (-199.8095). Electronic spaces larger than (8,27) are needed to beat multicomponent OOMP2, yet even (16,48) remains less accurate than NEO-CCSD. Protonic-space truncation for the largest electronic space: density error 0.307 -> 0.265 -> 0.190 for 4, 6, 13 active protonic orbitals, then flat - so 13 protonic orbitals suffice.
reference_short: Fajen and Brorsen, Multicomponent CASSCF Revisited: Large Active Spaces Are Needed for Qualitatively Accurate Protonic Densities, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2021)
notes: Metal-free multicomponent (metal_center = none); the quantum proton makes this a nuclear-electronic CASSCF. active_space_protocol: minimal CAS(10,10) covering all Fe(III) 3d electrons and orbitals; initial orbitals from the model one-electron Hamiltonian followed by AVAS. Active spaces for the transition-metal complexes come exclusively from the AVAS (atomic valence active space) procedure of Sayfutyarova et al., targeting the five 3d atomic orbitals on each metal centre taken from the MINAO minimal basis; double-d-shell guesses are available the same way. The practical appeal is that for a minimal or double-d-shell TMC calculation the only strictly necessary user input is the list of metal centre indices. AVAS supplies both the space definition and starting orbitals coherent with it. For aromatic pi systems the paper uses either broken-symmetry UHF natural orbitals (UNO) or PiAS, a simplified version of the pi-orbital guess of Sayfutyarova and Hammes-Schiffer that builds an inertia tensor over the pi centres and projects the 2p components along the principal axis, so it works for arbitrarily oriented molecules. Point-group symmetry was never exploited anywhere in the paper; active orbitals were localized with Foster-Boys where localization was used.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1Ag
Other: The clearest result in the paper about active-orbital choice: the convergence rate of the second-order TRAH algorithm depends crucially on it. Canonical and natural active orbitals converge slowly, taking nearly 90 iterations; localized active orbitals cut that dramatically. The explanation is chemical - localization disentangles the CAS-CI Hamiltonian into weakly coupled Fe(III) monomer blocks, each qualitatively a single high-spin CSF, which are then antiferromagnetically coupled. That coupled two-monomer CSF carries 98 percent of the weight in the final CI expansion. The first-order SXPT algorithm converged steadily in 19 iterations regardless, showing the AVAS starting orbitals are well matched to the chosen space.

Active spaces for the transition-metal complexes come exclusively from the AVAS (atomic valence active space) procedure of Sayfutyarova et al., targeting the five 3d atomic orbitals on each metal centre taken from the MINAO minimal basis; double-d-shell guesses are available the same way. The practical appeal is that for a minimal or double-d-shell TMC calculation the only strictly necessary user input is the list of metal centre indices. AVAS supplies both the space definition and starting orbitals coherent with it. For aromatic pi systems the paper uses either broken-symmetry UHF natural orbitals (UNO) or PiAS, a simplified version of the pi-orbital guess of Sayfutyarova and Hammes-Schiffer that builds an inertia tensor over the pi centres and projects the 2p components along the principal axis, so it works for arbitrarily oriented molecules. Point-group symmetry was never exploited anywhere in the paper; active orbitals were localized with Foster-Boys where localization was used.

active_space_protocol: CAS(6,6): the full pi valence space, three pi and three pi*, identical for ground and excited states. A size-consistency procedure worth reusing whenever CASSCF is applied to intermolecular complexes: orbital rotations are generally needed to keep CASSCF size-consistent even when MP2 or CI natural orbitals are used as the starting guess. The authors therefore first converged a CASSCF wave function for the dimer with the monomers pulled 100 A apart, confirmed that the supermolecular interaction energy vanished there, and then used those orbitals as the initial guess for the equilibrium-geometry dimer. MP2 orbitals seeded the initial CASSCF. Ground and excited states use an identical active space composition, and both dimer and monomer wave functions come from two-state state-averaged CAS calculations.

Excited-state SAPT(CAS) components (Table 1): elst -1.85, exch 2.82, ind -1.23, exch-ind 0.65, disp -2.88, exch-disp 0.33, Eint -2.16; change on excitation dEint(SAPT) +0.72.

CASPT2 overbinds the excited complex (-3.12 vs -2.67). The pi-pi* excitation destabilizes the X-H...pi contact, mainly through a 0.88 kcal/mol loss of electrostatic attraction and 0.17 kcal/mol less dispersion; Edisp/Eelst rises from 1.1 to 1.6.

active_space_protocol: a size rule rather than a fixed space: the pi valence space grows as (4k+2, 4k+2) with the number of fused rings k, always keeping equal electrons and orbitals. This is what makes v2RDM-CASSCF attractive here - it scales only polynomially with active-space size, and the paper notes spaces as large as (50,50) are reachable, well beyond CI-based CASSCF. An unexplained discrepancy: DMRG-PDFT and v2RDM-CASSCF-PDFT diverge for hexacene and heptacene despite the underlying v2RDM and DMRG gaps agreeing. Of all methods surveyed, ACI-DSRG-MRPT2 best matches experiment up to pentacene.

geometry_source: QM/MM optimized in this work. The protein-solvent system was equilibrated for 10 ns of classical AMOEBA MD, the CTZ+O2 coordinates were then manually replaced by the dioxetanone, and only a 932-atom relaxed region around the chromophore was optimized (rest frozen at the snapshot); QM region 177 atoms, comprising the chromophore plus hydrogen-bonding side chains. method: SA-CASSCF with polarizable QM/MM embedding in the AMOEBA force field (SA-CASSCF/AMOEBA), dynamically weighted with S0 as reference state and a 3 eV bandwidth in the PCM and QM/MM calculations; minimum-energy conical intersection searches on top
software: TeraChem for the QM part coupled to OpenMM for the MM part
active_space_orbital_description: chosen to contain enough active orbitals to describe the O-O bond dissociation of the dioxetanone ring; the low-lying states it produces are n->sigma* and sigma->sigma* local excitations in the O-O bond region
active_space_protocol: (8,9) sized around the breaking O-O bond; state-averaging over four singlets and two triplets, with dynamic weights referenced to S0 using a 3 eV bandwidth. A separate, much smaller SA(2)-CASSCF(4,3)/3-21G space was used only on an HBDI-valine model to parametrize the force field and to compare link-atom schemes
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlets and 2 triplets in the state-average

Environment changes the picture qualitatively. compound_name: Perfectly eclipsed pi-stacked ethylene oligomers (4, 6 and 8 units), toy models for hole and exciton migration
geometry_source: constructed models: all ethylene units at their ground-state neutral geometry, perfectly eclipsed with a uniform 4 A interplanar spacing
method: real-time CASSCF Ehrenfest electron dynamics: a fully converged CASSCF calculation is transformed to localized orbitals (hole migration) or natural bond orbitals (exciton migration), and the resulting configuration state functions are propagated in time, with nuclear motion either frozen or coupled through the Ehrenfest gradient
software: development version of Gaussian (Ehrenfest real-time CASSCF implementation)
active_space_orbital_description: one localized pi orbital per ethylene unit for hole migration; pi and pi* on each unit, obtained as natural bond orbitals, for exciton migration
active_space_protocol: sizing rule scales with the number of stacked units n: hole migration uses a doublet CAS(2n-1, n) with the n active pi orbitals localized one per ethylene unit; exciton migration uses CAS(2n, 2n) with pi and pi* per unit transformed to NBOs. The tabulated (7,4) here is the n = 4 hole-migration case. The authors note that a physically correct excited state of ethylene would need diffuse Rydberg-like functions, which this toy model deliberately neglects
multiplicities_studied: 2 — doublet for the cationic hole-migration cases; for the radical stacks the highest-spin ferromagnetic coupling was used, e.g. 2S+1 = 6 for the six-unit system, with a 2S+1 = 4 case also run
Other: Hole migration was followed for 4, 6 and 8 units with frozen nuclei, and for 4 units with coupled nuclear motion; the transferring hole passes through a transition-state-like geometry at which the terminal A and D C=C bond lengths become equal. Coherence length is effectively infinite in this perfectly eclipsed geometry - the charge propagates across the whole stack. Results are time-dependent CSF populations, not stationary energies.

compound_name: Hexatriene (1,3,5-hexatriene), vertical excited states - in-depth XS-CASSCF illustration
geometry_source: CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ geometry from the QUESTDB database
method: SA-CASSCF and XS-CASSCF at [0,0] and [0,0.5], all on a (6,6) reference; MR-CISD with Pople extensivity correction (MR-CISD+P) on the same (6,6) space; theoretical best estimates from QUESTDB
active_space_orbital_description: the six pi electrons in the six pi orbitals
active_space_protocol: CAS(6,6) pi valence space, state-averaged over the ground state and five excited states. XS-CASSCF is the corrective follow-up to this group's Qat ionic-character diagnostic (10.1021/acs.jpca.3c05559): SA-CASSCF overestimates singlet ionic pi-pi* states by 1-2 eV because the transition-density self-repulsion (two-electron exchange integrals) is not screened by sigma-correlation. XS-CASSCF scales those exchange terms down with two parameters [mu, nu] to mimic sigma-correlation at NO extra cost - mu scales the diagonal exchange (controls the ionic S1), nu the off-diagonal coupling (controls multiconfigurational covalent states). Practical guidance the paper establishes: mu = 0.0 (simply dropping the exchange integral g_pq,qp) is usually optimal and makes the S1 energy independent of the exchange integral, halving the CASSCF singlet-triplet gap to one exchange integral rather than two; nu = 0.0 is best when only the HOMO-LUMO transition matters, but nu = 0.5-0.7 is safer when higher multiconfigurational covalent states are of interest. The recommended default is [0.0, 0.5].

Vertical excitation energies (eV): 2 1Ag- (covalent) SA-CASSCF 5.57 / XS[0,0] 5.61 / XS[0,0.5] 5.34 / MR-CISD+P 5.53 / TBE 5.62; 1 1Bu+ (ionic HOMO-LUMO) SA-CASSCF 7.39 / XS[0,0] 5.32 / XS[0,0.5] 5.59 / MR-CISD+P 5.45 / TBE 5.37; 1 1Bu- SA-CASSCF 6.79 / XS[0,0] 8.49 (MR-CISD+P 6.81). The stated limitation is equally explicit: 'CASSCF is not a highly accurate method if metal-ligand bonds become considerably covalent' — a real concern with thiolate donors — and where it failed, SORCI on top of the same CAS(2,5) reference was used, with thresholds Tpre, Tnat and Tsel of 1e-5, 1e-5 and 1e-6 Eh.

point_group: D3 for the homoleptic complexes, C2 for the mixed-ligand ones
geometry_source: geometries optimized with density functional theory in the ground spin state, four functionals compared against the crystal structure with the meta-GGA giving the best match; no reoptimization at the multiconfigurational level
method: state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field with the spin-orbit mean-field operator diagonalized over the resulting states by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory to obtain the zero-field splitting; second-order N-electron valence perturbation theory on the same reference for dynamic correlation, and the ab initio results then mapped onto a ligand field parameterization
basis_set: TZVP on all atoms for the property calculations; the geometry optimizations used TZVP except SV(P) on carbon and hydrogen
relativistic_treatment: none beyond the spin-orbit mean-field operator
active_space_orbital_description: the five metal 3d-based orbitals
active_space_protocol: A minimal space: the four d electrons in the five metal d orbitals, state-averaged over 45 triplet and 5 quintet states so that the whole d-manifold is available for the spin-orbit treatment. The minimality is the paper's central methodological finding and it cuts both ways. Adding dynamic correlation perturbatively on this reference does fix the ground-state spin multiplicity, which the bare self-consistent-field calculation gets wrong, but it overestimates the quintet and singlet excited states in all four complexes and badly distorts the trigonal splitting of the lowest triplet - state-specific rather than state-averaged calculations did not help. Since both the singlet and quintet excited states matter for the low-lying spin levels, the paper concludes flatly that the perturbative correction is not applicable here in conjunction with a minimal active space. The self-consistent-field quintet energies, by contrast, are usable, and are the input to the ligand field analysis from which the magnetic parameters are derived. Doing better would mean correlating 33 electrons in 20 orbitals, which the authors call presently infeasible.
multiplicities_studied: triplet and quintet, with singlets spanned by the ligand field analysis
nroots_per_mult: 45 triplet and 5 quintet states state-averaged; the full d4 manifold of 210 microstates enters the magnetization calculation
electronic_structure_description: Quintet terms from 5Eg at 0, from 5T2g at 25440 (E) and 28107 cm-1 (A1), and triplets from 3T1g at 14714 (E) and 19091 cm-1 (A2). The trigonal splitting is positive as in the tris-dithiolate complex. D is large and positive at 20 cm-1 - roughly twice the tris-dithiolate value - with the easy plane again perpendicular to the threefold axis, magnetization 1.22 in plane and 0.00 along the axis.
Other: The ligand field fit gives the same sigma-antibonding energy of 10000 cm-1 as the tris-dithiolate complex but a much smaller out-of-plane pi-antibonding energy, 1230 cm-1 against 3700. The two ligands also differ in the phase relationship of their pi interaction - out-of-phase here, in-phase for the dithiolate - which by itself would invert the sign of the t2g splitting; the twist angle of the real structure overrides that and restores the same sign, but leaves the splitting much smaller, and the smaller gap is precisely why D is twice as large here. No magnetic measurements existed for this complex.
reference_short: Atanasov, Surawatanawong, Wieghardt and Neese, Coord. Chem. Rev. 257, 27 (2013)
notes: One of four iron(IV) complexes in the series, treated identically. States lying close to the low-energy charge-transfer manifold were omitted from the tabulated terms. The zero-field splitting parameters come from mapping the self-consistent-field results onto an angular overlap ligand field model, with the interelectronic repulsion parameters taken over by analogy from the chromium(III) dithiocarbamate analogue rather than fitted here. Computed high-field low-temperature magnetizations exceed the measured ones by 0.34 to 0.45 Bohr magnetons, but the trend across the series is reproduced. This is a review article, but these calculations are original to it.
correlation_correction: second-order N-electron valence perturbation theory on the same reference, with the perturbative energies entering only the diagonal of the spin-orbit matrix; judged inapplicable for these iron(IV) complexes and used mainly as a diagnostic

compound_name: Cr(H2O)6(2+), the divalent hexaquochromium complex and its Jahn-Teller distortion
ligand_set: six water ligands in an approximately octahedral first coordination sphere
point_group: Oh idealized; the effective geometry at all three minima is D2h
geometry_source: Potential energy surfaces mapped along the two eg normal modes by state-averaged CASSCF on a grid, with a second finer grid of 16 x 42 = 672 points. Geometry optimizations were also performed with the B3LYP and BP86 functionals and the TZVP basis set, giving two sets of bond distances; the difference between theory and experiment is about 0.01 A for the axial Cr-O bonds and at most about 0.049 A for the equatorial ones.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for mapping the potential energy surfaces along the eg normal modes, with multireference difference dedicated configuration interaction (MR-DDCI2) and spectroscopy-oriented configuration interaction (SORCI) at the stationary points for the D tensor; quasi-degenerate perturbation theory and second-order perturbation theory both used to extract D and E
basis_set: TZVP and the more extensively polarized TZVPP
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic treatment; the Breit-Pauli two-electron spin-orbit coupling operator approximated by the spin-orbit mean field (SOMF) approach
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in the five metal d-based orbitals, CAS(4,5). For the Table 2 CASSCF calculations the 4 d electrons were used together with the 5 d orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is the five metal d-based orbitals and nothing else, with the electron count set by the oxidation state, so the two complexes differ only in occupancy and can be compared directly. Everything the space omits is recovered by other means rather than by enlargement: dynamic correlation by MR-DDCI2 and SORCI single points at the stationary points of the CASSCF surface, spin-orbit coupling by the spin-orbit mean field approximation, and spin-spin coupling separately. The state averaging is deliberately exhaustive at first -- all 10 quartet and 35 doublet roots for Cr(III), all 5 quintet and 35 triplet roots for Cr(II) -- and only then truncated for the fine grid, where the five quintets and the eight most important triplets were kept so that a 16 x 42 = 672-point surface became affordable. Individually selecting MR thresholds were Tsel 1e-6 Eh, Tpre 1e-4 and Tnat 1e-5 Eh.
nroots_per_mult: All five quintet and 35 triplet states on the initial grid; the five quintets and the eight most important triplets on the finer 672-point grid
electronic_structure_description: Jahn-Teller stabilization energy and the splitting of the 5Eg ground term at the minimum of the CASSCF/TZVPP surface, in cm-1: CASSCF/TZVP 954 and 3984; CASSCF/TZVPP 1082 and 4625; MRDDCI2/TZVP 1188 and 4318; MRDDCI2/TZVPP 1457 and 4483; SORCI/TZVP 1340 and 4485; SORCI/TZVPP 1708 and 4630; experimental about 1600 and about 6500. When a SORCI calculation is performed at the experimentally determined Jahn-Teller radius rather than the computed one, the splitting rises to 6600 cm-1, in excellent agreement with the observed transition near 8000 cm-1 (of which about 1500 cm-1 is attributed to strain effects). The zero-field splitting D at the CASSCF/TZVPP minimum is -2.45 cm-1 at SORCI/TZVPP against an experimental -2.2 cm-1; at the experimentally determined Jahn-Teller radius it is -2.34 cm-1, taken as the best theoretical result. The computed E is 0.04 cm-1 against an experimental estimate below 0.1 cm-1; a finite E cannot be explained within sigma bonding alone, where zero would be obtained. Table 3 decomposition at the TZVPP level (SOC-triplets / SOC-quintets / SSC, cm-1): CASSCF/QDPT: -1.012 / -1.067 / -0.371, total D = -2.45 cm-1. SORCI: -1.068 / -1.020 / -0.360, total D = -2.448 cm-1. MR-DDCI2: -1.063 / -1.105 / -0.364, total D = -2.532 cm-1. Experimental D about -2.3 cm-1 (measured, as quoted in Table 3). CASSCF/QDPT with the TZVP basis (Table 6): SOC -2.2, SSC -0.38, total D = -2.58 cm-1. The spin-spin contribution is essentially geometry independent and is about 15 percent of the total D. Second-order perturbation theory reproduces the exact D to within 1.4 percent or 0.033 cm-1 across the theta normal mode. In D2h both the Oh T1g and T2g states map onto B1g + B2g + B3g and can spin-orbit-couple with the ground state.
Other: The five-orbital d-only space with four electrons gets the zero-field splitting right and the Jahn-Teller surface wrong, and the paper separates the two failures cleanly. On the surface, CASSCF/TZVPP underestimates both the Jahn-Teller energy (1082 against about 1600 cm-1) and the 5Eg splitting (4625 against about 6500 cm-1); adding dynamic correlation improves both monotonically -- MRDDCI2 to 1457 and SORCI to 1708 cm-1 for EJT -- but the splitting stays too small because the calculated Jahn-Teller radius is too short. Evaluating SORCI at the experimental radius instead raises the splitting to 6600 cm-1 and brings it into excellent agreement, so the residual error is geometric rather than electronic. Crucially, this does not contaminate the property of interest: by symmetry the 5Eg state contributes nothing to D, so its underestimated splitting is harmless. The D value itself is reproduced to -2.45 cm-1 at SORCI/TZVPP against -2.2 cm-1 experimental, and the authors note explicitly that the decomposition results are unchanged when MR-DDCI2 or SORCI replaces state-averaged CASSCF -- so for D the minimal space suffices and the correlation treatment is not load-bearing, the reverse of the situation for the surface. The spin-spin contribution is 15 percent of the total, needed for quantitative accuracy but ignorable qualitatively, and second-order perturbation theory reproduces the full quasi-degenerate treatment to 1.4 percent.

notes: The experimentally observed optical transition near 8000 cm-1 is assigned to the transition between the tetragonally split components of the 5Eg (Oh) ground term. ligand_set: six water ligands in an approximately octahedral first coordination sphere
point_group: Oh; the complex is inferred to adopt an average configuration in solution quite close to cubic
geometry_source: Potential energy surfaces mapped along the two eg normal modes by state-averaged CASSCF with the TZVP basis set. Geometry optimizations yielded Cr-O distances of 2.0 A, in fair agreement with experimental results.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for mapping the potential energy surfaces along the eg normal modes, with multireference difference dedicated configuration interaction (MR-DDCI2) and spectroscopy-oriented configuration interaction (SORCI) at the stationary points for the D tensor; quasi-degenerate perturbation theory and second-order perturbation theory both used to extract D and E

Individually selecting MR thresholds were Tsel 1e-6 Eh, Tpre 1e-4 and Tnat 1e-5 Eh.
electronic_structure_description: The d3 configuration gives a 4F ground term which under the octahedral ligand field splits into an orbitally nondegenerate 4A2g ground term and two triply degenerate 4T1g and 4T2g excited terms. Geometry optimizations gave Cr-O distances of 2.0 A. Second-order perturbation theory reproduces the exact D to within 10.4 percent or 0.08 cm-1. Distortions of only about 0.02 A are enough to induce the experimentally observed D value of 0.1 cm-1, from which it is inferred that the trivalent complex adopts an average configuration in solution quite close to cubic. The spin-spin contribution to D is essentially zero for this complex, in contrast to the divalent case. CASSCF/QDPT with the TZVP basis at the fully symmetric geometry (Table 6): SOC 0.000, SSC 0.000, total D = 0.000 cm-1.
Other: With an orbitally nondegenerate 4A2g ground term there is no Jahn-Teller distortion to map, so the same CAS(3,5) space is used purely to compute how the zero-field splitting responds to imposed geometric distortion -- and the answer is that 0.02 A of distortion produces the entire experimental D of 0.1 cm-1. That sensitivity is the finding: the property is so small and so steeply geometry-dependent that the calculation cannot be used to predict D from an optimized structure, only to invert the measured D into a statement about the average solution geometry. The perturbative treatment is also noticeably worse here than for the divalent complex, 10.4 percent error against 1.4 percent, though the absolute deviation is comparable (0.08 versus 0.033 cm-1) because D itself is twenty times smaller. Unlike the divalent complex the spin-spin contribution vanishes, so the whole of D comes from spin-orbit coupling to the 4T excited terms. The state averaging is over all 10 quartet and 35 doublet roots, i.e. the complete d3 manifold within the space, so no root selection enters this result.

notes: This complex was included because of the smallness of its associated D value. electronic_structure_description: Ground state of the d5 Cr(I) centre in a two-coordinate, quasi-linear N-Cr-N geometry. Computed zero-field splitting D = 0.2 cm-1 with E/D = 0.3, and an isotropic g tensor slightly smaller than the free-electron value. No slow relaxation of magnetisation is observed.
Other: The three metals in the same two-coordinate ligand field come out with completely different magnetic anisotropies from the same kind of calculation, and the paper uses that to explain a negative experimental result: the Cr(I) complex has D = 0.2 cm-1 with E/D = 0.3, the Mn(I) complex D = 1.9 cm-1 with E/D = 0.16, and the Co(I) complex an ideally axial D = -55 cm-1 with E/D = 0.16. Magnetic isotropy for Mn(I) and strongly non-axial anisotropy for Co(I) are what account for the absence of observable slow relaxation of magnetisation. | A d-shell-only active space with NEVPT2 on top is the standard tool for this kind of ligand-field analysis, and its output here is not just a number but a rhombicity: the E/D ratios are what decide whether a large axial D translates into single-molecule-magnet behaviour, and for these complexes they do not. | Experimental fits to the magnetic data give D = -100 cm-1 with |E/D| = 0.22 and g_parallel = 3.43 for one compound and D = 0.39 cm-1 with |E/D| = 5.5e-3 and g_parallel = 2.43 for another, so the computed and fitted D values agree in sign and order of magnitude but not in detail - a reminder that a d-only space plus NEVPT2 gives the right ligand-field picture without quantitative D values.
