method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by n-electron valence second-order perturbation theory, with spin-orbit coupling treated nonperturbatively by diagonalization over 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states; spin-Hamiltonian parameters extracted by the effective Hamiltonian approach, and the molar magnetic susceptibility computed from the same wave functions including both spin-orbit and Zeeman effects
basis_set: Relativistically recontracted def2-TZVP for hydrogen through barium and an all-electron relativistically contracted SARC basis of the same quality for rhenium; the initial minimal-space calculations used ANO-RCC-VDZ, with resolution of the identity and matching correlation fitting sets
relativistic_treatment: Second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian; spin-orbit coupling by the spin-orbit mean-field approximation, applied nonperturbatively
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in nine orbitals for the reported calculations: the five rhenium 5d orbitals together with the highest occupied, the lowest unoccupied and two further virtual orbitals of the o-benzoquinone ligand. The minimal space was four electrons in six orbitals, the five 5d orbitals plus the ligand's lowest unoccupied orbital; spaces up to eight electrons in ten orbitals were also tested.
active_space_protocol: Spaces were varied from four electrons in six orbitals up to eight in ten, and the authors report that similar results were obtained in all cases, which is the relevant check when the question is how much ligand character mixes into metal-based states. The minimal space is the smallest capable of representing the redox ambiguity: the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron.
nroots_per_mult: 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states in the reported state-averaged calculation
electronic_structure_description: A triplet ground state whose wave function has strongly multireference character: three configurations contribute substantially, and the state is a superposition of a rhenium(IV)-semiquinolate form and a rhenium(V)-catecholate form with comparable weights, the former predominating above 54 percent. The complex is therefore formally a rhenium(IV) semiquinolate but is more accurately a mixed-valence species. This matches the crystallography independently: C-O, C-C and Re-O distances at both 150 and 290 K lie between the semiquinolate and catecholate limits, giving an empirical metrical oxidation state of -1.5 for the dioxolene ligand. In the minimal space the quintet lies 0.38 eV (3060 reciprocal centimetres) above the triplet and the lowest singlet 1.36 eV (10940 reciprocal centimetres) above it. Spin-orbit coupling produces an anomalously large zero-field splitting of the pseudospin S = 1 ground state. SOC-CASSCF(6,9): D = 341 cm-1, E/D = 0.019, giso 1.78. SOC-CASSCF(6,9)/NEVPT2: D = 481 cm-1, E/D = 0.026, giso 1.77. These are consistent with the measured magnetic susceptibility from 5 to 300 K. Measured (fit of chi(T), model 2, one S = 1 centre): D = 816 cm-1, E/D = 0.31, g = 1.93. Measured (fit of chi(T), model 1, Re(IV) S = 3/2 coupled to semiquinone S = 1/2, J = -1024 cm-1): D = 572 cm-1 for Re(IV), E/D = 0.25, g = 1.94. All absorption bands in the visible region are assigned as ligand-to-metal charge transfer, with a significant intraligand contribution to the most intense band at 555 nm.
Other: The space is varied deliberately across a range and the paper reports the most reassuring possible outcome: similar results in all cases. A minimal space of four electrons in six orbitals -- the five rhenium 5d orbitals plus the lowest unoccupied orbital of the quinone -- was run first, then spaces enlarged as far as eight electrons in ten orbitals, with the reported calculations using six electrons in nine orbitals, adding the ligand's highest occupied orbital and two further virtuals. Stating that the answer is stable across that range is worth more than any single number, because the question being asked is precisely how much ligand character mixes into the metal-based states, and a result that moved as ligand orbitals were added would be an artifact of the space rather than a finding. The minimal space is defined by a clear rule -- the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron -- which is the smallest space capable of representing the redox ambiguity at issue. The chemical payoff is a wave function that cannot be reduced to a single oxidation state: three configurations contribute substantially, and the ground triplet is a superposition of a metal(IV)-semiquinone form and a metal(V)-catecholate form with comparable weights, the former predominating at above 54 percent. A 54-to-46 split is exactly the regime where a formal oxidation state stops being meaningful, and the calculation is what converts a qualitative suspicion of ligand noninnocence into a number. It also agrees independently with the crystallography: bond distances fall between the two limiting forms, giving an empirical metrical oxidation state of -1.5 for the ligand. Two independent lines of evidence for the same intermediate character is much stronger than either alone. A cost-driven compromise is stated plainly rather than hidden: the correlated calculations with the larger basis were too expensive on the real molecule, so tert-butyl groups were replaced by hydrogens and phenyl groups by methyls, and every reported spectrum and spin-Hamiltonian parameter comes from that truncated model rather than from the compound actually crystallized. Spin-orbit coupling is treated NONPERTURBATIVELY, by diagonalizing over 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states, which is necessary here because the resulting zero-field splitting is anomalously large -- 341 reciprocal centimetres at one level and 481 at the correlated level, values at which perturbative treatments of spin-orbit coupling are not valid. The 40 percent spread between those two numbers is itself informative about how much the correlation treatment matters for this property, even where it barely matters for the state composition.

An independent determination gives -52 with the same zero rhombicity. The large negative axial parameter is the signature of an easy-axis system. Measured (SQUID susceptibility and magnetization): D = -52(2) cm-1, E/D = 0.00(3), gx,y = 2.08(9), gz = 2.6(2). Measured (HFEPR, g_perp fixed at 2.08): D = -57(1) cm-1 (Table 3 lists -55). Measured (FD-FT THz-EPR): 2D' = 110(2) cm-1, |D| = 55(1) cm-1 assuming 0 <= E/D <= 0.03. Measured (VTVH MCD): D between -20 and -90 cm-1, gz 2.6-2.9.
Other: The space is the minimum that the physics allows - seven electrons in the five cobalt 3d-based orbitals - but the STATE MANIFOLD is complete: all states arising from the d7 configuration, namely 10 quartets and 40 doublets, are included. For a zero-field-splitting calculation that completeness is not optional. The splitting arises from spin-orbit mixing of excited states into the ground state, so any state left out is a contribution silently set to zero, and with only ten quartets and forty doublets in total there is no excuse for truncating. What makes the paper unusually strong as a test of the method is that the same chemical anion is measured in two different salts and the anisotropy differs not just in magnitude but in KIND: strongly axial in one, with an axial parameter of -55 reciprocal centimetres and essentially zero rhombicity, and rhombic in the other, with +11 and a rhombicity of 0.18. The sign of the axial parameter flips between two crystals of the same complex ion. Since the electronic description is identical - same metal, same ligands, same space, same manifold - the entire difference must come from the geometry the counterion imposes, so the calculation is being asked to reproduce a purely structural effect with everything else held fixed. That is a far more demanding test than matching one number, and it is the reason the study can claim a genuine magneto-structural correlation rather than a fitted agreement. The experimental side is correspondingly over-determined, with the parameters pinned independently by magnetometry, high-field electron paramagnetic resonance, variable-field variable-temperature magnetic circular dichroism, and frequency-domain terahertz spectroscopy; a value confirmed by four techniques leaves the calculation nowhere to hide. Spin-orbit coupling enters through a mean-field approximation and the spin-Hamiltonian parameters are extracted by an effective Hamiltonian mapping rather than by fitting. Scalar relativistic effects are handled with a second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess treatment on a relativistically recontracted triple-zeta basis, and geometries come from a dispersion-corrected density functional.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 8S7/2 from the 4f7 configuration, S = 7/2, splitting into four Kramers doublets. The lowest excited sextet states lie near 40000 cm-1 for Gd(III) and lower for Eu(II). For Gd(III) the 9-coordinate complex shows the smallest total splitting of the ground octet (0.0695 cm-1) and a negative D, while the 7- and 8-coordinate complexes have positive D. The Ni-O sigma bond is more covalent here than in the oxyl form. As in that species the pi*(xz) and pi*(yz) orbitals are nearly degenerate, and state-averaged CASSCF gives D = -201.1 cm-1 with E = 0.067 cm-1 - a larger axial splitting and an essentially vanishing rhombicity compared with the oxyl electromer.

The wider study finds that the energetic preference for Ni(III)=O over Ni(IV)=O implies that the relevant pi bonding is destabilised in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement just as it is in octahedral complexes. These species are proposed to perform hydrogen atom abstraction and oxo transfer; they are too reactive and transient for direct characterisation, and only indirect spectral evidence of their formation exists.

notes: The point of the paper is that the electronic structure of putative Ni(III)-oxo species is not unambiguously established, and the pair of near-degenerate electromers computed here is the answer offered: not one species but two, differing in where the unpaired electron sits and in the Ni-O bond length. The CASSCF contribution is confined to the zero-field splitting; everything else - geometries, spin-state energetics, reaction profile, spectra and reactivity - is B3LYP. Since the two electromers differ in exactly the Ni-O covalency that a d-only active space omits, the fact that it returns markedly different D values for them (-201.1 against -143.9 cm-1) comes entirely through the differing geometries rather than through any explicit treatment of the bond.

Computed zero-field-splitting parameters (D in cm-1, E/D, and gxx, gyy, gzz): CoOZn@C70 D = -184.6, E/D = 0.01, g = 1.41, 1.66, 4.28; CoOZn@C80 D = -148.1, E/D = 0.03, g = 1.94, 2.23, 3.72; CoZnScN@C76 D = -141.2, E/D = 0.01, g = 1.22, 1.80, 3.70; CoZnScN@C82 D = -150.1, E/D = 0.04, g = 1.86, 2.18, 3.72. The linearity around the Co(II) is greatest in CoOZn@C70, then CoZnScN@C82, then CoOZn@C80, which is the order of the computed anisotropy. Multi-determinant wavefunctions of the ground and excited states are reported for each, showing all CI coefficients above 10%.
Other: A minimal metal-only space - five 3d orbitals, seven electrons - is used unchanged across an entire screening ensemble of fullerene cages and isomers, which is the point: with the space fixed, differences in the computed zero-field splitting can be attributed to the cage rather than to the calculation. The authors' own justification for the setup is that ab initio CASSCF/NEVPT2 gives a better estimate of anisotropy than density functional methods, and that the NEVPT2 correction specifically is what makes the zfs parameters accurate, so the analysis is restricted to NEVPT2-corrected energies rather than raw CASSCF ones. Note what a (7,5) cannot see: nothing of the cage is active, so ligand-field effects enter only through the orbitals' response, and the paper's finding that the Co(II) ion moves freely inside the smaller cages - which would speed relaxation of magnetisation - comes from molecular dynamics rather than from the active space. That combination, DFT-based molecular dynamics coupled to CASSCF/NEVPT2 to capture conformational isomers, is described as employed here for the first time. These models are where the (7,5) space delivers its largest numbers - D up to about -185 cm-1 with E/D of 0.01, so almost purely axial - and the paper attributes the ordering across the four to the linearity of the coordination around the Co(II) rather than to cage size. The very anisotropic g tensors (gzz around 3.7-4.3 against gxx near 1.2-1.9) are the signature of the strong axial ligand field with weak transverse field that the small metal-only space is designed to capture. The practical claim is that these units offer a viable route to air-stable low-coordinate Co(II) centres.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 4A2 derived from 4F in Td parentage, S = 3/2. The three spin-allowed 4A2(4F) -> 4T1(4P) transitions are computed at 15125, 15808 and 16902 cm-1 for this molecule, against an experimental 15300, 15782 and 16670 cm-1 (Table 4). An ORCA simulation of the MCD spectrum confirms that the negative MCD band contains two of these spin-allowed transitions and that the higher-energy positive signal is spin-forbidden and must be left out of the crystal-field analysis.
Other: The choice of spin-orbit treatment moves D by about 2 cm-1 on a 6-10 cm-1 quantity, which is larger than the spread between the experimental techniques: on the same CASSCF(7,5)/NEVPT2 wavefunction, second-order perturbation theory gives 8.39 and 10.54 cm-1 for molecules 1 and 2 while the effective-Hamiltonian route gives 6.40 and 8.32. The same split appears in the MCD analysis (7.77 vs 6.63 for molecule 1, 6.01 vs 5.06 for molecule 2), so it is a property of the two ZFS extraction protocols rather than of the wavefunction. | A minimal five-orbital d space with NEVPT2 is enough to put both molecules in the 3-12 cm-1 band the authors report for six related pseudo-tetrahedral [CoL2Cl2] complexes, and to reproduce the positive sign and moderate rhombicity.

electronic_structure_description: Quartet (S = 3/2) ground state 4-1b_hs on a distorted square-pyramidal Mn(IV); the doublet 2-1b_ls lies 115.3 kJ/mol higher. The state-averaged CASSCF wavefunction is strongly mixed: the leading configuration (delta_xz)1(pi*_xy)1(pi*_yz)1(sigma*_z2)0(sigma*_x2-y2)0 carries only 47.6 percent, mixed with three excited quartet configurations at 15.6, 13.3 and 12.0 percent, all generated by promotion into the sigma*_z2 and sigma*_x2-y2 orbitals. NEVPT2 gives D = +/-0.38 cm-1 and E/D = 0.33
Other: The active space is strictly metal-only throughout: three electrons in five Mn 3d orbitals for the Mn(IV) species and four electrons in the same five 3d orbitals for the one-electron-reduced Mn(III) species, with no ligand orbital, no second d shell and no enlargement, convergence or basis test of any kind reported. The quantity the paper extracts from that space is precisely the quantity most sensitive to its composition - the weight of the leading configuration - and it is used causally, to explain why Mn(IV)=O is sluggish (66.3 percent leading weight, called dominantly single-reference) while Mn(IV)-OOH (47.6 percent) and Mn(IV)-OH (30.5 percent) are reactive. electronic_structure_description: Low-spin Mn(III), d4, S=1 at low temperature. Incomplete reversible LS-to-HS crossover begins above 400 K and reaches about 20% HS conversion at 400 K; ideal-solution fitting gives T1/2 = 560 K, DeltaH = 18.5 kJ mol-1 and DeltaS = 33.1 J K-1 mol-1. Other: This counterion series isolates packing and cation-anion control of spin state. At 100/240 K, 1 has average Mn-N/O distances 1.968/1.969 A and small octahedral CShM values 0.368/0.386; representative 100 K distances are Mn-Namine 2.0332, Mn-Nimine 1.9854 and Mn-O 1.8861 A. Strong N-H...Cl and C-H...Cl contacts form a 1D network that stabilizes the LS state, whereas the larger counterions in 2-4 permit HS-favoring aromatic interactions. omegaB97M-D4 comparisons of [Mn(ligand)]+ and [Mn(ligand)]Cl support thermodynamic/kinetic chloride stabilization of LS: LS-to-HS DeltaEel+ZPE is -0.522 versus -0.105 kcal mol-1 and LS-to-MECP is 2.525 versus 2.670 kcal mol-1, respectively. None of 1-4 shows slow magnetic relaxation. The Mn(III/II) reduction and Mn(III/IV) oxidation couples occur near -0.45 and +0.36 V versus Fc/Fc+

electronic_structure_description: High-spin Co(II), 3d7, S = 3/2, in a distorted octahedral {CoO5N} environment surrounded by three diamagnetic low-spin Co(III) ions. The free-ion 4F term is split by the pseudo-octahedral ligand field into 4T1g, 4T2g and 4A2g, and the real symmetry further splits the 4T1g term into three terms spanning 0 to about 2000 cm-1; spin-orbit coupling on those three lowest terms gives the six lowest Kramers doublets. The two lowest Kramers doublets can be described by an S = 3/2 spin Hamiltonian because the next doublets lie more than 1000 cm-1 higher, and effective Hamiltonian theory then gives D = -53.6 cm-1 with E/D = 0.294, against a POLYMAGNET fit of the measured magnetization giving D = -51.3 cm-1, E/D = 0.263 and g = 2.41. The transversal magnetic moment matrix element between the ground states of opposite magnetization is 0.59, well above the 0.1 threshold for efficient tunnelling, and the computed blocking barrier is U = 120 cm-1. Experimentally the compound shows only a small out-of-phase tail at zero field and clear field-induced slow relaxation at 500 Oe
Other: One active space, one protocol, two close relatives, and a sevenfold difference in accuracy. The identical CAS(7e,5o) metal-only space, the identical DLPNO-NEVPT2 correction, the identical basis and code are applied to the octahedral Co(II) centre of each complex, and the computed axial zero-field splitting is compared against a fit of the measured magnetization. For complex 1 the agreement is excellent: D = -53.6 cm-1 computed against -51.3 fitted, about four and a half percent. For complex 2 the same protocol gives -42.7 against -31.9 fitted, thirty-four percent too large. Nothing about the method changed; what changed is the molecule. Complex 1 contains exactly one paramagnetic centre, a single Co(II) surrounded by three diamagnetic low-spin Co(III) ions, so a single-ion 3d space is the whole magnetic problem. Complex 2 contains two exchange-coupled Co(II) ions, and the paper has to compute their coupling by an entirely separate broken-symmetry DFT calculation - so the single-ion multireference is being asked to reproduce a fitted parameter that the fit itself extracted from a two-centre spin Hamiltonian including J. The article never states how the second Co(II) was handled in the CASSCF for complex 2: no diamagnetic substitution is described, no fragment is named, and the methods text refers only to 'the CoII ion' in the singular. The second finding is that the multireference tunnelling diagnostic does not discriminate between the two compounds at all. SINGLE_ANISO gives transversal magnetic moment matrix elements between the ground states of opposite magnetization of 0.59 for 1 and 0.56 for 2, both far above the 0.1 threshold at which efficient relaxation is expected - essentially the same number. Yet complex 1 is a field-induced single-ion magnet and complex 2 shows no out-of-phase signal whatever, with or without an applied field. The single-ion diagnostic is degenerate across an SMM and a non-SMM, and the factor that actually separates them - the weak Co-Co exchange in 2 opening alternative relaxation pathways - lies outside the multireference entirely and is supplied by density functional theory. The space is complete within its own terms: all possible multiplets of the d7 configuration, ten quartets and forty doublets, are included rather than an energy-window subset. And the AILFT analysis locates the difference between the two complexes in the first coordination sphere: 10Dq is evidently lower in complex 2, attributed to the change of chromophore from {CoO5N} to {CoO3N3}. Against that, the space is bare - five 3d orbitals, no ligand orbital, no second d shell - and it is never enlarged or tested in either compound, so on the complex where it fails there is no evidence about whether composition or the correction is at fault. This is the member on which the protocol succeeds, and it is also the member with exactly one paramagnetic centre - the single-ion space and the single-ion physics coincide

electronic_structure_description: Co(II) with a 4A2 ground term. The first transition energy at CASSCF + NEVPT2 is 4200 reciprocal centimetres. In the spin-orbit multiplet spectrum the last member of the spin-only model space lies at 33.1 and the first multiplet outside it at 4174 reciprocal centimetres. The projection norm for the first member of the model space is 0.98 and the resulting validity score for the spin-Hamiltonian approximation is 1704. A real compound treated at its own experimental geometry.
Other: The multireference licenses or refuses a phenomenological model rather than a cheaper computational method, and it refuses it in two cases out of twelve. The spin-Hamiltonian formalism works in a model space of fictitious spin kets |S,M> only; here the CASSCF + NEVPT2 + spin-orbit multiplets are treated as the exact answer within the complete active space of dn configurations, the relativistic states are projected back onto the spin-only subspace, and the quality of that projection becomes a quantitative test of whether the spin Hamiltonian is entitled to exist for the compound. Two criteria: the projection norm N for each multiplet, which must not stray far from 1, and the gap separating the hypothetical spin-only manifold from the rest of the spin-orbit spectrum, combined into a score S. Of twelve complexes the paper reports two clear violations and two more it calls questionable. The failure condition is named: the projection breaks down when the ground term is orbitally (quasi)degenerate and the first transition energy falls below about 1000 reciprocal centimetres, the same divergence that makes the older second-order perturbative route to the D-tensor return false D, E and g values. Worst case is the pentacoordinate cobalt(II) member with a 4E ground term, projection norm 0.69 and score 6, against 0.999 and scores in the tens of thousands for the orbitally nondegenerate manganese(II) members. The active space is metal-only and complete within itself: five d orbitals holding the dn configuration, spanning all 45, 120, 210 or 252 kets for d2/d8, d3/d7, d4/d6 and d5, with no truncation by energy window, which is what makes the projection norm meaningful. The scale of the reduction is given for one example: [CoCl2(PPh3)2] has 337 electrons and 718 orbitals, of which 7 electrons and 5 orbitals are active, giving 120 relativistic states projected onto just 4 spin-only kets. The space carries no ligand orbital, no second d shell and no test of either, so metal-ligand covalency is absent from the reference being used to judge the approximation, and the paper offers no estimate of how much that matters for the projection norms. Eight of the twelve complexes are hypothetical: only [Co(PPh3)2Cl2], [Co(PPh3)2Br2], [Ni(biqu)Br2] and [Ni(cyclam)(N3)]+ are real compounds at their own experimental geometries, the other eight being produced by substituting the metal into a host geometry while holding the ligand field fixed, and the article does not state how the overall charge is handled when a divalent host ion is replaced by manganese(III). The paper limits its own licence: the calculations 'refer to the vacuum state of neutral molecules and ignore the presence of the solid-state environment (at least the dielectric properties)', and 'even more critical is evaluations for cationic complexes that ignore the anionic counterparts and Madelung potential', which applies to the five cationic cyclam-azide members. It nonetheless states that these calculations 'are superior over any semiempirical method, such as the GCFT', whose parameters it notes depend strongly on the choice of crystal-field poles even at fixed experimental geometry.

electronic_structure_description: Mn(III) with a 5B1 ground term. The first transition energy at CASSCF + NEVPT2 is 10786 reciprocal centimetres. In the spin-orbit multiplet spectrum the last member of the spin-only model space lies at 12.8 and the first multiplet outside it at 8953 reciprocal centimetres. The projection norm for the first member of the model space is 0.999 and the resulting validity score for the spin-Hamiltonian approximation is 9633. A metal-substituted model at the host compound's experimental geometry.
Other: The multireference licenses or refuses a phenomenological model rather than a cheaper computational method, and it refuses it in two cases out of twelve. The spin-Hamiltonian formalism works in a model space of fictitious spin kets |S,M> only; here the CASSCF + NEVPT2 + spin-orbit multiplets are treated as the exact answer within the complete active space of dn configurations, the relativistic states are projected back onto the spin-only subspace, and the quality of that projection becomes a quantitative test of whether the spin Hamiltonian is entitled to exist for the compound. Two criteria: the projection norm N for each multiplet, which must not stray far from 1, and the gap separating the hypothetical spin-only manifold from the rest of the spin-orbit spectrum, combined into a score S. Of twelve complexes the paper reports two clear violations and two more it calls questionable. The failure condition is named: the projection breaks down when the ground term is orbitally (quasi)degenerate and the first transition energy falls below about 1000 reciprocal centimetres, the same divergence that makes the older second-order perturbative route to the D-tensor return false D, E and g values. Worst case is the pentacoordinate cobalt(II) member with a 4E ground term, projection norm 0.69 and score 6, against 0.999 and scores in the tens of thousands for the orbitally nondegenerate manganese(II) members. The active space is metal-only and complete within itself: five d orbitals holding the dn configuration, spanning all 45, 120, 210 or 252 kets for d2/d8, d3/d7, d4/d6 and d5, with no truncation by energy window, which is what makes the projection norm meaningful. The scale of the reduction is given for one example: [CoCl2(PPh3)2] has 337 electrons and 718 orbitals, of which 7 electrons and 5 orbitals are active, giving 120 relativistic states projected onto just 4 spin-only kets. The space carries no ligand orbital, no second d shell and no test of either, so metal-ligand covalency is absent from the reference being used to judge the approximation, and the paper offers no estimate of how much that matters for the projection norms. Eight of the twelve complexes are hypothetical: only [Co(PPh3)2Cl2], [Co(PPh3)2Br2], [Ni(biqu)Br2] and [Ni(cyclam)(N3)]+ are real compounds at their own experimental geometries, the other eight being produced by substituting the metal into a host geometry while holding the ligand field fixed, and the article does not state how the overall charge is handled when a divalent host ion is replaced by manganese(III). The paper limits its own licence: the calculations 'refer to the vacuum state of neutral molecules and ignore the presence of the solid-state environment (at least the dielectric properties)', and 'even more critical is evaluations for cationic complexes that ignore the anionic counterparts and Madelung potential', which applies to the five cationic cyclam-azide members. electronic_structure_description: Ni(II) d8 in a pentagonal bipyramid. The CASSCF/NEVPT2 axial zero-field-splitting parameter is D = -11.8 reciprocal centimetres with E = -1.4 cm-1. For the nickel complexes the negative D comes from the first triplet excited state, whose contribution runs from -66.0 to -75.6 reciprocal centimetres across the series, partially cancelled by positive contributions of about 20 to 28 from the second and third triplet excited states.
Other: The chemical argument is about ligand-field effects and is read through a space that contains no ligand orbital. The spaces are bare metal 3d shells - CAS(8,5) for the nickel(II) complexes and CAS(7,5) for the cobalt(II) ones - with no ligand orbital, no second d shell, and no enlargement or sensitivity test anywhere. The study is about how replacing a weak sigma-donor aqua ligand by a stronger sigma-donor thiocyanate in the axial positions moves the d-orbital energies, and those energies are extracted by ab initio ligand field theory from that same metal-only space, so the covalency difference between an aqua and a thiocyanate donor - the variable being manipulated - is not representable in the space. The state manifold is complete: all the multiplets of each configuration are carried, 10 triplets and 15 singlets for the d8 nickel systems and 10 quartets and 40 doublets for the d7 cobalt ones, averaged over all of them rather than over an energy window. Two extraction routes from one wavefunction give systematically different answers and the paper reports it: the zero-field-splitting parameters are taken from an effective Hamiltonian approach, but the perturbative method in the same code was also run and 'the D values extracted by this method were found to be slightly overestimated as compared to those obtained from the effective Hamiltonian method' - same space, same correction, same wavefunction, a different number with a stated direction purely from how D is projected out. The decomposition of D identifies which factor drives the trend: for the nickel series the axial parameter is resolved into contributions from the first three triplet excited states, and across compounds 1 to 5 the second and third barely move, 26.9 to 21.2 and 25.9 to 19.8 reciprocal centimetres, while the first runs -66.0 to -75.6, so the whole variation in D from -11.8 to -25.7 is carried by the first excited state, whose energy is set by the d(xy) versus d(x2-y2) splitting and hence by distortion of the equatorial pentagon. The same substitution moves the two metals in opposite directions for one reason: replacing axial aqua by thiocyanate raises the d(z2) orbital in both and so reduces the positive contributions to D from states reached by promotion into it. In the nickel complexes, where D is negative, that makes D more negative - within the daplh family -11.8 and -11.5 become -18.6, and within the daphibh family -18.4 becomes -25.7 - while in the cobalt complexes, where D is positive, the same mechanism makes D smaller: 39.4, 38.6 and 39.4 for the aqua complexes against 36.8 and 36.9 for the thiocyanate ones.

The conclusions restate it - the sign of D is set by the relative positions of the three lowest spin-orbit multiplets, and 'in the case of E/D ~ 0.33, this stays uncertain'. The failure condition is tied to orbital degeneracy and predicted in advance from geometry: for pentacoordinate Ni(II) at the trigonal bipyramid (D3h, tau5 = 1) the ground term is the orbitally degenerate 3E and 'the D-parameter is undefined', with six spin-orbit multiplets in play that have 'no relationship to the spin-Hamiltonian parameters D and E'; at the tetragonal pyramid (C4v, tau5 = 0) the ground term is nondegenerate and D is positive; in between, at C2v, D runs from large negative to positive and crosses zero at tau5 about 0.2. The three complexes with 3E ground terms return the largest axial parameters in the study, -397, -510 and -544 reciprocal centimetres, and those are the cases where the spin Hamiltonian has no standing. The active space is the complete d8 manifold and nothing more - all 45 kets - the same space used by the semiempirical generalized crystal field theory run alongside it, so the two methods are compared on identical footing; but it carries no ligand orbital and no second d shell, and no enlargement or sensitivity test appears anywhere. electronic_structure_description: Ni(II) d8, S = 1, in a pentacoordinate NiN3Br2 environment of C2v symmetry (vOC-5 shape index 2.83, SPY-5 shape index 3.72). The ground electronic term is orbitally nondegenerate, with the first excitation energy at NEVPT2 being 6035 reciprocal centimetres. Spin-orbit coupling splits the ground term into spin-orbit multiplets from which an effective Hamiltonian gives an axial zero-field splitting parameter of D = +17 reciprocal centimetres. Experimentally D is reported as +11.0 from DC magnetic data, +13.9 from EPR and +13.8 from frequency-domain magnetic resonance
Other: The paper defines a threshold beyond which its own computed D-parameter is meaningless and marks the offending values in its table: 'E/|D| close to the critical value of 0.33 implies that the sign of D is uncertain and D stays meaningless; problematic values are printed in italics.' The conclusions restate it - the sign of D is set by the relative positions of the three lowest spin-orbit multiplets, and 'in the case of E/D ~ 0.33, this stays uncertain'. The failure condition is tied to orbital degeneracy and predicted in advance from geometry: for pentacoordinate Ni(II) at the trigonal bipyramid (D3h, tau5 = 1) the ground term is the orbitally degenerate 3E and 'the D-parameter is undefined', with six spin-orbit multiplets in play that have 'no relationship to the spin-Hamiltonian parameters D and E'; at the tetragonal pyramid (C4v, tau5 = 0) the ground term is nondegenerate and D is positive; in between, at C2v, D runs from large negative to positive and crosses zero at tau5 about 0.2. The three complexes with 3E ground terms return the largest axial parameters in the study, -397, -510 and -544 reciprocal centimetres, and those are the cases where the spin Hamiltonian has no standing. The active space is the complete d8 manifold and nothing more - all 45 kets - the same space used by the semiempirical generalized crystal field theory run alongside it, so the two methods are compared on identical footing; but it carries no ligand orbital and no second d shell, and no enlargement or sensitivity test appears anywhere. The experimental reference varies by technique: for the trigonal-bipyramidal complex 5 the measured D is -311 from magnetometry against -535 from EPR, and for complex 6 it is -179 by EPR, -110 by far-infrared magnetic spectroscopy and -205 from calculation.

electronic_structure_description: Ground state S = 3/2 (4A2 parentage). SOC-CASSCF(7,12)-NEVPT2: D = -6.6 cm-1, E = 1.65 cm-1. Measured (SQUID magnetometry fit): D = 8.0(1) cm-1, E = 0.8(4) cm-1, gxx = 1.61(1), gyy = 2.12(2), gzz = 1.90(2). Measured (HFEPR simulation, 5 K): D = 6.7(1) cm-1, E = 0.8(5) cm-1, gxx = 1.61(3), gyy = 2.12(5), gzz = 1.90(3). Measured (X-band EPR simulation, with HFEPR D/E/g): J = -0.7 cm-1 (intermolecular exchange). CASSCF(7,12)-NEVPT2: lowest 4A2->4T2 at 308 nm; lowest doublet has 2T1 character. Measured (absorption, MeCN-d3): spin-flip 4A2->2T1/2E bands and a 1200-1500 nm band assigned to a distorted 2T1-parentage state; NIR-II phosphorescence at ca. 1550 nm.
Other: CASSCF(7,12)-NEVPT2 reproduces the magnitude of the measured ZFS but gives the wrong sign of D (-6.6 vs +6.7 cm-1, sign of D>0 supported by variable-temperature HFEPR); the authors note the same behaviour for the V(II) analogue, where the sign of D depended on the active space chosen. The same level overestimates absolute spin-flip transition energies by ca. 2000-3000 cm-1 but reproduces the larger 2T1/2E spread in cisfac-[3]3+ than in mer-1/mer-2. A simulated MCD spectrum from CASSCF(7,7)-NEVPT2 did not match the experiment, attributed to 4A2->4T2 bands being hidden under 4CT bands. Calculations on the transfac and mer isomers of [3]3+ predict only a minor influence of ligand configuration on doublet energies, with the 2E-parentage states shifted up in the facial isomers (Figure S50).

electronic_structure_description: The lowest triplet excited state, whose three spin sublevels are split only by the relativistic spin-spin interaction. Other: Lowering the variational energy does not improve the derived property, and the energies are printed alongside so it can be checked. Across CAS(4,4), (8,8), (12,12), (14,14), (16,16), DMRG(18,18) and the full-pi DMRG(22,22) on pentacene (table 3) the total energy falls monotonically from -841.317403 to -841.577315 hartree, while D runs 0.0286, 0.0307, 0.0354, 0.0371, 0.0402, 0.0374, 0.0386 cm-1 - peaking at (16,16), dropping at (18,18) and only partly recovering at the complete space. Against a measured 0.0467 cm-1 the intermediate CAS(16,16) is closer to experiment than the complete full-pi space. E runs +0.0059, +0.0080, +0.0050, -0.0021, -0.0029, +0.0037, -0.0002 cm-1 against a measured -0.0018, changing sign three times. The point needs no active-space change at all: at the same full-pi DMRG-CASSCF(22,22), bond dimensions of 1024 and 1536 give an identical total energy to six decimal places, -841.577315 hartree, yet D differs by 0.0386 against 0.0398 cm-1 and E by -0.0002 against -0.0009. The authors state it: 'with increasing bond dimensions, the convergence of the ZFS parameters was slower compared to the convergence of the energy.' For anthracene the energy error against full configuration interaction falls 1.4661, 0.0567, 0.0009 and below 0.0001 cm-1 across M = 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 while D creeps 0.0586, 0.0618, 0.0634, 0.0642 toward its 0.0643 limit; for phenanthrene the energy error starts at 23.7229 cm-1 while D is already within 0.0008 cm-1 of the exact answer at the crudest bond dimension, then moves non-monotonically through -0.1245, -0.1255, -0.1250, -0.1252 to -0.1253, which the authors name as coincidental, saying it 'indicates that error cancellation may occur in the calculation of the ZFS parameters using the DMRG-CASSCF method'. Because the exact limit within the space is available the residual error is diagnosable: anthracene's D converges to 0.0643 cm-1 at full configuration interaction in the full-pi space against a measured 0.0702, still 8 percent low, and phenanthrene's E to 0.0151 cm-1 against a measured 0.027, still 44 percent low, so what survives belongs to the composition of the space (full-pi carries no sigma orbitals), to the perturbative treatment of the spin-spin operator, or to the geometries; the authors point at the second, noting 'there is a possibility to improve the convergence behavior along the bond dimension if the D tensor is evaluated in a nonperturbative manner'. What the large space buys is measured on all sixteen molecules: root-mean-square deviation and mean absolute percentage error for D are 0.0172 cm-1 and 12.9 percent for full-pi DMRG-CASSCF, against 0.0284 cm-1 and 28.1 percent for CASSCF(12,12) and 0.0422 cm-1 and 44.0 percent for LC-BLYP, so going from twelve orbitals to the complete pi valence halves the D error. The gain is property-specific: for E the same enlargement moves the error only from 51.5 to 46.4 percent, 'which indicated the difficulty of predicting E-values and suggested that a further increase in computational level may be necessary', and the rhombicity parameter eta is worse again at 68.0 percent. The space rule is automatic and orbital-class based - all valence pi orbitals every time, extracted either from natural orbitals of an MP2 density matrix or through the atomic valence active space module of PySCF, then localized and manually ordered for the DMRG sweep, an ordering step shown only in a supporting-information figure. Spin-orbit coupling was computed and found negligible rather than assumed away: below 0.0001 cm-1 even for the magnesium and zinc porphyrins, because the triplet is a pi-pi* excitation on the ring rather than on the metal, so every D reported is essentially pure spin-spin coupling. A basis check across cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ and cc-pVQZ found double-zeta sufficient.

notes: One of the two convergence test cases. Its D-value approaches 0.0586, 0.0618, 0.0634 and 0.0642 cm-1 at bond dimensions 256, 512, 1024 and 2048, reaching 0.0643 at the full configuration-interaction limit of the space - while the energy error against that limit collapses from 1.4661 to below 0.0001 cm-1 over the same range. The property converges far more slowly than the energy. Crucially, the exact value within the space is still 8 percent below the measured 0.0702 cm-1, so the residual error belongs to the pi-only composition, the perturbative spin-spin operator or the geometry, and not to any remaining correlation. Sixteen molecules were chosen because each has a measured triplet ZFS - thirteen all-benzenoid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and three porphyrins - and every one carries its own theoretical and experimental D, E and eta in Table 1, so each gets a row. The calculation supplies something the measurement cannot: electron spin resonance yields only the magnitudes |D| and |E|, and the paper lists all experimental D-values as positive by convention, while the computed D tensor delivers the SIGNS and the directions of the magnetic axes directly. Eight of the sixteen are predicted to have NEGATIVE D. For every molecule in the set the out-of-plane direction came out as a principal axis and as the lowest of the three spin sublevels - the Z axis where D is positive and the X axis where it is negative. A structural correlation is drawn and properly qualified: among molecules with the same number of pi orbitals, those with more Clar sextets show larger D-values, with the oligoacenes having only one sextet; the authors flag that whether Clar's rule can simply be applied here is not settled. They also caution that ZFS 'is not necessarily accounted for by the distribution of the spin density, which is a one-body property because the electron SSC is a two-body interaction'. Geometries come from two different levels within the same benchmark: triplet structures were optimized at CASPT2(12,12)/cc-pVTZ(-f) for the oligoacenes and at TD-DFT with LC-BLYP/def2-TZVP, range-separation parameter 0.15, for everything else - so a geometry-level difference runs through the set and is not controlled for. All experimental ZFS values are other groups' measurements, drawn from ten separate references, and get no rows of their own. That makes the residual error against experiment attributable to the space, the operator or the geometry rather than to unrecovered correlation within the space, since bond-dimension studies show the full configuration-interaction limit is reached. relativistic_treatment: no scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian; the relativistic content is the spin-spin and spin-orbit contributions to the zero-field splitting itself. notes: The molecule that demonstrates error cancellation, which the authors state. The paper states the small-M agreement is coincidental and indicates error cancellation. Its E-value tells the complementary story: it converges to 0.0151 cm-1 at the exact limit against a measured 0.027, still 44 percent low with nothing left to converge, which locates that error outside the correlation treatment entirely. Sixteen molecules were chosen because each has a measured triplet ZFS - thirteen all-benzenoid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and three porphyrins - and every one carries its own theoretical and experimental D, E and eta in Table 1, so each gets a row. Eight of the sixteen are predicted to have NEGATIVE D. geometry_source: triplet geometry optimized by TD-DFT at LC-BLYP/def2-TZVP with the range-separation parameter set to 0.15, the level used for every molecule outside the oligoacene series

software: PySCF for the DMRG-CASSCF and the active-orbital extraction, including its AVAS module; ORCA 5.0.3 for the TD-DFT geometries and the density-functional comparison

A cc-pVDZ/cc-pVTZ/cc-pVQZ comparison found double-zeta sufficient
soc_included: yes, and computed to be negligible - below 0.0001 cm-1 even for the magnesium and zinc porphyrins, because the triplet is a ring pi-pi* excitation rather than a metal-centred one
ss_included: yes - electron spin-spin coupling is the dominant contribution and the object of the study
active_space_orbital_description: the full valence pi space; the paper does not state the electron and orbital count for this molecule in the body, giving explicit sizes only for anthracene and phenanthrene at (14,14) and pentacene at (22,22)
active_space_protocol: an automatic orbital-class rule with no chemical selection: take all valence pi orbitals. The orbitals are extracted from natural orbitals of an MP2 density matrix or through the atomic valence active space module of PySCF, then localized and manually ordered for the DMRG sweep. Bond dimension M = 1024 throughout Table 1, with separate convergence studies at 256, 512, 1024 and 2048
nroots_per_mult: a single state; the triplet is treated state-specifically
electronic_structure_description: The lowest triplet excited state, whose three spin sublevels are split only by the relativistic spin-spin interaction. The computed D tensor gives D = -0.1019 cm-1 and E = 0.0128 cm-1 with a rhombicity eta of 0.13, against measured magnitudes of 0.1016 and 0.0286 cm-1 and a measured eta of 0.28. The experiment yields magnitudes only; the sign here is the calculation's own result. The out-of-plane direction is a principal axis and the lowest of the three sublevels
Other: Lowering the variational energy does not improve the derived property, and the energies are printed alongside so it can be checked. Across CAS(4,4), (8,8), (12,12), (14,14), (16,16), DMRG(18,18) and the full-pi DMRG(22,22) on pentacene (table 3) the total energy falls monotonically from -841.317403 to -841.577315 hartree, while D runs 0.0286, 0.0307, 0.0354, 0.0371, 0.0402, 0.0374, 0.0386 cm-1 - peaking at (16,16), dropping at (18,18) and only partly recovering at the complete space. Against a measured 0.0467 cm-1 the intermediate CAS(16,16) is closer to experiment than the complete full-pi space. E runs +0.0059, +0.0080, +0.0050, -0.0021, -0.0029, +0.0037, -0.0002 cm-1 against a measured -0.0018, changing sign three times. The point needs no active-space change at all: at the same full-pi DMRG-CASSCF(22,22), bond dimensions of 1024 and 1536 give an identical total energy to six decimal places, -841.577315 hartree, yet D differs by 0.0386 against 0.0398 cm-1 and E by -0.0002 against -0.0009. The authors state it: 'with increasing bond dimensions, the convergence of the ZFS parameters was slower compared to the convergence of the energy.' For anthracene the energy error against full configuration interaction falls 1.4661, 0.0567, 0.0009 and below 0.0001 cm-1 across M = 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 while D creeps 0.0586, 0.0618, 0.0634, 0.0642 toward its 0.0643 limit; for phenanthrene the energy error starts at 23.7229 cm-1 while D is already within 0.0008 cm-1 of the exact answer at the crudest bond dimension, then moves non-monotonically through -0.1245, -0.1255, -0.1250, -0.1252 to -0.1253, which the authors name as coincidental, saying it 'indicates that error cancellation may occur in the calculation of the ZFS parameters using the DMRG-CASSCF method'. Because the exact limit within the space is available the residual error is diagnosable: anthracene's D converges to 0.0643 cm-1 at full configuration interaction in the full-pi space against a measured 0.0702, still 8 percent low, and phenanthrene's E to 0.0151 cm-1 against a measured 0.027, still 44 percent low, so what survives belongs to the composition of the space (full-pi carries no sigma orbitals), to the perturbative treatment of the spin-spin operator, or to the geometries; the authors point at the second, noting 'there is a possibility to improve the convergence behavior along the bond dimension if the D tensor is evaluated in a nonperturbative manner'. What the large space buys is measured on all sixteen molecules: root-mean-square deviation and mean absolute percentage error for D are 0.0172 cm-1 and 12.9 percent for full-pi DMRG-CASSCF, against 0.0284 cm-1 and 28.1 percent for CASSCF(12,12) and 0.0422 cm-1 and 44.0 percent for LC-BLYP, so going from twelve orbitals to the complete pi valence halves the D error. The gain is property-specific: for E the same enlargement moves the error only from 51.5 to 46.4 percent, 'which indicated the difficulty of predicting E-values and suggested that a further increase in computational level may be necessary', and the rhombicity parameter eta is worse again at 68.0 percent. The space rule is automatic and orbital-class based - all valence pi orbitals every time, extracted either from natural orbitals of an MP2 density matrix or through the atomic valence active space module of PySCF, then localized and manually ordered for the DMRG sweep, an ordering step shown only in a supporting-information figure. Spin-orbit coupling was computed and found negligible rather than assumed away: below 0.0001 cm-1 even for the magnesium and zinc porphyrins, because the triplet is a pi-pi* excitation on the ring rather than on the metal, so every D reported is essentially pure spin-spin coupling. A basis check across cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ and cc-pVQZ found double-zeta sufficient.

The same wavefunction gets one parameter essentially exactly and the other wrong by more than half, which is the clearest single-molecule statement of the paper's D-versus-E finding. Predicted to have negative D. Sixteen molecules were chosen because each has a measured triplet ZFS - thirteen all-benzenoid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and three porphyrins - and every one carries its own theoretical and experimental D, E and eta in Table 1, so each gets a row. The calculation supplies something the measurement cannot: electron spin resonance yields only the magnitudes |D| and |E|, and the paper lists all experimental D-values as positive by convention, while the computed D tensor delivers the SIGNS and the directions of the magnetic axes directly. Eight of the sixteen are predicted to have NEGATIVE D. For every molecule in the set the out-of-plane direction came out as a principal axis and as the lowest of the three spin sublevels - the Z axis where D is positive and the X axis where it is negative. A structural correlation is drawn and properly qualified: among molecules with the same number of pi orbitals, those with more Clar sextets show larger D-values, with the oligoacenes having only one sextet; the authors flag that whether Clar's rule can simply be applied here is not settled. They also caution that ZFS 'is not necessarily accounted for by the distribution of the spin density, which is a one-body property because the electron SSC is a two-body interaction'. geometry_source: DFT-optimised high-spin ground-state geometry; the CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations are single points on it. The manganese(III) coordination environment is described as effectively square pyramidal with the acetate in the axial position.
method: CASSCF with NEVPT2 and ab initio ligand field theory (AILFT); DFT and TD-DFT
software: ORCA 5.0.2; Multiwfn 3.8 for the lambda parameter and delta-r index
basis_set: def2-TZVP with the def2-TZVP/C auxiliary Coulomb fitting basis
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess for the CASSCF calculations; spin-orbit and spin-spin coupling operators applied to obtain the zero-field splitting and the g tensor of the lowest spin-orbit state
active_space_orbital_description: The five manganese 3d orbitals holding the four d electrons of Mn(III)
active_space_protocol: CAS(4,5) spanning the five Mn 3d orbitals and the four d electrons - the minimal d-only space for Mn(III) - chosen specifically because it lets the ORCA ab initio ligand field theory module run, so that the wavefunction can be translated into ligand-field d-orbital energies. All multiplets of the d4 configuration are included in the wavefunction expansion, 10 quintets, 45 triplets and 50 singlets, and the zero-field splitting and g tensor of the lowest spin-orbit state are then obtained by applying spin-orbit and spin-spin coupling operators, with Douglas-Kroll-Hess relativistic treatment. The space is not varied and no ligand orbitals are correlated, which is the usual limitation of a d-only AILFT space: covalency with the porphyrin and the axial ligands enters only through the orbital optimisation. The calculations are single points on DFT-optimised high-spin geometries. The validation is against experiment and against DFT on the same geometries: NEVPT2 gives D of about -3.5 cm-1 for both complexes while DFT gives the same sign at roughly half the magnitude, and the authors note the NEVPT2 values agree with earlier experimental and computational work. The spin labels printed for the multiplets (S = 5/2, 3/2, 1) and for the optimised ground state geometry (S = 5/2) are wrong for a d4 ion and inconsistent with the quintet ground state the same text describes.
nroots_per_mult: all multiplets of the 3d4 configuration: 10 quintets, 45 triplets and 50 singlets (the article labels these as S = 5/2, 3/2 and 1 respectively, which is inconsistent with a d4 configuration, where the correct values are S = 2, 1 and 0)
electronic_structure_description: High-spin quintet (S = 2) ground state on a d4 Mn(III) centre, consistent with the observed high-spin behaviour. CASSCF/NEVPT2 zero-field splitting parameters: D = -3.49 cm-1 with E/D = 0.001491 (the table heading prints this as D/E), and g tensor components 1.98, 1.99, 1.99 giving g_iso = 1.99. The high-spin to low-spin energy difference is 63.51 kcal/mol. DFT on the same geometry gives D = -1.59 cm-1, E/D = 0.009202 and g = 1.99, 2.00, 2.00 with g_iso = 2.00 and a high-spin / low-spin gap of 51.91 kcal/mol - the same sign of D but about half the magnitude, and a gap 11.6 kcal/mol smaller. AILFT d-orbital energies relative to the lowest singly occupied d(xy): d(xz) at about 2100 cm-1 and d(yz) at about 2525 cm-1, close together; the highest singly occupied orbital is predominantly d(z2) at 8493 cm-1, pushed up by bonding with the acetate. The total d splitting, from the highest occupied to the lowest empty orbital, is 10487 cm-1.
Other: The parent complex against which the dyad is compared. Femtosecond transient absorption measurements place the formation time and lifetime of the excited 5T1 state at 1.5 and 13.9 ps for the related dyad, with (AcO)MnTPP behaving similarly. The wider study covers self-assembly of this and two further manganese(III) macrocycles - the tetra-4-tert-butylphenylporphyrin and the octakis(4-tert-butylphenyl)tetraazaporphyrin analogues - with 4-(10-phenylanthracen-9-yl)pyridine to give 1:1 dyads in toluene, characterised by fluorescence spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, 1H NMR, IR, ESR and cyclic voltammetry.
reference_short: E. N. Ovchenkova, A. A. Tsaturyan, N. G. Bichan et al., Chem. Asian J. 19, e202400095 (2024)
notes: Only this complex and its PyAn dyad receive the multireference treatment; the tert-butylphenyl porphyrin and tetraazaporphyrin members of the series are treated with DFT and TD-DFT only. The CAS(4,5) space here is doing a specific and limited job - feeding AILFT so that a ligand-field d-orbital diagram and a zero-field splitting can be extracted - rather than describing correlation in the porphyrin pi system, so the excited-state and charge-transfer analysis in the paper rests on TD-DFT, not on the CASSCF.

notes: The one species in the study with a direct experimental check on the computed magnetic parameters, and the agreement with the ESR data in both sign and magnitude is what the authors use to justify the protocol. electronic_structure_description: A four-coordinate high-spin Co(II) centre in a distorted tetrahedral CoO4 environment, giving easy-plane anisotropy. The computed axial zero-field splitting is positive - 17.9 per centimetre for the S enantiomer and 18.0 for the R - against 10.0 fitted from the magnetic data, and the rhombic term is 1.8 and 1.2 against 1.0 and 1.4 fitted. The computed g tensors are (2.411, 2.441, 2.167) and (2.421, 2.436, 2.168), nearly axial in the xy plane. Effective barriers of 46(1) and 41(1) K are measured under a 1000 Oe field. The first excited quartet state dominates the D value, and this compound's larger ground-to-first-excited gap is what keeps its D small and positive
Other: The calculation gets the sign right and the magnitude consistently twofold too large, and because two compounds with opposite signs behave the same way the overshoot is measurable rather than anecdotal. Against the values fitted from the magnetic data, the computed axial zero-field splitting runs 17.9 and 18.0 per centimetre against a fitted 10.0 for the difluoro compound, and -69.2 and -66.1 against a fitted -30.0 for the dinaphthyl one. The rhombic term behaves identically: 1.8 against 1.0, and -18.8 against -8.7. Four complexes, two opposite signs, and a ratio near two in every case. Nothing here shows the factor would transfer to a third compound. The 'experimental' reference is itself a constrained fit, and the constraint is one the calculation contradicts. The footnote to the comparison table reads: 'to avoid overparameterization during fitting in PHI, g(x) was constrained to equal g(y)'. But the CASSCF/RASSI-SO g tensors for the dinaphthyl compound are 1.951, 2.523 and 3.041 - g(x) and g(y) differing by more than half a unit. The measurement against which the calculation is judged was extracted under an assumption the calculation says is false, so the twofold discrepancy is not purely a failure of theory; part of it may be the price of a rhombic system fitted with an axial model. Two enantiomers must have identical magnetic anisotropy; any computed difference is pure protocol noise. Here the computed values differ by 0.1 per centimetre for the difluoro pair and 3.1 for the dinaphthyl pair - about 0.6 and 4.5 percent - each calculation having been run on its own separately determined crystal structure. That is a direct measure of how much the answer moves with structural and numerical noise. The fitted barriers scatter far more between the same pairs - 46(1) against 41(1) K, and 63(6) against 48(2) K, differences of 11 and 24 percent - so the experiment is noisier than the calculation between systems that must be identical. D is decomposed state by state and one term dominates, which reduces the design problem to a single energy gap. 'For all four complexes, the first excited quartet state provides the largest contribution to the D value. Accordingly, the magnitude of D is closely correlated with the energy separation between the ground state and the first excited state. Hence, for S/R-Co-N, the smaller ground-to-first-excited-state energy gaps account for their larger negative D values.' The gap is set by the ligand field and the ligand field by the 3,3' substituent. The structure-property control is unusually clean: the two compounds share the metal, the oxidation state, the CoO4 donor set, the BINOLate ligand class and the guanidinium counter-cations, differing only in the 3,3' substituent - fluorine against naphthyl. That change alone converts a distorted tetrahedron into a distorted seesaw with smaller dihedral and bite angles, and flips the anisotropy from easy-plane to easy-axis. The active space is never stated in the body - no electron count, no orbital count, no composition - the text saying only that 'additional computational details [are] given in the Supporting Information'

notes: The easy-plane member, and the one whose enantiomers agree most closely. The basis set is not stated in the body; it is deferred to the supporting information. No crystallographic symmetry is stated; the coordination geometry is a distorted tetrahedron. No active-space protocol is described: no selection rule, no root count, no state-averaging scheme and no basis set appear in the body. The one stated methodological choice is that the crystallographic geometries were used as input without optimization. Electronic spectrum: within 10 eV, 12 symmetry-allowed states, none with oscillator strength above 7.3e-2; only two significant features, near 6.4 and 8.1 eV.

compound_name: s-trans-1,3-butadiene — excited-state potential energy curves along the terminal twist coordinate
geometry_source: scan along a terminal twist coordinate with all other bonds and angles frozen at their S2 planar minimum values
method: SA-CASSCF compared with dynamically weighted CASSCF using a new dynamical-weight-with-spline (DWS) scheme; analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF derived for the first time, enabling energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: 4 electrons in 4 orbitals (the butadiene pi system)
active_space_protocol: (4,4) held fixed; the paper's subject is the STATE-AVERAGING scheme rather than the orbital space. SA-4-CASSCF/6-31G* (four states in the average) exhibits energy discontinuities in all states at the point where S3 — which is included in the state averaging — crosses S4, which is not. This is the general pathology: discontinuities appear in SA-CASSCF potential energy surfaces whenever a state left out of the average crosses one that is included, and they break energy conservation in excited-state dynamics. The remedy demonstrated here is dynamical weighting with a spline, DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF, which mimics SA-CASSCF while smoothly removing the discontinuities due to unweighted state crossings. Practical guidance: when choosing how many states to state-average, the risk is not only the orbital active space but which states are omitted from the average along the coordinate of interest
nroots_per_mult: 4 for SA-4-CASSCF; DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF uses a dynamical weight with an energy width parameter of 6 eV
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet (S0). States S0-S4 are followed along the terminal twist coordinate; the discontinuity arises at the S3/S4 intersection, with S3 included in and S4 excluded from the state averaging, and is visible even in S2. Absolute state energies are presented graphically rather than tabulated in the extracted text, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: Method contribution: a new dynamical weight with spline (DWS) scheme that reproduces SA-CASSCF behaviour while removing energy discontinuities from unweighted state crossings, plus the first derivation of analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF and other dynamically weighted schemes. This enables energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics in cases where SA-CASSCF fails. Butadiene's terminal twist coordinate is used as the demonstration because SA-CASSCF discontinuities there are severe
reference_short: Communication: Smoothing out excited-state dynamics: Analytical gradients for dynamically weighted CASSCF, J. Chem. Phys. 141, 171102 (2014)

method: CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCI with single and double excitations, plus the Pople size-consistency correction; R-dependent spin-orbit couplings and the radial derivative coupling <2 3Sigma_u+|d/dR|A 3Sigma_u+> also computed
basis_set: aug-cc-pV5Z in the short range (R < 6 a0)

active_space_protocol: single active space throughout: all 2s and 2p valence orbitals plus three extra bonding [sigma_g, pi_u(x,y)] orbitals, 1s cores optimized but doubly occupied; no build-up sequence. State-averaging scheme is the substantive choice: orbitals for 2 3Sigma_u+ come from a state-averaged calculation together with A 3Sigma_u+ and A' 3Delta_u; orbitals for A 3Sigma_u+ and A' 3Delta_u from a state average of only those two; all other states are lowest in their symmetry and optimized independently. In the MRCI, all configurations contributing more than 1% to the CASSCF wave function are used as references; A 3Sigma_u+ and A' 3Delta_u energies are obtained in a single calculation optimizing both states simultaneously, while 2 3Sigma_u+ is obtained by optimizing only the third B1u state
Other: Central methodological result: the near degeneracy in the long range of the same-symmetry states 2 3Sigma_u+ and A 3Sigma_u+ can produce unphysical mixing of these states in a CASSCF calculation; the authors derive the correct asymptotic behaviour dictated by the quadrupole-quadrupole interaction and show how to recover it. Three problems were encountered with the standard CASSCF(+MRCI) approach beyond R = 6 a0, including CASSCF convergence failures and discontinuities in the MRCI potentials. Vibrational energies G(v) and rotational constants B(v) reproduce all experimentally known levels of A 3Sigma_u+ to a few tenths of a percent, the largest errors being for the highest vibrational levels just below dissociation. R-dependent spin-orbit couplings between the eight ungerade states are reported

compound_name: H2SiN+ molecular ion (interstellar silicon-nitrogen chemistry; compared throughout with its SiNH2+ isomer)
geometry_source: geometry optimized at each level of theory (ROHF, MP2, MP3, MP4, CCSD(T) and CASSCF); the FOCI and SOCI single-point energies use the CASSCF geometry
method: CASSCF(10,10), with FOCI (first-order CI, 599 768 CSFs) and truncated SOCI (1 168 408 CSFs) single points at the CASSCF geometry; compared against ROHF, MP2, MP3, MP4 and CCSD(T)
basis_set: 6-311++G** on hydrogen and nitrogen; the expanded McLean-Chandler basis on silicon; 3-21G and 6-31G* used for preliminary work
active_space_orbital_description: all distributions of the 10 valence electrons among the 10 bonding, antibonding and nonbonding orbitals sigma(SiH1), sigma(SiH2), sigma(SiN), pi(SiN), sigma(pN), 2pN, sigma*(SiH1), sigma*(SiH2), sigma*(SiN), pi*(SiN); 7400 CSFs of 3A2 symmetry. Chosen because nondynamic correlation was expected to be essential with two valence holes (terminal in-plane 2pN and the 2p pi orbital on N)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 3A2 in C2v — an open-shell triplet lying below the closed-shell singlet, with silicon retaining sp2 hybridization rather than pyramidalizing. ROHF occupancy (1a1)2(2a1)2(3a1)2(1b2)2(4a1)2(5a1)2(6a1)2(2b2)2(2b1)1(7a1)2(3b2)1. The leading CSF carries only about 67% weight in the CASSCF wave function (versus more than 90% for the SiNH2+ isomer), with the next two at 5.2% and 3.2%; these three account for only 76% of the wave function, the rest spread over many tiny contributions. The small reference weight is what makes single-reference MPn treatments unreliable here. Geometry: r(SiN) 1.794 A, r(SiH) 1.485 A, angle SiNH 118.60 deg at CASSCF/6-311++G** (vs 1.785 / 1.464 / 118.37 at CCSD(T)). The Si-N bond is longer than in SiN (1.572 A), HNSi (1.551 A) or SiNH2+ (1.66 A) because the pi(SiN) bond is much weaker. H2SiN+ lies about 115 kcal/mol above the absolute minimum of the (H,H,Si,N)+ surface, the X 1A1 state of SiNH2+; ROHF puts this gap 40 kcal/mol lower, a difference entirely attributable to nondynamic correlation (85 kcal/mol recovered for SiNH2+ on going ROHF -> CASSCF versus only 46 kcal/mol for H2SiN+). Valence-virtual dynamic correlation, defined as CASSCF minus SOCI, is 90 kcal/mol (82 kcal/mol in SiNH2+). Dipole moment 3.40 D (CASSCF), 4.03 D (FOCI), 3.8 +/- 0.2 D (SOCI). Scaled CASSCF rotational constants recommended for the main isotopomer: A0 149.811, B0 15.405, C0 13.969 GHz. Scaled CASSCF vibrational frequencies (cm-1, relative intensity): SiH2 wagging 542 (19.3%), SiH2 out-of-plane 411 (9.1%), SiN stretch 719 (3.0%), SiH2 bending 955 (38.9%), symmetric SiH2 stretch 2315 (11.4%), antisymmetric SiH2 stretch 2330 (18.4%). Predicted intense bands near 550, 950 and 2300 cm-1. Energies (a.u.) at 6-311++G**: CASSCF -344.242081, FOCI -344.317341, SOCI -344.385545; gap to SiNH2+ X 1A1: 123.6 (CASSCF), 158.2 (FOCI), 115.2 (SOCI) kcal/mol. Scaled CASSCF frequencies are also given for the isotopomers HD28Si14N+, D2 28Si14N+, H2 28Si15N+, H2 29Si14N+, H2 30Si14N+ (Table VI). Recommended scaled-CASSCF rotational constants A0/B0/C0 (GHz) for other isotopomers (Table IV): HD28Si14N+ 102.432/14.690/12.847; D2 28Si14N+ 74.982/14.131/11.890; H2 29Si14N+ 149.811/15.275/13.862; H2 30Si14N+ 149.811/15.153/13.761; H2 28Si15N+ 149.811/14.726/13.408.
Other: CASSCF(10,10) changes the IR spectrum qualitatively relative to the single-reference MPn methods: CSF2 (5.2%) couples sigma(SiH2) with the in-plane 2pN orbital, so the out-of-plane SiH2 frequency drops from about 600 to 411 cm-1 with its intensity reduced by a factor 4, and the SiH2 stretching and SiN stretching modes gain relative intensity; MPn predicts a quasi-complete extinction of the SiH stretches. The authors conclude properly described nondynamic correlation is essential for H2SiN+, and that the zeroth-order wave function must be good enough for the property even for ground states. Going from MPn to CASSCF lengthens the SiH bond by 0.02 A, a consequence of the weight of CSF2 in the CASSCF wave function, which weakens the SiH bond; the SiN bond also lengthens by 0.01 A at the CASSCF level, contrary to what CSF3 would suggest.
reference_short: Interstellar silicon-nitrogen chemistry. III. The spectral signatures of the H2SiN+ molecular ion, J. Chem. Phys. 104, 1979 (1996)
notes: Frequencies quoted are scaled (scaling factors derived from experimental spectra of HNSi, HSiN, HSiNH2 and HNSiH2). The isomer SiNH2+ is a comparison throughout but its active space is not stated in this paper. The paper prints two CASSCF frequency scaling factors: 0.970 in the text ("CASSCF/6-311++G**: 0.970") and 0.941 in the Table V footnote ("Scaling factors are ... CASSCF 0.941").

method: SA-4-CASSCF and dynamically weighted DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF (dynamical weight with cubic spline, L=4, alpha=6 eV) with new analytical DW-CASSCF gradients; AIMD on S2 (pi pi*): 30 trajectories, 100 fs, 10 au timestep (adaptively decreased), electronic transitions disabled, all C-H bond lengths constrained to ground-state equilibrium values

electronic_structure_description: SA-4-CASSCF(4/4)/6-31G* potential curves show a discontinuity of about 0.05 eV in all states at a terminal twist angle of 43 deg, where the unweighted S4 crosses S3 (included in the average). In AIMD on S2, SA-4-CASSCF(4/4)/6-31g gives total-energy discontinuities of as much as about 0.1 eV in most of the 30 trajectories; DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF shows no discernible discontinuities, only a spread of about +-0.002 eV over 100 fs, arising near a terminal twist of 90 deg where S3-S2 and S2-S1 intersections occur.
Other: The discontinuity comes from the state-averaging choice, not the orbital space: a state left out of the average (S4) crossing one in it (S3) causes a discontinuous orbital change. Adding S4 to the average would remove this one, but S5 crosses S4 along other coordinates, so adding states is generally futile; DWS3-(4,6eV) reproduces the SA-4-CASSCF curves while removing the discontinuity, because S3 and S4 weights become equal at their crossing. Alpha too small stops the CASSCF converging; too large needs many extra states and deviates from SA-L results; alpha=6 eV decays like sech weights with beta=3 eV. Gradients with fixed weights only give large energy fluctuations, so the weight-derivative terms cannot be neglected. CASSCF(4/4) significantly overestimates the vertical S1-S2 gap relative to higher levels, mainly from missing dynamic correlation, and hydrogen migration seen at SA-CASSCF(4/4) needs sigma and sigma* orbitals in the active space; it was suppressed by constraining the C-H bonds so the (4/4) space could be used.
reference_short: W. J. Glover, J. Chem. Phys. 141, 171102 (2014)
notes: The author presents butadiene here only as a model to demonstrate DWS-CASSCF energy conservation, not as an accurate description of its excited-state dynamics. Multiplicity is not stated (states labelled S0-S8).

method: spin-orbit CAS(1,7) for the three Kramers doublets of the 2F5/2 multiplet (g-factors, angular-momentum expectation values); state-specific scalar-relativistic CAS(1,7) natural orbitals; QTAIM and IQA bonding analyses (the paper does not state which electron density was used)
active_space_orbital_description: one electron in the seven Ce 4f orbitals

CASSCF (DFT-optimised): D = -6.05 cm-1, E/D = 0.105, g = 2.213, 2.227, 2.295; ground Kramers doublet g = 0.648, 0.728, 6.820. Largest contributions to D and E (NEVPT2, Figure 9) from the lowest 4A1 and 4E(1) states (negative D and E); smaller opposite-sign contributions from the lowest 2A1 and 2E(2) doublets. NEVPT2-derived AOM parameters (X-ray): e_sigma(Namine) 3223, e_sigma/e_pi(Ntbta) 4169/1404, e_sigma/e_pis/e_pic(Nazide) 6193/2437/2018 cm-1 (CASSCF: 2255; 3664/1268; 6121/2408/2195). Experimental: chiMT fit (E = 0) |D| = 11.3 cm-1, g = 2.34; magnetization fit D = -10.7 cm-1, E/D = 0.22; ac susceptibility under Hdc = 3000 Oe, Ueff = -2D = 19.7 cm-1, tau0 = 1.60e-8 s, giving D = -9.9 cm-1. The doublet contributions to D are neglected by coupled-perturbed Kohn-Sham methods, whose D values deviate abnormally from experiment.

method: CASSCF (1 octet + 48 sextets, orbitals state-averaged over octet and sextets) with the spin-orbit matrix diagonalised; D tensor from a CASSCF spin-orbit Hamiltonian by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (QDPT); for this complex an MRCI step on the same CASSCF orbitals was also run, with all or a reduced number of sextet roots

relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH) formalism; spin-orbit coupling by QDPT
active_space_orbital_description: seven orbitals modelling the 4f7 configuration of the metal
multiplicities_studied: octet and sextet; couplings to quartet and doublet states were ignored
nroots_per_mult: 1 octet and 48 sextets, state-averaged in the orbital optimisation
electronic_structure_description: Ground state: octet, S = 7/2 (8S in the isolated ion), split by SO coupling to the excited sextets into four Kramers doublets. CASSCF(7,7)/QDPT at its own optimised geometry: D = 0.0269 cm-1, E/D = 0.2325 (Table 2); total splitting of the ground octet 0.3627 cm-1 (Fig. 12 discussion). Lowest excited sextets of the Gd(III) complexes near 40200 cm-1; 40300 cm-1 for this complex (Sec. 3.6). At the optimised Eu(II)(H2O)7 geometry (Gd@Eu): D = 0.0206 cm-1, E/D = 0.1170 (Table 2), total splitting 0.2571 cm-1.
Other: CASSCF (1 octet + 48 sextets) gives D = 0.02712 cm-1, and an MRCI step on the same orbitals with all states does not change it, since there are no excitations into or out of the active space and the MRCI is equivalent to the CASSCF. Keeping only the three lowest sextets (largest SO couplings to the octet) in the MRCI, with the CASSCF state average unchanged, raises D to 0.199 cm-1, the ground-octet splitting from 0.365 to 2.397 cm-1, and the lowest excited sextet from 40300 to 41200 cm-1; three sextets are therefore insufficient. With 16 sextet roots the ground splitting is 1.4163 cm-1; with 21 it is 0.3834 cm-1, reasonably reproducing the full result. Roots 17-21 (from the 6D state of the isolated ion) couple to the lowest three sextets (from 6P), which couple to the octet; the intermediate thirteen roots (from 6I) contribute little.
reference_short: Khan, Peters, Kowalewski & Odelius, Chem. Phys. 503 (2018) 56-64
notes: ss_included left empty: only the spin-orbit contribution is computed, via QDPT; couplings to quartet and doublet states were ignored. The geometry-swap values of Table 2 (Gd@Eu, Eu@Gd) are the same ion placed in the other ion's optimised geometry and are given in electronic_structure_description rather than as separate rows. The authors state their CASSCF carries a systematic error from overestimated sextet energies, and that their earlier work on aqueous Gd(III) found CASSCF underestimates the ZFS by 10-20%. D for this complex is printed as 0.0269 cm-1 in Table 2 and 0.02712 cm-1 in Sec. 3.6, and its ground-octet splitting as 0.3627 cm-1 (Sec. 3.5) and 0.365 cm-1 (Sec. 3.6); both are recorded as printed.

DFT-MRCI: S0 0.0 (GS 0.93); S1 2.74 (H->L 0.82; f 1.47); S2 3.52 (H-1->L 0.37, H->L+1 0.10; f 0.56); S3 4.13 (H->L+1 0.28, H-1->L 0.15, H-2->L 0.11; f 0.25); S4 4.46 (H-2->L 0.26, H->L+1 0.22, H-1->L 0.13; f 0.08). E162-protonated model (CASSCF geometry): red shift of ca. 0.17 eV (ca. 30 nm) at MS-CASPT2 and more than 0.37 eV (70 nm) at DFT-MRCI. At the optimised 1Bu-like geometry: S1 emission 489 nm, f 1.69, HOMO-LUMO ca. 50%; S2 holds ca. 8% HOMO-LUMO and ca. 24% HOMO-LUMO double excitation (f 0.091); MS-CASPT2 S1-S2 gap 7.3 kcal/mol; S3 305 nm, f 0.12. CD-MS-CASPT2//CASSCF(12,12) torsion from -172 deg: positive pathway nearly barrierless toward the S0/S1 crossing CI- (ca. -100 deg twist); negative pathway barrier ca. 3.8 kcal/mol at 155 deg, then CI+ at ca. 110 deg; energy from the -172 deg S1 start to CI+ ca. 8.8 kcal/mol, to CI- ca. 1.25 kcal/mol; excess energy after excitation ca. 3.6 kcal/mol; S1 HOMO-LUMO character 45% rising to 55% during torsion; beta-ionone part carries ca. +0.6 e after excitation and relaxation. Ground-state geometry: C13=C14 twisted to -171 deg, C10-C11 -169 deg, C14-C15 -163 deg (overall M-helicity); CASSCF BLA ca. 1.35-1.49 A versus 1.38-1.44 A at DFT; 1Bu-like geometry bonds C9-C15 1.38-1.42 A. DFT overestimates the conjugation along the chain while CASSCF yields a more polyenic structure with larger BLA, and the level of conjugation strongly affects the absorption maximum.

method: SA-CASSCF / SS- and MS-CASPT2 (S-IPEA; also 0-IPEA) and SC-NEVPT2
active_space_orbital_description: All 12 pi electrons of the RPSB conjugated chain; minimal CAS(12,12) has one p-type orbital per heavy atom of the conjugated chain (6 occupied + 6 virtual pi), CAS(12,13) adds one extra virtual pi orbital (SI Fig. S13(h))
active_space_protocol: (12,12) minimal pi space; (12,13) +1 virtual pi, production; (12,14) check; (12,15) CASSCF-level check
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0, S1) in production; 3 (S0, S1, S2) tested
Other: Going from CAS(12,12) to CAS(12,13) lowers the 2-state CASSCF excitation by ~0.05 eV, changes CASPT2 by at most 0.02 eV and raises NEVPT2 by <0.05 eV, bringing NEVPT2 closer to QMC; (12,14) and (12,15) change nothing further, so (12,13) is the smallest converged space. Three-state averaging is more sensitive (CASSCF drops up to 0.2 eV, CASPT2 0.1 eV from (12,12) to (12,13)) because S1 and S2 are close and must be described by the same CAS; with (12,13) 2- and 3-state CASPT2 agree better. CASPT2 reference weights are similar for the states and no intruder states were found. The old 0-IPEA CASPT2 Hamiltonian red-shifts the excitations by ~0.3 eV; the authors attribute the agreement of earlier CASPT2/MM rhodopsin studies with experiment to this error cancelling others. Adding MM charges blue-shifts CASPT2 by 0.4-0.6 eV vs 0.3-0.5 eV for NEVPT2.

notes: QM region is the chromophore only (boundary at Lys296, H-capped) embedded in AMBER point charges: a QM/MM cluster model, not a gas-phase molecule. CASSCF dominant configuration weights: ground state 0.785; 1B2u multiconfigurational (0.331, 0.172, 0.121). CASSCF reference weight in the CASPT2 ground-state wavefunction 0.56. The 1 1B2u state has a planar D2h minimum. With ZPE, CASPT2-IPEA places 2,3,7,8-TCDD 10.4 kJ/mol (g2 10.3) below 1,4,6,9-TCDD. CASPT2(g2) results are much closer to those obtained without any modification of the Fock operator.
