method: CASSCF (ab initio molecular dynamics, geometry optimisation, frequencies); MRSDCI single points
basis_set: effective core potential with valence double-zeta basis (5 valence electrons explicit)
active_space_orbital_description: All doublet configurations of the five valence electrons in five orbitals
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF: planar W-shaped minimum; trigonal-bipyramid local minimum is C2v (Jahn-Teller distorted from D3h), 0.51 eV higher (MRSDCI 0.07 eV). Planar pseudorotation barrier 0.04 eV (MRSDCI 0.08 eV); trigonal-bipyramid pseudorotation barrier 0.57 eV (MRSDCI 0.72 eV) via a C2v rectangular-pyramid TS (base sides 2.81 and 5.67 A, base-to-apex 3.60 A). CASSCF harmonic frequencies of the planar minimum: 51, 45, 120 (B2 pseudorotation mode), 129, 174, 226, 238, 289, 310 cm-1. Planar pseudorotation TS: B2 79i cm-1; real modes 13, 48, 140, 193, 217, 256, 281, 315 cm-1. Constant-temperature CASSCF-AIMD: pseudorotation on a sub-ps timescale down to 113 K, one event in 2.4 ps at 94 K, three events in 12 ps at the EPR temperature of 77 K. Authors' conclusion (abstract): the pseudorotating Li5 observed in prior EPR experiments at 77 K is quite likely planar, though originally suggested to be a trigonal bipyramid.
Other: GVB perfect pairing (a subset of the CAS(5,5) configurations) gives a much higher pseudorotation barrier (~0.14 eV upper bound) owing to a cusp from its explicit singlet pairing, and could not optimise the broken-symmetry pseudorotation TS at all; CASSCF optimises it and lowers the barrier to 0.04 eV. For the B2 pseudorotation mode CASSCF gives a frequency only 14% lower than GVB (120 vs 139 cm-1). MRSDCI on the CASSCF reference shrinks the planar/trigonal-bipyramid gap from 0.51 to 0.07 eV and doubles the planar pseudorotation barrier.
reference_short: Gibson & Carter, Chem. Phys. Lett. 271, 266 (1997)
notes: Point group of the planar minimum is not stated by this paper for its own structure (C2v planar W is attributed to previous work). Computed frequencies are harmonic.

method: SA-MCSCF (equal weights) + MR-CISD(+Q) and MR-AQCC; C and N 1s frozen post-MCSCF; interacting-space restriction

basis_set: d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ: aug-cc-pVDZ augmentation restricted to s,p on C/N and s on H, plus the second diffuse layer of d-aug-cc-pVDZ for the same sets (MCSCF also with full d-aug-cc-pVDZ)
active_space_orbital_description: eight valence orbitals 3n + 3pi + 2pi* for the first four valence states (4 states averaged); for the three lowest Rydberg states one auxiliary (3s Rydberg) orbital is added with at most single CAS->AUX excitations (7 states averaged, since preliminary MCSCF and later MR-CISD showed 3p Rydberg states appear only after the seventh state). electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 1A'. MR-AQCC/d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ (best): 1 1A'' (n-pi*) 6.06, 2 1A'' (n-pi*) 6.55, 2 1A' (pi-pi*) 6.55 eV. MR-CISD+Q valence-only (Table 5): 6.15, 6.68 (2 1A''), 6.70 (2 1A'); MR-CISD: 6.25, 6.78, 6.73. MR-CISD f(x10^2): 1A'' 0.0592, 2A'' 0.0031, 2A' 0.301. With AUX, MR-CISD+Q (Table 6): 6.16, 6.68, 6.69 eV; Rydberg pi-3s 7.69 and n-3s 7.89 eV (MR-CISD 7.66, 7.99). SA-MCSCF/d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ, 4 valence states: 6.27 (1A''), 6.52 (2A'), 6.77 (2A''); 7 states with AUX: 6.37, 6.58, 6.88, Rydberg 7.28, 7.72, 7.89 eV (f x10^2: 2.51, 4.37, 0.196, 0.0154, 0.0651, 3.25). d-aug-cc-pVDZ 7 states: 6.40, 6.58, 6.93, 7.17, 7.60, 7.82 eV. Closed-shell ground state weight ~0.87 (MCSCF). MR-CISD+Q 3s Rydberg energies consistent with the photoelectron-spectrum assignment of two ionizations near 11.3 eV. Additional MCSCF oscillator strengths (f x10^2): 4-state d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ (Table 4) 2.53 (1 1A''), 5.09 (2 1A'), 0.175 (2 1A''); 4-state d-aug-cc-pVDZ (Table 3) 6.30, 6.52, 6.80 eV with f 2.45, 5.19, 0.172; 7-state d-aug-cc-pVDZ (Table 1) f 2.44, 4.38, 0.191, 0.0246, 0.0731, 3.42. The authors propose that photodecomposition of 2H-tetrazole (at 193 nm) is likely initiated at the pi-pi* 2 1A' state (6.55 eV, MR-AQCC), whose oscillator strength is almost 100 times that of its degenerate n-pi* counterpart; the pi-pi* state has more pronounced multiconfigurational character. Expected error below 0.5 eV for the n-3s Rydberg state, greater accuracy for the pi-3s and valence states (greatest for valence at MR-AQCC).
Other: Dynamic correlation (MR-CISD) barely affects the 1 1A'' n-pi* state but raises the pi-pi* 2 1A' state markedly, making it quasi-degenerate with 2 1A''; the +Q correction reverses their order and MR-AQCC lowers the three valence states by a further 0.09, 0.13 and 0.15 eV, leaving 2 1A' and 2 1A'' degenerate. Only seven states were averaged because MCSCF/MR-CISD showed the 3p Rydberg states appear above the seventh state; SA-CASSCF oscillator strengths are inflated relative to MR-CISD (state-averaging contamination). In some MR-AQCC runs up to two intruder CSFs were added to the reference space. The authors state that as long as the basis is diffuse enough (d'-aug'-cc-pVDZ being about the minimum doubly augmented basis for the azoles), one does not need much larger active spaces to partition valence and Rydberg orbitals: a small valence CAS plus one auxiliary 3s orbital (single CAS->AUX excitations only) gives very small valence-Rydberg mixing already at the MCSCF level for all azoles tested. The authors call the reference space being a good representation of the final CI expansion 'a crucial requisite'.

electronic_structure_description: The singlet has a minimum near a 2.9-A Na-to-Mg3-plane distance at every reported level except MP2; optimized triplet structures are higher-order saddle points and do not converge at HF/CASSCF. At separations above about 5 A, NEVPT2 singlet and triplet surfaces converge to neutral Na and Mg3 fragments, and Mulliken charges on all sites approach zero rather than retaining Na+/Mg3(2-) ions. The Mg3 ring loses its aromatic NICS signature as the Na atoms withdraw the delocalized pi density. CASSCF/aug-cc-pVDZ optimized singlet (NImag = 0): Mg-Mg 3.15, Mg-Na 3.48, Na-Na 5.94 A.

The NEVPT2 triplet surface at very close distances is still not smooth, which the authors presume is due to a change in electronic state along the path. Single-determinant HF/B3LYP give problematic triplet dissociation and MP2 an unphysical decreasing long-range energy, while QCISD gives the proper qualitative dissociation.

The barrier exceeds De (50 kcal/mol) because the O-O2--O2- entity is a singlet and spin conservation makes dissociation to singlet O (~100 kcal/mol) the relevant reference; the saddle point is probably symmetric between the two Ca2+; moving the adsorbed O toward one Ca2+ at fixed O-O2- distance gains less than 0.01 kcal/mol. notes: Solid-state site: Ce3+ substituting Sr in the Sr3AlO4F lattice, treated as a Ce-centred cluster (Ce plus coordinating O2-/F-) embedded in 496-557 AIMPs within 10 A and 46,150-48,879 point charges; not an isolated molecule. nel = 1 (Ce3+ 4f1) and norb = 13 from the stated [4f, 5d, 6s] space are arithmetic. The D3h ring minimum is dominated by the pi->pi* doubly excited configuration; the contours of the two ground-state minima show a conical intersection along a nearly vertical line at theta about 85.5 deg. Leading CASSCF CI coefficients (Table I): 3A2 0.8844 (4b2->2b1), -0.3400; 3B2 0.9537; 3B1 0.8889 (6a1->2b1), -0.3160; 1A2 0.8605 (4b2->2b1), -0.4001; 1B1 0.8359, -0.4468; 1B2 0.7051 (1a2->2b1), -0.4074, -0.3310, 0.2113. ZPE corrections to the adiabatic excitation energies are 0.01-0.02 eV in magnitude. 1B2 oscillator strength 8.02e-2 (observed 8.8e-2); vertical 1B2 compared with observed peaks around 4.86 eV. 1B1 and 1B2 correlate with O(1D)+O2(1Delta g) and 3B1 with O(3P)+O2(1Delta g); 'These states are predicted to lie below their dissociation limit of 4.08 and 2.11 eV, respectively'. 1A2 and 3A2 are both dominated by 4b2->2b1; computed 1A2-3A2 splitting 0.25 eV (estimate of Arnold et al. 0.42 eV). method: CASSCF trajectory surface-hopping direct dynamics (state-specific / state-averaged over 2 roots), compared with MCTDH wavepacket dynamics on a five-mode linear vibronic coupling model fitted to CAS(5,6)/3-21G* energies

CAS(5,6)/3-21G* energies relative to the Franck-Condon point (Table 3, kcal/mol): D2h conical intersection -2.467, A+ minimum -3.756, X+ minima -24.462 (torsion 32.17 deg), planar D2h transition structure -24.077, D2d Jahn-Teller seam point -7.220. The FC point lies 244.896 kcal/mol (9.449 eV) above the neutral ground-state minimum. Fitted model Hamiltonian reproduces 106 CAS(5,6)/3-21G* points with RMSD 0.06 eV. Direct dynamics (80 trajectories, 100 fs, from A+): over half hop to the lower state within 10 fs; upper-state population stabilises at ~15% with no significant recurrence at 50 or 100 fs, whereas the wavepacket shows recurrences at 50 and 100 fs; 39 trajectories single crossing, 30 double, 5 multiple, 6 none; 8 recross via the D2h intersection and 5 via the D2d seam. QC vs fitted model: A+ minimum depth 3.8 (QC) / 4.3 (model) kcal/mol below FC; X+ minima a further 22.0 (QC) / 23.8 (model) kcal/mol below the conical intersection; planar TS barrier between them 0.4 (QC) / 1.8 (model) kcal/mol; model energy discrepancies ~0.5 kcal/mol, 1.6 at the X+ minima. The D2h intersection is sloped; the D2d Jahn-Teller seam lies 4.8 kcal/mol below it and is separated from it by a significant barrier on the upper surface. Table 3 CAS(5,6)/3-21G* geometries (RCC1, RCC2, RCH A; HCC deg; torsion deg): FC 1.329, 1.262, 1.073, 117.61, 0.0; CoIn 1.284, 1.360, 1.079, 118.62, 0.0; A+ min 1.304, 1.323, 1.077, 120.59, 0.0; X+ min 1.346, 1.248, 1.074, 119.12, 32.17; TS 1.358, 1.237, 1.073, 119.15, 0.0; JT 1.329, 1.262, 1.073, 117.61, 90.0. QC gradient-difference vector (0.0, +0.034, -0.036, +0.530, +0.017) along Q14; derivative coupling along Q5 (torsion) with value 0.295. Wavepacket: less than 10% left in the upper state after 20 fs; initial adiabatic A+ population 0.84. Trajectories: hops down start after 2 fs, up after 8 fs, transfer effectively finished after 30 fs; torsional period ~42 fs (model) vs ~55 fs (trajectories).
Other: State-averaged orbitals were needed for CASSCF convergence when the two surfaces are close, while state-specific orbitals were used elsewhere; the weights were switched gradually (0.1 per step over 5 steps once the gap fell below 0.05 hartree) to keep the surfaces smooth. Basis set judged non-critical for this theory-theory comparison: 6-31G* checks at several geometries showed no major differences from 3-21G*. The five-mode model fitted to the CAS(5,6) surfaces omits the D2d Jahn-Teller seam, which the direct dynamics reach at later times.
reference_short: Worth, Hunt & Robb, J. Phys. Chem. A 107, 621-631 (2003)
notes: Hop criterion: populated-state probability below 0.65; electronic propagation only when the gap is below 0.04 hartree; 5 fs wait after a hop. Direct-dynamics populations normalized to the quantum A+ population at t = 0.

The (3,3) space is described as the minimal CAS for the V 3dxy-O(R) 2py-V 3dxy pi overlap across the rung. The authors call the Fig. 1 double-well results 'rather qualitative': a detailed analysis would need a preliminary geometry optimization and a study of basis-set effects.

DDCI was used instead of CASPT2 because for adjacent V4 plaquettes J1 and J2 reach converged CASPT2 values at different level shifts (intruder states).

electronic_structure_description: Ground state X 2A''. At CI(X-A)2 the molecule is highly twisted (torsion phi and angle theta, both in the branching space). Apex at theta = 90.0 deg, phi = 90.0 deg; residual energy gap due to numerical optimisation 263.37 cm-1. A second twisted CI at theta = 88.5 deg, phi = 270.0 deg. Cone slopes d_theta(H22-H11)|CI = 0.34 rad-1 and d_theta H12|CI = 0.037 rad-1. Without initial impulsion the wavepacket flows toward the right well at 1.7 eV. A->X relaxation probability after 75 fs (Table 1): up to 0.75 from the LMB start (k_theta = -50 au, k_phi = -20 au, Ekin 1.13 eV); up to 0.46 from the EQ start (k_theta = -50 au, k_phi = -20 au, Ekin 1.26 eV). Table 1, A->X probability after 75 fs (k_phi, k_theta in au; LMB Ekin eV / P, EQ Ekin eV / P): (0,-20) 0.09/0.33, 0.10/0.02; (0,-40) 0.37/0.53, 0.43/0.02; (0,-50) 0.58/0.58, 0.68/0.02; (-10,0) 0.14/0.28, 0.14/0.02; (-10,-20) 0.23/0.50, 0.25/0.02; (-10,-40) 0.51/0.65, 0.58/0.09; (-10,-50) 0.72/0.65, 0.82/0.16; (-20,0) 0.54/0.18, 0.58/0.02; (-20,-20) 0.64/0.37, 0.69/0.10; (-20,-40) 0.92/0.70, 1.01/0.29; (-20,-50) 1.13/0.75, 1.26/0.46. Initial wavepacket positions: LMB theta0 = 103 deg, phi0 = 113 deg; EQ theta0 = 120 deg, phi0 = 180 deg. LMB case: after the interaction phi increases towards about 180 deg in both adiabatic states while theta oscillates around about 110 deg. EQ case: after funnelling the CI the torsion angle returns to about 180 deg in both states; the population remaining in the A state has a non-twisted geometry.

geometry_source: MP2/cc-pVDZ ground-state minimum
method: canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF (CASVB diabatization)
active_space_orbital_description: pi system: Boys-localized orbitals on the two dimethylaniline rings and the methine bridge (analogue of the formamidinium cation pi system). Reference localized orbitals are the Boys-localized active orbitals of an evenly weighted two-state SA-CASSCF(4,3)/cc-pVDZ calculation; at each electronic 'temperature' the canonical-ensemble active orbitals are unitarily transformed to minimise the least-squares distance from them.
electronic_structure_description: Canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF(4,3) over all six singlet CSFs at electronic 'temperatures' 1.5-3.5 eV: covalent (charge-delocalization) channel couplings -1.76 +/- 0.12 eV, ionic (chemical-bond) channel couplings -2.93 +/- 0.19 eV; bridge CSFs |121> and |202> quasi-degenerate and weakly coupled. Couplings below 1.0 eV are all smaller than 0.25 eV in magnitude at every 'temperature'. The ionic/covalent channel coupling ratio is close to sqrt(2), as expected from spin counting. Coupling of the polarized covalent CSFs |211>/|112> to their ionic counterparts |220>/|022> is nearly the same magnitude as their coupling to |202>; the coupling pattern is consistent with nearest-neighbour-only ring-bridge interaction. The dispersion of the ionic (chemical-bonding) bridge state |202> is larger than that of |121>. Both bridge states contribute strongly to S2 and S3, neither to S1 (by symmetry) nor S4; |202> contributes significantly to the ground adiabatic state, |121> much less. Both bridge states couple strongly to the resonating polarized covalent CSFs |211> and |112>.
Other: CAS(4,3) is chosen as 'the minimal complete quantum many-body model that describes coherent transport of an excess electronic charge and a bond-pair'. With a microcanonical (uniform-weight) ensemble the solution for this molecule and active space does not persist beyond three states, too few to resolve all six CSF energies and couplings; canonical weighting makes the full six-state support possible. The localized valence structure of the solution is robust, and the coupling matrix elements are not strongly dependent on the electronic 'temperature', across the visible (1.5-3.5 eV). SA-CASSCF gaps are too large by up to 2-3 eV; no PT2 results are reported here, but the author states that a multireference PT correction applied to CASSCF solutions like this one for HB in previous work reproduces the experimental gap to within reasonable accuracy.
reference_short: Olsen, J. Chem. Phys. 2015, 142, 044116

PJT parameters (MR-MRCI+Q diabatic): F = -7.8770 eV/A, K1 = 164.6141 eV/A^2, K2 = 142.8217 eV/A^2, Delta = 0.6739 eV; E1''(Q=0) = -19.5 (X unstable), E2''(Q=0) = 327.0 (A~ 2Sigma_g+ stable). At the MS-MR-CASPT2 minimum the N atom is displaced 0.027 A off centre. SS-CASPT2-cv total energy at Delta R = 0: -104.115799 au (reproducing Ref. 18). Total energies at Delta R(B-N) = 0, R(B-B) = 2.650 A (Fig. 1 caption, method order read from the Fig. 1 legend): SS-SR-CASPT2 -104.115714; MS-MR-CASPT2 (four states) -104.115321; MS-MR-CASPT2-cv -104.117560; MR-MRCI+Q -104.129299; MS-MR-CASPT2 -104.117475; MR-MRAQCC -104.124413; MR-MRCI -104.113284; SS-MRCI+Q -104.128735; SS-MRAQCC -104.123884; SS-MRCI -104.112906 au.

For the MR methods with two reference states (X and A~) the minima lie at Delta R(B-N) ~ +/-0.06 A with well depths of about 14-32 cm-1 at R(B-B) = 2.650 A; single-state SS-MRCI+Q gives a higher 42.8 cm-1 barrier. Two-state MS-MR-CASPT2 is very close to the more reliable MR-MRCI+Q and MR-MRAQCC and was therefore used for geometry optimizations and the 3D APES at low cost. Two-state and four-state MS-MR-CASPT2 curves are essentially identical, so only X and A~ 2Sigma_g+ drive the pseudo-Jahn-Teller effect. Core-valence correlation has a very small effect. The SS-MRCI double minimum contradicts Ref. 18's SACASSCF+1+2 centrosymmetric optimum, which the authors attribute to an optimizer defect on the flat surface; frequencies or a PEC scan are needed to confirm such structures. Four 2Sigma+ states are state-averaged because, with improper methods and wave functions, the two B atoms can end up in different electronic states and produce artifactual symmetry breaking, which SA-CASSCF 'can effectively avoid'.

S2 and T2 are ππ*, mainly in the thiophene ring with considerable delocalization into C-N-N (unpaired electrons mainly in AO5, AO9, AO10). CASPT2//CAS(12,11) vertical excitation energies at the S0 minimum: S1 58.4, S2 108.8 kcal/mol, compared with the 494 nm (57.9 kcal/mol) absorption peak in acetonitrile; S1 is populated at 490 nm and longer wavelengths. The S1 minimum and the S1/S0 MECI are indistinguishable, so S1 -> S0 IC is very efficient; on S0 the transition state to singlet 3-thienylcarbene + N2 has a barrier of 32.1 kcal/mol (Fig. 3a: S1(FC) 58.4, S1/S0 29.8, S0 TS 32.1, 3-TC_S1 + N2 30.3 kcal/mol). The S1/T2 crossing is in the S1 Franck-Condon region at 52.5 kcal/mol (text); T2/T1 conical intersection 2.6 kcal/mol from S1/T2; S1, T2 and T1 nearly degenerate from S1/T2 to T2/T1. S1-T2 SOC 35.1 cm-1 near S1/T2, attributed to the heavy-atom effect of S; T2 -> T1 IC on the order of a vibrational period, T2 acting as a bridge. An S0 scan in the C-N and C-S distances shows that α-TMC formation is stepwise (C-N fission to singlet 3-TC, then C-S fission and isomerization), not concerted. In T2 the C=N bond is mainly of double-bond character, and C=N fission from T2 correlates adiabatically with an excited triplet state of 3-thienylcarbene, which is not favorable in energy, so there is little possibility of C=N cleavage along the T2 pathway to the observed triplet 3-thienylcarbene.

Bright transition at 2.35 eV with f = 0.345 (experiment for CePn*2: intense broad band at 2.34 eV; literature TDDFT 2.85 eV, f = 0.071). D2h: strongly multiconfigurational 1Ag ground state 0.24 eV (23.2 kJ/mol) above the D2d ground state at CASPT2; antibonding au occupation 0.378 from deoccupation 0.388 of the bonding au; first excited state 1B2g at 0.93 eV. electronic_structure_description: Ground state: HF and CASSCF without polarization functions predict planar geometries (polarization functions introduce some amino-group nonplanarity); unsigned average bond-length errors 0.028 A (AM1), 0.016 A (HF/6-31G*), 0.013 A (CASSCF/6-31G) vs 9-methyladenine neutron diffraction. First singlet excited state: all three methods predict a rather puckered geometry; AM1-CI(4/4) and CASSCF(4/4) give pi->pi* character, CIS gives n->pi*. In the CASSCF(4/4) geometry the largest out-of-plane displacement is for the hydrogen on C8 (AM1-CI(4/4): hydrogen on N9). CIS: the pi->pi* state (first excited state of the vertical spectrum) has an almost stationary point; N1-C2 1.334 A in pi->pi* vs 1.388 A in n->pi*, with a marked C2-H2 out-of-plane displacement in n->pi*; at the avoided crossing the two states are completely mixed. The paper concludes the geometrically relaxed excited state of adenine has n->pi* character.
Other: The n->pi* state was not included in the CASSCF(4/4) (or AM1-CI(4/4)) space, so CASSCF(4/4) optimizes a pi->pi* first excited state while CIS/6-31G, which contains both, finds the n->pi* state lowest (its optimization had serious convergence problems because the character of S1 changed during it). The paper's conclusion is that relaxed S1 of adenine is n->pi*. The authors note the (4/4) restriction 'does not allow for inclusion of excitations of sigma->sigma* type', and on previous experience use CIS/6-31G rather than CASSCF(4/4) for the further photophysics.
reference_short: Broo, J. Phys. Chem. A 1998, 102, 526

CASSCF/MRCI: ground-state barrier along the umbrella coordinate 0.099 eV; two symmetry-allowed three-state conical intersections near S2 = +/-0.9 rad, connected by a hyperline of two-state intersections when all three bending modes are displaced. Fitted surface needs an 8th-order JT/PJT expansion (208 coefficients). X-band: extended single umbrella progression; theoretical 0-0 peak 9.878 eV (using the RCCSD(T) vertical IP 8.529 eV) vs expt 9.868 eV. A-band: nearly structureless, agrees with experiment; diffuseness attributed to exceptionally strong JT and PJT coupling. Dynamics: JT population transfer within 2E' in ~5 fs, excited-to-ground decay on ~10 fs scale, essentially complete by ~20 fs; adiabatic populations at 100 fs ~81%, 14% and 3.5%. A third (excited) 2A1' state lies below 2E' close to the planar geometry (-0.2 <= S2 <= 0.2), interacts with the 2A2'' ground state through the umbrella mode and strongly with 2E' through the e' mode; 2E' data in that interval were removed from the fit. At S2 = 0.55 rad, besides the JT intersection, the lower 2E' component and 2A2'' intersect at S5 ~ -1.4 rad (strongly avoided crossing for 1.0 <= S5 <= 3.0 rad), and two ground/first-excited conical intersections lie at S6 = +/-1.2 rad for S5 = 0.7 rad. At S2 = 0.9 rad (near the triple intersection) the 2A2'' state lies above 2E' and interacts with its upper component, and the two-state intersections and avoided crossings move closer to the JT intersection. Along the umbrella mode combined with the JT-active stretch no PJT intersection occurs and the stretch is only weakly JT-active. Six-mode dynamics details: the lower 2E' component carries 80% of the population within 4 fs, the upper component reaches a 1% minimum at ~11.5 fs, and the ground state is populated from ~5 fs. CASSCF(6,6)/6-311++G(2d,2p) S2 energy -230.550895 au, S0 -> S2 vertical excitation 7.82 eV (experiment 6.20 eV); S0 -> T1 and S0 -> S1 vertical excitations agree very well with experiment (values as in Ref. 5). Table 1 (ppm; sigma_iso(13C), sigma_iso(1H), NICS(0), NICS(1), NICS(0)zz, NICS(1)zz): S0 73.52, 24.90, -8.17, -9.53, -12.21, -27.83; T1 81.89, 29.31, 39.63, 30.10, 130.54, 90.61; S1 78.69, 29.54, 45.81, 34.67, 145.90, 102.76; S2 75.42, 21.25, -39.08, -36.68, -119.47, -117.59. Relative aromaticity order of the eight states (more aromatic to more antiaromatic): S2 C6H6 > S0 C6H6 > T1 C4H4 > S1 C4H4 > S2 C4H4 > S0 C4H4 > T1 C6H6 > S1 C6H6

Experiment: weak broad band at 390-480 nm and medium band at 300-350 nm. S0 CASSCF expansion: +0.89 closed-shell configuration, -0.15 and -0.15 double excitations into (dyz-pi*y) and (dxz-pi*x). dxz,yz = 0.84(3d Ru xz,yz) + 0.44(2p O x,y), dxy = 1.01(3d Ru xy) (as printed); the dxz,yz-pi*x,y antibonding orbitals are 0.54(3d Ru) - 0.68(2p O) + 0.81(2p N). geometry_source: potential energy curves computed for each state; spectroscopic constants derived assuming a Morse potential
method: CASSCF reference wavefunctions followed by multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI); Douglas-Kroll relativistic corrections
basis_set: Mn: (14s,9p,5d) Gaussian basis of Wachters augmented with 2p, 1d and 3f functions according to Bauschlicher, contracted (14s,11p,6d,3f)/[8s,6p,4d,1f]; N: cc-pVTZ
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF: the Mn 4s and 3d orbitals plus the N 2s and 2p orbitals; core (Mn 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p and N 1s) kept doubly occupied
ground_state_mult: 5 at the CASSCF level, 3 at the MRSDCI level
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF: 5Delta is the ground state, followed closely by 5Pi < 3Sigma-, all within a 2.2 eV span; between 5Pi and 3Sigma- the 5Pi is estimated lowest by only 2.4 kcal/mol (Andrews' value 0.8 kcal/mol). CASSCF wavefunctions: 5Pi ~ 0.642 |(3pi)4(1delta)2(4pi)1(10sigma)1> + ..., 3Sigma- ~ 0.725 |(3pi)4(1delta)2(4pi)0(10sigma)0> + .... MRSDCI: 3Sigma- is the lowest state (by 2.5 kcal/mol), followed by 5Pi < 3Pi < 5Delta; 5Pi ~ 0.704 |(3pi)4(1delta)2(9sigma)1(4pi)1> + ..., 3Sigma- ~ 0.766 |(3pi)4(1delta)2(9sigma)2(4pi)0> + .... Spectroscopic constants (Table 1, Morse fit): 3Sigma- Re 1.582 A, we 808 cm-1, De 0.69 eV, Te 0; 5Pi 1.721 A, 548 cm-1, 2.15 eV, Te 806 cm-1; 3Pi 1.704 A, 578 cm-1, 1.65 eV, Te 2662 cm-1; 5Delta 1.992 A, 467 cm-1, 3.55 eV, Te 2904 cm-1. Excited states 3Delta (we 1031 cm-1) and 1Sigma- (we 1029 cm-1) are more bound than the lowest states; a singlet state lies close to 16 kcal/mol above the ground state
Other: Going from CASSCF to MRSDCI, which adds four orbitals to the active space, reorders the states (CASSCF 5Delta ground state with 5Pi < 3Sigma- following; MRSDCI 3Sigma- < 5Pi < 3Pi < 5Delta), which the authors attribute to the larger recovery of dynamical correlation; the wavefunctions remain multiconfigurational at both levels. Consistent with paramagnetism from large PMR shifts. CASSCF: quintet 3030 cm-1 (~94% one configuration, MOs 5-8 each singly occupied), singlet 7120 cm-1 (~74% + ~12% MO 5 -> MO 8 pair transfer); CASPT2: singlet 3840, quintet 6550 cm-1. The very large CASPT2 quintet-triplet splitting (6550 cm-1) is attributed by the authors to the predominant contribution to the triplet of the configuration with an electron pair in the bonding orbital (MO 5).

(3); previously reported value 230 cm-1 (ab initio, NIR spectroscopy, DC magnetometry). On A2T2 the C2v saddle lies 1803 / 1779 and the C3v saddle 5278 / 4947 cm-1 above the D2d minima. A2T2/X2E MECI at a D2d geometry almost coinciding with the A2T2 minimum; CASPT2 MECI at S2a = -2.52 bohr, 62 cm-1 above that minimum. SO splitting of A2T2 at the reference geometry 363 cm-1; SO changes the E x e JT stabilization by +1 cm-1, the pseudorotation barrier by -7 cm-1, and the A2T2 D2d, C2v and C3v stationary points by 21, 288 and 10 cm-1. SO effects on the A2T2 D2d, C2v and C3v stationary-point energies are less than 6%, so SO coupling is neglected thereafter. The e mode is the tuning mode that brings the X2E and A2T2 sheets to the conical-intersection seam; the t2 modes are the coupling modes. The t2 bending mode is only weakly JT active but dominates the linear 2E-2T2 PJT coupling, and was chosen with the e mode for the five-state, five-mode (E+T2)x(e+t2) dynamics. MCTDH on the fitted surfaces: PJT coupling adds bands by intensity borrowing, and the 2T2 population decays ultrafast and nonadiabatically to 2E.

The most intense absorption channel, S0(pi)->S4(pi*), lies in the vacuum region (188 nm) and cannot serve as the main absorption channel; the direct S0->T1 channel is inefficient owing to its low oscillator strength. The relaxed T1 satisfies the Latva criterion (optimal T1-Ln resonance gap ~1500-4000 cm-1), so the T1 -> 5D channel is very efficient (Fig. 5). Because S1 and T1 lie close (Fig. 4), raising the temperature may enhance S1->T1 intersystem crossing, which the authors offer as the explanation of the anomalous temperature dependence (luminescence increasing on heating). The MO structure of the whole Eu(Macr)3 complex and of both calculation models coincides (the four HOMOs and the LUMO of the methacrylate anion), consistent with the PES/DFT data of ref 18.

Quantitatively the relative spin gaps (CASSCF) enlarge by as much as a factor of 3.3 from CAS(10e,10o) to CAS(22e,26o). Table I: average number of occupied CSFs (millions, Nw = 5e8) for S = 0-5: 333, 345, 338, 324, 300, 268; deterministic space ND = 5e4; convergence checked up to Nw = 1e9. CASCI -> CASSCF lowers the singlet by 94 mH and the S=5 state by 76 mH. CASCI J and J' about 1.44 mH. Singlet ground-state weights CASCI -> CASSCF: reference 74.4% -> 46.1%, MMCT 6.9% -> 12.9%, bridging-S LMCT 13.4% -> 27.9%, radial 3d->3d' 1.5% -> 2.1%, non-Hund 1.2% -> 3.7%. CASSCF local spin <S_A^2> of the triplet ~6.5 (S_A ~ 2); triplet and quintet have lower <S_A^2> than the singlet after CASSCF. Spin-spin alignment between the irons changes from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic starting from S = 4

LMCT contributions roughly double on orbital relaxation, lowering local spins; CASSCF delocalizes the Fe 3d orbitals onto the ligands, increasing |J|. Relative average error omega of the bilinear Heisenberg fit is below 1% for CASCI in all active spaces; for CASSCF it is at most 4%, and the biquadratic fit is below 1% in all cases. The paper states 'a substantial differential effect of ~15-20 mH due to the CASSCF orbital relaxation' (from (10e,10o) high-spin ROHF orbitals) across the dimer active spaces

relativistic_treatment: exact two-component (X2C) Hamiltonian with spin-orbit coupling in the variational orbital optimization
active_space_orbital_description: valence s and p orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Splittings/excitations in meV, unsigned percent error in parentheses (Table 1; SI Tables S1-S6 for t functionals). 2P1/2 -> 2P3/2: X2C-CASSCF 88 (14%); X2C-MC-PDFT stPBE 97 (4.9%), stBLYP 107 (4.9%); tPBE 77 (24.4%), tBLYP 88 (13.5%) (SI); literature 4C-CASSCF 85 (17%), CASPT2-SO 99 (2.9%); exp. 102.
Other: For the group-13 2P splitting, X2C-CASSCF (and literature 4C-CASSCF) with the small valence s,p active space underestimates the splitting, indicating that external correlation is needed; X2C-MC-PDFT improves it considerably (group %MUE 22% X2C-CASSCF vs 4.5% stPBE, 5.0% stBLYP). The good agreement of literature CASPT2-SO is attributed to its much larger active space, since a non-state-specific CASPT2 correction applied before perturbative SOC cannot directly change a within-term splitting of a free atom. For group-13 fine-structure splittings the st functionals agree better with experiment than the t functionals (group %MUE stPBE/stBLYP 4.5/5.0 vs tPBE/tBLYP 13/8.1).

notes: The paper states only "valence s and p orbitals in the active space" for the p-block atoms: norb = 4 is counted from that orbital list (one s, three p) and nel = 3 is the valence s+p electron count of the neutral group-13 atom, neither printed. electronic_structure_description: S0 -> S1 is n -> pi*. Table I (6-31G*, B3LYP geometry): CASSCF(8,8) 4.292 eV (f 0.0107), MRCIS(8,8) 4.168 eV (f 0.004211); a second (8,8) entry gives S1 4.372 (f 0.012920) / 4.190 eV (f 0.004168) and S2 6.626 (f 0.000487) / 6.740 eV (f 0.000050) (CASSCF / MRCIS); expt 3.71 eV (334 nm). TD-B3LYP/6-31G*: S1 3.95 eV, mainly HOMO -> LUMO. Simulated CASSCF(8,8) absorption 220-340 nm, maximum 290 nm (expt maximum ~318 nm). Two S1/S0 conical intersections (Table II): CI-I C-N=N out of the three-carbon plane, C3-C4-C5-N1 62.0 deg, N2-C3 3.67 A, N1-N2 1.185 A; CI-II coplanar, C3-C4-C5-N1 177.0 deg, N2-C3 4.807 A, N1-N2 1.206 A; CI-I is much steeper; LIIC path to CI-I barrierless, to CI-II with a barrier. Dynamics (363 trajectories, 2000 fs, 0.1 fs step, 0.05 fs where needed): one C-N bond breaks in S1 (quickly for ~four-fifths of trajectories, more slowly for one-fifth), hop in 60-450 fs (few to 720 fs), ~78% via CI-I and 22% via CI-II; second C-N bond breaks in S0 giving trimethylene biradical + N2. Products: cyclopropane ~77.8% (barrierless), propene ~12.5% ([1,2]-H shift, barrier ~17.8 kcal/mol CASSCF(8,8), ~4.8 kcal/mol MRCIS(8,8)), CH2 + C2H4 ~9.7% (endoergic by ~30 kcal/mol CASSCF(8,8), ~27.6 kcal/mol MRCIS(8,8), relative to the biradical). Remaining Table II CI geometry (CI-I / CI-II): N1-C5 1.463 / 1.430, C3-C4 1.498 / 1.498, C4-C5 1.526 / 1.538 A, C4-C5-N2-N1 -84.811 / -17.188 deg. Hopping geometries with C3-C4-C5-N1 between -100 and 100 deg and C3-N2 below 4 A lead to CI-I; those near +/-180 deg with C3-N2 above 4 A correlate with CI-II. CI-I is much steeper than CI-II, so population transfer through CI-I is expected to be faster; a transition-state search near the barrier on the LIIC path to CI-II was unsuccessful.
Other: Enlarging the space does not bring S0 -> S1 closer to experiment (3.71 eV): CASSCF 4.292 (8,8), 4.476 (8,9), 4.290 (10,10), 4.406 eV (10,8); MRCIS 4.168, 4.381, 4.168, 4.286 eV, so (8,8) was used. CASSCF overestimates the excitation energy, which the authors give as the cause of the blue-shifted simulated absorption maximum. 6-31+G* gave no significant improvement over 6-31G*; CASSCF(8,8) product-channel energies differ by at most 8.0 kcal/mol between the two bases. SA-2 justified by the ~51 kcal/mol S1-S2 gap at Franck-Condon and by S2/S3 staying away from S1 in a 4-state check along a trajectory. MRCIS(8,8) single points at the critical points of Fig. 4 agree qualitatively with CASSCF (maximum difference ~9.7 kcal/mol, trimethylene biradical), but lower the propene-forming barrier from ~17.8 to ~4.8 kcal/mol. MRCIS single-point energies along a complete CASSCF(8,8) trajectory show very good agreement with the CASSCF relative energies (Fig. 5).

geometry_source: solution search at R(Li-F) = 2.75 a0 (near equilibrium), traced along the binding curve; orbitals plotted at 4 a0
method: state-specific singlet CASSCF stationary points (Hessian indices 0-10, 1000 random starts each) compared with SA(2)-CASSCF(2,2) and FCI (from ref 47)

electronic_structure_description: Ionic ground state at equilibrium becoming covalent at dissociation. Near equilibrium the global-minimum SS solution has sigma/sigma* active orbitals; the second-lowest solution uses out-of-plane F 2px/y and 3px/y orbitals (occupations near 2 and 0), describing F radial correlation; the exact excited state is represented by only one solution plus a spurious symmetry-broken diradical solution. These characteristics reverse beyond the avoided crossing. In the dissociation limit the physical SS-CASSCF excited state tends to the exact FCI energy for Li+...F-, whereas equally weighted SA-CASSCF overestimates it. SS-CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G solutions shown in Fig. 7 (active natural occupations; energy): 1.9814/0.0186, -106.89419 Eh; 1.9908/0.0092, -106.88883 Eh; 1.3806/0.6194, -106.76134 Eh; 1.0000/1.0000, -106.78556 Eh. Bauschlicher-Langhoff discontinuity, with the original basis of ref 126 (1000 random starting points): at R(Li-F) = 8.5 a0 the global minimum is the covalent structure, with two local minima and two index-1 saddle points at higher energies representing the ionic configurations; the lowest ionic and covalent minima cross near R(Li-F) = 7.4 a0, and the covalent structure coalesces with an index-1 saddle point (pair annihilation point, a fold catastrophe), so there is no quasi-diabatic covalent solution at shorter bond lengths and the global-minimum energy has an unphysical cusp. This pair annihilation point is absent with 6-31G.
Other: Notation trap: this paper writes active spaces as (orbitals, electrons) where they differ: "(3,2)" is three active orbitals with two electrons (Table II: SS(1,2) = HF and SS(6,2) = FCI for H2/6-311G); recorded here as nel = 2. Unphysical SS solutions lacking the right active orbitals intersect quasi-diabatically at the avoided crossing, while the physical solutions behave adiabatically and avoid each other; the authors suggest a multiconfigurational nonorthogonal CI over both sets. A complete description of the avoided crossing needs dynamic correlation.

compound_name: Azomethane (CH3-N=N-CH3), cis-to-trans photoisomerization, both outside and inside an optical cavity
geometry_source: cis and trans ground-state minima optimized at B3LYP/6-31G* (Gaussian 16) with frequency analysis confirming they are stationary points; the S1/S0 conical intersection optimized at SA-2-CAS(6,4)/6-31G* using Yarkony's method in Molpro 2015. The reaction path is a rigid linear interpolation in internal coordinates from the CI geometry out to each isomer, 60 geometries total, not further optimized. B3LYP frequencies also drive the Wigner sampling of initial conditions
method: SA-2-CASSCF(6,4)/6-31G* for adiabatic energies, gradients, permanent and transition dipoles and nonadiabatic couplings in on-the-fly trajectory surface hopping (velocity Verlet, dt = 0.2 fs, 100 quantum steps per nuclear step, 500 trajectories); kernel ridge regression model of the dipoles trained on SA-2-CAS(6,4) data; inside the cavity a polariton basis of 2 electronic states x 3 Fock states (6 polaritonic states), cavity loss by the Lindblad jump superoperator
software: Gaussian 16 for the DFT geometries and frequencies; Molpro 2015 for the CASSCF and conical-intersection optimization
electronic_structure_description: The trans isomer lies about 0.5 eV below the cis isomer in the ground state. Rabi splitting between the upper and lower polariton states 68 meV (gc = 0.005 au) and 680 meV (gc = 0.05 au) at hbar*omega_c = 2.72 eV (Sec. 4.3). Transition dipole (Fig. 2): zero in all directions for the trans isomer by symmetry (|e> dark at trans), ~0.8 D along Y for the cis isomer (bright); dipoles along X < 0.7 D.
Other: Outside the cavity: dynamics is started from the cis isomer on Franck-Condon excitation (chosen because its ground-to-excited transition dipole is larger than the trans isomer's). There is no barrier on the excited-state surface between the cis minimum and the conical intersection, so nearly half the trajectories hop down within about 50 fs and essentially all are on the ground state by about 330 fs; the CNNC dihedral passes through +/-90 degrees at the intersection and the trans population rises to nearly 1 by about 70 fs. Inside the cavity (cavity frequency 2.72 eV, loss rate 4 meV, field polarized along Y): increasing the light-matter coupling from 0.005 to 0.05 a.u. slows the population transfer, raises the |g,1> photonic state population and hence the intracavity photon number, and significantly suppresses the trans population - i.e. the cis-to-trans isomerization is inhibited by strong coupling, because the reduced polaritonic nonadiabatic coupling keeps more trajectories on the upper state after they leave the Franck-Condon region. Increasing the cavity loss rate lowers the average photon number and further suppresses the cis-to-trans reaction, clearly so at gc = 0.05 au. Inside the cavity more trajectories are trapped oscillating around the cis 0 degree CNNC angle, more so at gc = 0.05 au, because of a large barrier on the third polaritonic surface peaking near 90 degrees. The (6e,4o) active space is stated to be large enough to describe the first two electronic states during the rotation of the molecule, so total energy is well conserved in the on-the-fly dynamics without cavity loss (SI). The authors caution that the Ebbesen photoisomerization experiments are in the collective coupling regime, unlike this single-molecule simulation. With the field polarized along Z (SI Sec. VI): at gc = 0.005 au the dynamics (trans population, CNNC dihedral evolution) is similar to outside the cavity; at gc = 0.05 au the E2/E1 avoided crossing shifts toward the cis side, the system stays longer on E1 because of a barrier on its surface, and the trans population decreases slightly relative to outside the cavity.

compound_name: Cu-catalysed oxidative addition / reductive elimination of iodobenzene with [Cu(I)(eta2-beta-diketone)(beta-diketonate)]- (complexes PhI...b, TSb-c, Cu(III) intermediate c, TSc-p, product complex a...p)
ligand_set: beta-diketone (eta2) and beta-diketonate; iodobenzene / phenyl and iodide in the OA-RE stationary points
geometry_source: omega-B97XD/SDD(Cu, I)/6-31G(d), PCM(DMSO) optimized (Gaussian 16); CASSCF/CASPT2 single points at these geometries
method: CASSCF(12e,12o)/CASPT2 single points (imaginary level shift 0.1 au, PCM DMSO) at DFT-optimised stationary points and along omega-B97XD IRCs; DFT functional comparison (B3LYP-D3, omega-B97XD, PBE0, TPSS, MN15); MP2 and CCSD comparison
basis_set: SDD with ECP10MDF (Cu) and ECP46MWB (I); cc-pVTZ on other atoms
relativistic_treatment: Stuttgart/Dresden effective core potentials ECP10MDF (Cu) and ECP46MWB (I)
active_space_orbital_description: five Cu 3d and five correlating 3d' (4d) orbitals ('double-shell' effect) plus one sigma bond orbital (or Cu 3p orbital) and its unoccupied partner describing bond cleavage/formation: in the OA step a C-C/C-I sigma (or Cu 3p) pair, the Cu-C sigma bond to phenyl being essential at TSb-c; in the RE step the Cu-C sigma (or Cu 3p) pair and, at TSc-p, the sigma bond between phenyl and diketone ligands. The space defined at each TS is used for all points of its IRC
electronic_structure_description: OA barrier (kcal/mol, electronic energy, from PhI...b): DFT B3LYP-D3 13.3, omega-B97XD 16.5, TPSS 10.5, PBE0 14.2, MN15 21.4; CASPT2//DFT 8.8, 8.6, 7.8, 6.1, 8.5. RE barrier from c: DFT 6.7, 1.3, 9.1, 4.2 (B3LYP-D3, omega-B97XD, TPSS, PBE0; no MN15 TS); CASPT2//DFT 6.0, 5.3, 7.9, 4.8. CASPT2 energy of c on other functionals' geometries above omega-B97XD by 1.9 (B3LYP-D3), 3.4 (TPSS), 1.0 (PBE0), 0.5 (MN15). On omega-B97XD geometries: MP2 8.7 and CASPT2 8.6 vs omega-B97XD 16.5 and CCSD 14.6 OA barriers; OA rate-determining at all levels. Along the omega-B97XD IRCs (cc-pVDZ): OA barrier 18.2 (omega-B97XD) vs 8.8 (CASPT2), CASPT2 maximum 1.1 kcal/mol above the CASPT2 energy at the DFT TS and shifted towards PhI...b; RE barrier 4.3 vs 9.9, CASPT2 maximum 1.5 above the DFT TS and shifted towards a...p. CASSCF Mulliken 3d population 9.90 -> 9.46 over OA, 9.51 -> 10.00 over RE (DFT NPA 9.88 -> 9.47 and 9.48 -> 9.89). 3d-pi natural-orbital occupation 1.98 -> 1.86 (3d-pi' 0.02 -> 0.14) over OA, 3d-pi mixing with C-I sigma*; 1.89 -> 1.98 (3d-pi' 0.14 -> 0.02) over RE, 3d-pi interacting with Cu-C sigma*. Weight of the HF configuration in CASSCF(12,12): PhI...b 0.95206, TSb-c 0.94770, c 0.91357, TSc-p 0.91490, a...p 0.95393; CASPT2 reference weights 0.45429-0.46624. Singlet-triplet gap of c: CASPT2//omega-B97XD 36.2 kcal/mol vs 11.8-19.6 for DFT functionals; triplet always above singlet, no intersystem crossing. omega-B97XD Gibbs activation free energies: OA 25.0 kcal/mol (rate-determining step), RE 15.5 kcal/mol; the barrier from c to TSc-p was slightly negative (-0.8 kcal/mol) because the harmonic free-energy correction failed for a shallow TS. MP2//omega-B97XD reaction energy to form c 6.6 kcal/mol, 'somewhat larger than the others'.
Other: Active-space test: CASSCF(10e,10o)/CASPT2 with only the five 3d and five 3d' orbitals gave an energy profile 'quantitatively the same' as CASSCF(12e,12o)/CASPT2, so the authors conclude the active-space size converged, 'because the multi-reference character less occurred in these Cu complexes' (90% or more HF configuration). CASPT2 reference weights (~45%) fall in the 27-51% range expected for 134 correlated electrons, and the 0.1 au imaginary shift removed intruder states. Versus DFT, CASPT2 barriers are much less sensitive to the functional used for the geometry (DFT OA barriers vary by up to 10.9 kcal/mol) and the CASPT2 OA barrier is about half the omega-B97XD and CCSD values. The 3d-pi occupations of c (1.86/0.14) indicate a larger static correlation at the Cu(III) species, so 'DFT does not work for quantitative energy calculations around the Cu(III) intermediate complex'. Basis test: cc-pVDZ vs cc-pVTZ changes activation energies by less than 1 kcal/mol (reaction energies larger with cc-pVDZ).
reference_short: He, Nakatani and Hada, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 25, 28871-28884 (2023)
notes: IRC curves were computed with cc-pVDZ on non-Cu/I atoms. The triplet TSb-c could not be located; its triplet energy was evaluated at the singlet geometry. Thus, the CASPT2 reaction energy of overall catalytic cycle is not quantitatively useful.'

electronic_structure_description: S1 is the n-pi* state; S1/S0 conical intersection near CNNC = 90 deg, reached at ca. 40 fs, and a symmetry-equivalent one at 270 deg reached from ca. 120 fs. Reference XMS-CASPT2 (NACV, no level shift, IPEA deactivated) dynamics: (I) ~30 fs with all molecules cis on S1; (II) first conical-intersection region up to ~60 fs, 20-25% S1->S0 decay with complete cis-to-trans isomerization; (III) ~40 fs population plateau, mostly trans; (IV) second strong-coupling region with further decay, some molecules returning to cis. Pathways (Fig. 2b): (i) stay on S1 49%; (ii) decay at 90 deg ending trans 17%; (iii) decay at the 270 deg intersection ending cis 19%; (iv) decay at the first intersection then ground-state barrier crossing ending cis 2%.
Other: All multiconfigurational methods (XMS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, CASSCF, each with the (6,4) space) reproduce the four regimes and their durations; CASSCF is the best performing method in reproducing the reference timescales and, ignoring MS-CASPT2, the decay yield. MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF overestimate the 'standard' pathways (ii) and (iv), i.e. too efficient decay through the first conical intersection. Computing LD overlaps from the CASSCF part of the CASPT2 wavefunction only (lLD) is a reasonable approximation here, with a slight underestimation of regime II. The suitability of the methods could hardly be predicted from a static analysis of the potential energy surfaces (SI rigid CNNC scans), so validating a method on static energetics before dynamics may not be sufficient; the authors restrict these conclusions to this reaction. Threshold-based XMS-CASPT2 (thrs) dynamics shows little difference from XMS-CASPT2 (NACV); the decay yield is well reproduced by XMS-CASPT2 with LD and lLD and is slightly faster with the threshold approach, which does not allow back-hopping; the XMS-CASPT2 (thrs) results indicate the threshold approach is not the main reason for the dominance of pathway (ii) in single-reference methods.

nroots_per_mult: 3 (state average over the three CASSCF(2,2) states with zeta-dependent weights)
electronic_structure_description: cCASSCF(2,2)/cc-pVDZ ground and first excited (charge-transfer, Li(2n+1)+Cl- vs Li(2n+1).Cl.) states scanned along the closest Li-Cl distance with zeta = 0.37. Across the Li(2n+1)Cl (n = 0-5) series the energy scale and bond energy are roughly the same ("the energy of the bond is quite local") and the equilibrium cluster-chlorine distance is around 2.1 A for all clusters, while the ground/first-excited crossing moves to larger distance for bigger clusters; EA(Cl)-IP(cluster) is linearly related to the estimated Coulomb energy at the crossing and the cluster IP is inversely related to the crossing position. Diabatic coupling at the crossing decreases roughly exponentially with cluster size (numerical noise or geometry effects for Li9Cl and Li11Cl), attributed to the increased crossing distance, while the maximum coupling (at R != Rcross) does not change dramatically. LiCl: the Gamma coupling of the first excited state to the bath states is effectively 0.
Other: For a standard (unconstrained) CASSCF(2,2) calculation both active orbitals would be located on the lithium cluster; the population constraint places one on Cl and one on the cluster. A population of unity was used, with similar results found in the range [0.9, 1.0].

method: SA-CASSCF (3 roots); SA-fUCCSD and SA-ADAPT (statevector-simulated VQE) as CASCI solvers in the same space
active_space_orbital_description: Rh 4d orbitals except 4d_z2, plus NO pi and pi* (NO sigma/sigma* and Rh 4d_z2 removed from the canonical space)

electronic_structure_description: SA-CASSCF(10,8): bonded closed-shell minimum near Rh-N 1.85 A; closed-shell/open-shell crossings near 2.10 and 2.20 A. Closed-shell CSF is ~50% of the expansion at 1.85 A; the leading CSF is charge transfer Rh(IV)->Rh(III) with NO+; Rh 4dxz->NO pi*x and 4dyz->NO pi*y add ~15% and ~20%. Two open-shell singlets are 88-90% single CSF (Rh 4dx2-y2 and 4dyz -> NO pi*x). 1176 CSFs. As Rh-N increases the Rh 4dyz->NO pi*y weight stays constant to ~2.1 A then falls, while 4dxz->pi*x grows; beyond ~2.2 A the 'closed-shell' state is better described as an open-shell singlet with unpaired electrons in Rh 4dxz and NO pi*x. At the largest Rh-N distances all three states have one electron in NO pi*x (favoured over pi*y because pi*y points toward the surface oxygen rows). Total energies ~ -5288 Eh. Simulated solvers vs SA-CASSCF(10,8) (Table 1; operators, MAD, max error in mEh): SA-fUCCSD(6) 810, 0.32, 0.79; SA-fUCCSD(8) 1080, 0.13, 0.23; SA-fUCCSD(10) 1350, 0.12, 0.22; SA-ADAPT 289 (average), 0.004, 0.015; modified SA-ADAPT agrees within ~1 microEh at equilibrium. SA-fUCCSD(6) errors reach ~1.0 and 0.6 mEh at the first crossing, reduced to ~0.15 mEh with parameters transferred from the previous geometry.
Other: The (10,8) space was chosen on chemical grounds from the canonical (12,11): the NO sigma/sigma* orbitals stayed near occupations 2.0/0.0 and took no part in the state crossing, and Rh 4d_z2 stayed essentially empty and tended to rotate out. A 2-state average lost the closed-shell state beyond Rh-N ~2.2 A; 3 states restored it without changing the orbital analysis. The authors note (10,8) (16 qubits, Jordan-Wigner) is on the larger side for near-term VQE but feasible on ideal statevector simulators; the reference energies are classical SA-CASSCF.

electronic_structure_description: Type B G-center (CsSiiCs) in silicon. notes: Site in a silicon lattice treated as a finite H-passivated cluster cut from the HSE06 supercell geometry, not an isolated molecule.
